I wanted to be the person who ended up taking him down— the person who showed him who was boss, and showed him just how cruel and harsh the world really was to us. Because, it really was cruel and harsh. It really was looking to lap us up, and make us into insignificant pond scum. Nobody wanted to have to acknowledge that. Not him, and especially not me. Though, at the same time, I also knew that it had to be acknowledged. Not just for his sake, or for my sake, but for both of our sakes.

This is why I pulled my one good arm back, and prepared to throw it at him— and then I let my arm drop to the ground. I stopped myself. Instead, I unclasped my hand, and put it into his, giving it a firm shake.

“You’re right,” I said, making sure to have wiped off my coming hurricane of anger. “I was wrong to try and fight you about all of this— you were right all along, after all. The both of us need to work together, if we ever plan on solving this case. I need somebody who really knows what they’re doing to be on my side. Now, please— be that person. Make sure that you’re the one who helps me out, rather than it being the other way around. I don’t want to have to do this alone anymore. Rather, I want to be able to side with somebody, and make them into an ally. I want to show somebody my secrets, so that they don’t go to waste once I truly meet my end…”
Paul chuckled.

“I’m sorry, but that’s never going to happen. You’ve already chosen your path— you’ve proven that you’re simply not the sort of person who works really well with other people. In fact, I’d say that you’re the sort of person who’s immune to such sorts of actions with other people. While I’d be really glad to take up a new partner, and solve this conundrum, you and I both know that you’re just not the sort of person who would be willing. In everything that you’ve ever done, you’ve proven yourself to be one of the most arrogant people on the field.”

Paul Stood there, still as a rock after that. He smiled, and I smiled back. I can’t quite put my finger on it—maybe it was the way that he breathed, his posture, or just his overall demeanor— but, Officer Paul was probably the first police officer that I’d ever met who really looked synonymous to a punching bag in my eyes. In fact, he perhaps even looked more like a punching bag then I expected. Because, after that, he began to bob back and forth. I stood there for quite some time— thinking. Waiting for a response out of me. It was as if he were digging for my anger. Digging for my rage.

Fine then,” I said with a sigh. “I guess that, if you’re done giving me your verbal beat down, then I’m done spending my time on you. You know, I was really looking forward to what sort of team that we would’ve made together. I’m certain that it would’ve been the sort that you never would’ve regretted… But, I get it. We both need to go our separate paths, and determine separate fates. I suppose that, in spite of all of this conversation, and everything that went wrong with it, I still understand your position. I still understand why to you don’t want to be my teammate. And, you know what? You’re actually right, to a sense. I never was the sort of person who worked well with others. Instead., I was the sort of person who always stuck to the mysterious, and tried to find out the answer to the mysterious on my own. All that I can say is that I thank you for waking me up, and I hope that it will help me in the future.”
It didn’t look like officer Paul really had a response for that. His smugness quickly subsided, and his hands came out of his pockets.
“So you’re just going to take the evidence for yourself, then?”
“If you want it, you can have it…
“No… No… I’ll be fine without it. I don’t need tit, unlike you. I have a good memory, and strong skills when it comes to induction. Though, there is one thing that I do need from you…”
“Yes?”

“Please tell me how the butler here looked… you might not have gotten any answers from me, concerning the driver of the car. But, the least that you can do, for the both of us, is tell me all that you can about the butler. Maybe, in this way, we can form a sort of way to track the suspect down. After all— both of us can agree that the butler must’ve had something to do with whatever happened…”
I nodded, reluctantly.
“I guess that I can tell you that,” I said. “But, I don’t actually remember much about the butler. It wasn’t until I was already in the tunnel that I got his name.”

“You have to have some sort of semblance of memory about the man. Don’t tell me that you’re just as clueless as any other cop would’ve been in this situation. You’re e one of the greatest detectives on the force! Come on now— buck up, and show me who’s boss.”

“That’s the thing...” I said. “I don’t actually think that I’m that much of a genius. Even if I were, I wouldn’t be able to find you the answers that you wanted. The truth of the matter is, they’re not that easy to get— even some of the smartest cops on the force wouldn’t have been able to remember well, if they were in my shoes. And, I just don’t have the greatest of memories— especially when things are stressful. In a way, everything that happens becomes a sort of lucid haze– some other, ulterior divine, takes me over. I can’t quite explain it, but it’s just so beautiful a thing. And, at the same time, it’s also so horrid. If only you could understand, it, you’d know full well. I just wish that my memory was better is all.”
“You’re a police officer, on the police force, and you don’t have a good memory?” Paul asked with a chuckle. “That’s rich. You, of all people, should be able to remember what happened.”
“I should,” I said, regretfully, “I honestly should. But, I strangely don’t. I can’t explain why, but…”
“Then explain what you do know, to me,” Paul said, with a sort to fury beginning to seep through his voice. “Tell me what you do know, because I don’t want to be kept wondering.”
“Well, the butler was very tall, and very thin,” I said. “He had balding hair, and a clean-shaven face. His hair was strangely bright red, though— he must’ve found a way to die it…”
“Interesting to know...” said Paul. “Is that all?”

“That’s all that I can really remember about him... I suppose that his voice was especially low, for a man in a suit. And, I suppose that it was odd that he was named Mr. Dom. But both of those things could easily be changed, if this is a master of disguise that we’re talking about her. We don’t really know. So, I’ve pretty much given you all of the best information that I really have…”
“Pretty pitiful for the best information…” Officer Paul said, with a frown. “But, I guess that it will have to do. It beats looking in the sewers for no clues, like you did.”
I waited for him to walk off, on his normal queue. Instead, he just stood there again— stood there, and waited for me to leave.

“Well, I guess that I’m going to go then…” I said, awkwardly staring at the floor on my way out. “But, thanks for all of the entertaining that you’d offered to my ramblings. You know, I really expected you to laugh me off, like most people do in these sorts of cases…”

“No,” Officer Paul said, watching me coldly as I walked out of the room. “I’m the sort of person who likes to study everything and anything— there’s nothing that I’m not willing to look at, and scrutinize. I’d say that it’s my biggest talent, and my biggest curse…”

“Good to know…” I said, heading out. I could still hardly believe that I’d survived the deadly trap in the bowels of the house, brought up a single clue, and yet I was still being reduced to something rather pitiful and powerless. There was nothing that I could really do, except beg and whimper. I was no longer at the level power that I so loved to exhort. Instead, I was trapped under a mess that I couldn’t hope to escape. Trapped, forever. “I hope to see you again.”
“I’m sure that you do,” Paul said, keenly avoiding the social que.

He acknowledged that I didn’t want to see him again. Though, what really got under my skin was the fact that he clearly wanted to see me again— he wanted to make me feel humiliated, just like he had in this encounter.

That was the single most annoying thing about Paul— if, not, disturbing. He wanted to keep you under his thumb, and make sure that you were tied down in just the way that he wanted you to be. He was the puppet master and you were just the puppet that he flung around. While it was fun for a time, it eventually came to the point where the fun was one sided. The only person who enjoyed beating me down was him. And even then, I had my doubts as to just how much it was really enjoyed by him— or anyone, for that matter. Perhaps there was no real enjoyment in it, but, instead, a sort of parasite of the mind. Something that took him, along with everybody involved with him, into a position where they had no sort of logic to sway them from falling into the classic mental traps that the mind held— the classic position of arrogance, and ignorance.

I’m the sort of person who likes to think of himself as being brilliant. The kind who is easily defined as being haughty and arrogant. At the very thought of declaring myself haughty and arrogant, I begin to feel so. Though, there’s nobody quite so much as that as Officer Paul tis.

The one thing that worries me is that There’s more to Officer Paul’s demeanor, and what he does, than simply the fact that he thinks he knows better. I fear the fact that, maybe, his character has something more suspect to it than I once wanted to believe. I used to think that he hated, me, merely because of the fact that I was somebody who was easy to hate— or, that I seemed like I might’ve been the criminal in question, to him. Though, I now begin got think that there was more to it than something so simple as tha.t There was another aspect— a part of me that was just so cold, and cruel, that It couldn’t recognize the fact that it was also very unintelligible. Though, this part of me did have something to it that I was beginning to think might’ve been right.

I had been wrong in thinking that Officer Paul thought that I was the criminal. Perhaps Officer Paul was the criminal… Perhaps he was in league with the very thing that I hatred. I didn’t want to think on this, but it was all starting to line up when I placed it in my head. He knew that when I stated the case— he knew everything about it, ‘m sure, and he was constantly after my position. In every respect, he wanted me dead. He wanted me to pay.

“Well, he denied my offer of partnership,” I said, “And, while I grant him the fact that I would’ve done the same, in his position, that doesn’t change the fact that I’m going to find somebody else. Nobody can just throw me to the wayside, pretend that I’m useless, and then expect go one without any sort of ramifications. I’m going to show him just how angry that I am. He’s going to know that I know exactly what I’m doing. Me, and a new partner, are going to expose him for the very person that he is. The entire group for what they are. And, there; nothing that well be able to prevent me from doing so.”

I drove down the long-winded and jagged straits that I liked to call the streets of Chicago, and I felt a bitter scent take flight over top of me— a puff of smoke. Or, maybe it was the bursting of fuel, form out of the back of my car. Whatever it was, I could feel the sort of regret in having wasted an opportunity to learn something new— a regret in knowing that wherever my enemy was, and whoever they were, they were one step ahead of me no matter wha.t. In this moment, I deeply hoped that Paul was my enemy, and not somebody else. It was the only explanation that I had in myself.

I sneezed form my nose. The entire room had an overpowering scent of roses to it, to the point that it made me want to fall flat. My nose had come to the point where it had become a miniature waterfall, and my eyes had taken a page from the roses’ book, making sure to turn themselves just as red as them.
“Please tell me that you’ll help me,” I said.

I could barely see across the room, because it was lit with so many fluorescent lightbulbs. Part of this had to do with my growing affection for the darkness, and living amongst that— my eyes were becoming too well adjusted to the rain-slicked streets, and lampposts that were so covered in water that their light was utterly drowned out. Though, I was also coming to a point, where I was beginning to wonder if this room had just been designed so that it could be overly obnoxious to a person like me.
“And, what makes you think that I’ll be able to help?”

I was in the room of Miss Mulligan. And, she made a good point— there were few things that she could actually help with, the more that I actually thought about it. Though, that didn’t change the fact that I needed help from somebody. And, she seemed to be the best possible choice that I could’ve come up with, weak as it may have been.

“You nearly drowned today, climbed through a maze, met up with somebody who hates you, and who also went to a crime scene— and, all on the eve of Eddy Mulligan’s funeral— and, you expect me to join you in your wacky crusade? You’re bound to get shot while doing this… And, if not, something worse will happened. Something worse always happens, with these sorts of things. Honestly, I don’t even know why you like this jo. To me, that sounds like a sort of torture. Though, I’ll grant you the respect for your career. Instead, I just ask you this— what makes you think that our job is worth any sort of respect? Why do you feel like I’s the right thing? And, most of all, why do you plan on dragging me into this? I usually find you to be pretty ridiculous, and hard to take seriously… But, this is a new sort of low. There’s nothing about what you do that I can honestly see worthwhile anymore! Honestly, just give it up. Eddy Mulligan is gone, and so is your career.”

I chuckled— not at the fact that she was wrong. She was actually completely right. I had no way to deny that. No—I laughed at the fact that I’d been placed into a corner. I actually had no true way of fighting back at what she’d said. She was right— I might as well should’ve given up on my crusade, should her help have been necessary for me to succeed in it. In fact, I probably should’ve gone way beyond that, and even admitted all of my mistakes— I probably should’ve dropped my career then and here.

Though, there was a solve of my career that I had, which was simply keeping me from doing so. I could feel that the day as beginning to wane, and I was more than willing to stretch it out as long as necessary. I had the unruly feeling that, if I chose to ignore all of my feelings of danger— if I chose to pretend that everything was going to be fine—I would fail myself. And, that would be the only way that anybody could keep their job.

The truth of the matter was, I needed to keep my job. Something internal, inside of myself, was ordering such an action to be carried out. It was the only way that I could succeed, and the only way in which I was willing to succeed. I had determined that things had to be done in a certain way. And, I wasn’t going to allow myself any leniency unless such was done in that way. I had a set idea in my head. And, that set idea wasn’t going to go away.

I needed a partner. And, if Amelia Mulligan was going to deny that of me, then I completely understood. But, I was going to keep looking, because I knew that I had to do what I had to do— it was simply something that I had an incredible passion for.

This was probably the very element that made it so funny. In spite of the fact that I knew I should’ve given up, and that the whole room around me spoke if a tranquility— of a rest that I needed to take—such rest was poison to me. I simply couldn’t take it, without feeling myself steadily whither inside. It was the sort of thing that turned me from a stone hearted, man, and simply into a hunk of stone, with his heart being the only remaining living element to him. I couldn’t do it— I had to let myself continue to fly from my problems.

“I’m sorry to hear that Amelia,” I said, making sure to have my smile melt from my fac. “I don’t mean to be the sort of person who seems to be giving out orders, and telling you to do something that you simply don’t want to do. Instead, I want to tell you to do something that you do want to do. I want to help you find your brother, before his funeral tomorrow.”
Amelia sniffled, and then laughed.

“You can’t expect to find him,” Amelia said. “And if you do, all that you’re going to do Is find a ghost. You don’t want to find Eddy Mulligan anymore… You know how this city works, and I’m sure that you know it. This place has too much garbage going around in it, and not enough to make up for this garbage. An alleviation period is on the horizon, and I’m sure of it. But, Eddy Mulligan coming back from the dead won’t be part of it. I wish that I could say otherwise… But, there’ s simply nothing that can be done. And, to be frank, if this is the path that you choose to take, then there’s nothing that I want to contribute– nothing that I could ever want to contribute to you, or the fallacious claims that you’re making. Even you, with everything that you know, can’t ever expect to make a dead man rise from the dead. I’d like you to acknowledge that.”

“Fine then…” I said, taking one last look around the room. “I never claimed that I can raise Eddy back from the dead. If I said that, then I agree that I deserve to be lambasted by you for as long as you want. I’m just saying that we might be able to find him, and then save him from whatever might’ve befallen him. He might not be dead yet. He might be safe. I’m going to keep out hope for him. And, even by the end of tonight, I’m not going to give up on what I know is the truth.”

“You know that you’re wrong…” Said Amelia. “You’re just putting me in the position where I look like I want things to have gone bad for my brother— where I want everything to look bleak and hopeless. But, let’s be honest with ourselves. You went under that house, and you saw a dead, rich man there… It was a conscious decision, by whoever the murderer was, to even give you aa note– a note to taunt you! Out of all people, you should know best that this whole mission is hopeless. You’ve gotten nowhere, even in your attempts to find answers….”

“You’re right. That’s why I’ve never claimed that I had the answers— just that I’m willing to look for them, wherever they may be. You’re right, on just about every front. I’m not going to be able to find the answers… I’m not going to be able to get what I want, no matter how hard that I look. This probably is all frivolous, and doomed for an end… But, do you know what else? None of that changes how I feel, about any of it. In the face of everything that seems like it’s about to go wrong, and in the face of all the travesties that I need to keep at bay, I think that I’m making a difference. And I hope, very sincerely, that I might be able to help you out, and give you exactly what’s needed. Your brother back…”

“Good luck with that…” Amelia said. “I know that I might sound sarcastic, and angry when I say that… And, I partially am. But, if you can find him— if you actually do think that he can be saved–then, I hope that things work out for you. I don’t think that it will, and I definitely think that you’re on a hunt to nowhere… But, at least I know that you’re not trying to prove something.”
I gave her a weak smile, and headed toward the door.
“I’ll probably be in the downtown area, if you change your mind about this and want to help me.”
“Eddy definitely hanged around there a lot, from what I know,” said Amelia. “Hopefully that’s where he is. I wish you luck, in that case.”
“Same to you,” I said.  “hopefully everything works out.”

I walked out the door, and into the whirlpool of rain that was streaking down the poor excuse of a building. The motel was dilapidated, and crumbling, just like most of the buildings that I’d come to know in this city. At this point, I was beginning to think that decay was probably the one defining trait of Chicago— decay, and crime. Thankfully, I was just decaying— at least I wasn’t the crime element.

“I suppose that this city, in spite of the way it looks upon first glance, is symmetrical,” I said, walking to my car. “In spit e of all the buildings sloping over, as if they were brick hunchbacks, there’s one element that’s integral to them that can’t really be neglected— they’re parallel to the slumping disrepair that a person like me, or the people that I try to stop, have to succumb to. In a way, the city and its streets are a pure representative of those who adhere to it…”

I looked up into the sky, where the clouds were nearly all over, and not a single star poked out. I strained my eyes to be able to just obtain a faint glimpse of it— I wanted, with all of my ability, to be able to see beyond all of the limitations that might’ve been trying to strike me down. Nothing made me feel so terrible as the concept that we were all doomed to fall into a cataclysm, similar to what Eddy Mulligan had fallen int. In a way, this drove me to act. I didn’t want to be ignored, upon my death-day. And so, I thought that making sure that I didn’t die on Eddy’s death-day was something that I couldn’t deny, either.

“It’s all just doomed to become naught,” I said, allowing the wind t whistle down my ears, and through my pores. The city, wet and tired as it was, still was alive. And, as long as it was alive, there was still a hope for it. That was something that I knew that I could always grip to, even when all else failed— even when the chances of going beyond that were gone form my reach.
The man, with a crinkled squint, smiled back into my soul. The keeper of Margaret Rosemary’s apartment was always something that haunted me.
I’d knocked down Miss. Rosemary’s door, with the heavy thrust of m y foot, and I was now studying the room as best as I could.
“I should’ve come her first…” I said, under my breath.”
“you shouldn’t have come here at all!” snapped the squinty man. “Now I don’t have a rent, thanks to you….”
I would’ve let the man have it, but I was busy making sure that there was nothing in the room that might help me out.
“I was just trying to stop the spree of crimes,” I said to the man. “I’m trying to make sure that places like these don’t get robbed.”

“Well, you’re doing a fine job of keeping that up. If you really wanted to do that, you should’ve gone to your little cubby hole in your police department, and thought up something better— because, what you’re doing isn’t all that effective…”
“Yes… I really appreciate it, Sherlock. Maybe if this place was a bit more organized, I wouldn’t have such a hard time.”
“It’s not my fault that my tenant was a slob!”
At this point, I gave up with the man. At this point, I’d assumed that he had no information for me— even if he did, he was only going to spin me in circles first, before I could even get to it.
Instead, I just kept studying the floor.

“I came here to get evidence, and instead I’m stuck trying to figure out a different mystery…” I said, grumbling rot myself. “I have a load of evidence in my car that I’m trying to figure out still, and I can’t even talk to somebody without having more questions stacked onto my to-do list…”

Miss Rosemary really had been a slob, though— if there was anything that the man had been right about, it had been this. Messes were painted across her floor, in the forms of wrappers, papers, blankets, and clothes. The walls were just as bad—entire constellations could’ve been made out of them, if I had tried hard enough.
“Did you ever have any sort of janitor come in here, and try cleaning this place up?”
I asked. “It would’ve made your building a lot easier for me to investigate— and, it would’ve made it easier for you to get better future tenants.”
“You know how this place works… You can’t buy anything without having to beg and plead. I just don’t make enough money for that kind of thing.”

I just allowed him to keep talking, ignoring everything that came out of his mouth. All that I really wanted to know was just how much money his hotel was really making— to be able to tell whether or not they would’ve been motivated to commit such a heinous crime as murder. And, I’d gotten my answer, as slimy and detestable as it was.

Something that I’ve never really thought about is just how magnificent it is to feel like you’re weightless– the ability to no longer feel the force of gravity pulling onto you. The ability to become, in effect, a sort of person that is free of all shackles. I don’t know—it’s that sort of sensation of being freed of all chains that really sharpens the senses, and dulls the overbearing dialogue of the mind. Though, something that I haven’t really noticed, until now, is just how prominent it really is, in my life. I’m constantly puling myself up into the air, so that I can jump back down— and feel weightless again. The pulley upward is a heavy one, and one that I’ve found to be near impossible to overcome. Though, it’s also something that I still thoroughly enjoy. Maybe it’s just because I love the feeling of being free so much, that nothing else matters— the effort of getting up there is measly.

However, what I always tend to forget is that every high height— every free fall— always has the result of the free faller falling back down. It doesn’t matter quite how much effort ifs put forth, or quite how many attempts are made at trying to avoid such a fall. It almost always seems inevitable, and that avoidance of such almost always seems impossible.

I was looking down into the bounty of evidence that I had clustered, since my study began. The owner of the place was still babbling on and on about how poor they were, and just how much they were in debt. I was just waiting for him to list some names. I knew that, if I let him talk long enough, he’d trip quickly.
In the meantime, I had collected a blanket with a blood stain, a shard of metal that had somehow made it onto the floor, and a very unique strip of fabric.

The fabric was probably the most important thing that I found, in my eyes. Mainly because it matched the same sort of material that my uniform was made out of— a blue, coarse fabric, firm and stiff. For me, this finding wasn’t something that could be quantified, in any sort of way. In this moment, I knew with a certainty that the culprit was Paul. Nothing could’ve convinced me otherwise, even in the face of the fact that I had a bias against him.
“What’s with the smile on your face?” the hotel owner asked. “Wipe it off, will you? It’s not like you just won the Olympic medal, or anything…”

“Yeah… Of course not,” I said, trying my best to comply. Though, in my head, I had just won the Olympic medal. There wasn’t really anything that quite compared to how I felt. It was as if all the pressures in my head had completely been stripped away, and I was now in a place of rest, and tranquility.
“So, how are you going to help me, exactly?” I finally asked the owner. “I know that you promised me that you had some sort of important information. But, I’m suddenly not so convinced.”

“Oh please…” he said, making a nasty squealing nose between the gums of his teeth. “I’ve already given you everything that you need to know. For god’s sake, you’ve been able to investigate this entire room, no problem. What more do you want? It isn’t like I know that entire place, inside out…”

“Who works here?” I asked. “I was just curious if you knew if any of them ever came into this room—I want to make sure that this entire place is inspected, and in the best way possible. I don’t want to end up carrying misinformation.”

“Ugh— then, you have no problem. The only people that ever go into this room are the electric people. They had to turn off her electricity, since she wouldn’t pay them. Other than that, nobody comes in the place. It’s largely abandoned…”

“Right,” I said, keeping my eye on all of the elements of the room. The place was just as I had last seen it to be, except sloppier of a mess. And, all that I had left was a bit of blood on a few bits of clothes, and a mess of a room.

“Mr. Kyler, I think that you’re just wasting your time in here. At this point, I think that it should’ve been made it clear to you that there’s really nothing to hide. The whole place is rather empty, and there’s not a ton of substance to your beliefs that something suspicious is going on. I understand your dislike for the way that my business is run— but, I don’t think that you have the right to act as if you can control m y business. I—.”

“I’m just here to investigate, and make sure that there’s nothing going on here that can’t be missed,” I said. “I’d strongly regret it if there happened to be somebody here who needed to be protected, and then I ended up being the one who ignored them— even when there were clues that I could’ve used, in order to prevent that. I’m just the sort of person who wants to make sure that everybody is safe. That might be a flaw of mine. But, I also see it as a duty…”
“Well if your duty starts to infringe on my rights to run my business, then what doesn’t that matter?”
“Because— I need to make sure that people are protected. If your rights are infringed in the process, then so be it. I’m not going to have any blood on me.”
“Neither am I. So, I advise that you get used to the feeling of me wanting you to leave.”
“I got used to that feeling a long time ago.”

I turned away from the room, and headed out. I didn’t even bother to push the man out of the way, in spite of my temptation to do so. It had all become very clear to me that he didn’t care about the truth. Instead, it was all about himself, and what he wanted.

In truth, that’s always what it was about. There was rarely ever a time when somebody was caught telling the truth, in this town. It was all selfishly motivated, and lacking of any sort of sympathy. In a sense, this gave me a sort of wish to give a sense of sympathy out— just so that I might be able to change the sphere in the face of the hungry streets, rabid to make sure that all upstanding people were abolished, I simply couldn’t do this. It was kept out of my reach, and out of my good comfort. My only option was to steadily decline from my control over the scenario, and tumble into a host of problems, which were all competing to eat me whole.

It was back into the leathery seat of my car, and down the water-pelted, oily road. Once again, I felt that I was taking a journey that I could not come back from. Once again, this gave me a warm sense of relief, and enlightenment. I knew that I was on my way out, and over into freedom.

I haven’t been sure quite what to expect when I decided to go down into the sewers, to pursue the person who was guilty of these crimes. Though, I did know one thing— there was nothing at this point that I was willing to do to give up, anymore. I was going to get through this maze, if it was the last thing that I did. I was convinced that this was what I had to do

It was a tiring exercise, and the uncertainty of its cause made it only more tiring. Though, I finally managed to struggle free of the cage in my mind, and eventually climb my way, up out of the place where I was at. Nothing that I did before this moment felt like it really mattered so much as it did now. Suddenly, I realized that I was no longer just fighting in order to keep myself aimed towards a focusing projection to the answer of my case, but also to the answer of my life— I was forcing myself to break free of the temptations to give up, in spite of how strong those temptations really were. It was as if they no longer had a hold over me.

My hands grasped against the smooth, pearly rungs of the ladder, before I was finally brought back to a reality where I saw the rungs as the rusted pieces of scrap metal that they were. I carried myself higher and higher, with my lumbering body using all of its strength to make sure that I made my way back out. at this point, my ideal concerns on the fate of myself had dripped away, and I was entirely entranced and entrenched by the true face of everything— the sewer’s muggy and muddled textures came back for my senses to squander upon, and the squalor of it all finally returned to a state from which I couldn’t deny it. I reached the top of the ladder, where the porthole was— it blocked me from getting passed it, as if it were against my mission— as if it didn’t want come to succeed, and that all of its efforts were being aimed toward the idea of having me fail. Though, I pushed against it anyway— I pushed against it, as well as the mental barriers that still threatened to pull me back down into the last abyss of the mind. Normally, I’m used to having myself give up at moments like these— at least, I’m used to feeling like there’s no way out, and that it is all the end. Strangely, that line o thought wasn’t so prominent this time around. Rather, I felt that it was all gone, and that there was nothing that could make it return to me.

The porthole thrust upward, with it moving from its position with a grinding screech, which made my ears bled to the point that I felt as if there were miniature rivers inside of them. I still pushed it upwards, until the seal was finally pulled of, and I was exposed to the relieving light above— my eyes filled with its dazzling light, and I immediately felt as if it had all finally climaxed to a point where I no longer had anything to be concerned about. There was no longer a single obstacle that could stand in my way— in this moment, I finally felt as if I ‘d reached the answer to might cause invincibility.

It was also at this point that the most reasoned and reactional borders of my mind began to return to me, and I realized just how much of a daze that I’d really been in, up until now. There was something in the sewers that had seemed to sap me of all of my strength and control, leaving me weak and dull-witted. I suddenly became aware of just how much of a miracle it was that I had come out unscathed and unaffected— it was as if the environmental forces, which had been rallying against me, didn’t have as single bit of malice to them— it was as if, by some stroke of luck, some other force had come down and intervened with the events that had been taking place. It was both a wonderful and alleviating thought.

With great care, I made sure to bend over and calmly place the porthole back where I had taken it from— I had the feeling that somebody might’ve been coming after me soon, if anybody was in here— and, I didn’t want to make myself fall into any more trouble than that of which was necessary.
“Go away!”

I couldn’t tell who had said this, at first. All that I knew, in the first moment when I had heard this plea of anger and bitterness, was that the person was one that I didn’t want to cross. The words were spewed with such a vitriol that I thought I might never be able to find something that could be likened to it. In all honesty, and brashness, the voice was something that made me want to go back into the sewer from whence I’d come. Granted, I was still in a slightly delusional state at this point.
“Well, I guess that this wasn’t well-worth it after all,” I muttered to myself. “All of that careful stealthiest, and I’ve already been found out.”

“You came here once!” they continued. I saw a light beam streak across the wall that was opposite to me— there was a guard in this factory. And, it sounded to me like I’d severed the end of a thin rope of patience that they held.
“You promised me that, if you came here and ambushed the place, you would leave for good! Why are you back here? What do you have planned?”

I looked around the room I was in. It was a factory setting, decked out with a mess of conveyor belts, shelves, tools, and a robust warehouse structure. I could smell the scent of sawdust kicking up into my nostrils, and the stink of the sewers below me was now so far off, that I could hardly even notice them.

“I’m Sergeant Kyler, of the police force!” I said. “I’m not a criminal, if that’s what you’re wondering. I came here on police business, so as to make sure that his place is secure— I suspect that it might be the target of a new crime spree. In fact, this was what I think the recent crime spree, which has been being displayed in all of the papers, was ultimately leading up to…”

I was tempted to hide behind one of the shelves, but I let the guard turn the corner, and find, me. Once I saw them, they looked like something short of a ghost. Their body was quivering, the energy in their movements withered, and their eyes was marked by a tacit lacking of tenacity.

“That’s not possible…” the guard said, looking at me in shock. “I haven’t even bothered to call… how did you know? Oh please… don’t tell me that it was that thing… It wasn’t me who robbed this place! I swear!”

“Calm down now— it’s not like this is the end of the world. The only reason that I’m shear is because I’ve been following the trial here. There’s something going on in this factory tonight— all of the clues are pointing to it. And— what thing are you talking about?”
The guards’ eyes swam around in desperation, and their breath sped up as if it were the revving motor of a car engine.
“You don’t want to know… They’re not the sort of thing that you ever want to know… trust me. It was a monster! A monster!”

I would’ve begun pressing more questions on them, but I soon realized that their terror was legitimate— there was something in their eyes that testified to something being incredibly wrong. I could even feel it in the air. The shadowy criminal had been here, and they’d wreaked havoc.
“Just tell me what happened?” I asked. “I already know what you’re talking about….”

“They swooped down from the rafters— they came in here through the pothole that you did. Then, they jumped on top of me— I don’t understand how it happened… it doesn’t make any sense… But, they managed to land straight on top of me, without even hearing themselves… And then— and then…”

Their voice had been stuttering throughout their entire speech, and their words were flying out of their mouth a mile a minute. Though, this moment, they stopped. Tit was as if some invisible hand had clasped around their mouth and giving them warning not to speak. I watched as their eyes glazed over— and suddenly, their muscles tensed. They no longer looked quite right, and I could see that it was no longer just their fear.

“Are you still there?” I asked, trying to get through to them. They didn’t say a word though. Even I they did, it didn’t make any sense. They seemed to be trapped within themselves, closed off from anything else. I could still see a hint of them in their eyes, struggling to break free– but, it slowly dissipated…  And then, it was gone, and they were on the floor. Limp. Motionless.
“What happened?” I said, still desperate to know. Though, I knew that I had no chance at knowing anymore. Any of my answers were once again gone from me.

“What happened,” I whispered to myself, one more. I now looked around the room, and whipped my flashlight about. I f I was being watched, I had to know— I was no longer willing to let myself be covered in a mess of questions. My fury had risen, and my patience, had been done away with. In this moment, when the man had dropped to the ground, I could finally see the severity to everything that was going on. And, I could no longer feel anything close to the amount of peace of mind that I had wanted to have.

“Clearly, you haven’t played your cards right…” I heard a new voice say— it was glowering onto me, and hanging from above. I couldn’t tell where it had come from, but there was no mistaking who it was.

“You’ve done enough,” I said. “You’ve played your game, and left me with more brain benders then I ever thought could’ve been conjured. I’m sick of it all, now. I just want you to end this charade, and tell me what’s going on. Is this all really worth it? Do you think that any of this is really going to be helpful to you, in the end? You’re just rummaging around, but never getting anywhere. It’s not going to help you, and it certainly isn’t helping society...”

“I don’t care for society… Society is the sort of thing that needs to be uprooted. You know this. You’ve tasted society, firsthand. You’ve also tasted what I have to offer. Clearly, the two are very different. Anarchy is the only way that you can properly people to make change, and shake them up by the roots.”

“Sometimes, we don’t have to take a violent approach to do that… Besides. You and me both can agree that your tactics don’t have any clear logic to them. You decide to rob a bunch of people, and steal all of their possessions, only to try and end it all? Why bother with all of them, if your ultimate goal is here? Why rob so little? Why make it so that you barely have any gain.”

“Various reasons. It’s not as if I can rob from them, and then use the money that I robbed. People would catch on to my sudden increase in wealth. We all know that you can’t make that sort of jump, without being caught. Besides— I mostly do this for what it will impact, more than what I can actually directly gain. I’m sure that you guessed that, just by the gravitas of my overall persona… Please don’t act like you’re not catching on. This was all very much done for the thrill of it... but, I don’t think that you’re asking me the right questions. I have a lot more to the plot that I’ve constructed than mere robberies, and acts of terrorizing the public. You know that. You know much more than most.”

The room around me was filled with a new atmosphere about it. The mere hearing of the voice of this man was something that had put me in a mood where I could no longer feel the fullness of anything. Something always followed him, and subtracted from the senses— something dulled my mind, and made me feel as if I were struggling to even keep slivers of it. There was also a sort of intimidation that he bore, and tried to strike down on me. Whenever I was under it, and forced to endure it, I felt that there was no way that I could survive it. It was very easy for me to fall into the feeling that everything was becoming exhausting, and dull. I was never going to get where I needed to go, and I knew it. I was doomed, so long as I was stuck under this man’s gaze.

“So, this is honestly how you feel that this should go down?” I asked. “With me fighting you, and you standing above me as if you’re some superior being? We can do something far more effective than this. I seem to have equaled you, in some sense. You slipped up, and I found ways in which to catch you. Isn’t that enough to earn your trust.  What are you really doing here? Why bother trying to go hear, and terrorize this guard— but not steal anything?”

I already knew the answers. It was hanging in the air— something that I was but ignoring. The only reason that I asked was because I wanted to pull back the answer for as long as I could. I was already inching away from where I was standing, and studying around for where a phone might be. At this point, I was certain that the police needed to be here, and not even the feeling of terror poking at m y heart wasn’t enough to keep me resisting it. This very well might’ve been my only shot— the only way to get this done. I was determined to take it, no matter what.

“You ask a very complicated question,” said the shadow. “But, you and I should both know just how complicated tit is… And fact, I think that you know far better than me. Think about it. This entire place is subject to a perverse nature, and a grotesque design. It isn’t as if there’s anything smart, or creative, to it. There’s also the way in which you’ve seemed to have looked into a place where there’s no clear way out. That’s something so typical of you— even you would admit that— but, now I’m actually going to have you face that fact, head on. Be honest with yourself. After all of the evidence that I’ve given you, is it really hard to know what’s going on? Are you really having that much of a struggle to figure it out? I’d prefer for you to be a strong person, and a strong mind, at the same time. I know that you want to make a difference. But, I also know that you want to know the truth… know the truth, or don’t. I don’t care. But, I do care about what you do. I do care about you— in my own way, of course. I’ve given you the clues. Now figure out the answer for yourself, or face the punishment that comes with it. That’s all that I can ask of you, and all that you should expect out of this.”

I had no idea what to think about his overlong speech. I knew that this was what he wanted me to believe.  I knew that he wanted to think that he was such a genius, and that everything he did was planned out with a precise perfection. Though, I also knew that he wasn’t quite somebody that I could fully trust. I simply saw a sort of ugliness in him— something that escaped all reason, and all control that I personally had. At least— a him. It might’ve been a she. That was one of many things that I couldn’t tell about this person. They were something else entirely, for me. There was no way in which I could predict their decisions, or their thoughts. The only thing that I could understand were their clues, and even then, their clues were very sparse and few.  Maybe I was just being paranoid and fearful, but I thought that he as one of the most terrifying foes that I faced. In fact, he was the only true foe that I’d ever faced.

All of his clues seemed to indicate that he was planning on trapping me in this place. Or— at the very least— making sure that he finally ended me, tonight. I wasn’t sure how I was going to get out of this one, or if I could get out of this one, Though, I was sure on one thing. My police force was going to be called over here, no matter what, and I wasn’t going to let anything stop me from doing that.

“So, is this really how you want this to end?” I asked, backing away, towards a telephone that I’d spotted. There was such an entanglement of tools and cement structures to this place, that I was concerned that I might run into a pillar. I didn’t even quite trust myself as I backed away, because I knew there was a chance that the shadowy figure might swoop down behind me, and make me pay for what I’d done. However, there was sweep of courage that flew through my chest. It was something that I couldn’t quite deny— something that left me with a swelling sense of pride, and strength. I had to back up, after feeling that. At that point, I knew that it was a duty that I had— both to myself, and also to the people around me.

“I’m sure that you think yourself to be such a genius…” the shadow said. “In fact, I wouldn’t be surprised if you saw yourself as something more than that. You aren’t a being who is very strong with his deduction skills, nor are you strong on reasoning. Instead, you fall flat in both arenas. I’d love to have the pleasure of asking you why. U t then, I have the keen feeling that you’ll fall apart very soon here.”
“I’m not overly interested in the concept of failure,” I said. “But sure— let’s imagine that I am… So what? What is in it for you? Why are you so obsessed?”

“Because, it’s about time that you try to make a difference in the meaningless course of your life. Something that you don’t understand, nor have ever understood, is that I’m the sole thing that has brought you meaning. I’m the only reason that you can still use logic to get yourself out of here. You are my servant, in a way. I brought you here, with all of my clues. I planned this, despite you thinking that you were the one who out-smarted me. I knew that to you would be here, and I knew that I could toy with you. You’re the sort of person who will never be able to get through any of this, without eventually getting caught by me. That’s the only thing that I don’t think you’ve ever realize.dd. You’re a person that’s doomed to get caught, and to get sent away. Everything that you’ve done is in service to my plans. And, you will fail from it….”
“Can’t I succeed?”

I had already grasped the phone— it’s surface was one that gave a gush of warm blood through my body, and allowed me to take a deep breath. The clicks of its knobs, as I turned them about, gave me even more f this overflowing river of relief. The police station steadily came closer to me, with each turn of the phone’s wheel. I could practically feel it coming to me, when it suddenly all stopped— it was forced to stop, because I was forced to stop. Behind, me the greatest fear of mine was standing. I couldn’t bear to look at it, but I couldn’t bear to move either. I was stuck in the position of a lack of position. I didn’t know what to say, what to think, or what to do…
I made the last turn, to the last number, and I placed the phone at my ear. I knew that the shadow could see me as I did this, but that didn’t matter.

“So, I see that you’ve finally given up on the easy way, have you?” the shadow asked. “Such a shame… I had such high hopes for you… I really thought that you might be able to express your full potential, rather than take the cowardly way out. I suppose that I was wrong…”

“You were wrong on quite a lot of things,” I said, waiting for the phone to pick up. For some reason, it wasn’t. My face was starting to become coated by a reddened brush of embarrassment. In an instant, all of my peace of mind had started to melt away.
“I see that you’re still trying to get through it all… but, you’re never going to get through to them…” said the shadow.

I wasn’t getting through them. I had been so slow, and I instantly realized why the phone wouldn’t work. In my rushing, I hadn’t even bothered to notice— but, the phone had been cut straight off of its wire.

“Well, I suppose that You should have thought things out a lot more,” said the shadow. “but, then again, I already knew about all that. You’re nothing short of an idiot. We’re all that way, in this city… but, I’ve caught on that you’re amongst the most prominent of them all.”
“I don’t know why that comes as such a shock to you. After all, didn’t you already know that I was an idiot?”

“I knew that you weren’t the sort of person who was very good in their strategy. I knew that you wouldn’t be able to pick up on everything that I’ve given you. Even now, you don’t know quite who I am, but, I guessed that you would at least be able to catch on to something so simple as severed telephone wire. Please, don’t insult me by acting like I haven’t thought through all of these things. I’ve looked at every possible route of your escape. I wouldn’t be surprised if there are one or two that I never accounted for— but then, you’d never account for them, either. You’re stuck in here, with me, and the only thing that you can do is watch.”
Not for the first time this week, I became aware of my broken arm. It was such a blockade to my full potential, and I know that I was about to pay for it.
A hard punch to the stomach. Than the side. Finally, I was hit in the head, and down on the floor.

“Such a pretty ending…” the shadow said. “I don’t know how you were able to get away from it all, with all of your other enemies… but, I’m glad that this is how it all ends up. You’re broken apart, and laying on the ground. I’ve put you through everything that I could come up with, and let you suffer the most terrible of pains. I’ve made you feel what it’s like to truly meet a threatening wit— not one of those piddle bits of jokes that you managed to scrounge up, after all of these years. I’s nice to see you finally break down... but then, it’s also a very sad ending for you. After all, you went down after three punches, and didn’t have a punch to give me in return.”

I wanted to give them what they were asking for, but they were right... They were right in all of it, as much as they wanted to rub it in my face. I didn’t have a way out of it all, and my plans really had fallen short.

The shadowy figure came closer, and began to stoop over me. I could feel its coal heart emanate from within itself— its oily gaze left a markedly disgusting waft of fumes in the air. Its fingers clasped mine, with it practically overturning them— with it biting down, and into my soul. I immediately thought that there was no other thing that I’d ever seen or experienced, so dark and foreboding as the figure that stood before me. In an instant, I realized that there was something to it that I simply couldn’t compare, or conjure up in my own mind. I stared into where I had finally found its eyes. Though, I found that the pair of black pearls were more than just eyes— they were also an entrance gate into a hellish world, of which I could hardly understand.

“Friedrich Nietzsche was right…” I said. I had tried to hold my words back, but they managed to go out in a puff of breath. In the same jarring punch that the shadow had given me, he’d also given me a twinge of a different sort of pain— a sort of pain where I could no longer control myself in. Instead, it was as if he’d dived into my mind— as if he was controlling me.
“About what?” asked the shadow. More of its powdery fog blew into my face. I could feel it control eye again— but I resisted it.
“Come on now,” the shadow repeated— this time with its voice holding a toxic weight of malice in it. “I haven’t dragged your ragged body this far, only for you to give in.”

I didn’t finish my sentence— I didn’t give in. I couldn’t. In an instant, I’d realized that this was what it had wanted. It had all been a ploy, from the start— a way to get me to confront him, face to face. I refused.
“If this is the face off it wants, then it will get it,” I thought to myself.
After a smattering of the telephone system to my head, and a downpour of pain and broken plastics, my tone had immediately shifted.
The face-off was over, as far as I was concerned.
“Tell me!” the shadow yelled, while still keeping its voice in tune enough, so that I couldn’t fully identify it.

The moon was like silk above me—its light was the only thing left to guide myself by. Somehow, the shadow had short-circuited all of the light in the building, in the midst of our fight. It was as if it were trying to impersonate the darkness of the factory— as if it thought that, in this way, it could somehow overcome me.

“I didn’t come all of this way, for you not to follow through on my game,” the shadow said, inflecting its voice in such a way that it now sounded sweet. In the meantime, it was clutching oft my sides– jabbing its claws as far inward as it could.

“Your heart is on its last stretch— we both know this, Sergeant Kyler. I can feel your pulse pumping through your bones with such a weakness… Don’t act like you couldn’t hide it from me, after all of this time… Now, I’m just curious— how much more are you willing to test your heart? All you have to do is state a few simple words— it will be over after that.”
“Fine,” I wheezed. “When you stare into the darkness— the darkness stares back into you.”

The shadow didn’t make a word, or utter a sound. However, I saw its smile bleed through the darkness— the moon’s light made sure to shine through, and reflect off of its teeth. In this subtle, short moment, the riotous grin shone out like a cold blade. I even felt it cut through my mind like one. The Cheshire cat wasn’t even anything that might’ve been able to compare.
“I always knew that you’d eventually attest to that fact— at some point…”
“How nice of you.” I said. “You must know me a lot better than I thought you would.”
“Our history goes a bit further back than this warehouse— I’m sure that you know that.”
“It goes back a lot further…” I said.

“Perhaps our dichotomies clashed, long before now. But, not us. Not in the way that you think. I’ll admit, however, that you definitely have me pinned down in some respects… You— the very essence of age, death, and the waning of all … Order… But, my dichotomy is clearly superior. The very essence of energy, recklessness, and life… Chaos. We’re about as opposite as can be. You’d think that are polarities would be repellant to each other. Instead, we act like magnets. I’m the flame, and you’re the dying moth— all burnt to a crisp, and out of your past flutter. Though, like all polar opposites, we still each need to have a pole upon which we can connect. The pole that exists between both of our dichotomies is a sense of reason. We both know how to rationalize things— tell ourselves a pretty story, and make some sense out of it. If we couldn’t reason, then you wouldn’t be here— instead, I would’ve made sure to turn you into a drooling puddle, in order to pay you back for your missteps.”

“Just get to the point,” I said, with a choke. I had been reduced to the floor now, leaning on the pillar where the telephone had been. The moonlight shone upon me like a spotlight, making me how with sweat. And, the shadow had leaned close, so as to put his hand around my throat— so as to keep me in my place. It had a heat to it that turned me into a ball of sweat and tears. Though, there was nothing that I could do to fight back against it.

“Tsk, tsk…  I would’ve thought that you would’ve learned a sense of patience, after all of the carnival games that I put you through… Please— let a person finish their speech before trying to interrupt. Then again, you’re only proving my point— the hypocrisy in your cause. You see, I came here to show you that the superior dichotomy, between order and chaos, is chaos. You might think that you’re the one who possesses the stance where everything might flow off of. But, you’re nothing more than a desperate joke, in that respect.”
“It would be nice if you came out of there, and showed your face,” I said.

To be honest, I wouldn’t have been able to see their face if I’d tried. After all of the beating that had gone through, my head was throbbing tremendously, and my eyesight had been reduced to a blurry smear.

“I have—you just haven’t figured it out yet, because you’re truly that ignorant to everything that’s going on around you… Not that I should be surprised. In all honestly, I’d be more surprised if you still had your wits about you, after everything that I’d just put you through…”
He’d hit my head so hard that I couldn’t see clearly. Everything truly had gone fuzzy. In a way, I felt like there was no way out of the place that I was in. I
‘d been beaten to submission, to the point where nearly every part of my body felt numb.
“I definitely wasn’t built for this,” I thought. “You know, it sure would’ve been nice if this place had had more than one guard…”

The sound of metal, scraping against a soft surface, breezed through the air. It had a rotten undertone to its decibels— if there was a way in which a sound could smell moldy, that was it. In nearly every way, I couldn’t trust it. I simply felt out of place, amongst it all. It was the sort of sound that leaves you on your knees— the sort of sound that makes your spirits sag into your gut, and then makes you wish that you actually had some guts.

“Well— I see that you’re not comfortable with that sound,” the shadow said, with far too much relish. “I’ll make sure to take a note of that— I’m sure that you think it to be very cook, and soothing… Don’t you?”
“Just get it over with, if you really want to keep this up…”

The shadow let out a sound, that was mixed with the honking of a horn, and a laugh. “I see… you really think that there’s a bone in my body that might be willing to give you some mercy. Don’t you?  I’m afraid that’s just not how it works. I’m going to make you feel pain in every part of your body. Each mark that I lay down on you will represent the people that your failed to help, and all of the victims of mine that suffered, under your watch. There were so many people that I captured… So many people that you could’ve saved, but never did. They were all right under your nose, if only you could’ve been more alert. I always made sure that I left something behind for you, and your friends. I always made sure that there was at least one way for you to make it through. Sadly, you were just too stupid. Even after everything that ‘d laid out, your mind was still twisted up by my brain twisters…”
“What can I say? You’re just too smart for me…”
The cold, gun metal was already rubbing against my ankle. I could feel the slit that its razor short edge made into my skin, and the thin grin that was being hidden under my blurred vision.

“This is fun…. Too much fun…” said the shadow. “I threaten you, and go through my whole spiel… And then, you cower back away, trying your hardest to find some sort of solid footing. I wish that this could just go on forever. It’s things like these that were just too beautiful to ever let end. In fact, I just don’t want it to end. You don’t deserve anything, except to be here, at my feet… Cowering…”
“Alright, I get it,” I said, still trying to maintain a wry sense of humor. I couldn’t though. Even as I tried to stay on my feet, all that came out was a grunt, and a groan.
“What’s wrong? You don’t have any fight left in you?” asked the shadowy figure.

A swift kick to what was left of my stomach. I felt as my head throbbed, and my whole body lost its stability. Though, tit still came near a devastating end— I could feel it beginning to careen into an unwanted madness.

My whole body felt sick. Devastated. I would’ve tried to pull myself up, but I simply couldn’t. There was nothing that I could confidently do. I was near-doomed. There were only a few hopes that I had left— but, none of them were ones that I could find a significant confidence in. It would’ve taken some sort of miracle to get out of here.

Another bash to the head. Then another. I could hear somebody singing now That is, I could hear them singing, up until I realized that it was actually the sound of the ringing in my ears. “no… This is just a few old trinkets that I collected.”
