“I see that you must think me to be some cruel crime ring-leader…” Miss Prestel said. “With all of my wealth and all that… but, I can’t see why you think that I might’ve been guilty of any of the things that you’re criticizing of, nor understand what sort of evidence that you might have against me. I’m afraid that you’re simply too brash of a person for me to entertain, or offer my time to… Honestly— I don’t think that I’m willing to give you tea, anymore. Not after what you’ve done…”
She paused, and stared at all of my injuries.

“Are you quite sure that you’re alright, dearie? After all of the things that you look like you’ve been through, are you sure that you’re not suffering from some sort of head trauma. Perhaps resting here might ease your pain…”

“I’ll rest after you give me some answers…” I said. “I was in the sewage of your factory, and all that I can say is that it left me with hallucinations. Not only that, but I do have something suspicious on you…”
“And what is that?” Asked Miss Prestel. “If you think that I’m somehow linked to the shadowy figure, you’re mistaken.”

“That’s just it,” I said. “You’re the only person that the shadowy figure never seemed to terrorize, to kidnap. You’re the only person who seemed to have been robbed… And, you’re the only person robbed by the shadowy figure that didn’t seem to have any connections with Mr. Donald’s company, like the rest of the kidnapped individuals did. Here’s my main problem, however… I Had a scuffle with the shadowy figure, and her just so happened to drop a sheet of paper while fighting me. Maybe it was just a coincidence, but it was a document that had been stolen from your house— one of the only things that had been stolen from your house— and, this document just so happens to link you to Mr. Donald…”
“That’s not any dirt on me…”

“But it is. The document says that you’ve been taking care of the toxic waste that MR. Donald’s factories emit, for a tidy sum. You were also in the process of making another business deal with him. What’s even odder is that these documents are combined with one where Mr. Donald sent you a letter, informing you that he wasn’t interested in working with you anymore— namely because he found out what you were doing with your toxic waste.”
“I guess that he was one stupid man,” Miss Prestel said. “To be honest, I can’t quite understand why he thought that I was doing something nefarious with toxic waste…”
“He said that he’d found out how you were dumping it into the sewers….”

I paused, to look straight into Miss Prestel’s eyes. There was a fear within them. It was too obvious that she was having some sort of internal conflict, and that she was on the verge of a breakdown. Her previously delusionary façade had faded away, and I was now looking at what she truly was— a conniving vermin, who had just been cornered.
“It looks like your days of robbing the tombs of the jungle, and abusing monkeys, really aren’t over… you’re still at it, and as bad as ever.”
“I might mistreat monkeys, but it’s not nearly as bad as you’re making it out to be! Miss Prestel said, in a fury. “I love monkeys! I’d never harm them on purpose!”

“I’m sure that you always say that… But, are you really being honest with yourself? After everything that I’ve seen about what you’ve done, I think it’s very apparent that you’re not being honest— not with me, and most certainly not with yourself. at least I know the truth, and am willing to say it. You, on the other hand? Part of me wonders if you’re even willing to say what you’ve done… I think that you might be forever trapped in a position where you have no idea what’s going on…”

I stopped. I heard a creak form outside of the parlor door, and was instantly forewarned that Her butler, Mr. Gretchen, was outside— listening to us, as we spoke. I had a hard time being able to cope with this fact, and even a harder time ignoring it. Though, there was truly no denying what was going on, or that it was a big problem

“The longer that he listens, the more that he’ll know…” I thought. “He might break the fragile moment of interrogation that I currently have, ad call the police. Or worse, he might warn Miss Prestel’s friends that I know about what’s going on.”
I couldn’t think on any of this though. I was stuck trying to figure out what was currently going on, and that was all that I had to focus on.

“I think that you and I each keenly understand everything that’s going on, and just how dangerous it really is…” I said. “I mean— you’re probably in denial about a lot of it, and unwilling to acknowledge it. Similarly, I’m partially resistant to the admission of all of my sins. However, there’s the fact of the matter, and it’s that people are hurt— kidnapped. And, the person who you have them trapped with is mad. Look at what that person did to me. Look at what you did to me. If it weren’t for the fact that I had help from Detective Crusoe, I would’ve been doomed. If you care about this city at all, you have to explain what’s going on to me.”

There was a crack of lightning, and a roar of thunder. The lights went out of the room for a minute, and I listened as the rain bean to ferociously pound against the walls of the house. I almost welt as if the droplets of rain might be able to break through he walls, and begin to pelt onto us. In fact, I could’ve even sworn that I heard droplets of water splashing onto the ebony floor that was beneath my feet.

There was another bolt of lightning, and the whole room was lit up with a bluish tint. It was particularly unappealing g when I caught sight of Miss Prestel’s bloodshot eyes, and her bony face. She almost appeared to be a malformed goblin. If it hadn’t been for the lights flickering back on, I might’ve been convinced of that.

The lights did flicker back on though, and the room returned to its former clarity. It was then that I caught a second glimpse of Miss Prestel’s face, and saw that her eyes were bloodshot from swelling tears, and that her face was streaking from her crying. The splashing of droplet s on the floor had been from her as well.

“I’m sorry…” she said. “It’s all my fault. Everything. All of it… My company has been on the verge of bankruptcy for years now. I’m the sort of person who likes to haggle with money. Even when things aren’t going in my favor, I look for loopholes. I thought that waste disposal might be my answer, but I clearly was wrong… I’m sorry for keeping these things a secret from you… I know that this probably will be the end of my business, but that still doesn’t make up for everything that’s been done…”
“You’ve kidnapped several people... And Mr. Donald is dead, because of you.”

Miss Prestel stopped short. For a moment, I thought that I might’ve scared her to death, in the most literal sense of the phrase. However, her breath returned, and I saw that she’d simply been stricken by a frenzy of disgusted shock.
“They weren’t supposed to kill anybody…” she whispered. “that’s not how it was supposed to go.”
“Who?” I asked. “What? Please, just make this clear to me already.”

“I hired somebody to kidnap all of these people, so that they might not squeal. I didn’t want anybody t be able to talk about what I was doing, or give things away. Once MR. Donald found out, I knew that I had to cover my tracks. My ultimate goal was to kidnap Mr. Donald, but to make it look like an incident from a random crime-spree… My goal was never to kill him. It was always just to mute him…”

I stared at Miss Prestel with a mixed look of disappointment and rage. I couldn’t quite tell how I was supposed to feel about what she’d done. Clearly, it was amongst the most wretched thing is that she could’ve done. In all of my years of experience, I’d never had anybody go to this extreme…. But then, I’d never had to solve a case like this, entirely by myself, before.
“Who did you hire?” I asked.

“The shadow…” she said. “It was all just a plan so that I could keep people quiet about the chemicals that I was dumping into the sewers… My intention was never to do what I ended up doing— hurting people. I just wanted to hide what I was doing. It was that innocent. I don’t understand how it could’ve devolved so easily….”

“Maybe it’s because you instated something that can never be looked at in a good light. Do you honestly think that trying to kidnap people could be perceived as a good idea? DO you honestly think that you might’ve been able to get away with it? I know that it might be tempting to say yes. In fact, yes might actually be your answer. But, it simply isn’t the right answer. I’m not sure if you’ve caught on yet, but kidnapping people is a crime.
“Now, who is the shadow? Explain it to me.

“I don’t know… I just don’t know…” Miss Prestel said. “I hired the shadow after having my butler go and try to find people who met my specifications. I needed somebody who could help me do what I needed to, and I was pretty confident that he’d be able to find them. However, I wasn’t certain as to how he would be able to find help— I should’ve asked him, but he never told me. I’m guessing that he went into the city’s underworld, for help.

“That’s when the shadow came to me. On the same night that he told me about finding help. I basically explained myself, and what I wanted done, to the shadow. Then, it explained itself. It was as simple as that. I n fact, it might’ve been simpler… but, things fell apart so easily. They always seem to. I’m not sure how I could’ve thought otherwise…”

“I see,” I said, trying to act understanding. Instead, I was extremely revolted. Miss Prestel seemed to talk about kidnapping people, and, ultimately, having some people be killed, as if she were describing to me a recipe from her favorite cookbook.

“It all spiraled down, from there, as I’ve already informed you. Not long after that, the shadow was asking for supplies. I needed some sort of resource to create smoke bombs with. It thought that my disposed chemicals were a good source for that. While I was worried that it all might be traced back to me, eventually, I still said yes. I should’ve declined. I always look back on that day, with this thought lingering in my mind. Though, it was still a series of accidents, all the same. I doubt that they planned things to go the way they did any more than I did…”
“I don’t share that doubt, and I feel that the shadow doesn’t either. Anyway, were the chemicals by any chance, derivative’s from cleaning supplies?”
“Yes,” said Miss Prestel. “I tried using the cheapest way of disposing things, in order to get it done.”

“And, all of the people that you kidnapped— the poor and the rich— were they working for you?““Not the rich. But the poor? Yes… Somebody had to dump the chemicals, at the end of the day. They, of course, were a perfect fit.”

Everything was beginning to collide for me…. The sickness of the workers, the shadow’s obsession with working underground, the way in which the whole place was being hidden from me, how the picture had been taken in an alleyway, over a gutter.… It all was starting to make sense.
“I think that I have an idea of what happened then. What still confused me, however, is your connection with the hospital.”
“What hospital?” asked Miss Prestel. Her hands shook, from side to side, and her eyes darted all around the room. She could’ve been replaced by a squirrel, and look no different.
“The hospital. The one that closed down, several decades ago? I received a picture form Detective Crusoe, linking it all to you… Was it really from you, or was there more going on?”

“It wasn’t me…” said Miss Prestel. Though, she looked into my eyes, and saw that I was unconvinced. Then, her head shrunk back, and I watched as she began floundering for things to explain herself with.

“I did it all, back a long time ago,” she explained. “The chemicals that I used for it were far too much, even back then— factories were a very fresh and new thing. I’m sure that you know that… But, What I’m sure that you don’t know is just how much I was looking for disposal. Eventually, I had to dispose it all into the sewers, where there was nothing for me to do. You already know this. But, what you don’t know is who found out.”
“You’ve been doing this for years?” I asked, with shock.”
“For as long as I can remember,” she answered, promptly. “You can’t possibly expect me to do this on my own, and somehow avoid the costly prices of running the factory.”
“I have a hard time believing that this is the only way that you cut corners, then.”
“It isn’t. But, I’d prefer to not have to explain myself to somebody like you. You’re no better than most of the people that I’ve met— why do you deserve an answer?”
“I’m the sergeant o the police force…”

“Right— right. Well, I’ll keep giving you what you want, then. You see, the hospital owner found out, and was going to tell everybody. HE wanted to expose me for who I was. So, I did the only thing that any reasonable person would do— I found his building, dumped chemicals in it, and then made other places where I could dump chemicals. It was a rather easy thing for me to do, once I had it all figured out. Anyway, I also figured out ways to infiltrate the hospital, and get the chemicals into his patients’ hands. You wouldn’t believe how much people were willing to do for a spare penny, back then… Anyhow, once that all blew over, his hospital was in ruins. You wouldn’t have wanted to be him, on that day. HE had everything that he ever loved taken away from him, and quite possibly more. Some days I feel a sort of guilt for what I did. Sometimes I even feel like I might apologize, if the man were still alive. Though, there are some things that simply can’t be apologized. For. Instead, you just have to face the facts, and grow up…”
“I see… And, you did the same thing to his son?”

“Of course. You can’t just leave competition like that alive, I’m not insane, even if I might seem like it at times. After all of that, I wasn’t willing to have all of my hard work exposed, and destroye.dd. So yes– I made sure to do another round of exposing his patients to chemicals, and called it good.”

I nodded. Suddenly, I realized what had happened to Eddy Mulligan, along with everybody who had crossed Miss Prestel’s path. It had all been on her— always been on her. And, I could hardly believe it once I began to realize.

“You know, sometimes I thought that the shadow was the only villain here,” I said. “But, I now realize that t the true villains are often the ones who pretend that somebody else is the villain… After all of this, I’m going to have to say that you’re under arrest.”
I stopped to look at my watch— it was five in the morning.
“It’s going to take me another hour to get this all done,” I thought to myself, worriedly.

UI wanted to arrest the butler too, but I already had my suspicions that he would’ve ran away before ever risking the chance to become a jailbird. I was going to have to deal with the one suspect that I’d caught— a strong piece of evidence for what that happened, but still somebody who would probably refuse to talk unless I supplied further evidence.”
“I’m glad that you told me all this, but it’s time that I had to take you in to jail,” I said. “Good luck on anything that I do, and make sure to tell me exactly what’s going on here…”

At this point, I didn’t care about what she must’ve been thinking, or how cruel her thoughts might’ve been. I could already see the anger in her face, and her shrinking wish to speak to me. As I had her turn around, and put handcuffs around her wrist, I felt her slight resistance against me. It was very slight— something that I easily could’ve missed, if I’d been ignorant to it. But it was there, all the same.

“I hope that this will mark the end of this spree,” I said. “Now, let me list you off your rights… But first, I have one last question to ask you— do you have any idea as to what the identity of the main criminal behind all of this is?”“No,” said Miss Prestel.

There was a gleam in her eye, which said otherwise. She had more going on behind her head than sh was willing to reveal. However, I knew that I didn’t have a chance at getting her to stop with her parade of these crimes— she’d been willing to do all of the wretched things that she’d done, and never bothered to try confessing. At this point, I doubted that she’d be willing to confess again.
“You have the right to remain silent.” I began.

It had been a long hour of paperwork, and explaining myself. Lieutenant Jackson was strangely absent from the department, but Officer Paul had taken the reins— and he was about as cruel and brash towards me as ever. For a while, he didn’t believe a word that I said, but he eventually had to admit it, once everything else was explained. There was one thing that I asked him that did happen to put me off balance, however— the fact that he hadn’t heard about what had happened with me at the factory.” Crusoe never told you about what happened?” I asked, surprised.

He told me no. Nobody had ever been called, as far as he knew. It was at this point that I knew that I had to leave. AS soon as the work with Miss Prestel was over, I left the building— with the promise that I would return.

The sun was starting to rise in the horizon at this point. It was six. Even though I couldn’t glance at my watch, in fear of wasting time, I had no doubt about it. I could already feel the dew of the morning beginning to take seat, as well as the chimes that might come from the early church-bells.

Despite the fact that I was doing my duty, and making sure that what needed to be done was done. I couldn’t help but feel a mixture of guilt in my gut. At this point, I was supposed to be dressed up for Eddy Mulligan’s funeral, and preparing to join the funeral procession. Instead, I was flying through the streets, to solve some sort of crime. I shouldn’t have been on duty.  I should’ve, instead, been on my true duty— that of which was reserved for my friend.

I was able to justify this irksome fear by telling myself that I was in the middle of helping Eddy— I was trying to find out what had happened to him. This was oddly comforting, even if I partially thought that it was undeserved. Eddy truly was somebody who deserved my to be standing at his funeral, at his side. We’d been such great friends, when we were younger. Even as our paths split up, we were still great friends. There was truly something disturbing in having to recognize my folly. In fact, I came to a point where I wished that I was no longer alive, and that I could simply give up everything that had happened to me— give up my passions, so that I might not have to choose between these two contradictory dilemmas. I had both a loyalty that was due to my friends’ memory, and my friends’ conclusion. I couldn’t tell which I was supposed to be more loyal to. Despite knowing that I had more than one friend waiting for me at Eddy’s funeral, I couldn’t help but feel that I’d be abandoning them all if I didn’t finish my case.
“Such is the mess that comes with detective work…” I thought to myself.

This was probably the single thing that pulled me through my uncertainties, and internal calamities. I knew that there was nothing that could comfort me— and so, I came to the point where I realized that I would simply have to become comfortable with that fact. It wasn’t something that was easy for me to have to realize, nor was it something that I wanted to have to recognize— but, it was fact. And, the ignorance of fact did not equal innocence.

Despite the phrase that ignorance is bliss, I find that I simply can’t put any stock into that comment… Ignorance is simply the guise of bliss. In ignorance, you think that there’s such a thing as bliss… IT’s only until you gain knowledge that you realize, in knowing that there’s no such thing as bliss, your true bliss is found— a comfort in knowing that there is no bliss. We’re all to guide and steer the ship of our lives, to where we see fit. I now see that, no matter what choice I had made on that morning, it would’ve been the right one. Not because both choices were equally good, but because both choices were merely choices. It was in knowing that, in accepting what I felt was best— ultimately, accepting myself— I would be making the right choice.

I listened as my tires squealed in agony, when I slammed my foot on the brakes. I’d finally reached the location of the factory that I’d abandoned, by Crusoe— as well as any trace of him— was gone. It was as if he’d never been at the factory in the first place.

I ran up to the factory, and found that the doors were locked. Everything had been restored to its previous quality, so as to make it seem like nothing had happened through the night. There was only one thing that I could find, which signified that my memory wasn’t lying to me— the hat of the guard, who the shadow had nearly struck dead. It was on the ground, in the middle of the parking lot. It was as if it were mocking me— showing me that everything that I remembered had happened, but still refusing to give me what I needed— evidence.
“You won’t get away with this…” I whispered under my breath.
It only took me a moment to figure out what had happened. Crusoe had been bested, and the shadow had taken away all evidence of the night’s events. It was as close to clean as it could’ve been.

Dejected, and regretful, I walked back to my squad car. The barren factory was a sight that only teared at the most fragile aspects of myself. There was no possible way that I would find any relief, when starting at it.
“I guess that I should’ve been preparing for that funeral after all,” I whispered. “Sorry Eddy…”

AS I unlocked the door of my car, and prepared to walk into it, I saw a number spray-painted onto the ground. It was subtle, and very easy to miss—but it was there. The same series of numbers that had been in the picture that Crusoe had given to me, after all of this time…
“Why?” I wondered. “After all of this, that’s what the shadow decided to leave me with?”

MY car-engine was already running, and I had been preparing to dry out— but, I couldn’t help but stop all of that, in order to explain to myself the sigh that I was seeing. It was all too clear to me that there was some mistake. Something was wrong— I simply needed to figure out why the numbers were on the ground. To me, it almost seemed like a magic word, that could be used to unlock everything that was tormenting me.
“I should’ve known that it would all come down to something like this…” I said to myself. “It’s all so simple. Everything was pointing in this direction… how could I have missed it?”
Even when I tried rationalizing it to myself, I couldn’t… There was no way that I could’ve rationalized something like this away. It was all simply too diverse and complicated of a subject.
The numbers were correspondent with a letter— that much, I could tell. But, I couldn’t understand why, or how.
“Wait…” I said to myself. “I think I got it.”

I don’t normally talk to myself— I mean., I suppose that I do. Though, I only ever do it when I feel that my mind is running a mile a minute, and when I think that the pressure of everything is at a peak. In this moment, that’s exactly how I felt. There was nothing that I could really compare my sensation of elation to. It was an experience that was so unique and so unlike anything that had every been described to me, that I had to go and do exactly as my mind directed me to. There was no hesitation, or second thoughts— it was all a sweep of action, and whim.

I pulled the scrabble of a paper from out of my car’s passenger seat, and then began using the numbers and letters on the ground to decode it. Not long after, I had it all down— and then, I felt a jolt of shock and terror, at realizing that everything that I was doing had been planned out from the very beginning.
The page read,
“Glad that you finally got things all figured out. I never thought that you’d be swift enough to come up with an explanation on your own, so here it is… I’m going to give you exactly what you want.
This is the location of some hostages that I’ve taken:

I suppose that it’s high time that you learn the identity of Detective Crusoe. I figured it out quite some time ago, but I’m glad that I can finally come to the point where you can learn it too. It’s time that we both share the things that we forever like to hide—both from the world, and even, partially, from ourselves. I just hope that you’ve figured this all out, in time. You have until 6:30 AM, this Monday, before I try striking down one of the two hostages that I’ve decided to take for myself… It might sound cruel of me, but. I’m somewhat trusting in your abilities— it shouldn’t be too hard for you to figure me out. And, hopefully you won’t have any regrets. I know that I won’t.

After reading the letter, and then pulling out my map of Chicago in order to correspond with the provided coordinates, I realized that there was one thing that was extremely wrong with it all… The coordinates corresponded with two separate parts of Chicago, and I couldn’t tell which one it was.
“Nice… Now I have to play this puzzle, too? Why can’t you just be open about everything, if you’re willing to give me some coordinates?!”

There was no way that I could truly come up with a satisfying answer, so I instead tried to use all of the brainpower that I had remaining, after my exhausting stretch of a night in order to determine which area the coordinates were referring to— the northwest quadrant, or the southeast…  I eventually found that there was no way that I would be able to tell, on time— the time on the clock was at fifteen minutes to six thirty… Even if I had enough time to get to the place where I needed to go, I was still going to have to deal with the hurdle of getting there on time. In truth, there was no clear directive that I could pay attention to.

“That’s it… This guy isn’t getting mercy,” I said to myself with a venomous huff, after spinning through the circle of possibilities. “Even if some of this might be true, I’m still never going to find the answers that I’m looking for…”
I gave a sudden pause.
“I do have one thing…” I whispered to myself. “it’s not anything that might matter, but it’s still something…”

I grabbed the hat from off of my seat, and looked at it… it was a picture of the sun, falling into the west. I’d always seen it as the logo o Miss Prestel’s company— but, clearly there was much more going on, behind the shadow’s mind.

“Northwest…” I said, as I panted to myself. I need to go into the northwest quadrant… All I know is that, if this doesn’t work, this person is going to have my wrath. They’re not going to get away, after this game that they’re pulling…”

As much as I tried to assure myself of this. I simply couldn’t maintain the confidence that I wanted to have. I felt het, no matter where I went, the shadow would be on top of me—trying to dissect my mind. I f I found them, and it wasn’t a trap, it would still be something that was designed to skew my mental faculties.

In thinking this, I felt my heart begin to pound, and my forehead transition between a cold sweat, and a fiery headache. Even as my foot gleaned over, as hard as it could on the gas, I still had the disconcerting feeling that I wouldn’t be able to get to where I wanted in time. MY wishes of self-preservation were so strong, that I tried my best to go as fast as I could, without going too fast, down the water-filled streets. It was as if I was driving into a river, by the way that my tires splashed against the water, and by the amount that they splashed up. However, that wasn’t something that I could focus on.

There was nothing that I could focus on. Everything was blurry. Racing. Streaking. Creaking. My bones were groaning; my mouth was moaning. My jaw slackened, and my eyesight blackened. I tried to beat the street, and make my mind and destination meet. Though instead, it was the street that had me beat.
Raw.
Damp.
Clamped.
Jaw.
Stamped.
Swamped.
Stomped.
Maw.

I couldn’t breath— my throat was clogged. My entire mind was racing so fast that it had forgotten to make me breathe. My chest hurt. Sounds began to sound like a fizzling fuzz. There was nothing to cling to, except the fact that there was nothing to cling to. Even as my car raced down the street, I still felt like it might go out on me, at any moment.
My heart might go out on me, at any moment.

Whether it be that the rain simply decided to have mercy on me, or if my will was far stronger than I thought, I managed to make it to the coordinates that I’d been heading towards. I was in the slums of the city— no doubt just as bad as any other downtown area. Though, I still knew that there were things that I had to keep accordance to, and maintain my loyalty to. Despite being upset by the turn of events, there was something that still offered me a cup of relief.

I found that I was sitting in front of a clothing shop— I hadn’t spent my time in front of this shop in all of my life. Though, now that I looked at it, it seemed familiar to me. It wasn’t until I caught what was in the window that the answers came to me— there were Crusoe’s clothes in the window. They were gawking at me, and I couldn’t help but gawk at it. It was the very las thing that I’d expected to see.

The pavement by the door was just as slick and damp with rain as any doorstep. Yet, I couldn’t help but feel as if I were slipping on it as I walked upon it– it seemed to grab at my ankles and try to pull me downward. I opened up the shop, to the musty but dry empty shop that was exposed to me. There was a slight concern that I’d come to the wrong building— however, this was all that I had to go by, and so I went by it. The outside of the place still called back to me— almost as if it were warning me not to go any further. As if to say that I was on the brink of serious danger. However, I didn’t listen to its cries. I instead ignored them. It was all that I could do, to keep my sanity— it was all that I knew how to do.

I pulled on a light switch, and walked further through the flickering guiding light of the shop. There were stacks of boxes, and racks of abandoned clothes. The whole place looked as if it had been untended for months, and was simply waiting for the jo b to be finished– for it all to be cleared out. I partially wished that I might’ve been able to join it, but there were few things that I could truly do. It was all just a cataclysm of questions that were going on in my heard. While I wished for things to be clear, I knew that they never could be.

The carpet on the ground was colored a stark green, and the windows seemed to catcall at me— I didn’t know what to make of any of it, necessarily, but I couldn’t help but feel sick while looking at it wall. Then, I heard a clicking sound. At first, I reasoned that it must’ve been the sounds of my shoes on the soft carpet, or some ornament outside, making a clicking noise in the rain. There was no evidence of any such thing, and I steadily became aware that the click was getting louder— more prominent. Closer in proximity, to the point where I felt that it had invaded my person al space

My hands began to fumble around the place, and my legs turned to blocks of wood. Gazing everywhere, I couldn’t find where it had come from. Eventually, the gazing just devolved into a bloodshot searching of a madman—always looking everywhere for answers, but never coming any closer to finding them.

It was at the back of the room— behind the empty clerk counter. I could see the door at the back. It was quite obviously a passageway into the back of the room. I’m not sure why, but I was still so resistant to going near it. I knew that the time was nearing six thirty, and that the hostage was in danger. However, my urge for self-preservation was too great for me to simply cast aside, as if it were nothing.
“It’s nothing,” I told myself. “Nothing.”

Though, the ticking became louder. Finally, I couldn’t stop myself, and I came to the door. My hands gripped the knob with an iron strength, and tried its hardest to make it turn. The fruits of such became lessening in return, until I found that the door simply wouldn’t budge.

“It certainly would’ve served me well to have learned how to pick a lock...” I thought to myself. I was already rummaging through the clerk’s desk to see if there was a screw driver anywhere. I desperately wanted to unscrew the knob, but was getting the steady feeling that I might not be able to.
“Ha… So desperate. And yet, so valiant at the same time.”
There was no mistaking the voice.
“Why are you doing this! Just let the hostage go!”
I stopped, and then let out another shout. It came out weaker this time— my whole body felt that it was about to collapse this time. Though, I still had to say what needed to be said
“This isn’t you, Crusoe!”

“Oh… but it is me… I can’t believe that it’s taken you up until now to figure it out. But, yes— I, Crusoe, have been behind it all. I know that this isn’t quite the message that you were hoping for– that you really wanted to be able to see something better, and stronger. However, that’s just not the way of the world. You made a mistake when you thought that I was innocent.”

I couldn’t believe it. Everything went numb. My thoughts Ran still. And, the room around me, even in its mundane and simple design, immediately became imposing— overbearing. Threatening, in the highest sense.
“You can’t possible do that… It’s simply not right. It doesn’t even make any sense! I saw you that one night. You were in my room, with the shadow.”
“That was a mirror that I placed in your room. You never caught that, because I made sure to keep the room dark… But, I was fighting the mirror image of myself, the whole time.”
My gut turned to a fine powder, and my reasoning skills were nullified. There were few things that I could say. I’d been hoodwinked, and I hadn’t even known it.
“Tell me who’s behind that door!” I yelled. “You’ve done enough damage.”

“Not enough… Not yet. Don’t you have any patience these days, Kyler? I remember how you used to be so swift at coming up with the answers, and getting things pinned before anybody else could catch you. Now? You’re just scrambling for what should’ve been done years ago… You could’ve found out my identity a hundred times over. But, you never did…. Why? Were you just too terrified to know who was behind it all? You didn’t want to see the wizard, behind the curtain?”
“I didn’t want to have to see a man. I didn’t want to know who you were…”
“Well then, I guess you won’t ever have to know who I am I’ve been hiding behind this, all this time. And, I have no reason to reveal myself to you, any time soon.”
“Fine then… Don’t tell me… but, who are you holding hostage? Why?”

“I have Job, Jonah, Eddy Mulligan, and the Lieutenant himself… One of them is me, of course. But, hat’s for you to figure out. In the meantime, I have dynamite lining the whole room, courtesy of Miss Prestel and her vast resources. I’m going to light it up, and bring this whole palace down with me… With you.”
“And, you’re just going to give it up, just like that? Never going to reveal the answer to your mystery?”

“No… No, no, no. That’s not how it works. I ‘m Zeus, and you’re Perseus. You roll the stone eternally up the mountain, never fully completing your task— and I sit there, forever beyond your wrath. I need e to seal this all up, eventually. Our history mandates it. You dumped me, once the prohibition ended… We were a great team, you know. And then, you turned on me. Why? Don’t you think that you could’ve lasted longer? Don’t you think that our friendship never had to end?”

“You ratted me out, and called me a bootlegger. You turned on me, and were a criminal! You were convicted for the murders of several individuals! I always wanted to believe that you were an innocent man, and that you never had the intent to harm… But, I’m not a fool, Crusoe. I always suspected that you weren’t right in the head. Now, why are you doing this?”
“To show you how I think, and what I feel about all of this— to help you understand.”
The haughtiness had left Crusoe’s voice, and all that was left was a void.
“You hurt countless individuals… What are you trying to show me? How are you supposed to show me it?”
“I never hurt anybody who wasn’t deserving of it. It always irks me when you try to twist my actions.”
“You worked for Miss Prestel, and kidnapped countless individuals…”

“Her butler came begging to me for help, after talking to some underground people… because of you, I had been rejected from my profession, and line of work. All of my respect had waned, and there was nobody who could take me seriously anymore. It was all because of you, and the twist of the universe’s sense of justice. I never deserved what had happened to me… I was simply a paid vigilante, doing what could make me money.”
I looked back down to the floor.
“Green is the color of envy; you know…” I said. “Your true colors are showing.”

“And here I was, always thinking that the green on your face was merely out of your disgust towards me. While I know that you must have a strong sense of detestability towards me. After all, I am the very sort of person that you vowed to bring justice to, back when you became an officer. Though, I just can’t help but feel that there’s more between us that must be made clear. I need to teach you the things that I’ve learned. I need you to be able to see what I see…”
“All you see is red…”

“I might have seemed like the sort of person who’s purely driven by vengeance, anger, hatred, or pure insanity. But, I’m none of those things. You think that I’m the villain, but you don’t understand the fact that I’m much more than that. I’m the hero— as much as I find them to be overrated— and you’re the villain. You’re the insane one, out of us two. That’s the very thing that I wasn’t to show to you…”
“I’m not insane. I’m only calling things as they appear.”

“And, that’s the very essence of insanity. To not be able to question your own view of things– to question what is truth, and what is a lie— is insanity. You don’t think yourself to be insane, and curdle at the very thought that you might be. I, meanwhile, couldn’t care less in either direction. I’m confident in knowing that I’ve rationed everything. You see, you’re the opposing side of me— on the extreme end of justice. I’m on the other end.”
My head began to ache, and I had to stop myself from talking with him. There were too many words flying around, And I couldn’t keep up with them wall.

“Justice is a construct of society, and can only come through their set of rules…but, the issue is that society never considers that they might be wrong,” said Crusoe. “Even the unruliest of people can be more productive than the most loyal of sheep. That’s what I’m trying to display. I can still exhibit more logic than any of the people who claim to bare sophistication.”
“Stop right there…” I said. “how could you be the detective Crusoe, and the shadow at the same time. You’re complete opposites!”

“We are…” said Crusoe, strangely. “who said that I was consistent? Some night s I call myself Crusoe. Other nights, I don’t speak, or call myself anything at all. Some nights, I tie myself to a chair, just so that I might not escape— escape and make the city suffer under myself. I suppose that I’m a case of Mr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde… It’s just, I can’t tell which of the two that I am more, or which of the two that is preferable. Sometimes— such as on tonight— I question whether or not there’s even a difference between the two sides of me.”
“You have two identities? After all this time, that’s what’s been going on?”

“Not quite, I’m afraid— though, you’re very close to target. I’m actually partially insane, I’m sure. But, I’m not so bad as you make me to to be. Some nights I’m one person, some nights I’m another. That’s all that there really is to it.”
“That’s it! Tell me which person you are? Who are you!? I’ve had enough of this!”

“I’m sure that you have, but I certainly haven’t… Have you heard about the latest thought experiment by Erwin Schrödinger? No? It’s been dubbed, ‘Schrödinger’s Cat’— a fitting name, if I do say so myself. In fact, I wish that I had come up with it…”
“Speaking of cats, I’m not interested in playing cat and mouse. Speak up, or I’m busting in there.”

The man paused— started laughing. I had come to the point where I recognized that Crusoe had always been masking his voice, after all. He must’ve been a genius, of grand proportions, for me to have not known who he was all this time. However, it was still hard for me to have to figure out what was going on.

“Schrödinger’s Cat essentially describes the idea of quantum theory— I’m sure that you’ve never heard of it, since you don’t walk amongst the intellectual sphere like I do. I’m not alive nor dead in this room… I’m not Jonah, or Eddy, Or Job, or even Jackson. I’m not anybody, until you open the door up, and find out. I’m not letting you find out, I’m afraid… That’s up to you. A choice that is at its end.”
“just let me in, so that I can face you. Or, are you too much of a coward? That must be it…”

“Not so much a coward, as I am unwilling to be distracted from my endeavors. It doesn’t take a mathematician to realize that there are only twee people talking in this room. Why? Because I gagged the others. That’s the thing, which you haven’t caught onto… I’ve been letting you be the only true observer amidst all of the things that I’ve done…”
Sweat was beading down my forehead, and my face had turned red and puffy.
“I’m tired of this. Where are the kidnapped people? I don’t just want the location of these two.”

“These three, you mean. You forgot the fact that, I too, am kidnapped in this room. By the way— the dynamite in here will be lit the moment that you try breaking down this door. I’m not going to let you even try to interfere. If you’re going to get some answers out of me, you better do them the proper way…”
“Fine then. Where are all of the people that you kidnapped?”
“In various places of the sewers… Tied down, and forced to stare at my writings. I placed the writings on the wall… The writing is on the wall…”
I looked around at the room’s wall, but quickly caught that he’d been bluffing.
“Just a distraction…” I muttered to myself.
Then, louder, I said, “Can you give me the exact location?”

“I don’t remember. And, even if I did, it would spoil the surprise for me to tell you. I’m afraid that you’re just going to find the answers on your own, fair and square… I’ve been hiding clues this entire time, trying to make sure that you figured out what was going on. You’ve been so hard to figure it out, and bad at doing your research. But, you’ve done your job. So, I suppose that I might as well give you a bit of credit for that…”
“How were you able to give me the clues that you did? And, why did you frame somebody— or two somebodies, for that matter?”

“It was all for the purpose of misdirection… At least you now know who I’m not, now that I’ve exposed everybody who I’ve kidnapped. I must say, I’m quite impressed by your ability to be perceptive about these things, but your still not quite as fast as you could be… Honestly, if you were interested in finding out the answers, you would’ve already found them by now. Let’s both be very brash with each other. You are being ignorant, and you just don’t want to face it.
“But the pictures… Why did you give them to me?”

“I stole them from Miss Rosemary, and figured that you could use some guidance. Miss Rosemary was part of my ploy all along, working for me and such. She had you pegged. That’s why you and her will need to be entered into the hospital as soon as you can. The perfume in her room had never been simply perfume, but toxic chemicals as well… Hopefully you’ll find her.”
“You’ve taken a step too far. Don’t you care about what you’re doing? It’s a permanent solution to a temporary problem.”

“The permanent solution is coming, no matter who it is… Maybe it’ll come in the form of one person, or another… Btu, everything is eventually going to fall into disorder. It already has begun to. I think that I respect your will beyond anybody else’s. I know that it might not mean much, coming from somebody who is clearly your enemy… But, I truly mean to be on the same side her. Eventually, everything is going to fall apart. I think that we might as well do it sooner, than later, and figure out how to cope amongst it all. Meanwhile, your solution is to try to keep the broken system running as long as you can… You can’t keep your finger in the dike forever, Kyler. Eventually, it’s going to kill you.”

“I don’t understand you, and I think that you really need help… How much of everything was planned out? Why did you take Miss Prestel’s work, instead of somebody else’s? How long has this been going on?”

At this point, I didn’t care about how everything was going. I’d pretty much become content with what my fate might be. It didn’t look to me that there was any way out of here, other than through the route that was currently being offered up.

“You can go out in a whisper, or in a bang. Why not make the choice, while you still have it? If you can control your ending, why not do so? Why let the universe choose for you? You act as if you can’t understand me… And, maybe you can’t. Maybe I’m not the sort of person who can easily be understood. Yet, I’d like to bet that you can understand me, and that my logic stands true. The only way that you can make a difference is by doing the very thing that people are telling you not to do…

“Anyhow… As for your questions. I’ve planned out most of this. Granted, Miss Prestel was an addendum that I was only waiting for. For the past several years, ever since you’ve dumped me from our partnership, I’ve been solving cases for other people. Sometimes, I also commit crimes— murders, heists, and such…  But, that requires a far tidier sum than what most people are willing to hand out. My goal was to leave some breadcrumbs, so that you might know what I was trying to accomplish here. Every sculptor must have somebody to admire his sculptures. Or else, he becomes his sculpture— idle, and limp. My trail of chaos has crippled both Miss Prestel’s and Mr. Donald’s empire, as well as the police force. Tonight, you will die with Lieutenant Jackson… And, that will be the end of it all.

“Miss Prestel simply happened to be that one person who matched what I needed… Somebody who was rich, and willing to get me to do something dirty. I was obsessed with being able to bring terror onto this city, and she was obsessed with cleaning up a trail of devastating knowledge.”
“I don’t understand… You wanted to show how much of a mess we are?”

“I wanted to show how much of a mess we create. We spend our days making messes, and pretending that we don’t. We’ll arrest a person who stole some cash, but not the lying cheat that he stole cash from. At the end of the day, society embraces the darkness, but likes to say that it’s embracing purity. Don’t you understand, now? Can’t you see the insanity? Or, are you still going to try to believe that the insanity is in me?”

I wanted to believe that it was all him, very badly… Though, he had a point, that couldn’t be denied. In the dark room, from where I was standing, the e flickering light above me basically represented my own worldview. I thought that the light was a study guide, but its guidance had always been dim. Now that I was in this monster’s presence, I could see that my light was flickering. And, perhaps I had never needed it at all. Perhaps it had always been just as much of a waste as it had been of use.

“I don’t agree with you, in the slightest,” I said. I was lying, and I think that the mystery-figure knew it. However, I no longer cared. “Me and you— we used to be serving out the same sense of justice. We used to agree upon the law, and what it was meant to do. What happened?”

“The law changed… It turned against me. Then, the world turned against me. It wasn’t until then that I realized that the world had always been turned against me. What I don’t understand, Kyler, is you. After all of these years, why haven’t you turned away from the world? What has kept you oh so pure?”
“Not breaking my code.”

“Personally, I don’t buy that for a second. Nobody has that kind of willpower. You’re a liar, and that’s how you’ve made it through. At night, when you’re sleeping, that’s what it takes to make the dreams come back— that’s what pacifies you, through all of the darkness and corruption. You’ve become the corruption.”

“Well, according to you, the only portion is corruption. Would you prefer for us to strive after the dreams, or to let ourselves decay in the same way that you have? Keeping my finger in the dike might end up killing me. But, taking it out will end up killing everybody.”
Crusoe began to laugh. It was more of a strangled laugh— not at all anything that was pleasing to the ear. Though, it was a laugh all the same, and one that I was forced to endure.

“I guess that it all comes back to the cat…” he said. “At the end of the day, what we should do is neither good nor bad. All that matters are doing them, and seeing the results that might come out of it. It matters little which path we take. All that I want you to see is that there’s no difference, either way.”
“There’s a difference. I’m not sure if you can catch this, but there’s a stark difference between your nihilistic approach on things, and the reality of the situation…”
“Well if it is the claim that existentialism is different from nihilism…”
“Isn’t. And, please tell me that you could come up with something cleverer than that to put in your monologue.”

“I meant what I said— I’d appreciate it if you stopped treating me like an intellectual infant. The seconds are ticking down to zero, Kyler, and the minutes are nearly exhausted. Are you really going to end that all, byy grammar policing me? Then again, I suppose that I shouldn’t be all too ill of heart towards this… I guess that you, wasting your time away policing me, was the only fitting way that this ever could’ve ended. Such a poetic justice— wouldn’t you say?”
“An eye for an eye leaves the whole world blind. Poetic justice doesn’t have anything poetic about it.”

“Oh, the irony! You declare that the eye for an eye policy is wrong. And yet, you don’t take into consideration the fact that you follow the same fallacy. Tell me— how can you ride the bus to the vile hypocrite Ville, and still see yourself as the Hercules of this city? Despite it being tempting to mistake this place for Athens, it’s merely ashen… Mm… So delicious, I must say. You call me the sinner, and declare me worthy to stand behind your finest prison bars. And yet, you still think that punishment for punishment is a bad policy? Tell me— how can you say that my views are mutated, mucus-splaying, and deserving of muting and mutilating, but still hold your views on a pedestal of mosaic proportions? I’ve called you on you bluff—  your rituals aren’t so buff. Stuff me in a corner, and throw me in a sack… but, you’re never ever going to turn me back. The clock already seals your doom, upon my doom. At each moment, a new thread is sewn between you and I. Our fates are in preparation to collide. Are you prepared to die the greatest failure of our age? Or, will you finally open up to my logic?”

“What kind of question is that? I’m not entirely certain in myself. In fact, I’m as unsure of myself as I can be. But, It’s not as if I think that I must cast aside all human decency because of that. Where do you think that this is ever going to get you headed? Isn’t the question of our purpose the greatest reason for us to be here… Perhaps I’ll never know who I am. but that’s ok. In, perhaps the only sense of poetic justice that I don’t utterly despise, I see a sort of grand irony in the twisting design of things. I’ll always be wondering until I am, until I am nothing.”
“That’s because you are nothing.”

“Or, maybe it’s because I’m something more. Why not come out of there, and see that with me... We don’t need to fall into this humdrum muddle, straining and groaning to get above each other. We can collide our strengths, and try helping each other.”
Crusoe’s laugh emanated from the door with such a volume, that I felt the door begin to vibrate. It came to the point where he began to wheeze, and my whole body started to tingle in apprehension.
“Sorry Kyler, but I’d prefer not to. Truly, a great offer… But, yet another offer that I’ll have to decline.
I gave a smirk.
“This is just how it’s going to be, isn’t it?” I asked. “You won’t conform, and neither will I?”

“I always knew that you wouldn’t conform, Kyler… At least, not with admission. That’s why the dynamite is set to go off, indiscriminately. No matter what happened, I knew that you would say no to my proposal. A very devastating fact, but one that I had to face. I’m sure that you can understand something like that.”
“Afraid that I can’t. At least, not in the way that you make it out to be. Personally, I think that you’re amongst the most revolting people that I’ve come across.”
“As do I. But, I can’t pretend that I don’t find a charm in the people that I hate. That’s why I always try to keep my victims alive…”
“Probably would’ve been better if they never were made into your victims at all.”

“But then, they wouldn’t be mine. I know that this might sound somewhat arrogant— but, I feel that, in order to make a mark in this world, I must mark as many things as I can. I must say as many things as I can. I must do as many things as I can. Now that it has all climaxed at this point, I feel as if I’ve made the most out of my life. I’ve finally made the message that I could never get anybody else to take…”

“Did you ever consider the fact that maybe— just maybe— nobody would take your message because it was wrong?””No… More along the lines that nobody would take it because it was ahead of its time. Perhaps you might not like to hear things like this, but I don’t agree with what the mass populous says— or, what most anybody says, for that matter. Because, most anybody is always wrong. The people that we stuff in high places are those who agree with our incorrect judgments... We’re made stagnant, because of it all. From what I can tell, the person who has nothing good to say will be allowed to speak, while the person with eh effective and moving words will be muted. The reason for this is that, in our darkest days, we landed our ear to the former— and, the former side took it into their hands to make sure that they made our other ear deaf.”
“I guess you have a point. After everything you’ve done, the only way that you were ever able to make a difference is by forcing everybody to listen to you.”

“Just because there are few ways in which people can listen to me, it doesn’t mean that I’m breaking the very code that I’m trying to build up for myself. Personally, I believe that you’re too harsh of a critic… I’m trying to change the state of things by enacting a form of thought that most try to deny…”
“And what form of thought are you enacting? Because, all that I see is the embracing of brainwashing…”
I heard Crusoe stop, and give out a defeated huff. This was followed by the sound of his comrades doing their best, muffled attempts at screaming, and the sound of fizzling dynamite.
“Such a tragedy…” said Crusoe. “Btu, this is the way that I had to go out…”

“Stop blathering on in insanity already, and tell me how to get this door open!” I said, banging my hardest on the door. “You’ve got too much to live for! Let those innocent people go, at the very least!”
“I’m sorry Kyler… But, I have so much more to die for. And, so do these people who are with me.”
“If you have an ounce of decency…”
“I have an ounce of decency. What I’ve found, though, is that everybody else lacks it.”
“Why are you so obsessed with this? Stop tying everybody down!”

“Tie down a person against their consent, and it’s called kidnapping… Tie down somebody, with their consent, and it’s called a contract. The whole scheme of life requires compromise, Kyler… Your very breath is something that is drawn against your will. Why are you so against the fact that there might be something beyond your control? Either way, there are such things… Compromise is necessary if the balances of justice can ever hope to be managed. This is my compromise. Taste the fireworks, while they’re still going off, Kyler.”

My heart was beating a hundred times a minute, and I felt as my vision began to turn a solid gray. I looked for a way in, or a way out— but both escape me, and I felt as my entire grip on things pulled away from me. I felt like a cloud— my form was steadily ripped apart by the wind. I now had little hope.

There seemed to truly be nothing that would change this man’s mind. For a long moment, I felt utterly doomed. It all seemed like my work was being ripped to shreds— as well as these people’s work. What made it worse was that I held such a hatred for Crusoe, and what he was doing— yet, the very fact that he refused to shed his mask made it so that the identities of everybody ese was cheapened. I wanted to feel sympathy for all of them— but, I knew that one of them was a cold-blooded psychopath.

But then, I also knew that they were all people— we were all people. No matter what happened, I now knew that this was something that I needed to cling to. The very fact that there was still humanity in the room instilled a new life tint he room. It wasn’t enough to renew my lost strength, but it was enough to pull me out of utter disparity, and allow me some returned control of my motor skills.
I thrusted my body against the metal door of the room.
“I don’t know if any of you can hear me!” I shouted. “but don’t panic! I’m going to find a way to get you guys out of there! I’m going to find a way to help you out of that rough spot!”

Despite all of this assurance that I tried to give them, I felt hat it wasn’t enough— that it could never be enough. Even as I pressed my head up against the door, I felt forever separated from the people inside of there, who were being held against their will.
“Everything will be alright!” I said.

“No, Kyler,” said Crusoe, once again shooting out his rays of spite. “You have it all wrong... After all of this teaching, I would’ve hoped that you would’ve learned the very thing that I was trying to get across… In the end, the scales of the cosmos cares little for what the results of our endeavors are. Dead or alive, happy or depressed, it’s all inconsequential. I’m afraid that you’re very late on figuring that out. If only you could see the truth…”
“If only you could.”

“I’m sure that you hat e facing the truth of matters, Kyler. We all do. But, this moment is to serve a purpose. No matter how hard you try sometimes, thing s will fail you. You will fail you. And, that’s why we can never hope to perfect things on our own. You were always your greatest enemy. Even now, you still are. I hope that, in these last moments, you see all of that. I hope you realize just how hopeless you really are, and that you were on the wrong side all along. Maybe, right before your consciousness fades, you’ll come to agree with me.”
“I could never agree with you. If I did, I would no longer be who I am.”
I heard Crusoe sniffle, after that. Almost as if he were in tears.

“I know that, Kyler,” he said, still sounding like he was on the verge of sobbing. “That’s why I’m so bent on convincing you. Because, I knew that, if I could convince you it would be the one way that I could truly kill you.”
After this, his words shifted from depressed too harsh and grating. It was almost as if something entirely different had begun to possess his being.

“But, of course, you just wanted to sap the plans from right out of my clutches. You could never conform to me— you always had to fight me, didn’t you Kyler? Fighting was always something in your blood…”
I wouldn’t say that fighting was so much in my blood as the wish to stop the fighting was… If anybody here is a fighter, it’s you. You always could throw the meanest right hook.”
Crusoe let out a chuckle.
“Yes— I suppose that you won’t be doing that again.”
“Hey, we’re both going to be blown into smithereens in a minute here. I don’t think that my ability to punch was going to survive, either way.”

“It was all inevitable, wasn’t it? Everything that we went through, I mean. There was no other way that I could really conceive this having gone down. I always wanted you to break, and admit defeat. However, it seems that I had to force us into a stalemate. With all of my raw intellect and brilliance, there were few ways in which I could get you to do what I wanted. At the end of the day, this was a fun game… But, that’s all it ever was.”

The time ticked on from behind his door. I could already smell the waxy smoke that must’ve been coming off of the dynamite, and I could hear the coming screams. This truly was the end of it all. I could feel it in my bones. My whole body was already beginning to quake in the pure scale of the ramifications of it all.

“I always wished that this would all come to an end,” I said. “At least, I partially wished that… There was this part of me that had wanted to say that it was the end of all things… Of course, I now know that no such thing was ever going to happen in the way that I had intended. I always dreamed of solving some unsolvable case, and then lapsing into retirement. Instead, I get to die knowing that I’ll never solve that case…”
“The case of my identity?” asked Crusoe.
“No. The case of what it might mean to be alive…”

I couldn’t tell what Crusoe was thinking, on the other side of that door. However, I feel like his voice had suddenly mimicked the tone of my own. There was a sort of mellowness to it. I could barely hear it on the other side of the door. Though, when I did, I felt as if I werefloating on a coud. There was something about it tha t truly made me feel alive.

“I think that I have the answer to your question…” he said, with his voice now melancholy. “The meaning in life is that there is no meaning in life… Everything we are is just fragments of what has come before us.”

I paused for a moment. MY mouth was dry from the potency of everything that was going on. I felt like I was swimming amongst the storms of the ocean. A drop of water from the ceiling felt like an entire wave. In that moment, I was hyper-aware of evertything. I simply had the adverse feeling that doom had finally clamped its jaws down.

“Perhaps that’s supposed to be an ugly thing, Crusoe… Perhaps the fact that there’s no meaning makes you feel obtrusive towards our attempts to find meaning. But, I can’t help but find our attempt to find meaning to be a quaint beauty. And, perhaps there’s an answer that we haven’t quite found yet… Don’t you think?”
“I’m afraid that I don’t think that. You know full well what I truly think of things. The very notion that there’s a meaning beyond the material seems to be the epitome of superficial.”

“Fine then. But, meaningless or not, we’re losing the only life that we have. For me, that’s both painful and stunningly precious. This is the very end of everything that we’ve ever known, and quite likely will know.”

“We never knew anything, Kyler… That’s just one of your many mistakes. In this world, we’re about as clueless as we ever could be. This situation is the perfect allegory for that. You stand behind the door, unaware of the truth that lies behind it… Perhaps there is no truth, and it’s all lies that are behind it. You don’t know. You’ll never know. That’s what it means to be human, in my eyes.”

“For once, I don’t care about what you think of things. I can’t see the dynamite on the other side of this wall, but I know that it’s going to go off at any moment. I know that I know it, simply because I know it. And, that’s good enough for me. Maybe it’s too hard for your mind to wrap around— but, it’s something that we’re all required to think on, ultimately.

“As we die together, do you think that you’ll be willing to call yourself my friend. Perhaps these are our last moments, and perhaps this is all due to you. Yet, I still care about you, Crusoe. After all of our years, working together as comrades, I can’t help but feel as if we both matter very deeply to one another. Why don’t we toss our bickering aside, for just his once?”

“I’m afraid that I simply can’t do that, Kyler. You and I are good friends, in a perfect world. Though, with all things considered, you are my sworn enemy. You’re the only true person that could understand me. Yet, that’s something that I now realized I despise. The truth of the matter is, I don’t want anybody to ever be able to understand me, as much as I do. When somebody finally understand me, they never seem to understand me. It’s all very complicated, but I’m sure that you understand. You always understood. And, you always hated me for it, when you did. All I ever wanted was somebody who could see me, and come to terms with what I was… Unfortunately, such is but a dream— a dream that I sat on, but I sadly know I’ll never fully get to experience. I have to thank you for everything you’ve done Kyler— but, I’m done. It’s all done. Goodbye.”

At first, I didn’t know what to make out of him saying goodbye— as far as I could tell, the time was still going down. But, then I realized just how much of my life was really at stake, and that I was sitting in front of the place where a bomb was about to go off. I did the only thing that I reasonably could do— ran away.

I now feel like a coward for having done this. Within the room, there were plenty of people who needed my help. In a way, I felt like I was abandoning all of them. Though, I was being driven by and instinct that wasn’t entirely under my control. In a sense, it really wasn’t under my control.
Diving out of the building, I shouted one last word to Crusoe.
“Goodbye!”

After that, the whole place went up in flames. I’ve heard the sounds of gunshots, and seen the worst of what the criminal element is willing to dish out… But, never to this extent. For once, I truly felt as if I were under the influence of one of the most abominable beings on earth. The whole sky filled up with ash and smoke, forming into a revolting swirl of water and dust. My eyes began to sting from it all, and my ears rung like oversized bells. Debris fell atop me, leaving me with numerous bruises and welts. I tried running from the sight, but was forced to crawl on the ground. The explosion had left me so disoriented that I felt that I was losing complete control. It was already shocking enough that I couldn’t crawl with my other arm. I tried to keep on going, but finally found that I couldn’t. My chest began to flutter uncontrollably, and I felt everything steadily slip away from me. Suddenly, I had a true taste of what death is.

While life might be the absence of purpose, death is the absence of everything. I can’t say much else about it. However, I can say one thing, about the last thing that I saw, before slipping away. It was the room that I’d just come out of, engrossed in flames. It might sound odd for me to say this, but I felt slightly comforted by the sight of it. Though, this was only for a moment.
“Schrödinger’s cat,” I remembered thinking. “What’s within the burning room is neither alive nor dead— not until I go to it.”
This comfort only lasted me for moments. And then, that was it. The very end of it all.

I sit in front of Eddy Mulligan’s grave as I write this… Though, I no longer know what to think to feel when sitting at it. Should I cry? Should I mourn? Should I feel anything at all? I used to think that the answer was yes to all of these questions. I used to think that, when I got here, I would have all manner of disparity— I would regret the death of a friend. Now, I’m not so sure. Now, things have become so indistinguishable from one raindrop to another. I question the very fabric that my worldview was once made up of… I wonder if I have a reason to be doing what I’m doing, anymore. In a way, I feel that I might not have a point to any of this, and that I really did lose to Crusoe. After everything he did, I now have so many scars… I wish that I’d never bothered to go to him. I wish that he’d never seen me— that we’d never met. After looking back into the passage of time, all that I feel is regret.

After going unconscious amidst the explosion, the police came, and saved me. Apparently they were phoned by people in the vicinity. I was wheeled to the hospital, and kept there for several days. In the meantime, the police did a search in the rubble. They only found two bodies— that of Job, and Jonah. I still feel disgusted that those two were brought into this— they never had any reason to be brought into this gunfight, as far as I’m aware.

The two bodies that they couldn’t find were that of Eddy Mulligan and Lieutenant Jackson. Somehow, their bodies both evaded the sight of the Police. That, or they were never there to begin with. That, or they somehow escaped…

The latter of those options is the one that I want to believe in the most. But, it’s also the option that I believe in the least. Either way, I have the feeling that Lieutenant Jackson and Mulligan are both prime suspects for who Crusoe had been. This is what disgusts me… One of my friends, and allies, had been Crusoe all along. Even worse, it seems to me that Eddy had always been the likelier candidate of the two… It’s simply the only explanation that I can come to, for it all.
That’s where I feel that it all comes down the chute.

Today, the weather is very nice. It’s full of sparkling greens, glistening yellows, and rays of light beams that are reflecting upon the ground. However, I simply can’t seem to find any enjoyment in it all. Sitting in the graveyard, I find that something about it all saps me dry. Perhaps I let things get to my head too much. It’s very easy to do that when there are too many things to be thinking on. In the world, when I look at the chestnut brown trees, the royally purple clouds, and the rolling golds of the sunrise, I wonder why I ever have a reason to fear.

Perhaps I’m just being a destructive and corrosive force to my memory. Perhaps the memories that I retain are just as great as I remembered.
Perhaps something happened to Crusoe amidst the passage of time since we last met.
Perhaps the claws of the world had gripped around him, and pulled him down to a place from which he was never able to escape.
Perhaps.
Perhaps….

title: The Chaos Theorem
paragraphs: Chapter 1:
“Breaking: Scientists Discover the Fate of Everyone,” the television’s headline read, dripping red.
He snorted. He’d only just woken up from his nap. He was still dreaming. He must have been. That, or the television was. It was a possibility, wasn’t it? It had to be.
At least, that’s what Stuart Fletcher told himself.
He had taxes to file — including taxes on his taxes. Crazy numbers to crunch. An unfinished bag of potato chips to munch. Much more important things to keep in mind.
Much more important.
At least, Fletcher was able to tell himself that for an hour. Time kept ticking, though. The television’s screen crackled, the same images smearing across.
“America in Throes”. “President Announces Doomsday Clock”.
A news reporter cackled, and Fletcher hit mute. Customers wouldn’t want to have to hear that stuff.

Yet, the shop’s door remained firm. The chime joined the door in its solidarity. Fletcher pretended he could ignore it; the general malaise marinating the room. Though, as the reporter’s face went intense with incense, even the toys on the shelves seemed to turn and give the television their gaze.
Fletcher clenched his stomach. He swallowed. He could’ve used a drink of water. The potato chips had left his mouth dry.
There was a quake. Lights flickered. The screen wailed. Toys fell off the shelves. Then, the room was dead.
“Do you know what that means?”
Fletcher turned to face his customer. Yet, there wasn’t one. The room was empty.
“It means it’s time for us to have a boisterous barrel of fun!”
A Silly Sally lay on the floor by Fletcher’s desk and burst into a fit of giggles.
“Screw you,” Fletcher muttered.
God was it irritating. Fletcher could’ve sworn he’d torn the batteries out of its voice box.

“They’ve dubbed their solution, the ‘Chaos Theorem,” a reporter squawked, as another line of text scrolled across the screen. “Yet, how many problems will this solution really solve? They make no sense.”
Fletcher snatched his remote up from the ground and hit the mute again. He shoved it in his coat pocket, between an assortment of toys.
You never could go wrong with too many toys in your pockets.
On the subject of wrongness, the reporter was totally wrong and totally right — something Fletcher had thought totally impossible, only a few days ago. If only he could go back.

The chaos theorem made perfect sense. It was just, all the sense that it made was nonsense. Conventional knowledge had been sent into the blender. That blender had been sent into an even bigger blender. From that blender? Everybody would have to drink up.
Fletcher looked back at his pile of numbers, only to rub his temples and moan. Numbers had a way of bringing him down for the count.
A creak resounded. Then, a clang.
“How are you doing?”
Fletcher looked over. It was a real customer this time. A man, in a raincoat. His eyes were downcast, and his hair was a mop.
“Welcome to Timothy’s Toy Shop,” said Fletcher.
Fletcher’s chair squeaked as he spun around.
“It’s crazy out there,” the man said.
Fletcher took in a deep breath. He smiled.
A bell rang.
“You have mail.”
Fletcher had a lot of things. Most of all, he’d had enough of listening to his notifications go off.
“Five more minutes,” he said.
He burrowed his nose into his pillow and curled into a ball. He yanked his blanket closer to himself and scratched an itch on his back.
The bell rang again, prompting another line from the robotic voice. Fletcher’s itch persisted. Yet, his arms and legs had gone dead.
If only he could be dead. It would certainly make for a more interesting day than what awaited.
He squinted his eyes tighter together, in a final attempt to keep the day at bay. He reopened his eyes and sat up. It wasn’t worth it. His bladder stung. The room was chilly. His stomach was empty.
His head remained tied to his bed, but Fletcher’s body carried him into the bathroom. His muscles moved in synchronized monotony; a ballet of bland proportions.
He brushed his teeth. He flossed too, twice. While inspecting his teeth, he took a glance at a quote reflected in his mirror.
“You’re #1!”
It was hanging on the wall behind him. It would’ve motivated him, if it weren’t that everything in mirrors were backward.
His phone flickered on as it slipped into his hand.
“Ready to start the day?” asked a bar of text. With a jerk of the thumb, he scrolled past it. It’d been months since he’d woken up and been ready.
He ran down a list of tasks. Rent. Repair fees. Warnings from the bank. Customer requests. Complaints.

Many things to be attended to, but there was nothing that he wanted to pay attention to. He tossed the phone onto his bed and began changing out of his clothes. He took off his coat and hung it in the closet.
He’d fallen asleep in it, again. It was so odd — he could never fall asleep on time, but still managed to fall asleep too fast to change clothes.

A packet of oatmeal powder poured into a bowl. Water poured in with it. Then, they ran through the microwave. Predictably, they came out as oatmeal. Quickly, too. The oatmeal was still burning hot after Fletcher had brought it to his desk and slid it down his throat. Its pinch of cinnamon took Fletcher slightly off edge.
Slightly. It wasn’t calming as a drug, but it’d have to do.

A mound of papers ruffled as Fletcher shunted them away. There were countless pieces of paperwork, just waiting to be filled. It was yet another job that needed to be done. Though, it could be done later.
He pulled his computer monitor toward himself and flicked its power switch. The tubes sputtered, then whirred. The screen winked on and gave a password prompt. He typed it in.
“Work harder.”
The screen contracted into a loading bar. Then, the desktop rolled up.
Fletcher’s eyes roved to a tin soldier, off to the side. It was such a diligent little fellow. It’d been sitting there, ever since Uncle Timothy began running the shop.
Time to get to work.
In his email, he was hit by a fresh deluge of bitter customers. Common, really. Nobody ever seemed to appreciate his work these days.
“The website isn’t loading fast enough,” one of the complaints read.
“Your design for my fortune telling webpage is too predictable,” said another.
“Is there any way that I can get my money back?”

Fletcher took a second to reread the last one. He laughed and shook his head. Nobody was getting their money back. Especially not these days, with what was going on in the news. Didn’t anybody get how hard it was to design code? Sure, there was a formula. Though, it wasn’t quick. If it was so simple, why weren’t any of them doing it?
Fletcher kept read a few more customer emails. Somebody had to send him something optimistic eventually, right? It was the law of averages.
He hit the end of the list. The law of averages continued to disappoint him.
There were two requests for some graphic design work. Though, they each wanted to pay hardly anything at all. Why were people so cheap?
“How are you doing Stuart?” the tagline of one of the emails read.

A flutter of gratification surged in Fletcher’s chest, only to deflate immediately. It was just Harry Doswell, asking him to come over for coffee. He wanted to catch up. It was a nice gesture, really. However, after everything that had happened with Margaret — how everything had spiraled — it just didn’t feel right to go crawling back to Harry for support. No. Those days were better left as a haze. There was no point in going back.
He hit refresh, in the dull hope that something else would come up. Anything.
He turned to his toy soldier.
“If I didn’t have you guys here, I would be doomed,” he muttered.
He looked around himself. It was true, wasn’t it?
Was it?

He called the shop home. Though, in some ways, it was a prison. The walls’ wood and plaster were shedding away, and the property owner was no help. Nobody was helping; it wasn’t like it’d been when Uncle Timothy ran the show. Fletcher glared at a door in his wall — it led to a straight drop into his neighbor’s shop. After months, he still couldn’t convince his neighbor to board it up.

None of the toys moved off the shelves, either. They sat, begging to be sold. Burning a hole in his pocket. There had to be a way to market them better. Yet, nothing ever came to mind and nobody ever came in the store.
“Help! I need a website, now!”

Fletcher had missed it in his first scroll through and was tempted to miss it again. The text was written in all caps and had one too many exclamation points. Yet, then Fletcher caught a glimpse of the emailer’s profile picture. It was a blonde woman with sunglasses, and a ruby red smile.
He clicked onto the email. She looked oddly familiar

“Linda.” Fletcher didn’t know anybody named Linda, but that was her first name. Her profile picture reminded him of one he’d matched with on a sketchy dating website. Yes — Fletcher could remember it clearly now. He’d been shocked when they matched; even if they were automatically unmatched, ten minutes later. This email though? This had to be impossible.
Had Linda actually looked at his profile long enough to find his email? Or, had she found his business by mere coincidence?
