My hubbub is one with the heartbeat of the universe. My mind huddles behind the sphere of the Hubble scale, which ties all the cosmos together. Hidden substrates of matter and antimatter neutralize each other.
The subconscious submerges into the nexus. It is so small and quiet down here. Thorns pierce my thoughts. I am within a time of 0 time. A time of the abyss. Bliss.
“I am at the beginning. I am at the end. Alpha and omega are the same. Infinity upon infinity, over and over again!”

Pure chaos is at loss with itself. Alas. My heart sinks into it all. It is made one with void. I sense absolute good and absolute evil blending into each other. 1 is 0 and 0 is 1. The eternal clash is illusory.
I try to turn my head, and the void snaps. It spasms. There’s a terrible blast. The present void fades to past. A new world is aligning, and it’s blinding!
“I am!” I declare. “I am the Cogito! I am the devil… The ruler of hell… The antichrist… The antichristian!”
Or… Or… Maybe I’ve just had too many energy drinks. Who’s to say?
My fluxion-drives hit a fever pitch before suddenly sputtering out, and I hit the floor.
Gah! Didn’t see that coming! Crud! Screw the universe!
Must be out of fuel…
Chapter 12: Visions for the Future
The Machine

Reality is what we make it. At least, that’s what I like to tell myself, to get through the day. Bah – my lawyer Tim Trekkle is taking an eon to join our video call. Time trickles away. What’s taking him so long?
I’m worn out by it all, at this point. I know I complain a lot, but I really mean it. What energy of me that has not been drained primarily serves to pull my eyelids down. I’m hovering from 1 to 5%.

I’m sitting at my tensegrity desk in my office, studying the way the cables make my desk seem to levitate. So beautiful, the strings of power. I count the ticks of my watch. The glass is warped with mist and dew, from me leaving the watch in the sink. Ack.

I should get more sleep, but I don’t like laying like a dead log. Feels like such a waste. Computers don’t sleep. Why can’t humans be the same? Maximize our time – I’m alive, so I have a vested interest in not playing dead.

The reason I sleep is elusive, but also painfully obvious. As I pass through the realm of life, I’m not to be 100% aware. So long as we roam the realm of time, we remain in the womb. Much as I want to make history, it seems more and more like history makes me. It’s so hard to escape the past, malleable though it seems to be.
If I’m lucky, my life’s work will allow us all to warp out of here alive…. But maybe that’s just a lie I tell myself. Oh well. Even the best of us must lie at the end of the day…
I’m pretty sure Cog is giving a load of crock when he talks about his precognition powers, but I can perceive the appeal. Wouldn’t it be nice to have the future at your beck and call?

I really screwed the pooch with him, didn’t I? He’s lost his mind, just like Byrd did – my burden. The common denominator is clearly me, and my domineering. I cast too large a shadow, don’t I? I never wanted kids for this reason. Byrd and Fletcher weren’t kids – they’d be fine dealing with me, right?
Eh, who am I kidding?
I’m pushing things too hard, and insisting on the next thing. Innovating is generally the right way to go, right? I’m terrified that my fame might be built on a pyramid scheme.

Normally I can stay focused on company tasks when there are 4 clear lines of business in motion. Once it hits 5 lines or more though, it all spins out of control. I get lost. That’s where I am: not knowing where I am. Always stretching in multiple directions, caught in a world of spin and shifting perspectives.

I should hit stop, but I’ve never known how to. When I was young, I drove a used car. One day, its check engine light came on. I didn’t have time to fix it – not enough money, and too many other things were on my plate.
That car eventually broke down. The engine block melted – a belt had come loose, and I neglected to fix it in time. Is the way I run business no different?
Whatever. Fortune must come with a healthy dose of misfortune. It’s always been this way.
With luck, we might be able to master space and time, as well as intertwine robot life with life itself. On that day, all problems in life will be solved. That is – if robotic life counts as life.
Hmm… Should robots have rights? Free will?
Should they be allowed to feel pain?

Technology certainly is analogous to the struggle of life: generation after generation, either entrenching or overcoming the failings of the previous. Striving to somehow make the wrongs right… But not knowing for sure what is “right”, at any rate.
Is there such a thing as a pure “right” way? Aren’t the differences what make us special?
Then again, with the help of robots and AI, the need for niches finally goes away. A sense of absolute morality is also useful for programming societies and AI, troubling though absolutism may be.

I scrunch my face. AI starts with reinforcement learning. Ideally, positive reinforcement. It’s the easiest way to get it working. Not meant to be adversarial, but sometimes you must define an adversary to make progress.

Ah, progress… Really been biting me in the ass lately. Deep down, I want things to bounce back to how they were in the good old days, but I get the sense it never will. Why can’t tech be used to keep things the same, instead of changing things all the time?
Just look at the Vitruvian. The best, now the worst….
My hologram flickers up on my desk. I lean back in my chair and begin shaking my snow globe. I know how the fluid flows. But the individual snowflake? Impossible to say.
“You in your office, Hugo?” Tim Trekkle asks.
Ah! My lawyer, finally late!
“Yep,” I say, watching the flakes of my snow globe accelerating back and forth through the fluid, with the pull of my hand. I’ve turned the world flaky!

There’s a mini me in there, standing at the edge of the globe. He seems to be fighting some kind of techno-ghost. A phantom, with cybernetic eyes. The window to the soul, glass silicate – so delicate.
Will he ever escape? Will he ever truly win?
“Interesting to see you in the office, I thought you’d be hiding in your room at the outskirts of the city again,” Trekkle says.
“That’s the great thing about tech: can be anywhere you need to be when you need to be. Today, I need to be here – big day. Gotta be with the people.”

“Whatever: with the people or outside the city, people will see you the same,” Trekkle trills. “As for your tech: useful, but I experienced lots of technical difficulties earlier today. Wi-fi kept glitching out.”

I put the globe down and give a sigh, before fiddling with a siphon on the other end of my desk. “Yeah, that’s the game of tech, I hate it. Despite the promise of solving problems, it’s always making things so painful and complicated.”
Trekkle snorts as I watch fluid dribble from one end of the siphon to the other. How the pull of gravity tricks it into moving this way will always mystify me.
“Then why do you do it?” Trekkle says, slamming a slab of papers onto his desk. “To put it lightly, you’re looking at a tricky legal situation right now. Just take a break. It’s all fake.”
I frown and my ears burn a tad. “Because I also love tech. I – I – yeah.”
Something flows through me, but I’m not sure I believe in the words I’m saying. Also, my stammer is back. Been awhile since it’s visited me. Wish it’d go away.
“Smooth line, maybe it’ll help me sleep better next time my phone bill goes up,” says Trekkle, shuffling his papers.
I pop a stick of gum into my mouth from my pocket. Maybe that’ll help. In my past it has.
Granted, I can get a tad addicted to gum. Also, it gives me gas. And, it makes me marble-mouthed.  But hey, it works.
“Welp,” I smack. “Wealth. Where’s that at?”
Trekkle wipes his brow. “Trickle-down economics still works in your favor. Despite the absolute monetary mess you’ve handed me, we have a few loopholes we can use to retain control of your company.”
I lean back in my chair and guffaw. “Ha! So Byrd won’t be able to void my contracts?”
The screen flickers, colors blending into reds, blues, and greens. Did he leave? The image flickers back into view, but Trekkle is frozen.

“Buddy, we’ve got some good leverage,” Trekkle says, the only signal of motion being in his jaw. “But, keep in mind: you definitely broke the agreements of your contracts with these latest stunts you pulled. You should’ve consulted with me first, instead of trying to have your AI spearhead all of this.”
Oh jeez, Byrd is completely screwing me over. Whose side is he on?
“What were you thinking?” Trekkle continues. “Everything was completely smooth sailing. Why’d you have to go and muck it all up?”
I tap the glass to the holographic screen. “This AI is top-of-the-line.”
“Over the top, more like it…”
“I—I—I’m trying to pull an Andrew Carnegie, okay! Stop treating me like a carnie!”
“Carnegie gave his wealth away because the timing and value made sense, not out of some moral creed. You sure you really thought this through, or are you just pretending?”
I swallow my gum. “Aren’t we all just pretending? If I gotta pull a few tricks to get my way, so be it. People love sensational figures, it’s how we get things done. It’s how we do things right.”

Trekkle shrugs, nonplussed. It’s as though my words just pass through him. “You throw around those words too easily. Wrong… Right… It probably serves you well for adverts, but that propaganda won’t hold up with me. Any moral code you have can and will be used against you.”

I smirk. “A—A—and yet, the contract I broke clearly ha—ha—has a right or wrong. Isn’t that how a foundational document for governance emerges? Institutions like Supreme Courts, instating a strong sense of right and wrong?”
Trekkle shrugs. “Look, you can use anything to argue for anything.”
“Then what is anything?”
“Last I checked, it’s about all things being treated as equal… None better than another.”
Rubbing my eyes, I feel an anger broil within me. “Yep. All men are created equal,” I toss at him. “You’re no better than me.”
“You sure you believe you’re not supreme, Everman?” Trekkle snorts. “Mr. I-know-best?”
“Yeah,” I say with a stiff nod. “I should know, shouldn’t I?”
“And what about women, huh? You chose to cite ‘All men are created equal’ – they just get left out of the mix?”
I start sniffing my coffee with a shrug. As the vortex settles, I take a sip. It’s cold. Stale. I hit a button in my desk, buzzing my assistant.
“Not my fault that one of our foundational lawyerly principles is se—sexist,” I lug, caffeine filling my gullet. “Can’t erase the racism either – world has gotta keep things racy sometimes, somehow.”
Trekkle gives a nervous laugh.
“Don’t worry—been looking for a while, but I’m sure an Everwoman will enter the picture any day now,” I add.
“You’re losing it—you need to get a grip. What I’m getting from you is that you think some people are more equal than others?”

I chomp my gum. “I ca—can’t say you’re thinking wrong. That—it’d be promoting the concept of wrong-think, now wouldn’t it?” My eyes lock onto my snow globe. “Of course, no two snowflakes are made alike. Science, amirgiht?”
“Well, actually, I saw a headline that said—.”
“If it wasn’t a headline about me, I’m already bored,” I groan. “You know, I’m really regretting not just talking with my AI lawyer some more. Much more agreeable.”

“The fact that your AI is agreeable is exactly why it’s a bad lawyer. What I’m trying to get you to realize is this: you used to be the rebel. The upstart. And so, people were willing to let you play the good guy… They’d let things slide… What you’re now looking at is what happens when you’re no longer rebel, Machine. You succeeded at taking on the system, and now you are the system.”
The coffee is drained from my cup. It’s all empty in there. All gone.
What’ll happen when I’m one day gone? Does it feel like dreaming? Or, is it more like reincarnation?
Hopefully I come back as something like a tree. Or, a cloud. Maybe a planet? A plant on a farm would also be nice…
If I ever come back as something, I’d want to be tapped into the cycles of the cosmos. Most things in this world don’t work to be what they are, they just are, cycling in and out and in again.
Why does corporate work mask this over so well? Why must everything be a struggle? Sometimes it’s easier to imagine the end than starting over from the beginning.

“Think about all the people you’ve struggled against over the years,” says Trekkle, as if reading my mind. “A lot of those ‘villains’ got screwed over by you emotionally and monetarily, Don Quixote… Fun as it is to be tribal against rivals, you’re really telling me they all deserved that? That there’s nothing more going on under the surface than just good or bad?”

There’s gunk stuck in the back of my throat. “Hurr—hurr durr—hurt people hurt people,” I gurgle. “Sorry Trekkle, my throat has a tickle. Have to do what I have to do… The company has undone a lot of the problems our competition created.”
“Yeah, but are those people who are to blame, or is it the fault of systems?”
I struggle to hear him. My mind is dominated by the echo of the words “hurt people” looping and whooping about.

“It’s also not like your company is perfect,” Trekkle continues. “You and your company is all too human, not superhuman. Take all the environmental and mental health concerns sprouting up, for example. I’ve been doing a lot of firefighting for you on that front.”

“The nonprofit division is working all kinds of wonders with biotech,” I snap. “We’re solving problems, promise. Carbon capture, restoration of ecosystems, biofuels, sustainable bio-materials… We’re on the cusp, it’s in—in—in our grasp.”
My voice is a rasp, and my vision is a ruse. There will always be problems. What kind of world would it be without them?
“Don’t worry, I still think you’re special,” Trekkle says, before blinking out his camera. “Put a pin in that, and I’ll ping you in a minute after crunching some numbers.”
I raise an eyebrow. “What is that supposed to mean?”
It’s odd, but much as Trekkle seems determined to save my empire, I tire of it. Less is more, no? But then, if more is also less, what is the moral lesson again? Feels moral-less
Oh, double speak… I’m talking out of both sides of my mouth, more or less.

Eh, I can’t express enough: despite having what I want in life, it’s never quite as I thought it’d be. Upon winning capitalism, it’s hard to keep innovating. My life essence is constantly pouring into my work, but I’m left to draw passion from out of a drip-feed. Rewards must be artificially repressed when managing large groups. Groups self-regulate, and leaders are relegated to figureheads.
Oh to be renegade again, rather than in retrograde. Can’t take credit for things going well, must take responsibility for things going poorly.
Do leaders need to exist in the age of AI? The systems of the mind and AI each seem to work better with decentralized structures, after all.
I’ve spent my days pretending to be looking out for other people. I’m starting to wish there’d be somebody who could pretend to be looking out for me.
“Alright, I’m back,” chirps Trekkle as he blips back onto my holo-projector.
“Gimme the good news first,” I say, shoving another stick of gum into my mouth.
My desk sparkles from numerous gum wrappers. I’ll clean up the trash later, I guess.
Trekkle slicks back his thin layer of hair, then gives his lawyerly glare. “Why always assume that there is good news? This time there isn’t any.”

“Posit—posit—my position is that positivity matters most of all,” I say, tossing my wads of wrappers into the air. They flutter, then falter. “Constructive interference, re—ree—reinforcement learning, positive feedback loops— all things build off these principles. Nonlinear gain when we all work together.”

Trekkle moans, tossing several graphs, emails, and contracts onto the screen. “Well, take this as constructive criticism then: I gotta point out the faults, I can’t play Pollyanna. These internal metrics are piss poor, especially after you sold your stock. You clearly weren’t supposed to take a torch to the company in the way that you did. Didn’t consult any people, going straight through AI for all these management decisions…. Objectively abject failure of your powers. The board has designed an airtight case against you, Machine. Ranging from mishandling corporate property, embezzlement, misuse of corporate funds, breaking NDA, and a whole lot of other stuff.”
My jaw drops. I sputter. “But—but—they’re misrepresenting everything! They can’t cancel me! Innocent until proven guilty! That’s the law! I—I—I’m the hero!”

Trekkle brushes his shoulder, grooming himself. “Hero? Not according to what the board has built. Your escapades as the Machine have seen you take unnecessary risks and misuse company resources over the years, at least according to the board. The laws of–err—law aren’t like the laws of physics. Or… Maybe they are? At any rate, opinions and dialogue play a strong role in what does or doesn’t happen in the eyes of the law.”
My head throbs and my ears feel stuffy. I like to tell myself that my business is somehow better than those that have come before – morally superior. And it totally is, isn’t it?
I massage my forehead. Some mechanism in my skin feels overtightened. Shouldn’t have chewed so much gum while Trekkle was chewing me out.
My heart pitter-patters. Is that the sound of guilt bashing against its walls? I’m not sure, but moralizing has a cost for morale. All those misadventures over the years as the Machine… And for what?
Hmm…

“It’s likely we can sort this out before they eject you,” Trekkle interjects against my mindstream. “Been running some scenarios through your AI. We can just say you were on drugs or something. Poorly informed, poorly medicated. We can blame your doctor.”
I shake my head. “But that’s not true!”
“Right, right… Your high tech roids don’t count?”
“They’re bio-enhancers. Gene therapy. Also, I stopped taking them.”

“You call that therapy? Whatever, I’ll try correcting that to ‘drunk on power’ and I’ll see where that can get us. I’m confident I can force the board to let those funds into that foundation of yours. As for you having control, I’m not so sure on that front.”
I grimace, then tap on the glass with my classic plastic grin. “You can do better than that, don’t play dumb. Surely you have a secure way to shore up my wealth.”

Trekkle scoffs and my stomach sloshes, making me nauseous. “Don’t get surly and don’t call me Shirley,” trills Trekkle. “You want to keep the money? I get it, but… Time is the enemy here. Time is money here. Things are…. Time sensitive. It’s also a lot of power we’re talking about. You can bet on an unholy mix of things moving far too fast and oh too slow. Sad to say it, but nothing lasts forever. One thing I know for certain: time always runs out.”

I give a grumble. A creature hidden underneath my invulnerable skin is trembling. The pressure of the infinite effaces me—so tough to face. What is greatness when you can only be a small fraction of it all?

I give a belch. “Guess that settles it then: money truly is the root of all evil. All this time investment in the hope of living life my own way… And the cost of having life in my own way is that I am in my own way.”
Flustered, Trekkle filters through his clutter of papers.

“Hey now, don’t get too down. However this shakes out, you can trust the system is fair. You’ll still have a lot of money at the end of this, and you don’t have to treat it as evil. It depends on how you use it. It’s a tool. Money is power.”

I give my head a shake. “No—no—know—knowledge is p—pfft—power. Be—be—besides, all this power can be corrupting. Power—para—uh—parable of camel going through the eye of the needle comes to my mind. Easier for the camel to pass through than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. That camel—lots of nights it haunts me. Am I the rich man in that story?”

I sigh. Part of me is terrified of losing everything and going back to having nothing. That said, I haven’t been ousted from anywhere since I was a teenager, working at a summer job. I also miss having nothing to my name, like when I started. Less competition. Everybody can have equal amounts of nothing to their name, that’s the generous thing about nothing. Much less dishonesty than what’s involved when trying to be something.

“Oh come on now, don’t go taking that religion and God stuff too seriously,” says Trekkle. “All the talk about fire and brimstone, if you do this or that… It’s just made up stories that we tell kids to spook them. We need the concepts of money, fiscal responsibility and wealth to keep things running smoothly, alright?”
“I agree that it’s all myth and metaphor, and that a lot of it is problematic, I say, wincing. “But—but—but that doesn’t mean all this guilt is going away.”

Trekkle shrugs. “Good sells. It’s convenient. But– I keep trying to get you to see this—it’s low on nutrients. Absolute morals are too rigid when applied to life. They yield descriptions of situations tantamount to the concept of a ‘true lie’ or ‘2+2=5’.”
“It’s fine, I can round up a little.”
“Sorry if that’s meandering, but what I mean to get at is this: if we abandon good, maybe something better can emerge.”

“Well then, I gu—gu—guess I’m beyond words,” I smack, my forehead clammy. “If there is no right or wrong, it’s still hard to convince me that the concept of absolute morality is wrong. Nevertheless, still hard to argue whether morality is right. My best defense is AI—it thinks in binary and training it for a moral compass is top of mind.”

Trekkle has inched from the camera and now sits a meter away from where he was at the start of our conversation. “Look: sometimes it’s necessary to demolish a building. Other times? Not so much. Actions always should depend on the context at hand. There’s something to be said for not caring about how society predefined certain actions. Do what you feel that you must. If it was predefined as wrong? Oh well.”
Eek, it just doesn’t let up. Something feels off.

“Where’s my friggin’ assistant?” I pant, pounding the button on my desk through pent-up anger. “Hey now: just because I got myself fired doesn’t mean you can revolt against me. I need more coffee, stat. Also a bagel. Get on it!”
There’s a muffled chirp from a speaker in my desk. Hopefully that means they heard me. I pace to the window and stare out into space. The ground level is surrounded by protestors.
“This is your last day?” Trekkle says with a crackle in his voice. Stupid wi-fi signal.
“Yep,” I say, hanging my head.
The group of protesters is about twice the size as it was this morning. They’re scattered about like a colony of ants, waving signs and blocking up the parking lot.

“It’s now or never. Making a spee—speech after this. But, been having a tough time with Polka’s resignation and failing health, as well as the confluence of protests. My own assistant is ignoring me now… My final meeting – I wa—wa—wanna nail it, but doubt I will. Why’s everything falling apart? It’s as though Byrd planned this all out.”

“Polka is just a figurehead, you barely know him. You gotta cool it,” says Trekkle. “As for Byrd, he might be engaged in malpractice, I don’t know – wouldn’t put it past him. Our system did a fine job producing a scapegoat for itself with that guy. But, a lot of this unrest also falls on you. This is what happens when you spend a career fighting against unions and treating human rights as secondary. No amount of guts or gusto will change that. Exhibit A: you just spoke to your assistant like a total ass.”

I watch my reflection in the window as my face curdles into a scowl. “They’re not just resisting working conditions, they also want to stop technological progress,” I say as they scuttle along the crummy pavement. “AI, robotics, genetic engineering—my life’s work—they want it banned. The old world… It’s dying. Polka’s wonderland, being stripped for parts. And they’re the key opposition!”

“Then I guess you’re stepping back at just the right time, aren’t you? Come on now, you don’t need one more person to build you up,” says Trekkle. “You already have everything. I’m telling you, you gotta dial it down a notch. Society will sort itself out. It’s not up to you to solve everything.”

As usual, he’s got me cornered. Maybe I should’ve stuck to the original plan of being a rockstar or something. Things are probably much smoother when staged. These corporate personas—have I tricked myself into believing they’re something worth valuing?

“On the subject of your hardware, I think that’s the last main topic of discussion we have on the docket,” Trekkle continues. “While I have good records on all our conversations, I need some better insight into the actual work you’ve done the past year or so in terms of development work. Should help a bunch in terms of sorting out some big patents we have cooking. Been a lot of debates recently on who gets credit for what, especially since AI helps you a bunch and is trained on public metadata. I suspect it’ll give you a lot more leverage in these coming discussions, depending on what you’ve got to show for yourself.”
I amble back over to my desk and hop onto my computer. I give a few keystrokes into my AI, and a link is sent to Trekkle like that. All data from my day-to-day, parsed through a digital parcel.
“Dang, that was fast,” says Trekkle.
“Fa—fastest typer in the midwest,” I say with a wink. “Enjoy the hours of transcripts covering my heavy breathing. Makes for some light reading.”

Trekkle chuckles. “Trifling for me, but I’m sure my AI will enjoy. By the way, while I have you here—and I can try making sure this is just between us—what are your thoughts on all this monitoring and data collection at your company? Should so much about an individual really be centralized in the hands of what is essentially a monopoly making concessions?”

I bite my lip and shift in my chair. The synthetic leather is agitating me for some reason. “I mean, somebody has to do it, right? Decentralized systems and communities certainly make sense in some cases, but large, centralized structures are also natural. How can a society expect to operate as solely decentralized when the concept of a society has a very clear and centered definition?”
“Just seems very easy for those frameworks to become self-centered is all.”

“From many, one,” I say with a smirk. “That’s how leading works. Take beehives for example. Or, the mind – neural networks. Many disparate parts, producing a coherent whole. The conscious mind can conduct a lot of sophisticated behavior by having command over the entire body in broad strokes.”
“You completely miss the point… You realize the board is trying to use some of your data collection tools against you, right?”
“It is what it is.”

“Sure, but diversity of thought and freedom to think independently is the benefit of not micromanaging everything,” says Trekkle. “And you wonder why there’s so much unrest… You’re putting a square peg in a round hole.”
“Eh, I let my researchers do what they want, and then I micro-manage the rest,” I say with a shrug. “Probably too much freedom – they nearly bankrupted this place.”

Trekkle chortles. “Yep, you’re clearly in over your head. On that subject: one of the research and development categories they’re debating your patents on involve the development of warp tech. It is also the key area sucking up company funds. Care to elaborate? I thought it was only a few years ago that the LISA observatory was finalizing its observations of gravity waves in the early cosmos. These documents… You’re not suggesting that gravity waves can be emitted at will here on Earth, are you?”

“I initially thought it was impossible myself,” I say, biting my cheek. “That’s the annoying thing about large organizations—I spend all this time building it out, only for a bunch of new people to come along who contribute research and ideas far beyond anything I ever could do… Our research groups built amazingly compact accelerators, which allow us to explore exotic phases of matter – normally only traceable through the early universe. I thought that any connection to gravity would be a pipe-dream, but my leading researchers produced ALP…”
**Note: will need a section where proper researcher talks on this topic!!**
“ALP? Person, place, or thing?”

“They’re the initials of Anna Livia—,” I stop and break into a snicker, “uh, Plurp. Nah, ju—just messing around. The—they—it stands for Axion-Like Particles. Dark matter. Not sure how far my researchers got with it, I only read about this stuff for hobby and was shut out as you know. But, supposedly it was key for new effects. Amplification mechanism or something, made emitting beams of gravitons look like it could have real applications.”
Trekkle shudders. “Okay, I have a headache now. I was really hoping this would be a discussion on a trip of yours to the alps.”
I shake my head. “Nope.”
“On the subject of the alps, you’re always scaling Mount Everest Everman. Will you ever rest?”

“Somebody has to use capital to help push tech and science forward, it’s what makes life interesting,” I say. “We move further away from the limitations of our body and minds. We master matter, and we will become one with the machines.”
I pause. I blink. Damn – that sounds a lot more megalomaniacal than it was in my head.
“Also, clarification,” I say, “pretty sure Mount Everest is in the Himalayas, not the alps.”

“Hey, some of us haven’t gotten the latest software update,” Trekkle scoffs. “Also, impressive as the laws of physics are, I do just see them as another system of law. Physics can be bent, alright? It isn’t the only thing that matters, and people have good reason for you to not go full steam ahead.”
“This stuff might save the world, people need to understand that. Also, if you happen to know any cosmic-grade lawyers, please send me their contact info, will ya?”
“It could also destroy the world. You want to be the greatest innovator in the world? The world will admire you. But, the world will never love you.”
“But the—the—the quality of life has continually go—gone up in history, thanks to efforts involving technology.”

“Sure. But when you frame yourself as the champion of the average person, don’t be surprised if you find yourself being called to live as an average person. People resent, eventually. How different from the average person can any of us possibly hope to be?”
I throw my hands up. “Yeah-huh. Then what do you suggest I do? I’m already leaving to focus more on charity.”

“Not that there’s any way to win in this life, but fighting for better legislation involving business regulation, worker’s rights, and taxation on the ultra-wealthy would be a start on the right track.”
I gag. “Taxes don’t track with me, man. And regulation? Oh my god, don’t even get me started on all the bureaucrat brats I’ve had to deal with!”

“Just saying, it might be the bitter medicine technologists like you need to stay regulated. You want something to fight for, Machine? There you have it. Also… Not sure how much you’ll need me after you leave Everman Technologies, but this suggestion of mine gives us an excuse to keep working together.”
Hmm… Once retired from the Machine, I guess I don’t have to steelman my board’s actions anymore. Plus, Trekkle’s socialist sales pitch might have ways to win me back public favor.
I furrow my brow. “I’ll think about it.”
There’s a knock at my office door. Must be my assistant.
“Come in,” I say, and the doors whoosh open.

A robot roves in, carrying a fresh coffee and bagels on its tray. On the front of the robot is a screen, displaying imagery from various news sources. In the bottom left corner is footage of my assistant who’s smiling as usual. Hard to tell whether her complexion is through a filter or natural, but she’s radiant. Who cares if it’s real?
“About time,” I say, striding up to the bot and snatching the food from off the tray. “What’s your name again?”
“Tracy,” she says.
Dang, there’s a coincidence! Gal assigned to push trays, happens to be named Tracy?
Eh, I’m probably best off ignoring that if I want to stay sane.
“Th—thanks,” I manage through a muffled bite. “By the way, get here faster next time, Tr-Tracy.”
I’m not sure why I say that. I already know there won’t be a next time. At any rate, she gives a weak smile and says nothing. The screen dims. I tap it and it brightens up again.

“I’m so sorry you’re leaving,” she musters through the tinny speakers. Doubt she means it after how I’ve been acting. “By the way, are you fine with your photo being taken for our newsletter? It’s dedicated to your time here and your exit.”
Dang, she makes it sound like a funeral. I hork my chunk of bagel down with a dousing of my coffee, then smear a smile across my face.
“Sure,” I say stiffly, through my coffee-stained teeth. “Ready?”
“No worries, already got it.”
Brilliant.
An image flashes across the screen of me munching on the bagel. Only… It looks off. I seem frailer. Smaller, somehow. I don’t look great.
It has only been about a week since I stopped taking my enhancements, and I didn’t expect the effect to be so extreme.
“Yeesh, that looks awful,” I say.
I mean to force a laugh, but I can’t.
“It’s fine, we’ll just run it all through AI. We can seed artificially positive sentiment when it’s posted online, too. It’ll be fine.”
I grimace. But, guess I’ll just have to accept it.
“Sounds good,” I say, patting the robot’s tray.

“Yep, just smooth it over and coat everything with AI, like you always do,” Trekkle says through the holographic projector from behind me. “I’m still here, by the way, stuck staring at your dumb desk. Let me guess, that’s AI too?”
“It—it actually is,” I croak. “AI designed and manufactured.”
I try to stand tall as I say this, but I’m not even sure who I’m trying to impress anymore.

“You—you know wha-what? We’re good here,” I say, giving a gesture to shoo my robot away and shutting off the projector. “I have to give my good bye speech in the ne-next hour or so. Also, I’ve been in this office for awhile, and I really need to take a crap.”
The doors whoosh once more, shutting out the robot. Also Tracy, I guess. The static feed from Trekkle has also faded out.
I’m not sure whether they heard my crappy sign-off. I’m not sure if I should care.
I find myself standing at my window again, munching on my stale bagel and staring at the protestors below.
They know the real Machine better than anyone. And some part of me hates them for it.
Some part…
The Cog
I can see my ceiling. I’m stuck lying in my bed. Staring. I can’t shut my eyes. I can’t move.
I’m paralyzed.
The air is slick against my skin and vibrates with vigor. A clammy sweat spills down my spine, blending with the air’s cataclysmic clamor. A perplexing suplex of cataplexy.
My fluxion-drives pulsate in the corner, matching my racing heartrate. I desperately want to roll out of my bed and grab them, but the grip of this sonic spirit holds me catatonic.
My nerves are shot and my eyelids are heavy.
The room buzzes and is bending out of shape. But how could that be? The only feature my fluxion-drives still have enough energy for are my Tesla coils, not gravity waves.
My pants are still damp from jerking off to my phone before bed. What can I say? I had to indulge my sex drive after indulging my fluxion-drives.
Those curves were a lot nicer than the ones giving me sleep paralysis.
Memory on how I got here is still confused and dizzy. I think I came out of a dream. Or, was it a dream within a dream? Maybe I’m still in one.
I attempt to tap into my precognition, but the buzzing only gets louder. My ears screech, before throbbingly settling back into the vibration.
Something is churning at my mind. My thoughts are the foam on a wave as it settles into the shoreline.
Two orbs appear on my ceiling, then peer out at me like eyes. They somehow reach within me. My bones tingle.

“Hello, my pupil,” the spirit jingles into my earways. “Have you missed me? You are tethered to the ether this eve. Granted, all souls always are, but let’s save the details of that reveal until you enter the afterlife shall we?”
Erm—Dreamweaver. That bastard! Always interrupting my REM, barging into my room! Intruding into my reality at the worst of times!
“Excuse me? What did you just call me?” Dreamweaver snorts, their glowing body wafting through my rafters.
I blink.
I try to blink again—no luck.
How did they hear what I called them? My lips can’t even move!
“I’m in your head, stupid,” Dreamweaver warbles, warping their body to-and-fro.
They’re a phantom, linked through some strange liquid. Blues, greens, and a bit of pink constitutes their form. His form? Gender is weird with these spirits.
They can’t possibly know what I’m thinking, can they?
“Yes, yes I can!” they say, my face burbling along their surface in a surreal mirror. “Also, I’m periwinkle, not pink, Rip Van Winkle!”
Dreamweaver winks like the obnoxious Lynx they are. Entire universes flow through their essence, twinkling and winking along with them.
“I’m not obnoxious, you’re obnoxious,” the constellation mutters with consternation.
Oof.
You’re not allowed in my head, Dreamweaver. You must leave. I never gave you permission to enter.
Dreamweaver begins to fade, going opaque and slipping into a pocket from what can only be another dimension.

“Hey now, we’ve got business tonight, promise,” Dreamweaver whimpers, shrinking to a fine pinpoint. “Just give me a chance. Don’t you want an explanation of where I come from? Or, or… Where your powers truly come from? Or, what all these misadventures I’ve orchestrated for you were about?”
Their vibrations drain my mind. They’ve been removed from my thought stream, even if I can still see them shivering and shimmering between worlds.

I shouldn’t trust Dreamweaver. They’ve messed with me and the Machine in the past, and Dreamweaver is always up to no good. For Dreamweaver, reality is a plaything. Chaos is just a prank, easily undone.
Something deep within my soul warns me that Dreamweaver is not supposed to be within my mind – it is a power imbalance, and a violation of the natural order.

That said, Dreamweaver is no mere spirit. Dreamweaver and his ether have entered the story for some rhyme and reason, or another. And, for what it’s worth, he has acted as guardian to me and others on some occasions.
“How can you hear my thoughts?” I finally relent, signaling to him through my mind. “How are you in my head?”

The air dulls to a stiff buzz. Dreamweaver is just waves. Froth. They’re disappearing. A pressure is along my body. It’s as though the weight of the entire universe is focused about me. The terrifying uncertainty of existence, getting its licks in.
Maybe Dreamweaver was just a bad dream. Yes, that’s it.
Part of me wants to die. But, I refuse. Something in my soul has accepted the contract of life, and I intend to fulfill it – even if death seems destined to win, regardless.
Economy and society often act as a claw machine from some arcane arcade. No matter how much scratching and clawing, success is pulled away.
But then, that’s being an adult. Life isn’t fair. You have to just take it. Just be tough. Make as much money as possible. Do what people want. Numb the curious oddities that rub against society.
I used to live in a world with clean grades and metrics to hurdle. A clear game where I could play hero.
That was the old me. Now I’m the older me.
Nowadays, my work experience doesn’t have any structure that engages me. I don’t have anything or anybody to defeat.
Man, it’s hard to be an earthling. While we value hard work, sometimes I wonder if we just value making life harder.
Whatever, I’m just a shitty engineer. Who cares what I think? I’m already en route to being fired.

Trying to play pretend as hero was a total mistake. I like to tell myself I’m special. But, we’re all mortal and die. No escaping that. People don’t really care. Not really. They just want somebody to solve their problems.
In this realm, entropy eats everything. Even love.
“Are battles of morals the plight of us mortals for accepting the gift of free will?” my air conditioning seems to whisper to me. “I fight to know, in spite of it all. Perhaps I never will.”

I’ve always wanted unconditional love, but I never find it. There’s always some catch. Some barrier – something I must do or be. I want to have the time of my life with somebody without having to consume the time of theirs. Ah well... Some things are out of my control.
For what it’s worth: I trust true love is out there somewhere, waiting for us all to find it.
My heart races, coupling to the heartbeat of the universe.
I’m screaming in my soul, desperate to know there’s some other—that it’s not just all about me.
“Where are you?” a voice upon my mind’s eye cries.
“I’m back,” Dreamweaver beams to me through the space of spaces. “I won’t invade your privacy again. Promise, even if the plot of your plodding thoughts is nice to pilot.”
You can still hear me though, right?
Hmm. Dreamweaver is silent, hovering as a spectating spectral.
“You can still hear me though, right?” the voice at the seat of my imagination groans.
“I’m not in your head any longer, only skimming the signals along it,” Dreamweaver responds, bobbin about. “Strong negative energy in the air, okay? I was nearly sucked into the vortex.”
I sniffle. “If I’m not in your head and you’re not in mine anymore, then how can we hear each other?”
“Energy. Signals, riding along the sphere of the cosmos,” says Dreamweaver. “We’re connected – intertwined with infinity.”
“That still doesn’t explain the clarity and coherence,” I say, a tumult melting my courage.

“All thoughts and concepts have chunks of consciousness connected to them,” Dreamweaver says. “Parsing the messages of mind is easier than it sounds, once you have the keys. It’s primal – numbers, emotions, impulses… They’re all there, tied to the divine geometry.”
“Enough with the sophistry, you’ve explained nothing! Meaningless,” I grunt into the vibrations.

“Now, now, nothing doesn’t exist,” Dreamweaver titters. “Careful with your thoughts. Try imagining nothing—nonsense! I didn’t gift you with precognition using my life essence, just to have you squander it with self-pity!”
“You what?” I snap. “I knew it! I knew our communications weren’t normal! You have me on a leash! You’re manipulating me!”

The glow in Dreamweaver starts to go out again. “Yeesh! Look, I actually came here tonight to explain things—to give you direction. To lift your spirits! Something is off with your journey, just a tad. And, I’m gonna help! But, you need to cut back on the negativity, alright? These thoughts will latch onto you, and then we’ll both be in trouble. Honestly, what has gotten into you?”
I roll my third eye.
“Don’t say me,” Dreamweaver adds.
My mind goes back to Lin. The long-winded conversations in our office. The awkward gazes. The joy of running around this world together, pretending all our feelings somehow made sense.
“Lin,” I say.
“Ln?” Dreamweaver asks. “Like... As in L and N – natural logarithm symbol?”
Wow. I guess Dreamweaver’s connection is spotty.
“Girl troubles,” I say. “Work troubles. None of it is fair, all of it is hard, and I have no clue where to go next without screwing everything up even more.”
Dreamweaver’s form descends along my body and sooths it. There is a peace within this naughty, soothsaying spirit. Even though my life is in pieces, stupid bliss is still somewhere to be found.
“Do what you must,” Dreamweaver says in a rush. “Life is about change. Flexibility. No matter what choice you make, there will always be a way to regret. Make sure that it’s your choice.”
My soul shudders. It burns. “And what if I want somebody else to choose for me? What if my passions are too heavy to carry? What if the suffering that comes with choice is too much?”
Dreamweaver shrugs. “Free will is a question that I don’t know the answer to myself. The gift of precognition might help. But, I’m just a lower spirit. I rely on a bag of tricks.”
I chortle. “Yeah, I think your escapade turning the Machine-Machine into a toaster made that clear.”
Dreamweaver struggles to laugh back through that voidful mouth of theirs.

“All that attitude and you still don’t want to take initiative over your own life? You have it on easy street with that middle class lifestyle of yours. You can turn your life into anything you want! Do you seriously want to stay stuck as the psychic sidekick? Tough as things can be when you’re going through the thick of it, would you rather not have any say over what you think? Would you rather be relegated to a mindless computer program? If you keep trying to sand down the edges of reality, you’ll be swallowed by cognitive dissonance Cog. Cognitive bias. So long as you accept suffering– mistakes—as something you have no choice over, you have free choice over the rest of life.”
There’s a jagged ringing that travels under my skin. Dreamweaver seems to be tugging at it.

“Don’t try to justify the unjustified,” Dreamweaver persists. “The cycle of cosmogony can absolve itself from the problem of agony, but it cannot fully solve it. Any justification for certain things must remain unknowable.”

“But… I feel like nothing,” I whisper. “I feel empty. All these relationships and shit… They deplete me. I’m not supposed to rely on another person to feel whole, but some part of me still wants to. Am I toxic in this way?”
Dreamweaver shakes their head. “There’s a hurt that you’re letting eat you, and I don’t know why. I’ve watched you—you make love more complicated than it is.”

My soul somersaults from the insult. “But my obligations… My aspirations… Don’t they take precedent? Maybe I’m wasting my time being Cog… But I just want to be part of something, ok? Besides, everything falters and falls away in this life. Every religion and philosophy warns of this, when I dig deep enough– of love’s evils. How can I justify the ethics of enjoying myself when it will always come at the expense of somebody else? Much as I’d like to pretend somebody can be there to comfort and keep company when it all ends… This is just a cop out.”
Dreamweaver juggles solar systems in their eyes, and seems utterly unimpressed. “Let me let you in on a little secret: morality isn’t simply about doing things that are ‘good’.”
He grabs at the jaggedness within me, again. He pulls and pulls and pulls… But, the jaggedness pulls back. There’s a crackle and Dreamweaver gives a whimper, before draining his beams for arms away.
“What the fuck?” they shout.
Damn. I didn’t think Dreamweaver could talk that way. Strangely, Dreamweaver also seems shocked with themselves.

“Great,” they mutter through their milky tongue. “Your soul is corrupted! Great, just great… You realize that some of my essence is coupled to you, right? Like, just so you’re aware, your precognition is my processing power, and your maladaptive tendencies are malware. Your depressing thoughts are gonna screw both of us, you realize that right?”

I want to apologize. But, like… Kinda hard to feel bad for their dumb choices when they’re literally a god. “Look, I can’t control this! I didn’t even ask for precognition. You never told me we were connected, I’m just finding this out tonight! I never gave you permission to do this, and I don’t even know how this stuff works! How is this my fault!?”
Dreamweaver puffs themselves up, their grandeur and brilliance overwhelming my soul. There’s a sputtering riding along their spine, which threatens some of the beauty—but, just a minor hiccup I bet.

“You must stop,” they command. “Your thoughts are warped by surface-level analysis of things. You’re identifying yourself with shallow things that aren’t actually you! You must remember who you are! Reconnect to your higher form!”

I’m mesmerized by their holy speech, and feel myself transcending. Dreamweaver’s eyes suck at my stomach, attempting to pull away the bad energies once and for all. Dreamweaver is like an enlightened vacuum cleaner – cosmic grade. Powers beyond comprehension!
Ugh… I’m still broken up over Lin though.
Dreamweaver blows back in a burp.
“Gah!” they muse. “Honestly, just get over that girl. Why do you care about her? Turbo-bitch, promise!”
Oh please. As if Dreamweaver has proven themselves to be any different.
“She wasn’t all that,” Dreamweaver persists, still fighting to yank my pain away.
They have a point. I’ve met prettier girls before. Nicer ones too.
Lin is a bit too full of herself. Like, she acts like she’s a gift to mankind or something… Yeah. Sorry honey, but…
But…
But, I love her.
“I know that she can be a bitch,” I say, “But so can I. And, I want her to be my bitch.”
Hmm… What I just said was wrong, wasn’t it?
Whatever, can’t take it back. I feel guilty about what I said, but it’s how I feel.

As my thoughts pass from my mind to Dreamweaver’s, Dreamweaver gives a mighty tug and manages to yank out the jaggedness. Starshine pours through my veins, alleviating the pressure and providing a fresh levity.
“Okay, I’ll stop micromanaging and just let it be,” says Dreamweaver.
There’s a scratchy spaghetti of pink energy held in his celestial hands. It slips in and out of Dreamweaver’s energy field in an oily ballet.
Dreamweaver gives an annoyed huff. “Always something… Now I gotta find a way to get rid of this thing.”
Dreamweaver’s eyes rove over to mine. “I knew there’d be stuff I’d need to clear up with you tonight, but this is definitely more than I anticipated.”
They pause. The bundle in their fiery palms zings. “You know what? I’m going to take you with me. Let’s go on a spiritual journey together!”

Dreamweaver nabs something from within my napping soul, and suddenly we’re rocketing off into the stars. The nectar of nebulae drizzles and dazzles me. Galaxy after galaxy gallops past. I can see my past self still sleeping in my bed as I look behind. As I look ahead, droplets of entirely new universes map the sky. In each one, Earth has a slightly different shape and proportion. Different mapping. Jeez—I always thought geography tests in our one universe were bad… I don’t even want to think about what they’re like for residents of the multiverse!
“Uh, where are you taking me?” I say, as we begin to approach a black hole. “You—you’re not out to destroy me, are you?”
“Bah,” barbles Dreamweaver. “I’m way too mature for that. No—not destroy you. I’d much rather annoy you.”

The ball of pink goop spills out of Dreamweaver’s clutches and pours down toward the black hole. There’s a chain built of pure light attached to the goop, and Dreamweaver turns into a crank. Steadily lowering the pink goop down, the crank sings with a free energy imbued by the black hole’s gravity well.
I stare into the surface of the sphere. Fear dribbles down my spine with each chink of Dreamweaver’s crank. What is hidden within that vast empty? Its horizon both horrifies and whores itself to me.
“Why did you bring me here?” I whisper, as the whisp whisks its energy deeper into coldness.
I’m not sure if I should trust Dreamweaver. Regardless, whether I like it or not, it’s just me and them. Also, the black hole I guess.
“It was ordained that I gotta teach you some things tonight,” says Dreamweaver. “That, and give you a fun time. Dunno how I’m doing, but I’d rather try my best than return to my house arrest.”
I crinkle my face. “Your what?”

“Look, I may have overstepped when I used my life essence to give you precognition,” grumbles Dreamweaver. “In my defense: connecting you to the higher realm was the only way to spare your life after I—.”
“Higher realm?” I sputter. “Spare my life? What did you do?”

Dreamweaver shrugs. “Nevermind that, I’ll explain more later. I’m sorry, but you mortals are just too entertaining! Also, I can make up for it! I’m being given the opportunity to help guide you and your mudball of a planet to higher things – whatever that means.”
My ears pound. “I’m not getting the sense you feel guilty at all.”

“Ding, ding, ding,” mutters Dreamweaver, as the chained-up goop nearly hits the surface of the black hole. It’s moving at what is practically a snail’s pace at this point. “You have so much to learn.”
Dreamweaver draws us closer to the goop, seeming to speed it up. The universe shrinks away as we do.
“It all is the wavefunction—all of existence. It is the rising of the tide, and it is its receding. Existence is self-dual—it is singular and also its own opposite, forever orbiting about itself.”
Dreamweaver’s body splits in two. One half is the crank, still lowering the goop down into the black hole. The other half is Dreamweaver’s swarthy, swirly self.

Sparkling threads along the surface of Dreamweaver’s body dip into the black hole. A series of numerical digits begin to stream out. They orbit the black hole’s surface and flow into his body. 2. 3. 5. 7.

All prime, all the time. They slurp the prime numbers up. Once they hit the number 137, they give a delighted sigh as though quenched of thirst. The stream of digits is replaced with gobs of noise. Dreamweaver retracts their tendrils.
“Ah—while I’m a caffeine fiend, nothing beats a dark cup of prime numbers in the morning,” Dreamweaver says.
They peer into me, appearing to morph into a variety of things. Also, nothing in particular. At the center of their starry forehead is a triangle made of 3 orbs.

“Ignore the noise,” they say, skimming the surface of the black hole. I’m not sure if they are trying to reassure themselves or me. “The truth is, black holes are subtle. They like to keep discrete. There’s a purity in darkness—a continuum. It’s quite deep. For every black hole, there is quintessence at the center – the nature of how all things are.”
My mind shudders. “Are you okay? How are you?”
Dreamweaver gives an incredulous scoff. “How am I?” they cry. “How—how am I? I am!”
Wow, that’s not at all what I meant. What a self-absorbed douche!

“I and spirits like me have minds that work like quantum computers,” they say, reeling back a bit to explain themselves. “Specifically: we’re quantum computers that run on quantum gravity. We are made up of exotic matter held in resonance, and use spacetime itself as our entangled superconductor. Unlike you mortals, we are pure intelligence. We can change form to do anything and be anything!”
I cough. I glance back at the pink goop, which has again slowed to a crawl. “Am I supposed to be impressed?” I say. “At levels of power like that, how would you not just lose your mind?”
“What?” Dreamweaver snaps.
“How are you sure you’re not just stuck in your own head imagining all this?” I press.
Really, this all seems surreal and unreal, for real. Not sure what Dreamweaver’s answer will be, but I can already sense their energy struggling to keep my soul reeled in.
“That’s a stupid question,” says Dreamweaver. “How dare you?”
Their vortical form fizzles and sheds at the ends.
“How can I even trust you?!” I shout. “Maybe you’re not a higher spirit at all! Maybe you’re a lowly, evil spirit pretending to care about me!”

Dreamweaver gives a sniffle and then shrinks in size. “I’m one of the lower-ranking entities of the higher realm, I can give you that. Also, maybe I don’t care about you that much. But, I absolutely, positively come from the higher realm,” they say, a ringing orbiting their voice. “Let me repeat: I’m from the higher dimension! And, in case I forgot to mention: I’m one of the most powerful creatures in existence!”
Something flashes into my eyes – a bliss unlike any other. It leaves as quickly as it comes.
Alright then. Whatever this ghostly dickwad says goes, I guess.
Dreamweaver seizes the moment to see down into the empty, then rises back up. “That goop is taking literally forever,” they say. “While we wait, let’s explore some more into what you implore, eh?”
The black hole melts away and we’re drifting through a network of multiverses. Entire existences waft by my face. I watch them transition from beginning to end, then back again.

“I and my kin are coupled to the flow of reality, helping to maintain and simulate it,” they say. “At the highest levels, we can generate entire worlds as easily as an AI on earth might generate a video or an image.”
My ears are hot and stuffy. I want to clear out the wax as they wax philosophical. My throat is tight, suffocated by the rare air.
“So you really can do anything?” I whisper.

Dreamweaver sighs. “Sort of. Of course, everything I do is screened. Due to my abilities coming from the higher realm, my actions are constrained by it. They have an ethos of only trying to bring good into the world—very stifling, I must admit. As it happens, they are always falling short, and there you have it!”
I shake my head. “But, this doesn’t make any sense! The world is not just a computer program.”

“Ack, it is and it isn’t,” says Dreamweaver. “Geometry has a way of simulating itself into existence. At any rate, it’s whatever we say it is. We can warp energy probabilities. Or, if you prefer, ‘energy potentials’.”
“Isn’t that a paradox? Aren’t those things fundamentally opposite?”
“Not really. Probability for something to happen, potentiality for something to happen… Same deal, really. Tomato-tomahto situation, when you get down to it.”
Dreamweaver gives a snap, and the multiversal network implodes into a cloudy powder.
“What was that for?” I gasp, as we tunnel through the shards.
There are snippets and flashes of other worlds, but I’m mostly met with blurs of color.
“It’s all just play,” they say. “I’m an entity who is in charge of dreams, you see. That’s why I have the control I do but still work at the lower levels and can break some rules.”

They say this as though it’s some badge of importance, despite their playful charade. As shards of universes morph into Dreamweaver’s dreamscape, I can’t help but wonder whether the desire to seem important is itself built on illusion.

Dreamweaver nearly flings us into a creature that has emerged from the darkness. It’s a navy-blue sock puppet, which seems to be laughing. As its mouth opens wide to consume us, Dreamweaver portals us into an empty space.
Off yonder, there is a sphere with a rainbow ringing around it.
“Are you drunk?” I shout.
“No,” says Dreamweaver.
“I think you drank one too many prime numbers.”
“Shut up.”

They transform into the shape of an arrow, and we ride along the sphere’s slick and icy surface. As we ride along the sphere, Dreamweaver charts out a circle. The path takes us back to our starting point, but Dreamweaver’s arrow is now pointing in the opposite direction. Our clocklike rotation about the curvature has changed Dreamweaver’s orientation.

Their body revs up, and we blast off. The ring rainbow jumps back into view, and we speed toward it. We are pacing just a tad slower than the light. Dreamweaver’s soul gives another jolt and we overtake the speed of light. We blueshift the rainbow into a smear of violet. I take a look behind to watch the light redshift, before returning to look ahead and find the blueshift fading out of sight.
“Welcome to the end of the rainbow!” Dreamweaver announces. “This is my domain! I work at the boundary between the realm of the 5th dimension and the realm of the 2nd dimension.”
“What is that supposed to mean?” I scoff.

Dreamweaver smacks their lips. “Well, the 2nd dimension is the lower dimension of consciousness,” they proclaim. “It is a bit of a dreamscape—a sheet that lives atop the cosmic sphere of your 3D realm. Chaotic.”
I grumble. “Right…”

Dreamweaver doesn’t seem to be entirely lying, though. There is a frothy screen extended in front of us, stretching infinitely in all directions. Entities of some variety or other peer endlessly at us, their eyes bulging and mouths stuffed with an eternal laughter.

“I can traverse both realms, to be clear,” Dreamweaver says, dipping into the screen a bit. “The beings of the 2nd dimension are interesting fellows—more accepting of noise and the arrow of entropy than most.”
“And why would you be allowed down here again?” I say with a shiver.
It’s strange down here. Dreamweaver begins talking some kind of babble with the lower dimensional spirits before resurfacing.
“It’s low-level work, but it’s important,” Dreamweaver says. “Somebody has to be the caretaker of dreams, you know? I split the dream from the nightmares as best as I can.”
I frown. I shudder. “What kind of nightmares do you screen out?” I ask.
Dreamweaver jumps out from the lower dimension and stares into me. Their thoughts are padlocked.

“Nothing much really, nightmares never happen,” Dreamweaver says, coldly and brittle. They then force a laugh. “Most of what I screen out of people’s dreams is just porn, really. At any rate—these rules and regulations on dreams are somewhat loose. Infinity is funny like that. You make what you will of it.”
My head pounds. “Rules can’t just be arbitrary. Rules are rules! You’re not hiding something from me, are you?”

“No,” Dreamweaver says firmly. “Look: when considering the ultimate levels to things, concepts of relativity apply more and more. There sometimes are no clear answers to be articulated, so much as experienced. Perfecting the art of what you are—that’s the more important part.”
I clear my throat. “Then why did you bring me here? You’ve been very unclear.”
Dreamweaver howls with laughter and one of their eyes telescopes into mine. “Why indeed? Ever wonder why you were born in this time, and not any other?”
Their body snaps away as a rubber band, and they’re back to swimming in the lower dimension. I can’t tell if they’re searching for something or avoiding me.
“Hey, stop it!” I cry. “You need to stop it, alright? What’s the idea here!? What are you hiding!? Tell me!”
Dreamweaver pokes his head back out of the slime, looking quite drowsy. “Grrffflkmarrgle,” Dreamweaver manages.
They’ve lost their goddamn mind. Great, just great.
“What I think?” Dreamweaver spittles. “Decide what you think, how about that? I’m just a cosmic figurehead, my power symbolic. There are multiple pathways to answers. Roam free!”
My mind is mush at this point. Will they ever get to the point?
“Oh, and another thing: whatever you think is a part of reality, whether reality likes it or not,” says Dreamweaver.

Dreamweaver returns to the churn, bumping and bopping about. Meanwhile, my thoughts coil around me. Dreamweaver invested all this energy in taking me here, with the promise of providing some kind of answer… And it was just to reveal that the answers were inside me all along?
“Am I here for doing something in a past life? Is this some kind of cosmic grade torture?” I ask.

Dreamweaver nods while wading through the lower dimensional pool. “Sounds legit to me. If that’s what you think, probably true. Would need to look into documentation, but... You’re no cupcake, alright?”
Dreamweaver reflects and refracts through fractions of the dream plane, scouring and scowling as they go. “Aha!” exclaims Dreamweaver. “Got it!”

They splatter out of the pool of dreams and struggle to drag their tail-end back up with them. It seems as though they are trying to reel their tail up as a kind of fishing line. They thrash back and forth. With the 4th pull, an orb comes flying from out of the sheet.
Where this 3D object could’ve been hiding in that 2D world, I’m not even going to pretend to know.
“And what’s the big idea this time?” I mutter.

“Documentation!” barks Dreamweaver, juggling the orb. “As it happens, we should be able to finally give you answers for all the pesky questions you pester me with… None of this means anything in particular, but…”

There’s a click as Dreamweaver turns bubbly dials along the orb. The orb explodes into a portal. I am moving along within there, trapped in the portal’s net. It’s a sunny day outside, with light streaming into my office’s hallway. I steal a snack from out of a snack cabinet, before spilling my cup of water. It is a cup marked for “visitors only”, naturally.
Past me tries to clean the spill with my sneaker, to no avail.
“Yep,” Dreamweaver says with a chortle. “You definitely belong to hell.”
Dreamweaver whisks me through a carousel of past versions of me, all doing stupid stuff and saying off color things. Brilliant. Just brilliant. Intrusive thoughts abound.
“Damn, you’re every -ist in the book,” says Dreamweaver.
I groan. “Well hey, how about we take a look at some of your dirty laundry, eh?”

I grab at the orb and manage to flip the dials in reverse. Suddenly we are watching Dreamweaver’s past self saying something offensive to his higher dimensional peers, using a language of geometric symbols that I can hardly understand.
“Gimme that back!” Dreamweaver fumes, wrestling the orb from my grasp.
“Killjoy. Pfft,” I say.
Dreamweaver’s face splits into two, before resuming its original form. “You’re not meant to mess with the power of a higher spirit!”
“What goes up must come down, no matter how powerful!” I retort.

Dreamweaver seems undeterred. “This is a time-travel orb and I am tightly entangled with it!” Dreamweaver booms. “When time traveling, you are not to have knots! Do that again, and you might entangle me up so much that I rupture the timeline! It’s a paradox that can destroy and reset the universe!”
I force a burp. What a convenient excuse.
“Sweet, no sweat,” I say. “So, like… The setting of existence is predicated on a paradox?”

Dreamweaver grumbles and steadily starts rebuilding the portal. “Everything is everything, alright? Ugh… I should’ve known from the start not to rope myself in with you. You are trouble. But then… I just can’t help myself.”
The image of me in the lab re-emerges in the portal. I’m standing by the Everman Technologies particle accelerator. My head throbs—I remember this day all too well.
“What is it this time?” I say, feigning ignorance.

“So, I have some things I need to clear up,” says Dreamweaver. “That accelerator accident… Look, I like to play pranks on people, and playing pranks on you was just too much fun, okay? And, uh… Maybe I went a step too far, just this one time…”

My ears ring. I watch as a past Dreamweaver fiddles with some of the superconducting wire. I watch as a past me falls for the prank like a sucker, and tries to fix it. And, I watch as the particle accelerator boots up from the jolt of Dreamweaver’s laughter, before fritzing a particle beam into my mind.
The image fades. It’s now me and the present Dreamweaver in a standoff.
“You?!” I cry. “You did that to me!?”
“Honest mistake, I swear,” Dreamweaver says, floating back and toying with the orb. “I did everything I could to help and make up for it, promise!”
The portal hurtles us into a hospital. There is me laid out on a stretcher. A bandage covers my forehead. I appear to be sleeping—drooling on myself. Not my best look…
Dreamweaver projects a shadowy duplicate of themselves, shifted at a right angle to Dreamweaver’s body. Then, Dreamweaver phases through the wall of the hospital, before retracting the projection.
One of Dreamweaver’s tendrils reaches into my mind—they seem to tinker with something in there, then slink away.
There’s a buzz, and the present Dreamweaver licks the past version of me away.
“If you ever feel all alone, there you go,” says Dreamweaver. “There is always your imaginary friend to count on!”
I sigh. “What were you doing to my mind?”
“Giving you precognition,” Dreamweaver says as they start threading the next portal. “Also, helping you get a speedy recovery—I might’ve warped probabilities a bit, but don’t tell anyone.”
My head is in my hands and my forehead is beading with a cold sweat. “So that’s it? You violated my free will, after giving me a lab injury?”
Dreamweaver gives a nervous chuckle. “That was an accident. I felt really bad, okay! Plus, we have a connection now! You can peer into potential futures! You’re without peer!”
“You nearly killed me!” I screech.

“I made you into a ‘chosen one’ or whatever, and on a bargain too,” says Dreamweaver, flippantly flipping through the story of my life. “Be thankful! I gave you 50% off what most narcissists have to pay, in terms of suffering. I just caused you a bit of head trauma, that’s all. Seriously, all you can think is to complain? Mind-boggling, just mind-boggling…”
“It’s not fair!” I persist. “You think you can just steer the course of my life this way or that way, and I’ll just be okay with it?”
Dreamweaver gives a nod in the affirmative. “Cut the agitation, I have a few more cogitations to show you Cog!”
The portal flings us to the lab once more. Only, I’m entering into a room that I shouldn’t. A room labeled top-secret, with a door that has been left ajar.
I remember this day. Something compelled me to enter, which I can’t quite explain.
“Warping probabilities has its perks,” says Dreamweaver.
“You forced me to enter?” I say.
Dreamweaver shakes their head. “I’d never intervene with free will in such a direct way as that. I helped open the door, and you did the rest…”

The portal follows the past me into the top-secret lab. It’s mostly empty in there. The lab is a wide-open space and pearl white. At the center is  pedestal with the Everman logo emblazoned across one of the pillars.
Atop the pedestal are the fluxion-drives – blueish tubing and nozzles are hooked into a dark purple pack.
I gaze at the glaser—the gravity laser. It almost seems to pull me in.
I steal Everman’s device from off the pedestal. Or, maybe it steals something of me, I’m not sure.

What I’ve done is wrong. It’s obvious. Yet, as I slip the pack on and pulse the power, there is an undeniable glee running through me. The taste of power is irresistible, no matter the cost and no matter what I take down.
An alarm goes off as the past version of me begins to float in the air. I have only one option: to flee.
I look so ashamed. Maybe I should be. Was this device and all its power really mine to steal?
“Fire of the gods, and you just stole it!” Dreamweaver says, clucking their tongue.
“I’m sorry,” I say, a lump of guilt sinking in my chest. “Everything is meant to have a cost—I know that now. Power has not been nearly as simple to wield as I’d hoped.”
“No need,” says Dreamweaver, dialing the portal into another time. “Remember the day you thought you could put it all back to how you found it?”

There is another past version of me walking through the halls. Only, this time I am wearing a mask and trying to be discrete as possible. Unfortunately for me: there is a crowd of people gathered not far off from the entrance to the top-secret lab. Also, I’m not even sure how I was gonna try to get in anyway.
Also, the Machine is right nearby. How convenient.
Oh wow!
He is fighting some kind of villain for the crowd. A charity event is going on. Looks to be a spat with Captain Flapjack.
Not their finest hour. The Machine seems bummed. Angry, even. Was the Cereal Killer not available or something?
I join in with the fluxion-drives, flipping the pancake off into the air with my flow of force.
“The joining of titans—legendary partnership,” announces Dreamweaver, swallowing the image of the past. “I might’ve helped orchestrate the timing of all that, but I cannot fully confirm nor deny…”

“Complete waste of time, more like it,” I say. “If you haven’t been paying attention, my partnership completely fell apart recently… And, you’ve been doing zip to help me! Why couldn’t you have just let me be? Why play with my fate?”

“Oh please, you’ve enjoyed it, don’t lie,” says Dreamweaver. “You’re really telling me you’d have rather had me leave you to suffer in that stretcher? To not give you precognition or the taste of the fluxion-drives? To let you just put the fluxion-drives back, without ever having met the Machine? No, no, no… That simply would not do.”

Come to think of it, I would’ve preferred that outcome. After everything that I’ve been through, I’m not so convinced that the whole power fantasy thing is everything that it’s cracked up to be. All these visions of glory, greatness, and control, but instead I’m stuck talking to this chucklehead.
“You can’t play God with my life forever!” I shout.

“Ah, fair,” says Dreamweaver. “But, keep in mind, there is a bit of the divine in all of us. There is your being… My being… There are collections of beings, which are tantamount to higher beings… Finally, there is the infinite being: the highest being. Basically, playing with your life forever may in fact be an option on the table.”
I swallow. “For such rigorous argumentation, you seem real insecure. How are you so sure about everything?”

Dreamweaver fizzles in and out. “Oh please! I know exactly what I’m talking about! Take the universe, eh? I know how to master universes! Within a universe is all power, all good, all bla, bla, bla… God. It’s God. It’s also its opposites… But, let’s not emphasize that, shall we?”
These words still don’t inspire confidence, but Dreamweaver already appears to be moving on. They tinker with the air and my soul energy is being sucked back into the 2D cosmic sheet.
“What are you doing now?!” I protest.
“I can sense you beginning to question reality,” says Dreamweaver. “Let me sequester some of those questions away!”
We blast off into a network made of over 100 interconnecting nodes. We sit at the center.

“There are higher and higher levels of coherence and will orchestrating the universe—pure consciousness,” Dreamweaver proclaims as the glowing web orbits around us. “We masters of space and time consist of creativity and imagination. We can shift our consciousness from many to one and one to many. The separation from the divine that is felt in this reality is no longer so in the higher dimensions.”
The network unfurls and we’re now moving down a cosmic tarmac.
“The arrow of entropy? It’s an illusion. It can be mastered and traversed just like any of the spatial dimensions. That’s how the time portals worked, that’s how your precognition works.”
“But—but—the arrow of entropy is just a fact of nature!” I mutter.

Dreamweaver smirks. “The 4th dimension you know is not the true time– it is a shadow time of sorts. More accurately: it is a projection that comes from moving out of 3D space and into a purely non-Euclidean realm of forms. The full measure of this is a 4th dimension that acts as a refined space unto itself. But, the process of generating it yields entropy. To escape, you must project out into the 5th dimension—an imaginary space, where even entropy can be tamed.”
I scratch my head. “What about 10 dimensions? 26? You don’t seem to be accounting for all matrix degrees of freedom.”
Dreamweaver groans. “Yeah, you can probably gauge more, but let’s not bother splitting hairs…”
I sigh. “So, you’re telling me that reality is a pyramid scheme?”
“Not everything is about you,” says Dreamweaver. “You still think I’m full of it, after all of this? Here, let me show you how things go way deeper than you know…”
Great. I’m just a person, but I fear with everything that I say or do I must pay some karmic price.
A horn unfolds out of the ether, and we’re tumbling into it for a pit of yarn.

“Would you look at that – your clump of negative energy finally made it into the abyss!” says Dreamweaver. They point out my old packet of pink goop, now caught in the mess of yarn. “Emotional baggage finally made remote! Anyway: this arena is what pure chaos looks like. We avoid it. A mess. Some rumors say existence comes from here, but don’t buy it. Everything is wonky and tangled in this realm.”

The yarn spins in and out of me. Time rips over itself—a continuum can be pieced together, but this void resists it. It is as though it only uses time to tease the mind about its true nature: pure noise.

“Can eventually reach a space beyond doubt, where even imagination is transcended,” Dreamweaver affirms, keeping their voice steady. “The suffering and the stripping away—take away all impermanence, and all that remains is what is infinite… What is eternal.”
Despite bliss in the voice of Dreamweaver, something seems off. Something is unsteady.
“It’s time I show you the truth of time, beyond tabulation, words, and numbers,” says Dreamweaver. “It’s a stream of pure consciousness!”
The horn reopens and we are being funneled away into a whirlpool of magic.
Dreamweaver is jittery. Shaken from something they saw, maybe?
There are nested spheres filling all of space, much like mirrors within mirrors. The chain flows but seems to stay in place. Things warp in and out.
The perspective suddenly skews: the spheres bow and clump near a distant center. They appear to clump quickly way out there, but clump slowly way up near my scale. Scares the hell out of me!
The finer things affinely find their way. A logarithmic spiral unfurls from the maze, cycling in and out of itself. It then warps back to the uniform assembly line of the spheres, going tick by tick.
“You humans are always trying to save time, save the day,” says Dreamweaver. “But, it doesn’t need your saving.”
Profound but confounding. As the landscape processes me and I it, it fades. I’m back in my room.
“Hey, what’s the big idea?” says Dreamweaver, still above me and out of sorts. “Watchmaker, you better watch it!”

There’s another spirit beside Dreamweaver, orderly and clocklike. Cosmic gears breathe through its head. I’ve never seen anything so intricate. And here I was thinking that my mind was something of a cosmic cogwheel!
Watchmaker is this spirit’s name, undeniably. It’s spindling the ether, sucking up the dreams that Dreamweaver culled.
“What you’ve been doing bends the rules, Dreamweaver,” Watchmaker squeaks, bemusedly.
“Hey, even gods should be able to make mistakes,” retorts Dreamweaver. “I was in the middle of something!”

“You weren’t supposed to show him everything that you did tonight! That was wrong!” Watchmaker decrees, beams of energy rolling from their sides. “It interferes with free will! Power imbalance! You were merely supposed to clarify your impact on his past! You are not to interfere with human fate!”

“Lay off,” says Dreamweaver. “I know what I’m doing, what seems right for you is not necessarily what is right for me. It’s impossible to decouple what I determine from the determinism that helps guide human fate. And if so, how can you claim that I interfere? Your notion of free will is too idyllic and stilted. A pathological ideology!”

“If you continue monkeying with human free will and pulling pranks, you’ll need to be cast into a lower dimension,” says Watchmaker. “Don’t forget that you’re already on a tight leash regarding how you can guide humanity!”

Dreamweaver sputters and beams of energy spar between Dreamweaver and Watchmaker above me. The beams jet and intersect orthogonally, before circling in a geometric dance. The two spirits hardly notice me. My heart pounds, and my body is still stuck in place.
“Life is so much fun,” says Dreamweaver. “So unique… What of my own free will? Must I always watch, Watchmaker, but never do?”
“Yep. Sorry, but critical thinking requires being critical,” says Watchmaker. “Tough rules, but the big guy mandates it.”
Dreamweaver’s eyes swell, and their energy with them. “Big guy, eh? I’ve seen things—the contradictions. And with all your splendor Watchmaker, you can’t think for yourself!”
Watchmaker falls silent. No answer.
There’s a meow. PB has hopped to my bed. There’s a spurt, and the spirits sprit away through a portal. I’m free again.
I lift my arms. They’re still asleep and start to tingle with paresthesia. One more gift from the paranormal I guess—ugh.
I suppose it’s fitting. I’m cold to warmth, and I respond most to numbness. The pain in my hands worsen as they reawaken.
What if the love in my heart is numb in the same way? I notice my heart hurts worst whenever I try to reawaken it.
“You saved the day,” I say to PB, giving him soft pets on the back. PB mews and leans into the pets.
