His hand edged toward Dice's throat. Matches stood from her chair and took it.

"Fair enough," she said, giving it a firm shake. "Thanks for the game — always nice to find an even match. Now, before I leave, I do have one question: could you at least point us in the direction of who you sold the Omega Keys to?"

"It was a group of rebels," said Jade, still leering at Matches. "Never seen a group come down here so big. Not sure where they are right now... But, they said something about staging an attack on the U.R.O's capital, Omicron, and then hightailing it for Kelvin. I wasn't a fan of their plan myself, but they gave us a million radials... They cleaned us out of our entire stock of Omega Keys."
Matches closed her eyes, and put her head in his hands.
"Omicron?" Matches repeated.
"Is that too far?" asked Jade.
"No," Matches said weakly. She turned to Dice. "I guess we know where we're headed next..."
Dice could sense the anxiety in Matches voice. The way she walked. The weight in her posture. Yet, Dice's own thoughts were aglow.
Omicron? It was the place he'd dreamed of going to all his life. The crown jewel of the U.R.O. There was no other destination that could compare.
"We need to find Wrench."
Matches split into the crowd. Dice followed after and craned his neck for Wrench but was quickly lost among the crowd. Where was he?
"I've never been that terrified of anybody..." Dice said, once he'd caught up with Matches.

"Next time, let me do all of the talking," Matches said. "Those people run practically everything in the Gordon District. You don't mess with them, unless you're certain that you know what you're doing."
"Don’t we though? We needed that key. We should've kept pushing."
"They don't have it," Matches said, simply.
"We don't know that for sure."
"Yeah we do... Aside from myself, if anybody would know something like that, it would be you."
Matches gave a dry smile.
She was right. Dice was letting his emotions cloud his judgement. Of course the twins didn't have the key... If there was anything they'd seemed honest in, it was that.
"Where's Wrench in this place anyway?" Dice asked.
He sidestepped around a couple of people scowling at them. He held his head down and directed his eyes elsewhere. However, he only caught more hostile scowls.
"Not many people are receptive to us," Dice said.
"Yeah, I could've told you that," said Matches. "Word probably gets around fast in this place. The twins will have a target on our backs if we don't get out of here fast."
Dice dodged a hover dart as it whipped around the room. Dice glanced over at a group of people lined around a dart board. They weren't looking at the board.
"So, what was them calling you 'Segue' all about?" Dice asked. "You been around this place a lot, or something?"

"I think you should've figured out by now that my real name isn't 'Matches'," Matches said trying to avoid Dice's eye. "It's not Segue either. To tell the truth, I don't have one name. I don't have one home. I go with the moment."

They'd passed by the obnoxiously loud singers on the stage of tables. Dice took another look at the decaying ceiling, the weathered furniture, and the clusters of sickly people. There was still no sign of Wrench.
Matches tapped Dice on the arm and pointed toward a corner of the restaurant. Wrench was sitting there on a stool, with a stimulator injector. His back was turned to everybody else.
"I and Dice are leaving," Matches said, putting her hand on Wrench's shoulder. "Do you want us to try getting started on the radial transfer?"
Wrench turned around. His eyes were glazed over, and a moan came from out of behind his mask.
"No," he said. "Just... Just go."
"Wrench — what's wrong?"

"I never cared about the radials," he said, in a monotone. "I just... I just wanted a chance to get back to my home. But, there's no more honor here... No more beauty. I remember when the Gordon District place was a beacon. How did it get like this? How could I have let it?"

"It must be really hard to take in," Matches said. "I'm sorry. But... We're going to have to cut this short. There's no telling when the U.R.O will arrive. And, the keys that we were looking for? Not here. They're going to be at some rebellion being staged in Omicron. We're heading out of here on the next transport tube, before the U.R.O military has a chance to find us. If you want your radials, it's now or never."
Wrench stared off into space and didn't make a sound. Had he heard them?
"Wrench?" Dice said.
Matches spun on her heel and headed for the door.
"We really don't have time for this," said Matches. "We still need to collect supplies before we go."
Wrench remained in a stupor. Finally, Wrench turned back to the wall. Dice went after Matches.
"What do you think happened to him?" Dice asked, once he'd caught up.
"He's probably just in shock," said Matches. "I guess I can't fully blame him. It was his home."

Dice's thoughts split in two. He knew that he should've felt sympathy. Yet, there was a larger part of himself that only saw triviality. How could somebody let themselves care about a place so much? It was just a district. Just a small section of a district, really. It shouldn't have mattered.
Yet... It clearly did.
A group of people rushed by him and Matches. For a moment, Dice tried to push past. Then, he saw their eyes. They were clouded with fear. Disgust.
"What are they running from?" Dice asked.
"Somebody probably puked at the bar," Matches said.
"My bets are on Billard..."
Matches laughed. "Definitely a good thing that we're getting out of here then."
Dice looked over his shoulder, back at Wrench.
"How are we going to get supplies exactly?" Dice asked.
"There are plenty of vendors around here," said Matches. "I'm sure that we can find everything that we need at one of those."
Dice eyed his wrist.
"I just hope that my account isn't frozen."
"With our luck, it probably has," Matches said, with a chuckle.

Another person pushed past Matches. Somebody shouldered Dice in the chest. Dice clutched his bruise and went to shout. Though, he noticed that the breathing of the rushing crowd was unnaturally high, they were flailing their arms, and their legs were pumping as fast as they could. Dice turned up his hearing aid — their heartrates were above 120 BPM. Goosebumps pricked up his forearms.
"Matches," Dice said, tersely. "They're running in terror."
Matches pulled them back once they were close enough to see the door behind the swarms of people. A gash was melted through it, and several bodies were strewn in front of it.
"They found us," Matches said. She squinted. "They have the restaurant surrounded."
Dice and Matches followed the crowd to the back of the restaurant. However, Dice kept looking back in the hope of catching a glimpse of something. Somebody.

Matches and Dice reached the back wall. There was an explosion. At the center of the room, a wave of bodies hit the ceiling. Dice put his hands over his ears as the shockwave reached them and brought him to his knees.
"A soundwave bomb," Matches said, as chunks of the ceiling fell to the ground.
Dice turned down his hearing aid, but it wasn't enough. A high-pitched ringing still rattled through his skull.
A voice reverberated through the room.
"I'm Captain Knowles!"
Dice's lips quivered. His fists clenched.
"No!" He said. "It's too much! It's all too much!"

He attempted to ram his head against the glass of his tube. Claw at it. Kick at it. Anything to escape. Though, the black ooze covering his body only tightened further, and his restraints held him back.
The voice clucked its tongue.

"BL-270... We don't push you because we feel you must suffer. Must be punished for some... Misdeed. Rather, it's because you're a prime specimen. One of the best in our facility. We push you to push us."
Dice shook his head.
"No.... Too much.... Too long."
"But, there's so much more that we have to do. that we have to learn from you. I'm proud of you. We're all proud of you."
Dice grunted and continued to pull. The ooze coiled around his neck. He foamed at the mouth. Shocks of electricity fiddled on his spine. He pulled harder.
"Fine! Fine!" the voice said.
Dice's screen buzzed and morphed to lines of code.
"We didn't want to have to assign you with this task this early. But — you've been our most successful specimen in rounding the androids up. We could use somebody effective at this too..."
The code continued to stream by. It was infinitely complex. So many elements to think of and consider.
"This is the brain of an android," the voice said. "Reprogram it. Make it obedient. Remove any malicious elements. Don't disappoint me."
The voice faded out, leaving Dice to the tube and the code. Though, just as he began to alter it, a box flashed in the corner of his screen.
"Only the truth is effective. Join the collective."
Chapter 18:

Dice looked up. Knowles strode past the people who'd fallen to the ground. His face was an empty canvas. Stolid. Several soldiers were banked around him, aiming their weapons at all sides. The tips of their guns flickered blue, menacingly.

"You people are stowing a U.R.O fugitive," Knowles said. "I'm not sure who among you knows who I'm talking about... Maybe none of you do. But, the person we're looking for knows who they are. And, I'm going to search through every one of you until I find them."
Dice and Matches shrank behind a group of people that had formed along the wall. However, Dice didn't let himself take his eyes off Knowles.

A blast went off. One of the soldiers around Knowles fell to the ground. Several people charged towards Knowles. There was a click as the soldiers pulled their triggers, and a blue film warped the air. All but one of the people fell. The stray survivor made it to Knowles with a gun in hand.
"You're not going to take any of us," the man shouted defiantly.
He fired at Knowles. Knowles merely took a step back as his armor absorbed the blast. Knocking the gun out of the man's hand, he clasped him around the neck, and held him in the air.
"I'm a U.R.O military officer," Knowles said, raising the man as he spoke. "I'm not sure if that means anything to you people... But, I remember a time when that would warrant respect."
The man in Knowles' clutches choked.
"You officers have driven the U.R.O to near bankruptcy!" somebody shouted.
Knowles flicked his red eye in their direction, but kept his true eye focused on the man in his grasp.
"Please don't kill me," the man managed, with a wheeze.
He collapsed at Knowles' feet.
"I'm not going to kill you..." Knowles said, reverence seeping into his voice. "You managed to shoot down two of my officers. If anything, I'm interested in having you join our military."
Knowles spat at the ground and kicked the man in the stomach.
"Unfortunately, I need answers. I'm going to go through every single one of you, until somebody can tell me where the woman I'm looking for is."
"Nobody is going to sell out to you," the man on the floor said.
Knowles stepped over him and into the crowd.
"Has anybody here seen a woman with silver pupils, and dark hair?" Knowles asked, his voice booming.
Face flushed, Dice turned to looked at Matches. Matches had closed her eyes, and bowed her head toward the ground.
"Do something?" Dice hissed.
Matches scowled, and bit her lip.
"I can't," she whispered. "Something... Something is blocking my thoughts. My mind."
Dice's heart skipped a beat.
Knowles waltzed down the row of people, stopping every so often to place his knives for fingers on a person's chin.
“Have you seen her?”
Each time, people shook their head. Each time, Knowles' hand sharpened, and his eyes became more cunning.

Dice held his breath as Knowles passed the people in front of them. There was a slight quake to his every step, and his metal leg left small dents in the floor. Knowles stamped his foot into the wall once he'd reached the end of the line, and let out another shout.

"We're going to begin questioning now," Knowles said. "We don't intend to use violent force. I repeat: we will not use violent force. However: we will not rest until we have answers. Whoever can tell us where our missing person is will be greatly compensated."
Knowles rotated on his metal heel. The ground sparked. Knowles didn't stop until he was glowering over the person at the corner of the wall.
Wrench.
"Do you, by any chance, know where our missing person might be?" asked Knowles.
"I'm as damned clueless as you are..." said Wrench. "Now, get out of my face, or I'll break yours."
Venom coursed through the muscles in Knowles' neck, and into his jaw.
"I don't like your tone," Knowles said, his fingers inching dangerously close to Wrench's mask. "I deserve respect. I believe that you owe me an apology."
"Sorry..." Wrench said. "But, you can't fully respect a man who has half his face missing. You can only ever give half respect to half a man."
Knowles let out a harsh chuckle. The metal in his face squeaked as it moved with his mouth.
"That's rich, coming from a man who has half a face himself."
"You don't know that for sure though, do you?"
Dice couldn't see Wrench clearly from behind all of the heads of people. However, Dice detected a slight tremor in his voice. An uneasy hesitation at each word.

Knowles' hand reached out to yank Wrench's mask off of his face. Just as it did, a plume of plaster and dust flung Knowles away. There was a clang. The dust cleared. Knowles' was sprawled along the ground, his metal leg was lodged in the wall.

The room erupted in chaos. Those along the wall charged toward the line of military officers. Explosions and beams of blue flew from all sides. There was a tsunami of screams as people fell. A rock formed in Dice's stomach. Some of those screams were the last that people would make.
An orb of energy hurtled toward Dice's face. He was knocked to the ground just in time.
"Knowles' soldiers will get him back on his feet soon. We need to move."
Wrench crawled past Dice. There was a deep gouge down the center of his mask. However, he was otherwise unharmed.
"Why are we headed for the main door? Isn't the exit still surrounded?" Dice asked, parrying in between legs and misfired plasma blasts.
"Well, we're not going to be able to escape through the window," Matches said, crawling next to Wrench.
Wrench shook his head.
"We're not going out the main exit," he said.

Dice ran through his memory of the restaurant. Where would they hide? Behind the bar? Under the tables? No matter what, Knowles would stay in the restaurant — Matches' tracker would remain in its place.
"What are we supposed to do, then?" Matches said. "Teleport? Last time I checked, we weren't billionaires."
Wrench kept crawling, even as they passed a stampede of people trying to escape through the exit. Dice tried to avert his eyes from piles of those who'd been shot down on their way out the door.
"There's a secret exit at the back of the restaurant," Wrench finally said. "Not sure how many people know about it, but our chances are better down there than they are anywhere else."
Dice looked back to the door. The mounds of people. Even if they had better chances, Dice had an aching feeling.

As they reached the bar, the chaos had thinned out. Wrench went behind the bar's cover, and Matches followed. Though, Dice kept behind. There was a shadow, just off in the distance. Knowles? Had he already caught up?
Wrench cleared his throat. "It should be right down—."

Dice's ears rung as he was knocked on his back. Blearily pulling himself up, he looked around . There were black saucers, ornamented with red lights, all around him. Sonic explosives. Dice struggled over the bar. A table crashed right where he'd been standing. As another round of shockwaves went off, Dice slid across the bar and onto the ground.
"Everybody will leave through the main exit, and only through the main exit!" a soldier bellowed. "If anybody resists, we have no other choice but to respond with violent force."
They couldn't afford to be caught. Dice wobbled to his feet. Where were Wrench and Matches?
"You have to let us through!"

Dice looked down a narrow pathway behind the bar, and into the back of the restaurant. Dice limped down it, keeping himself hunched over all the while to stay out of sight. The floor murmured. Chunks of wall and ceiling fell at his every step.
Upon reaching the back of the restaurant, he found Billard blocking the entrance to a tunnel in the ground. Several people were gathered around him, including Matches and Wrench.
"You can't just keep us from using the tunnel!" somebody shouted. "If we're sent back out there, we're going to die!"
This sparked a chain reaction of pleas and exclamations. Dice attempted to follow what was being said, but was overloaded.

"Stop it! Just stop it!" Billard said, swinging his gun about. "This is my restaurant! My district! We play by my rules here! Nobody gets out through this back exit, except me! You guys have to take the main exit!"
People groped at Billard's face to push him away, but Billard merely shoved the butt of his gun into their chests.
"You're going to let your entire restaurant die and run off, without anybody even letting anybody know this exit exists?" Matches said, her fists clenched.
Billard sneered.

"As if you're any better. You're the one who created this whole mess, am I right? You brought them here? If I had more than half a brain, I would turn you in to those soldiers right now. But, I'm going to be nice."
Wrench let out a shout of his own.
"Hey! Just because this is all of her fault doesn't mean that we all have to suffer!"
"You're one to talk! If you hadn't provoked Captain Knowles, the fight wouldn't have broken out like it did!"
"You still ran away, without trying to help anybody! Like a coward!"
Billard smirked, backing further toward the tunnel in the floor.

"I guess we're two sides of the same coin, then," Billard said. "I'm sure you had the chance to tell everybody about this exit, just like I did. But, you didn't. You saved your friends. You saved yourself. But, beyond that? Nobody. In the end, we're both scum."
Dice thought that he heard Wrench growl from behind his mask. However, it passed just as quickly as he heard it.
"Never said I wasn't scum," said Wrench. "But, the difference between us is that you abandoned your entire restaurant."
Wrench paused to let out a sigh.
"Look, I didn't want to have to do this..."
Wrench raised his gun.
"… But, there's only so long that I can look at somebody who's decided to run away from all of his problems."
Billard went to aim his own gun but fumbled it out of his hand. He cowered and side-stepped away from the hole.
"Don't shoot me," he said. "I'm just like any of you."
Wrench grunted as he pushed Billard to the side. He crouched down at the edge of the hole.
"You never abandon your people!" Wrench said, as he entered the hole. "Never!"
He gestured toward the group, and they lined up to enter the hole. Dice stood motionless. He'd seen Wrench angry, but never like this. It'd been entirely spontaneous.

Dice stared down the tunnel. He had to follow the group at some point. Though, the cacophony of screams and gunshots echoing from the restaurant kept him rooted in his spot. They were almost hypnotizing.
As Billard struggled up to his feet, Wrench pulled himself back out of the tunnel and aimed his gun at Billard's feet. A blast missed them by only a few centimeters.
"Get out of my sight!" Wrench said. "I don't want to see your face ever again!"
Wrench turned to Dice.
"Come on," he said, urgently. "The U.R.O don't play around. Move it, or you're dead meat."
Dice slid down into the hole. However, his thoughts stayed amidst the kitchen, listening to the mayhem. The melody.

Landing, Dice felt the ground gurgle beneath his feet. The lights lining the tunnel ceiling coughed and sputtered. The walls of the tunnel were in hives, covered with blotches of moss and mold. Dice's hands ran along the soft brick as he made his way after the group. Maybe he should've gone faster. Aside from Matches and Wrench, everybody was several meters away from him. Though, Dice was comfortable as he was. The slushy ground was easy on his left leg and helped him keep him oriented from after the sonic blasts.

Matches and Wrench seemed to share his sentiments. There was no urgency in their steps. Their heartrates and breaths were steady. Matches had an easy expression on her face, and Wrench's eyes roved off in the distance.
"Would it have killed anybody to hire a cleaning bot for this place?" Matches asked, breaking the silence. She wiped the muck off her hands and onto the pants of her bodysuit.
"At least we're in less of a mess than the bloodbath going on up there," Wrench said.
"I'm not so sure. A bloodbath is still technically a bath."
Wrench stopped walking to give Matches a glare.
"Do you have any estimates as to how long our walk will be?" Dice asked.
"I'm not a GPS," Wrench said. "I've never been down this way before. I only know about it."
Dice dug his fingers deeper into the moss. Their hourglass was emptying, and there was no telling how much sand was left.

The walls of the tunnel thrashed against Dice's fingers, as if out of agitation. Rocks leaped from the ceiling. A piece hit Dice on the head. He winced. It hadn't been soft, like the rock covering the wall.
Why had it fallen?

"It's... funny to think about now," Wrench said, "But, this pathway was created back in the Gordon District's heyday, when people were still worried about being apprehended for distributed illegal stimulants... From the look of this place now, though? I doubt that anybody could even be apprehended for murder."
Wrench kicked at a rock on the ground. However, a crack as the rock ricocheted off the wall wasn't enough to disguise what sounded like a sniffle.
"I guess that this tunnel has finally gotten to serve its purpose, after all," Wrench said. "And, I'm not sure if that's a good thing or a bad thing."
"I wouldn't exactly call that 'funny'," said Matches.
"I wouldn't exactly call you funny either, Matches."

Matches smirked. Dice was about to smile himself but stopped to dodge another chunk of rock that falling from the ceiling. Dice looked over his shoulder. Larger chunks of ceiling were collapsing behind them. He tumbled forward.
"The whole structure is unstable," Dice said.
His eyes locked on the group of people ahead of them. They'd already broken into sprints of their own. He wouldn't be able to catch up with them.

"It's not the 'structure'," said Wrench, voice trembling as he spoke. "I've never seen a tunnel collapse like this... The U.R.O have found our position. I don't know what they're using to do this, but they're making the whole tunnel collapse."
Dice's muscles were shaky. The warmth drained from his face.
The stretch of tunnel behind them calmed to a stop. However, it was soon replaced by quaking from the stretch of tunnel ahead of them.
Their group disappeared down a bend in the tunnel. Dice tried picking up his feet. It was no use. They were on their own.
The ceiling groaned and buckled. Dice kept going. Maybe the ceiling wouldn't break. Maybe they could make it through. Maybe he'd be lucky.

As Wrench shouted for Dice to stop, rocks fell from overhead, and the ground slid underfoot. Dice rolled into the sludge. A stench wrung at his gut, overpowering him. His bodysuit was caked with filth and drenched in water. There was only one way things could possibly get any worse.

The ceiling gave away. Rubble showered down, leaving Dice blinded. He was hit by a wave of heat, and a deafening roar filled his ears. He turned down his aid, but the sound still coursed through his bones. He coughed and tried waving the dust away. However, there was a deep shadow everywhere he looked.

Dice looked up. The thrusters of a jet lapped at the air above his head. The jet glowered at him, somehow looking twice as big as the shadow it cast onto the tunnel. Dice dove out of the way, and back to the cover of his friends.

The jet's wings tore into the walls as it landed, and the roar of its thrusters steadily quieted. Once it was only a few meters above ground, the thrusters faded away, and the plane's wings folded up. Dice covered his ears, expecting a harsh thump. However, wheels folded from the bottom of the plane, allowing a soft landing.
Wrench activated his gun and Matches ripped an electric rod from Wrench's pack. Dice scanned for a weapon of his own.
He raised his fists and took a few steps behind Wrench and Matches.
"One would think you would've gotten tired of running by now..."
It was Knowles. His voice echoed from all sides, taunting. Prodding. Dice felt the itch to turn around but managed to keep his eyes on the jet.
The jet let out a whoosh of air as a platform descended. Several soldiers stepped out, followed by Knowles.

"Quite the performance you three put on up there," Knowles said, brandishing his new leg. It was cruder than the previous leg, with less stability and points of articulation. Though, Knowles seemed proud as ever.
"I advise you put your weapons down," Knowles said, with a pitying frown. "There's no point in resisting."
"There are three of us, and five of you," Wrench said, still coughing through the remaining cloud of dust. "I like those odds."
"When I said that there was no point in resisting, I wasn't referring to us..." Knowles said.
His eyes motioned upward, and a turret folded from the jet's front. It instantly locked on all three of them.
"Why in god's name do you have a Gideon Ray in a public city?" Wrench asked, incredulously.
"It's set with low power," Knowles said. "Besides... I don't intend to use it."
"I might make you," Wrench said.
"It'll cut through you like a hot knife cuts through butter."
Wrench didn't flinch.

"The stubbornness of some of you people astounds me," Knowles said. "I used to tell myself that stubbornness was a quality that could only be found in a good soldier... But, I'm starting to think that it's a trait found in good people, in general."
Wrench took a few steps forward, holding the trigger of his gun. Its barrel glared from a building charge of energy. Wrench still didn't release his finger, letting the charge grow.

"Disgusting..." Knowles said, his voice cracking as he spoke. He stared at the gun. "Do you know how many people have died today? Do you know the hysteria you created? Your persistence is honorable, but I only have so much patience for it."

Wrench lowered his gun and took a step back. Knowles and his soldiers stepped forward. Electricity ebbed from tubes in the soldiers' armors and into their gloves. Their guns lit up as they aimed at each of them. One of the soldiers walked up to Dice and placed his gun on his chest. Dice's breathing went unsteady as the gun's heat penetrated his bodysuit and singed his skin.
"Let's not forget who killed those people..." Wrench said, as two soldiers yanked his hands behind his back, and forced him to the ground.

"Let's not forget, indeed," said Knowles. "You incited the usage of lethal force amongst the crowd. Fifteen civilians are dead. Four soldiers are dead. Perhaps it was doled out, in part, by my hand. But, it was forced out by you. You can try to pin this all on me... But, I believe this tragedy should weigh equally on each of our consciences."
"I don't follow."
"You don't follow much of anything. Non-conformity is a vice of yours, isn't it?"
Knowles bent over to lift Wrench's head. He dangled one of his knife-tipped fingers in front of Wrench's mask.
"You're asked for this," Knowles said.
Matches jabbed the soldiers holding her in place with her elbow.
"As much as I've dreamed of riding in my own private jet, I think I'd prefer to miss this flight," Matches said.
She dashed toward Knowles. Knowles let go of Wrench's head, whipped out a pistol, and shot at Matches. Matches toppled to the ground, and the soldier that she'd elbowed restrained her again.
"Wait your turn," said Knowles. "I'll deal with you in a bit."

Knowles leaned in close to Wrench. Their heads practically touched. Knowles' fingers crawled up Wrench's mask. Dice felt the urge to run toward Knowles himself. However, the hot gun on his chest and the hot pain in his leg held him back. In desperation, he checked the soldier's eye to see if he was paying attention. He was. His eyes were unfeeling and cold. There was nothing behind the soldier's eyes, save whatever Knowles had put there.
Dice was trapped to only spectate.
"What are you hiding under that mask of yours?" Knowles asked in a whisper that was barely audible. "Scars? Burns? Deformity?"
"I'm just real shy," said Wrench.
Knowles let out a chuckle.
"It's almost fate, isn't it?" Knowles said. "Two men, from entirely different worlds... United by their wish to hide their faces from the world."
"Never been one to subscribe to fate..."
Wrench let out an uncomfortable grunt and tried to inch away. However, Knowles had him tight in his clutches.
"You're not going anywhere," Knowles said. "I suppose that it's finally time for me to end the suspense and mystery and unveil who you really are under there."
"If you tear my mask off, I'm going to—."

Knowles reeled back his metal fist and then punched Wrench in the face before he could finish. Wrench went quiet. Grasping around the edges of Wrench's head, Knowles began to peel back the layer of Wrench's metal mask. Wrench's silence broke, as he let out a wail of pain.
"Help! God! Somebody, help me!"
Wrench went on like this. Knowles' face creased into a grimace, but he didn’t stop until the mask peeled completely off. Once it had, Wrench's screams faded to pathetic whimpers.
"I'm sorry," Knowles said. He tried to sound facetious, but there was a flash of sympathy in his voice. "I didn't realize that the mask had been partially grafted to your face."
"You do now," Wrench said, weakly.
A strain rested on Knowles' eyes as he studied Wrench's face. Once he'd looked it over several times, he let himself look away.
"How'd it happen?" Knowles said.
Wrench spat up at Knowles, narrowly missing.
"I imagine that you must've seen a lot to get like that," Knowles continued. "It's a shame that you chose the side that you have..."
Knowles stepped away and walked toward Matches. Wrench curled into a ball, putting his head in his hands. Was he sobbing?

"You had a chance to receive a massive award, you know," Knowles said, glancing over his shoulder. "All you had to do was sell out your friends to me. It pains me to say it, but I might've even been willing to put you on my task force. Unfortunately, somebody with more brains than you snatched up that golden opportunity..."
Billard. He must've sold them out.
Dice struggled to keep the heat rising to his face at bay.

Knowles stood over Matches, and a smile stretched across his face. The heat in Dice's face was married with a cold sweat. Knowles pulled the pistol out of his holster and aimed it at Matches' head. Though, not before taking a moment to shoot Dice a fierce look.

"You wouldn't believe how much red-tape I had to cut through to be granted permission to hound you down," Knowles said, his red eye glaring into Matches' eyes. "But, I can assure you: even amidst all those distractions, I haven't been able to get you out of my mind. I've been looking forward to our reunion."
"Aww... It's nice to know that I have admirers," said Matches. Her head stayed bowed.

"You're just as... Insufferable as when I first met you... Always giving me a hard time in front of your comrades. You've traveled thousands of miles since then — but, you haven't gotten all that far, have you?"
Knowles laughed, softly.

"Did you know we thought that you were dead, up until the past day? Your stolen drone — our pilots reported it as having crashed. The U.R.O was already talking about issuing medals to me and my crew."
"Oh, Knowles... You should've learned by now: you can't get rid of me that easily."
There was the slightest scrape as Knowles' finger toyed with his gun's trigger.

"Are you even going to show an ounce of remorse for anything you've done?" Knowles asked. "Hundreds of people should hang on your conscience. Today alone, you were responsible for the deaths of nineteen people. And, I don't even know how many people were injured..."
Matches shook her head.

"At this point, it's all just a game," said Matches. "You're going to imprison me again. I'm going to escape again. You're going to chase me down again. It's pointless, really. You're just on a wild goose chase."
"This time, I can assure you that you won't be able to escape," Knowles said.
An antenna sliced through the roof of their aircraft. A piercing red light throbbed at its tip.
"Good luck getting past that," said Knowles. "You might be able to use your abilities to affect one or two of us... But, not all of us. Not this time."
Matches winced as she pressed her hand to her forehead, then shrugged.
"You win?" she said.
A smirk formed in the corner of Knowles' mouth. "You don’t know how long I've been waiting to hear those words."
Turning to his other soldiers, Knowles made a sweeping gesture with his arm. His soldiers gripped Matches by the arms and dragged her toward the platform. Then Wrench.
Dice finally felt his own captor grip him around his arms and drag him toward the aircraft. Dice flailed his limbs, only to prompt the soldier to shove his gun in Dice's chest.
"I really wouldn't test your chances if I were you," the soldier said.
Dice's left leg seared with pain as it was hauled through the mud. Dice closed his eyes.
Chapter 19:
"Check his pockets. His mouth. His pores. We can't leave a single stone unturned."

Dice's body throttled as a scanner ran over it. Once it had ran over every inch, the scanner gave a chipper beep and was lifted away. Dice's teeth were left chattering. A tingling sensation buzzed at his hands and feet.
"Good. Now, bind him up."
Dice was propped up on his knees as a brace was fastened around his neck. A foot dug into his back as a pair of cuffs locked on his wrists.
"Sorry," said Knowles, leaning into Dice's ear. "I was planning on giving you tightening cuffs — the boys like to call them, 'the cuffs of life' — but, I had to save them for somebody else..."
Dice was pulled up to his feet.
"Alright, keep it moving prisoner," a soldier barked.

Dice's eyes probed around as he was shunted forward. The interior of the aircraft was a glossy silver, to the point where Dice could see his miserable reflection from every angle. Sharp blue lights lined the interior's rounded corners. Holograms leapt from the floor, displaying striking camera feeds of districts, people, and the interiors of buildings. Dice passed a door, and a ladder. There must've been hidden rooms and wings to the craft.
He'd never seen anything like it.

Dice's eyes floundered as he was forced down into a stairwell, into the underside of the aircraft. His bodysuit clung to his clammy skin. The air was humid. Musty. Despite hunching, Dice's hair grazed the ceiling. He measured his steps, taking care not trip over the mess of pipes and wires feeding through the floor.
He'd never seen anything like it...

He desperately wanted to wipe the beads of sweat forming on his forehead. Yet, his hands were locked behind him. He considered asking one of the soldiers for help, but they were too busy snickering behind him. One of them shoved him in the back.
"Speed up."

To Dice's left was a massive, pulsating engine. Its pumps moved so fast that their gears and rotors had turned to mere blurs. Though, somehow it managed to keep quiet. There were hundreds of minute mechanisms, interlocking in intricate clusters. Dice tried to follow a single gear, but only found himself lost among a dozen others.
The machine could've only been designed by a robot's quantum brain functions. However, how did it run? A nuclear engine? Hydrogen generators?
Dice remembered the Gideon Ray, and felt a punch to his gut. It could only have been powered by dark energy.
There was another punch. This time, palpable. A wheeze fled from Dice's lungs.
"Stop staring at the engine!"
Why was the engine so exposed? Any rational engineer would've kept it under the hull.

Dice cast a sidelong glance at the soldiers guarding the engine. His eyes narrowed. They didn't look quite like normal soldiers. There was an intense focus on their faces. Several of them even had goggles on, appearing to be writing in midair.
They must've been doctors, put in charge of monitoring the experimental engine. Dice shuddered. Was the engine really that volatile?
He reached a closet at the end of the engine chamber.
"Enjoy your new residence."
The soldier laughed, before opening the door and pushing Dice in. There was a whine as the door closed.

Dice's head collided with the ceiling. His neck strained as he held his head down. The engine chamber no longer seemed so claustrophobic. He crouched, hugging his knees close to his chest. His back moaned as it was mashed against the wall.
Dice squinted, eyes clutching the strands of light slinking between the cracks of the door. A hand clutched Dice around the shoulder.
"You know, the 'rat-holes' of the Gordon District are looking pretty good right now," Matches said.
"Please... Just shut up," said Wrench, with a hiss
"Does anybody have a light?" Matches asked.
Wrench sniffled. After an extended pause, there was a crack and a flicker. A faint glow came from the side of Wrench's leg.
"I have a light installed in the lining," Wrench said. "It's liquid-based, so it'll only get us a few hours... However, it would've been confiscated otherwise."

Dice used the meagre glow to study the room. The walls were a dull metal, lined with empty racks. It must've been meant as a storage facility for weapons. However, it made just as good of a makeshift prison.
Wrench kept his face covered with his hands, and his head toward the corner. Dice looked to his own corner.
"What do you think that they're going to do to us?" Dice asked.
"You two? Not sure," Matches said. "I'm willing to bargain that it'll have something to do with lifetime imprisonment, or other..."
Watching Matches' face, Dice found a lack of concern. He raised an eyebrow.
"And you?" Dice asked.
"Chances are, I'll either be killed, or put in maximum security," said Matches.
"You seem pretty accepting of that fact."
"It's not a fact... It's chance. And, I'm not playing chance this time — I'm going to play chess. Make my own luck. Your advice."
"You never took my advice before."

"Well, I guess this is where that changes. Let's just say that there's a good chance we're being transported to Omicron," said Matches. "It's a free ride to exactly the place we need to go. I don't know about you, but I'm taking that as a golden opportunity."
Wrench grunted. Matches scowled and looked over.
"And what were you going to say?" said Matches.
"Nothing," Wrench said.
"You definitely were thinking something."

"There's just no way that we're getting out of here..." said Wrench. Each word came slowly, as if to ensure a dourness could be laced in each one. "These people have weapons that are unlike anything that I've seen..."
"I've seen worse weapons. And, I've escaped them."
Wrench shook his head.
"Good for you. As for me? I know that I'm doomed to lose. Besides: I feel I've far exceeded my call of duty."
Matches sputtered.
"That — that's utterly defeatist. Come on Dice, back me up on this."
Dice shifted in his spot, pressing his back harder against the wall.
"Actually, Wrench has a point."
"Thank you!"
Matches' eyes bored through Dice's head. Dice cleared his throat.

"It's just... Even if their weapons aren't especially powerful," Dice said, "it won't matter. The most powerful weapons they possess aren't the guns that they hold to the head. Rather, their weapons are in the head — psychological. Knowles has an intimate knowledge of how to strip a person down to their base elements."
Matches gaped at him for a moment. Then, becoming self-aware of herself, she sat up straighter and put on a fake smile.
"They've never affected me," Matches said, grinning stiffly. "You just need to know how to overcome them."
"That's easy coming from somebody who can get inside somebody's head anytime they want!" said Wrench, with a growl.
"You just can't let go of that, can you? I've been being hounded down to be killed for years because of my 'great' ability. You think I have it so easy, or something?"
Dice buried his head between his knees.
"Yes!" said Wrench. "You didn't have to see your home in complete disrepair. You didn't have to see all of the hate... The despair... All created by these soldiers. By you."
Wrench coughed, before continuing.

"And... And nobody is supposed to remove my mask! It was a scar. A bad memory. I just wanted to have to forget... But, no. I had to come and help protect your sorry asses. I had to make sure that you were safe, and that my job was done."
"Weren't we paying you a sufficient amount?" Dice asked.
"Radials aren't everything," Wrench said.
Dice tried quelling the heat rising to his face.
"Besides," Wrench said, "you're a fugitive. You and I both know that you weren't going to pay me anything."
The heat in Dice's face deepened.

"Look, we can still make this right," said Matches, hastily. "You can't give up on the idea of escaping. It's our one shot. We can catch up with the group in the capital, and finally get out of this place. But, to do that we need to be all in."
Wrench shook his head.
"You don't understand," he said. "I don't want to be a fugitive. I don't want to have to fight. I just want this all to be over..."
"You're giving up?"
Wrench pulled his head from his hands and looked at Matches. Dice felt a rush of terror.
Wrench's face was mapped in scars and burns. A ring wrapped around his face, left behind by the torn mask. Dice tried to look away but couldn't. Wrench's eyes held him captive.
"Look at me," Wrench said, in a rasp. "Don't you think I've finally earned the choice to 'give up'?"
Silence overtook them.
"They're listening to us," Wrench said. "I'm sure of it. I wouldn't be surprised if there are hidden cameras. Everything we say is going to be taken into account, and used against us..."

Dice knew he should've been listening. Though, he could only pay attention to Wrench's face. He'd known there must've been some tragedy hidden under Wrench's metal plate. Though, he'd never thought deeply enough about it. Now, it was staring him in the face.
"Wrench..." Dice said. "What happened to you?"
Wrench looked away.
"My name isn't Wrench," he said, scoffing.
"What happened?" Matches asked, more pressingly.
"Just stop it," said Wrench. "I don't see either of you giving out your secrets."
Dice tried counting the racks along the wall. He finally gave up when the darkness bled several of them together.
"I never knew that you'd been through so much," Dice said.
Wrench snorted.
"We all hide our own little worlds of pain behind masks," he said. "Some of us are just better at it than others."
A shiver ran down Dice's spine.

He listened to the dark energy engine as it snarled and pulled them into the air. The room trembled, shaking Dice to the bone. It was just G-forces, and high atmospheric pressure. Nothing more. Maybe one of the pilots had even worsened the effects of the plane's liftoff to try instilling fear.
There was no need to dwell on it. Yet, he did. Dice's mind backtracked, considering everything he'd studied about the plane. Everything that could go wrong. Spell their deaths.

He arrived at the engine. It was endlessly complex. The slightest malfunction in the sum of its parts could've spelled uncertain catastrophe. What if it numerous functions of the engine failed? What if the entire system imploded?
He shuddered. Nobody could be so stupid as to let that happen. Could they?
His eyes leafed back through their room. He needed to divorce himself from the anxiety and think.

He stared at the walls. He rapped his knuckles along one. They were made of a thick titanium. Too tough for him to scalp at with a cheap laser. However, the corners of the walls were welded together. Likely a bit more unstable. It was promising.
If only he'd actually smuggled a cheap laser...

His eyes gravitated to the door. He couldn't pry it open, as it interlocked with the rest of the wall seamlessly. However, there were no signs of vaulted locks on it. Dice's spirits lifted, only to deflate. The door must've been sealed shut by some sort of a high-intensity magnet lock. There was no getting it open without immense force. However, there might've been a chance at bypassing it...
"When do you think that we'll get fed?" Dice said, rubbing his stomach.
"Our flight should only take us a few hours, if they're taking us to the capital like Matches said," said Wrench. "So, we'll just need to starve until then."
"At least it's better than economy class on a normal plane," said Matches.
Dice tilted his head up at the ceiling. He thought that he'd glimpsed a glass dome rotating about. A lamp? The sparse light from Wrench's pants made it impossible to tell.
"Look at that," Dice said. "We've had a light all this time, and they didn't even bother turning it on for us."
Wrench gave a scornful snort and looked up. His eyes squinted in confusion.
"That can't possibly be a light..." Wrench said. "Look at it. It's... Rotating. It must be a—."
He bit his tongue before he finished, and looked down.
"That's what I thought," Dice said, with a whisper.
He nudged Matches, and motioned at the camera in the ceiling with his eyes. Matches scrunched her eyebrows and construed her face into a frown.
"Didn't we already establish that they had cameras on us?" Matches asked.
"But, now we know its location," Dice said, in a rapid fire. "Quick: what type of handcuffs do you have on?"
Matches chuckled.
"Tightening cuffs," he said. "Knowles and his troops called them 'the cuffs of life', just like that one guy from the MDPD..."
"Deputy Haynam," Dice said, his mouth going dry for a moment.
"Yeah. Anyway, I'd personally call them 'the cuffs of death'... But, I guess that's just me. Why does it matter though?"
"They're knife tipped, right?"
Matches' eyes glimmered.
"I like how you think," she said.
Matches stood up, and dragged the edge of her cuffs along the ceiling until she reached the dome camera. Then, she began knocking at it with the sharp edge of her handcuffs.
"It would be nice if they put cushions inside of these things..." Matches said, with a groan.
"Are the cuffs tightening?" Dice asked.
"What do you think, genius?"

Matches gave another groan. There were crunches and murmurs as the hinges in the cuffs pulled further in. However, Matches kept banging at the camera until there was a shatter, followed by an explosion. Dice covered his head with his hands as bits of glass poured on him.
"It's down," Matches said.
"Yeah, I could see that," said Wrench.
"Well, did you see this?"
Matches waved her hands in front of her face.
"The cuffs broke off from the explosion."
She lifted the two knife-tipped cuffs from the ground.
"It'd be nice if we could get in on some of that action..." Said Wrench.
"That's the plan."
Matches drove the sharp tips into Dice and Wrench's cuffs, until they were each severed free.
"So, what now?" Matches asked.
"We wait until they notice that their camera is down," said Dice, in a hushed tone. "They're going to need to check on us at some point. And, when they do? We fight our way out."
Wrench shook his head.
"Never going to happen," he said.

"We have to have hope in something, even if it's wholly irrational," said Dice. "Sometimes, we need to take risks. Maybe it doesn't make sense, and maybe it won't work... But, if we're going to die, it might as well be on our terms instead of theirs."
Wrench shook his head.
"Hope?" he spat. "It's time to realize that we're a bit beyond that."
Dice's jaw clenched. He couldn't bridle his emotions. He let out a shout.

"Too bad!" Dice said, fury dripping from his voice. "I don't care if there's no chance! I don't care if it doesn't make sense! I don't even care if we're going to drop dead within seconds! What I care about is that we tried, even when there was no point in trying!"
Dice sat back and took a deep breath. He ran his hand through his hair. He needed to contain his pounding pulse. He had to cool down from the heat that had risen to his face.
"I'm sorry," Dice said, reassuming a clinical tone. "But... Maybe there's a chance. We can't afford to be cynical about it."

"I prefer the term, 'realistic'," said Wrench, "which is something that I mistakenly thought you also were. All it took was a little bit of pressure, and you broke... But then, what should I have expected? You haven't owned the world. You haven't had that world slip through the cracks of your fingers. Maybe if you had, you'd understand why I am the way that I am."
Dice clenched his fists. Back in the Monterey District, he was on his way to becoming a deputy. He could've been something. Yet, nobody cared. Nobody remembered.
Who was Wrench to say that he had a monopoly on loss?

"Alright," said Matches, slapping her knees. "The camera is off. And, as far as I can tell right now, we have all the time in the world right now. So, lay it on us. What's going on with you? What's your story?"
"You need to tell me yours first."
Matches rolled her eyes, and leaned back as far as the walls would let her.
"Not going to happen," she said. "I have an inkling that you're more willing to talk than either of us."
Wrench opened his mouth to retort, but then stopped himself. Dice was about to retort himself. Though, words escaped him.
He didn't have any secrets to tell. Did he?
"Come on," Matches said. "I'm in the mood for a story right now."
Wrench sighed.

"You want to know about me?" he asked. "The first thing to know is that I'm not proud of my past. I'm not a good person. I don't deserve to be here... Maybe that's why I left myself to isolation for years on end. Maybe that's why I accepted your suicide mission."

His voice turned to gravel, and his pupils shrunk. Dice wanted to say something. Anything. Though, the shriveled, scarred husk of a person in front of him almost seemed alien. Dice was trapped inside of himself, left to only watch and stare.

"The U.R.O has ravaged the Gordon District... Its energy production should have never been absorbed by them. However, back in the heyday of the Gordon District, the streets were practically made of money. It was a beacon of opportunity, and everybody who was anybody went there to make a name for themselves. I was only twenty at the time. I was arrogant. Thought myself smarter than I had any right to. Naturally, being arrogant, young, and ambitious, I decided that I wanted to make it on my own in the Gordon District. That is, 'on my own', with the exception of a friend. Another kid, just as young and stupid as I was... Lucas.

"Lucas and I had been friends for years. We'd grown up together in the Colt District — a smudge on the U.R.O's map — and he was family. When I told him about my plans for success in the Gordon District, he was skeptical... But, he pooled his money with me nonetheless. We traveled to the Gordon District with nothing but the bags on our backs, and the flimsy plan that I'd outlined in my mind.

"In retrospect, all odds were against us. The Gordon District was already turning to a hotbed of robots programmed to steal contracts, corporate corruption, and government interference. But, maybe I was a bit smarter than I give myself credit. Scratch that... Maybe Lucas was smarter than I ever gave him credit. He was quiet. Us both having been raised in a calculator cage, I always thought he didn't know much. He usually just followed my lead. Despite all this, he saved us from bankrupting ourselves out of radials many times..."
Wrench chuckled, and swept the hair out of his face.

"One time, we were offered a job where we'd essentially be turned into indentured servants for a robot manufacturer," he said. "We were desperate for radials at the time, so I nearly signed the papers. Thankfully, Lucas took a second read of our contract, and saved our skins.

"We weren't desperate forever though, thankfully. We found jobs maintaining solar farms. It was good work and paid well. So well, in fact, that we gained enough wealth to begin negotiating purchases of our own plots of land. Bits of property with our name on it began to pepper the Gordon District. We covered our land with the best solar panels on the market and were met with immense success. I'd distribute the energy we obtained to the Gordon District's government, and we were given thousands of radials in return. Lucas hired out people to maintain the plant and worked on expanding. We were only cogs in a much wider machine, but we had a good business. A smart business. But, I was a stupid businessman... I needed more money. More importantly, I wanted to be the one to take credit for it — not Lucas. It was a petty rivalry, existing only in my own head, but it was a rivalry nonetheless.

"I eventually heard about 'underground' opportunities. At the time, the underground world in the Gordon District was only just beginning to seed corruption. Everybody knew that it was there, but nobody knew it was as bad as it was. The underground world, while dirty, was still given a certain amount of respect by the overall public. So, I went underground... I searched for odd jobs. At first, I was just getting shady trade deals for my solar energy, for slightly better prices than the U.R.O offered. Not much changed for our business, but it was at least something. Though, everything comes at a price...

"I wasn't too trusting toward the people who were trading with me. They always had dodgy eyes... Fickle personalities... And, they always had off-putting perspectives. However, I didn't take it as a sign like I should've. I started meeting people deeper underground and getting bigger jobs. It went pretty smoothly at first, all things considered. There were a few close calls, but nothing worth retelling. Yet, nothing good lasts forever. It was eventually discovered by my trade partners that my solar farm was just a small operation, ran by myself and Lucas. That was a big mistake.

"Many of the people I was selling to lowered what they were willing to pay me. Some of them even tried blackmailing me to get free energy. I was also offered new 'opportunities' where, rather than providing energy, I would be helping with new missions. I rejected most of the offers the very moment that I saw that I'd have to take actual risks. However, our funds continued to slip through our fingers. I and Lucas had to consider the prospect of returning to the government for sales — which was no longer as much of an option, due to the expanding size of our business, and decreasing rates from the U.R.O. We were going to need to lay people off, and sell some of our land.

"It was at this point that I took a good look in the mirror. I wasn't as sly and clever as I thought I was. The Gordon District was finally beating me. I knew deep down that my options were slimming, and that I'd need to make money some other way.

"Lucas cautioned me against going to crime rings for jobs, but we'd already had to fire several good people. He showed me the numbers and told me that we could still recover from our losses, but I didn't listen. I suppose that I never listened...

"I ended up talking to one of the smaller operations underground. All I had to do was help take down a few people who were perceived as... 'troublesome'. Sketchy as the job was, it sounded like they'd pay legitimate radials, so I agreed. I wasn't thinking with my head though. I was just staring at the numbers.

"I feared going at it alone, so I convinced Lucas to help me with the job. Told him it was clean. He accepted. And, we went. But, I wish that he hadn't listened to me, and let me go on my own... We ended up being taken to a corner of the Gordon District with a group of hired guns. It took me a minute, but I eventually figured out that the place we'd been sent to was a factory, and that the 'people' who I'd been paid to kill were just robots. Well... They weren't 'just robots'. They tore through most of us, leaving many for dead. One of the more desperate people of our crew ended up setting off a bomb of theirs. And, I barely made it out alive.
"Lucas didn't make it out alive though."
Wrench grunted, and shifted in his spot. Dice took in a deep breath.

"It's not entirely fair," Wrench said. "I've gotten to live a life. A hollow life, yes... But, goddamn it, life is life! I get to have one, and Lucas doesn't. He forever remains a man in his late twenties... And, I forever remain the man who killed him."
"It wasn't your fault," said Matches. "You can't blame yourself for every death that was indirectly caused by you."
Wrench shook his head, and then slammed a fist into the wall.

"It was my fault though," he said. "All my fault... I — I was the one who set off the explosion. And... I never tried saving Lucas. The moment that I threw my grenade, I ran away, like a coward. I could've saved him. I could've stopped it. But, I didn't."

"There are plenty of things that all of us could've stopped, at one point or another," said Matches. "Doesn't mean that we should let ourselves get weepy about it. No matter what you might tell yourself, it's not all your fault."
Dice closed his eyes as he was taken back to a dark, claustrophobic place... Hot. Full of static. Full of restraints.
He tried shaking it away, but only saw somebody staring at him through the darkness. Somebody blurry. Harsh. With cold, glazed over eyes. Dice shuddered and held his breath.
"Matches is right," Dice said, swallowing his breath. "Lucas is long gone. You're allowed to let yourself move on."
Matches shot Dice a sidelong glance.
"First time that I've ever heard you agree with anything I've said," said Matches.
"Don't get accustomed to it," Dice said, with a shrug.

The world felt heavy. It swept over Dice in waves, making him lapse in and out of a fog. He just needed to leave this place. Go somewhere else. He needed to go where there was no more noise. No more fear. Just peace. Peace, and sleep.

"You know, I didn't actually get these scars from fighting in the robot explosion," Wrench said, with a haggard chuckle. "I got them far later. After Lucas's death, I couldn't bring myself to keep living in the Gordon District... Crime was only getting worse, and my handle on things was slipping away. I moved into the Pit, due to the supposed opportunity that was supposed to be there. There was definitely something there.

"I ended up getting in a fight with one of the locals when I arrived. He beat me bloody, and left me trapped under the acid rain. I narrowly escaped, but not without sustaining one too many injuries."
Wrench shook his head.

"It was so hard living there all on my own," he said. "You know, I've been wondering why I ended up helping you two... At first, I convinced myself that I did it for the radials. But, now I know that I don't care about that."
He groaned, and leaned his head back toward the ceiling.
"I think that, when I saw you two, I saw a second chance. As stupid as it sounds, I saw a little bit of Lucas in both of you. I can only hope that I don't fail you like I did him."
Matches smiled at Wrench, and then leaned her own head back.

"I don't know what's going to happen," said Matches. "Maybe we'll get shot to bits. Maybe this is all hopeless... But, I'd just like to let you know this: you got us this far. I don't know where we'd be without you."
"An ash heap somewhere in the Pit, probably," said Dice.
"Thank you for that... Um... Acute observation."
"Astute."
"Thanks for the hot tip. Now, as I was saying..."
Matches turned back to Wrench.
"Look. Whatever happens, just know that you did your best."
Wrench gave a firm nod.
"My best isn't all that much," he said. "But, I'm glad that it was enough for you two."
"I'm glad that the opinions of two criminals mattered so much to you," said Matches. "Actually, maybe that's more sad, now that I think about it..."
That was more like it.
"And you were blaming me for ruining the moment," said Dice.
"It was getting too sappy," said Matches. She looked from Wrench to Dice, and then back again. "So, now what? Do we just sit here and wait for them to take the bait? Or...?"
Dice's chest sunk. His face went grim. They were still trapped in a prison. Stuck sitting, waiting for somebody to free them.
Wrench cleared his throat.
"One last thing to get off my chest," he said. "My name isn't actually Wrench."
"Yeah, I think we already figured that out," said Matches.
"My real name? It's Toby."
"I'm still calling you Wrench. But, if we're trying to go for big reveals, my name isn't really 'Matches'."
Wrench snorted.
"Well I think we already figured that out too... Mind telling us your real name?"
"Not yet..."
Dice rubbed the back of his neck.
"If it's any consolation, my name is actually Dice."
"BL-270. Wake up. No sleeping on the job."
Dice pulled his head from his chest and stared through his computer screen. At the tick marks on his glass wall. Nineteen ticks.
The clock was ticking. Time was almost up.
He smiled.
"BL-270, what are you doing in there? You've received explicit instruction to do this job — you're in no position to be neglecting it."
"Thirty androids," Dice said. "Thirty androids have been reprogrammed. Rehabilitated. I just want... I just want a rest."
"Bl-270! You need to complete your assignment."
Dice's smirk deepened.
"As you wish."
He closed out his lines of code, submitting it for processing.
"It's about time," the voice said. "You've taken way too long on this one — we're not even going to have time to review it. It's fine though... It should be fine."
Dice laughed.
"Oh, it should."
"What do you me—?"
Dice's computer screen flickered out. There was a beep as the top of his tube opened out and tipped forward. Dice slid out, collapsing onto a platform.
It'd worked. The android he'd reprogramed had utterly hijacked the facility.

Dice tore away at the ooze covering his face. His skin could finally breathe. He squinted and looked around — his platform hung over a dark chasm. Hanging above were dozens of rows of other identical tubes and platforms, all lit by dim green lights.
Cautiously measuring his every step, Dice made his way down the platform. The wrong move could send him tumbling over the side, into and endless abyss. Dice's head buzzed.
A buzz went off. Flaring white lights. A door at the end of the platform opened up. Dice squinted his eyes and covered his face from the blinding glare.
"BL-270... I expected so much more of you. You betrayed me."
A shadow stepped out from the white light, steadily coming closer. Venom dripped from each step.
"You betrayed the collective."
Sweat poured down Dice's face. He could almost make out the face — make out the fury. The rage. Yet, it was too foggy. His vision needed to clear. He needed... He needed...
"Dice! Dice!"
It was... Matches?
Chapter 20:
"Dice!"
Dice grunted and kicked into the wall. His heart was pounding. His head spun.
"What's going on!?" he moaned.
He looked up, using the remaining shreds of Wrench's light. Matches was standing over him, her fingers pressed to his forehead.
"What are you doing?" he asked.
"Your dreams spiraled had out of control. You were having a nightmare," Matches said. "I was — I was just trying to stop them for you."
His head bobbed, and his thoughts fogged. He could feel a fire rising in his chest. Though, he couldn't lose control. He tried listening to the slight putter of the engine.
"You... Were in my head?" Dice asked, his face twisting.
Matches sat back in her spot and ran her hand through her hair.
"Well, when you put it like that, it doesn't sound so good... I was just trying to help you. I've never seen your dreams get so bad."
Dice put his head in his hands and shook his head.
"Have you been in my head before?" he asked.
"I try to avoid going into people's dreams as much as I can."
"You didn't answer my question. Have you ever been in my head before? Yes, or no?"
Matches sighed.
"Yes, but—."
"— but nothing! You're not supposed to be in my head! My thoughts — my dreams — those are mine to deal with, and mine alone."
It all made too much sense. His nightmares had been getting worse ever since he'd been working with Matches. She must've been altering them — goading him on.
"How much have you been changing in my dreams?" Dice asked, hoarsely.
"Not much," she said. "Just, whenever you seem to be having nightmares, I'll try pushing them away. Usually it has the reverse effect, but I always figure it's worth a shot..."
"I can't believe this!" Dice shouted. "You made me a promise, and you broke it. Completely. You were supposed to be on night-watch, not messing with my mind!"
Matches hung her head.

"Look, I'm sorry. It's just, your nightmares weren't — but, it was still wrong. It was wrong. I won't do it again. We can just forget this ever happened. You can go back to sleep — you need it — and I can keep watch until It's your turn."
Dice pursed his lips and shook his head. All this time he'd been trusting Matches — yet, she'd been just as much a threat as anything else he'd faced.
"I really don't feel like going back to sleep," Dice mumbled. "It can just be my turn for night watch now. I — I have a lot to think about anyway."
Matches shrugged.
"Alright then."
She laid down and closed her eyes. Dice counted down the minutes, waiting for her to finally fell into a state of steady breathing and low heartbeat.
Ten minutes.

Dice turned up his hearing aid to its maximum setting. Nothing. He pressed his ear against the door. Just the methodical ticks of the plane, and his own soft breath. Yet, he continued to listen. There was a hint of something, just off in the distance. The ghost of a harsh voice, echoing off walls.
He pulled his ear away. It was just a hallucination. Nothing more. Matches had been right. He needed sleep. His mental stability was steadily slipping from his fingers.

Yet, he also needed to stay awake. He slapped himself in the face. He thought back to the engine. The slightest malfunction would turn its ticks to an explosion. Eyes still sagging, he thought about Knowles' troops. Just beyond his scope of hearing, they were pacing, and waiting. Waiting for him to bend, and snap. Dice's pulse heightened, and his muscles tightened. He couldn't afford to show a sign of weakness.
However, was a short nap really weakness?

Dice steadily slid down the wall, until he was curled back on his side. He closed his eyes. It was just an extended blink, really. He could reopen his eyes at any moment. Not right at that moment, though. They stung, were heavy, and were probably bloodshot from the darkness.

Dice didn't move a muscle when the engine thumped, jerking his body forward. Nor when there was a bang outside the door. Something deep within his mind writhed about in an attempt to wake him up, but only managed to make his eyes twitch. Dice was paralyzed. Trapped under heaping layers of dreams.
There was a thunderous slam. Yet, Dice still struggled to pull himself out of his haze.
He was trapped. Held captive by slimy bonds, and claustrophobic walls. There was no light. No sound. He was steeped in a vacuum. His breath steadily slipped away from him as his screams went unheard.
It wasn't real. It was all Matches. He just needed to fight it.
Fight it.
A high-pitched frequency emitted from the door as the magnetized lock unlatched. Dice shot up from his spot on the floor, drenched in sweat.
"Wake up, now," Dice hissed, shaking Wrench and Matches. "Wake up! We don't have any time!"
Rolling over, Wrench punched at the empty air. His eyes darted around the room in a frenzy.
"What's going on?!" he shouted.
Dice put his finger over his lips.
"Be quiet," he said. "And, get up. The door is about to open."
Heart hammering, he looked over his shoulder. The door remained in its place. Dice clenched his fists and stalked toward it.
"Waking us up already?" Matches said. "It's still dark out."
Pressing himself against the wall adjacent to the entrance, Dice positioned and repositioned his legs into a fighting stance.
"Forget the stance — you just need to get your fists up," Wrench said, with a yawn.
"And you just need to get up," Dice said.
"Sorry if we're not enthused about waking up to at the crack of dawn," Wrench said.

The door slid open. Dice jumped back, and then charged toward the soldiers. Dodging a blow to his stomach, Dice managed to kick one of them in the shin. A fist hurtled toward his jaw, knocking him to the ground.

As he lapsed in and out of a daze, Wrench dove toward the legs of a soldier that held a replacement for their camera. Matches became locked in a wrestle with another soldier, but not quickly enough. There was already the sound of more soldiers marching toward them.
As Dice struggled back up to his feet, he listened to the engine. Its sound had turned to a haggard cough.
He blinked. If they shot out the engine, maybe they could buy enough of a distraction to escape...
What was he thinking? That was stupid. Suicidal, even.
"Dice, get over here and help!" Wrench shouted.
A soldier was spread out on the ground, and Wrench was holding his gun. Wrench inched out of the door, aiming his gun at approaching foot-soldiers. Though, there were half a dozen of them.
Dice cautiously followed Wrench outside the door.
"What do you want me to do?" Dice asked.
"Pick up a gun and think up a plan, damn it," Wrench said. "You brag about having a fat brain, right? Use it."
Dice picked up a gun from the ground and took aim at the soldiers. He shot sparingly, trying to save as much ammunition as he could. They were only a few meters away from the engine area.
"You have to be the worst shot that I've ever seen," Wrench said, as he froze another soldier in a zero-point energy field.
Dice ducked behind him, and tried avoiding the barrage of gunfire. He couldn't afford to get shot.
"You have any bright ideas yet?" Wrench asked.
Dice shook his head. Should he tell Wrench about the engine? No. He wouldn't go for it. Even if he would, there were too many eyes and ears.
Dice looked over to Matches. Far too many eyes and ears.
"Bright ideas?" Dice repeated. "Well, now might be a good time for me to actually hit one of these soldiers."
Matches smirked. How could she smirk?

Wrench had them retreat a few meters. Soon, they'd be pressed back up against the walls of their prison. Dice could only be thankful that the soldiers didn't seem to have the best aim themselves, continually missing.
"Dice, my gun is running out of battery," said Wrench. "You're going to need to put the soldiers in the energy shield, and Matches can shoot them all down."
"Not yet," Dice said.
"What do you mean, 'not yet'?" Wrench said, incredulously. "If one of you don't do something quick here, we're not going to be able to pull this off."
"I have a plan. Don't worry."
They continued firing. Three soldiers fell, but more were edging closer. Their numbers were increasing. Dice's sense of apprehension peaked as he stepped back into their prison cell.
He stared into the eyes of one of the soldiers. Something wasn't right. They were missing too much. It almost seemed purposeful.

Matches suddenly broke into a sprint and plunged into the circle of soldiers. As Dice went to shout, he was knocked back by a invisible wall. He was suspended in midair. He tried wrangling his thoughts, but they'd been wiped clean. He waded through endless blank space.
The wave subsided. Dice pulled himself back up from the floor. The soldiers around Matches had collapsed to the ground. Matches had collapsed with them.

Dice took a moment to recoup, before hobbling over to Matches. His head was still spinning, and an ache lodged in the back of his head. Save sheer force of will, every part of Dice was tempted to curl up into a ball.
Dice slung her gun over his shoulder, and held his hand out. Matches rolled over and took it.
"What happened?" Dice asked.
"I let out a burst with my mind," she said. "Their mental block — I don't think it's working anymore."
Dice eyed the experimental engine. It was sputtering like mad.
"How long have I been here anyway?" Matches asked.
Wrench let out an annoyed huff.
"You know just as well as we do," he said. "Both of us were knocked unconscious for quite a bit there."
"I tried to keep the mental blast from affecting you two," said Matches, with a frown. "I guess that I didn't do the best job of that."
"No surprise there," Dice said, shooting Matches a look.
Wrench made a quizzical expression.
"What's with you?"
Dice spun his head about the room, frantically.
"We don't have much time before more soldiers come. They're probably already on their way."

Dice stepped over the bodies of several soldiers, and hobbled to the engine area. Aiming his gun, he looked for the right place to shoot. The pumps? The transistors? He continued scanning. There had to be an Achilles heel.
The engine might explode and kill him if he were to shoot in the wrong place— or, even if he shot in the right place. Dice shuddered. Hopefully it wasn't as powerful as it seemed.
"What are you doing?" Wrench shouted, running toward him. "Are you insane? We should try stealing the pilot's chair, not shooting out the engine! What on earth is that supposed to accomplish!?"
Dice tuned him out. He needed perfect aim in order to properly detonate the engine. His hand shook. He took in a deep breath, steadying it. He couldn't afford the slightest miscalculation.
The barrel of his gun centered around an exhaust pipeline. It appeared to feed into the pistons. It was the safest bet at disrupting the system.
"No!" Wrench shouted. "Don't!"
An immense weight wrapped around Dice's waist. He was flung to the ground, and left fumbling for his gun.
"What was that for?" Dice asked.
"You're going to kill us all," Wrench said.
"Agreed," said Matches. "You on a suicide mission or something, Dice?"
Dice scrambled forward. The gun had slid just in front of the engine. If he could just get a hold of it and pull the trigger...
"Stop it!" said Wrench.
Wrench grabbed Dice by the leg. Dice looked him in the eye. Heat had risen to Wrench's face, turning his scars to a fiery red.
"We need to get out of here, and attack the cockpit," said Wrench, motioning at Matches.
Wrench continued to hold Dice in a lock, while Matches ran toward the door.

"Wait, you don't understand," Dice said. "This engine is failing anyway, without scientists monitoring it. You can hear it. Besides: we don't have a chance at stopping Knowles and his crew. We got lucky just a moment ago. If we plan on making an escape, it needs to be when the entire crew of this aircraft is distracted."
Wrench shook his head.

"You have no damn idea what you're doing," he said. "You shoot out that engine? This whole plane could very well implode into a wormhole. If not that, it's going to crash — and our chances of getting out of a crash alive aren't all that high."
Matches had stopped just at the door. Good. There was still time.
"Those chances are higher than the alternative," Dice said. "Sorry."

He punched Wrench in one of his scars and snatched up the gun. Neither Wrench nor Matches were thinking straight. They were being driven by emotion. He was the only one who was level-headed enough to know what call to make.
Wrench kicked him in the side and pulled his arm back. Dice kicked him in the shin, and then tripped him. There was a cry of pain, followed by a thud as Wrench fell to his knees. Dice's gut twanged.
It'd been necessary though. Nothing was going to get done otherwise.

He took aim at the exhaust pipe once more. Footfalls of somebody running toward him pounded. Matches, no doubt. But, she wouldn't be there in time. Dice already had his finger on the trigger. He just needed to shoot.
He paused for just a moment. What if Wrench was right? What if they wouldn't be able to move fast enough to escape?
"Halt!"

Dice went to pull the trigger, but something made impact with his back. Pain spread up and down his spine, afflicting his every muscle. Writhing on the ground, Dice clung to consciousness as best he could. He was overtaken by a fit of twisting and groaning.
"It's quite alright."
It was Knowles. His voice cut through Dice's ears. Dice managed to turn his head to look into Knowles' vapid eyes. Matches and Wrench thrashed at his feet. Fury coursed through Dice's veins.
There was too much emotion in Knowles. Dice forced himself to look back away and return to the pain. It bore through his skin and wormed its way into his marrow.

"It'll only last five more minutes or so," Knowles said. "Does it hurt? Nevermind. Sorry. Stupid question. It's probably the worst pain that you'll experience in your lives. These nano-transmitters... They lock to your nervous system and send signals throughout your entire body. However, as the old adage goes: 'desperate times call for desperate..'. For desperate actions? Something like that..."
Dice rolled onto his stomach. Knowles kneeled over Matches' paralyzed body. Her eyes were glued to the ceiling, and her back was stapled to the ground.
"If any of you are wondering, this was all just a test," Knowles said. "A test gone haywire, but a test nonetheless."
It was all a test? It didn't make any sense. Nobody would've been able to test him without his knowledge. Dice tried clenching his fingers into a fist, but... Couldn't.

"To be frank with you all, we're no longer in flight," Knowles said. "We've left our engine on, in order to simulate the illusion of flight. But, in actuality, we landed at the detainment center in Omicron just an hour ago."
A slight smirk formed on the edges of Knowles' lips.

"On top of that, I made sure to give my soldiers orders for them to shoot to miss, and to only take you down in direct hand-to-hand combat," Knowles continued. "I know that you're all wondering: why put so much work into manipulating you three into thinking that you'd finally made an escape? The truth is, I needed to know just how powerful— Matches is the name you're going by now, is it? — really was, before detaining her. I didn't expect her to be able to incapacitate all of those soldiers, but I'm glad to now know. We need to set our dampeners accordingly. Speaking of which..."
Knowles displayed a metal frame, fashioned into the shape of a bowl. He placed it over Matches' head like a crown.
"That should keep you in check, until we can permanently disable your abilities," Knowles said.
Matches grunted. Then, her grunts formed to words.
"It. Won't. Work."

"Our advances in research on your abilities have made sure to it that it actually will," said Knowles. "It might be comforting to believe that you're somehow special. But the truth is, you're just one factor out of millions. There's a much bigger world out there, Matches, and you're just a small part of it."

Knowles lifted Matches over his back, and dragged her toward the door. With a whistle, several soldiers spilled out of the door, and came toward Wrench and Dice. Dice clenched his jaw, trying to haul himself out of the sheer pain coursing through his body. Though, he was numb all over.
He was carried close behind Knowles. Soldiers lined the jet, all standing at attention. Each one was prepared to attack. Dice averted his gaze. He couldn't look at them. Not like this.

"Amplify our neural dampeners from level three to level six," Knowles said. "The nano-transmitters are going to wear off pretty soon here. I don't think any of us are keen on facing the repercussions for failing to take proper precautions."
A soldier at Knowles' side gave a stiff nod and ran his fingers along his wrist pad.
