As they reached the end of the aircraft, a drawbridge lowered. Dice was dragged down it, and onto a vast runway. Aircraft and military vehicles of all kinds were parked along it. Though, what Dice found more interesting were the countless robots lining the runway's sides. They were all dismantled and disarmed, standing with slumped postures. They gave off an imposing air nonetheless. Their heavyset builds eluded to a processing power that would put any of Knowles' troops to shame.
Why were they all shut off? Another cruel "test" from Knowles?

Dice squinted as he peered over the glaring tips of the military vehicles. The sun was unfolding from the horizon and pulling Omicron's skyline with it — countless rows of chrome monuments, dipped in a marmalade glow. Dice's eyes watered. Basking just under the sun was a crystal pyramid. The U.R.O's largest supercomputer. His eyes jumped to the left, focusing on the rooftop of a nearby building. Holograms leaped over it, in a ballet. His ears picked up a faint melody. It must've been hosting some kind of celebration.

"Welcome to Omicron, the jewel of the U.R.O," Knowles said, in a half chuckle. "The center of hopes, dreams, and half the world's economy. Sorry that you all had to visit it here, in Fort Omicron, rather than one of the more touristy places.... But, hey: we serve the best last meals here."

The runway strip dragged for hundreds of meters as an oversized black brushstroke. At its end was a dome building, which stretched half a mile. Its sides glistened and winked. It seemed glass, but it mirrored its surroundings so seamlessly that Dice questioned whether he was looking into a parallel reality. The reflection was flawless — too flawless. On the outskirts of the dome were warped strands of light. Dice focused on one, and watched it beam across the sky as a stray bolt of electricity.
There must've been some sort of energy barrier surrounding the dome.
"Welcome back to Omicron!"

A man strode in front of them. Silver glasses were fitted around his eyes, blending them into his equally silver hair. Pushing aside the bodyguards flanking his side, he stepped forward to give Knowles a firm handshake.
"President Fischer!" Knowles said, flashing a smile. "I wasn't expecting to see you here! Is the morale parade going well?"
President Fischer snorted.
"Could be going better. There's this massive riot... But, we're fine. It's fine."
He laughed, and then eyed Matches. Wrench. Dice.
Dice shriveled inside. He tried to scowl, but only felt the muscles in his face slacken.

"Anyway, I needed a pick-me-up, and a little birdy told me that you finally captured 'Segue'… Needed to see it for myself. Let's just say, you can color me impressed. And, look at that: you brought some new faces with her too."
"She's going by 'Matches' now. And yes, she grew quite the posse this time around."
President Fischer slapped Knowles on the back. "Of course she is, and of course she did..."
The President leaned into Matches' face and smiled.
"You're doing the lord's work, Knowles. Putting her in maximum security, here... You have no idea how many lives you're saving."

Knowles closed his eyes and shook his head. "My troops inadvertently caused the deaths of several civilians while chasing her. I don't know if I could bear chasing her down again. I don't know if the U.R.O could bear it. You're sure you don't want to destroy her?"
President Fischer cast Knowles a pitying look.

"Knowles, you know why we can't afford to do that. She's a vital resource if we plan on winning this war with the Kelvin Union. Besides: she's safe here. This is the strongest base in the U.R.O! You honestly think she'll escape it?"
"It's no surprise that the military base in Omicron would be the biggest and ugliest..." Wrench said, spitting on the ground.
"Regaining your faculties, I see," said Knowles, with an uncomfortable waver in his voice. "At least I can concur with half of wha—."
The President placed his hand on Knowles' chest, pushing him aside.
"Don't worry," the President said, with a chuckle. "I can handle this guy..."
The President flashed a smirk at Wrench, and stared him in the eye

"This base was indeed created as the biggest, due to Omicron being the largest and most pivotal city in the U.R.O. We can't afford a lapse in defense and must take all precautions to ensure that we're protected."
He gestured to his right, and his left. There were towering walls on each side of him, reinforced with steel and hot red energy shields.

"We've installed the finest technology, in order to ensure the safety of our people," Knowles jumped in, savoring each word. "It's our duty to make sure that our great nation is protected from external threats."
Dice coughed as he regained control of his voice.
"And we're threats?" he asked.
Knowles and the President joined in a sigh of regret. The muscles in Dice's neck tightened.
"You're not exactly what I would call a threat, so much as an incidental symptom of a far more widespread problem," said the President. "You can read about it in my latest book: The Ailments of —."

"You merely tried to aid a threat..." Knowles said, cutting him off. "Perhaps you didn't know the sheer gravity of assisting 'Matches'. Perhaps I didn't do the best job getting my intentions across. Nonetheless, we're separated by a deep chasm. I can't neglect detaining you without a severe blight to my career. It might not be the most venerable of circumstances, but it's necessary for progress."
Dice wanted to hate what Knowles' said with every fiber of his being. Yet, his neck relaxed. Somehow, Knowles' words rang true.
There was a buzz. The President lifted his forearm to his eyes.
"Crap. Well, would you look at that?" the President said, with a snort. "Sorry fellas, but I have to get going. Duty calls."
The President's hair whipped through the air, and there was a steady beating. As the President backed away, a helicopter landed behind him.
"Wait, what?" Knowles said. "You just got here!"
"Yes, well, word apparently got out. So, I better get out. My intel says some rioters are making their way here. I'm going to fancy a guess that they want a headshot — and not the good kind."
"What!?"

"I know, right? Most people want the good kind... Especially of my face. I mean, look at me! That said, when you're popular enough, you get a fair share of hatred. People have been trying to assassinate me all day... No matter, though. My mansion in the Balcombe District is calling my name."
The President waltzed up his drawbridge, while his bodyguards folded back around him.
"I had so much that I wanted to talk to you about though... I have excellent battle strategies for how to invade the—."

"Don't worry," the President said, shouting over the roar of his helicopter. "We can chit-chat later. For now, your... Your command is that you get 'Matches' in her cell, or whatever. Do that, and you just might have a seat in the Senate waiting for you in a month. Alright boys, let's get the hell out of here..."
The helicopter sputtered, and then lifted into the air.
"But, President Fischer... We really need to discuss the —."
"A seat in the Senate, Knowles! Don't! Push! It!"

As the helicopter flew off into the horizon, an alarm went off. Aircraft flew down the runway and launched into the air. Soldiers ran toward turrets lining the walls. Dice's hands went clammy. As he went to wipe them on his pants, he remembered they were handcuffed.
"Great, just great..." Knowles muttered. "Son of a bitch sends the mob after us, and then decides to ditch..."
He cleared his throat.
"They should be able to walk on their own now," Knowles said to the other soldiers. "Set them down, and pick up the pace."

Dice's knees buckled as he was dropped to the ground. He broke into a brisk walk after being shoved from behind several times. Dice could smell the sweat streaming down everybody's faces. Knowles was moving with an unusual lack of form. All of his troops were.
There was an explosion off in the distance.
"Come on people, what did I say? Pick up the pace!"
His voice broke off, and he broke into a jog. Dice tried to keep up, but his leg was on fire. He looked over to Wrench. His face was mapped in pain as well.
"What's going on?" Dice asked.
"Shut up, and speed up," said a soldier behind him, with a grunt.

They were only about fifty meters away from the entrance to the dome base. A section of the energy field was already giving away to let them in. Though, behind him was the roar of more aircraft as they flew into the sky. Dice craned his neck over the base's high walls. Smoke had clouded over Omicron's pearly skyline.
"They having a barbecue over there?" Wrench said, in a strained breath.
He was just shoved forward and knocked to the ground. Dice looked behind for their soldier, only to find him fleeing with a wild look in his eye.
"Everybody needs to move! Somebody, help me get Matches into the base. Ignore the others. Whatever we do, we need to get behind that shield!"
Dice moved as he could, trying to catch up with them. He watched as the soldiers worked together to lift up Matches and run her past the shield. Dice's heart pounded, and his mouth went dry.
"Wrench, come on!" he said.
Wrench was still struggling behind him, trying to keep up the pace.

It thundered overhead. Dice looked up and saw a fiery missile with a trail behind it. It was nosediving toward the airstrip. Dice picked up his feet. He just needed to get to the other side of the energy field. It wasn't that far.

Though, the soldiers were only getting farther away and edging closer to the energy field. Wrench was getting further too. Dice swallowed. He was alone, in handcuffs, hobbling for his life. He looked up and had the itching suspicion that he was about to be obliterated by a missile as well.
As the soldiers made it past the energy field, it closed behind them.
That was it. Matches was gone, left at their mercy. Whatever laid beyond the field and within the fort? It was up to her alone to overcome it. Dice's gut became heavy.
There was absolutely nothing he could do.
Chapter 21:
Wrench wore a downcast look, sweat knitting into his brow.
"I don't think we're getting out of here," said Dice, looking up at the missile. It had sped up as it drew into the airstrip.
"I wasn't prepared for this," said Wrench, coming to Dice's side. He stooped over to catch his breath.
"I think Matches was," Dice said. "Would've been nice if she'd given us a heads up..."
"Not her fault. Can't expect her to tell us everything — she's prepared for damn near anything."
"Except death," Dice said.
Wrench raised his eyebrows. "Out of any of us, Matches seems most ready for even that."
Silence hovered over the airstrip, until broken apart by a boom. A dull ringing nipping at his ears, Dice stumbled back. He looked up to find a fading ball of fire and smoke.
"Yes! Did you see that?" said Wrench.
Dice nodded and grinned.
"Is it wrong that I'm glad Knowles' troops hit their target? That, in a weird way, I want them to win?"
"I know this much: I didn't want to stay the missile's target."
Dice's grin splintered off.
"Yeah, but... If they win, we go into their prison. We become just as much a pawn of the U.R.O as any of the troops."
"Yeah, but you already said that you want them to win. Better put: you don't want to die. So, aren't you their pawn already?"

The fireball turned to flakes of ash. Dice was so small. As a flake drifted away in a gust, Dice's eyes drifted with it. Wrench was right, wasn't he? They were just cogs in a sprawling, purposeless machine.

The sky flared as another missile was blasted out of the sky. Thrashing, the ground knocked Dice over. Dice retched. His ears pounded. Rolling over, he wriggled his body. He needed to get back on his feet. Though, his cuffs kept him down, as if to taunt him.
"Watch me," Wrench said, voice warbling below the explosion's lingering hum.
Wrench rocked on his back, before using the momentum to spring back to his feet. Debris on the ground bit into Dices back as he mimicked Wrench. Just back, and forth.
After a few tries, he was on his feet.
"God almighty," said Wrench.

A crater defiled the center of the airstrip. Soldiers ran toward it from all sides, while a fire burst through. Dice's ears were clouded by a pulsating thud, but he could still make out the fire's roar.

Taking queue from the fire's smoke, the last of the U.R.O's aircraft rose from the strip. Missiles flew through the sky from all sides. Holes ripped through the base's walls, leaving trails of urgency and desperation. Dice watched the corner of his eye to see soldiers reactivating some of their robots.
"Things don't look good," Dice said.
"What else is new?" Wrench said, face twisting into a scowl.
Despite Wrench's efforts, Dice caught a flurry of concern and confusion hidden behind his scowl. It was in the way that his lips twitched and eyes swam.
"Come on Wrench. Chin up. Give me some sort of plan here. I need something."
Wrench sighed and shook his head. "It's not... Nothing is clear. I—."
Wrench jerked around and ducked. A blaster narrowly missed his head. Dice ducked after him. Wrench's eyes narrowed, filling with stiff resolution. Dice could hear the wheels turning in Wrench's head.
"You know what? Scratch what I just said. I know exactly what we're going to do."
Dice smirked. "And, what's that?"
Wrench pointed at the rows of turrets and robots along the wall. Most were shooting into the distance at enemy forces. However, some had turned around, taking aim at Wrench and him.
As one of them blasted at Wrench, Wrench jumped out of the way, and held his cuffed hands out. The blaster hit them, breaking the locks. Dice stared, dumbfounded.
"Come on," Wrench said, eagerly.
"Are you insane? I could lose my arm!"
Another blast went off. Wrench pushed Dice forward, and then gripped his arms.
"What — what are you —?"
Dice held back a wince. Part of his forearm had was singed.
"Well, would you look at that?" said Wrench. "You still have both of your arms, free to use now."
Dice stretched his arms out but grunted as he eyed the steaming burn on his right forearm.
"Most of them, anyway," Dice mumbled. Then, raising his voice he said, "Why are they shooting at us? We're clearly not the threat here."
"If you want to ask them, be my guest," Wrench, speeding up as he headed for the energy shields.

Several more blasts landed at Dice's feet. Even as his leg shot with pain, Dice picked up his pace. Explosions went off in the distance, turning Dice's hearing to mush. Dice turned down his hearing aid, but his ears still throbbed.
"Have they mistaken us for the enemy?" Dice asked.

"No," Wrench said, with a raspy chuckle. "How is it that you can think so highly and lowly of the U.R.O at the same time? Look: we are the enemy, as of right now. You think they see loose prisoners as loyal? They don't have time to arrest us, and it's better for them if we die here than escape and live to kick their sorry asses at a later date."
Dice kept his head down as several more blasts whizzed overhead.
"If the objective is to escape, then why are we going toward the energy field?" Dice asked. "All we're doing is getting closer to the prison."
"That's the idea."
"But, if that's your idea, we have no way of getting inside the prison."
"God, you're slow. That's the wrong idea."
Dice shot Wrench a look but said nothing more.

The thin foil of the energy barrier was mere centimeters from Dice's face. Would it be so bad if he touched it? He reached out his hand, but a shock of electricity leapt from the field, cautioning him.
"So, where's your brilliant way of getting in?" Dice asked.
Wrench gave Dice a tired smirk and patted him on the back. Every scar on his face told a different story. Yet, Wrench's face told the biggest one: he just wanted this all to end.
"You have no imagination," Wrench said.
He tilted his chin upward. Five missiles fell from the sky. They'd nearly reached the field when one was shot out of the sky by a U.R.O jet. Then another. Dice bit his lip.
The remaining three missiles made impact. The field fizzled, before brightening. Dice took a step back and shielded his eyes as sparks of energy darted along it.
"It's only become stronger," Dice said.
"From where I'm standing, it looks like that's the goal," Wrench said. "Those resistance fighters don't look like they're aiming to take out the field with missiles..."

A barrage of missiles flew at the jet. The jet managed to shoot four out of the sky, but the rest made impact with the jet's hull. Rendered a deformed husk, the jet fell toward the energy shield. Dice ducked as there was another explosion, followed by a whoosh. The air sucked out of Dice's lungs. He reopened his eyes to find the jet had imploded into a wormhole. The electric barrier warped as it fed into the wormhole and disappeared. Scrambling back, Dice could already feel the wormhole pulling at his hair and skin.

Wrench jumped on top of him, holding him down. The energy field sparked and hissed. There was a slight zap on Dice's skin. Then complete silence. Dice pushed Wrench off of him to find that the base was wide open, and utterly exposed to attack.
"How did you know they were going to do that?" Dice said.
"Lucky guess," Wrench said, walking off to the fort. "Maybe that plan of yours back in Knowles' ship wasn't so stupid after all..."
Dice's heart was a stretched rubber-band. He wheezed as he kept after Wrench. His leg ached. Yet, fear sunk into the back of his mind, propelling him forward
Off in the distance, Knowles and his crew were walking away from the base. They moved methodically, with purpose. Dice squinted his eyes. Was Matches still with them?

Dull cries went off overhead as U.R.O aircraft engaged in firefights.  Haphazardly arcing over the base, they pelted the ground with the sparks of their blasts and missiles. They were the worst U.R.O pilots Dice had ever seen.
One of them dropped a missile on the base, collapsing an entire section of roof. Dice's eyes widened. They were resistance pilots. The U.R.O planes had been hijacked.
Dice took in a deep breath of relief. They were saved.
Though, there was no getting further away from the jets, and the jets were only getting closer to imploding the base.
"You sure about this?" asked Dice.
Wrench shook his head.
"No. But, we need to save Matches."

More U.R.O jets flew overhead. This time, they left behind trails of people. People rained from the sky, outfitted with sleek jetpacks and compact armor. As they landed, they began firing toward the U.R.O base.
As they began to take aim at Dice and Wrench, Dice raised his arms in surrender.
"We're fugitives!" Dice explained. "The U.R.O captured us and sent us here to be detained! We're one of you!"

One of the resistance fighters snarled. Though, a man barked from the back, prompting them to lower their guns and march off toward the base. A man stepped out from the fray. He was tall and lean. His hair was a dirty blond, and his face was smeared in only more layers of dirt.
"Fugitives, eh?" he said. "You enemies of the U.R.O?"
Dice nodded, only to find that the man's face darkened. The man raised his gun.

"We'll let you stay with us, for now," the man said. He took a glance at Wrench. "It looks like you can take some hits, and I'd rather it be from them, than from us. But, make no mistake: we're not 'enemies' of the U.R.O. And, if you are? We'll make sure to give you just as great of a punishment, or worse."
He lowered his gun, and reached out his hand. Dice went to take it, but the man gave his hand to Wrench instead.
"Alright, hazing is over," he said, smiling. "I'm Vert, by the way. Vert Muller."
"You a commander?" Wrench asked. "A general?"
Vert burst into laughter and shook his head.
"You have the wrong idea scar — scarred guy. Scarred man? I'm looking for a nickname, but I can't come up with one..."
Wrench gave a withering look. "Off to a great start, aren't we? It's Wrench, and he's Dice."
"Nice nicknames? Don't worry, we can workshop them. Anyway, as I was saying: I'm their leader, but I'm no commander. This isn't a military operation."
"Then what the hell is it?"
Vert shrugged.
"A reigniting. A clan. And you're now part of it."
An aircraft crashed in front of them. Jumping back, Vert fired at it with a fury.
"Clansmen, get them some firearms, before... Arms... fire them," Vert shouted to the clansmen still falling from the air.
He broke into a sprint toward the rest of his crew.
As more clansmen landed, they offered Dice and Wrench spare blasters. As Wrench took his, Dice shook his head and sidestepped away.
"I'd prefer not to use weapons," Dice said. "I don't have any stake in this fight."

The fighters and Wrench shot annoyed scowls, before moving toward the base. Knowles and his soldiers were already raining hellfire on the clansmen, knocking them down with ease. The only thing keeping the Clan's numbers from shriveling to nothing was the steady stream still coming from the air.
"Maybe we should just get out of here," Dice said.
"You insane?" Wrench said. "We can't just leave Matches behind."
Despite Wrench's words, Dice took a look behind. The airstrip was littered in fallen aircraft and wounded soldiers. He swallowed and turned back to Wrench.
"The only way for us to get out of this mess is to power through," Wrench said.
"We're on the losing side."
"We need to lose smart then," Wrench said. Then, he stared Dice dead in the eyes. They were cold, and rigid. "If we get captured again, shoot me."
Wrench aimed his gun and fired ahead, letting his morbid words hang between them.
After several minutes of watching Wrench blast into nowhere, Dice saw Vert hurtling toward them. His face was flushed, and eyes were glazed with a terror.
"There's too much," Vert said. "We're not going to win this. I wasn't prepared..."
"Really? I never would've guessed..." Wrench said,
Layers of blood and grease sloped down Vert's face. His eyes wouldn't stop moving, and a fixed grimace was on his lips.

"These U.R.O troops are more aggressive than any of us accounted for," continued Vert. "We decided to attack here last minute — no prior planning. So stupid. We only have about fifty more volunteers coming, before we're clean out of people."
"That's nice to know," Wrench said, still edging closer to the battle zone.

They were only fifteen meters away from Knowles, who was busy slinging people around like dolls. People fled, but Knowles only worked faster. Screams bloomed. They withered. Even as Knowles was caught in maelstrom of firepower, he kept his pace.
"He's a tough one, that guy," Vert said.
Dice glanced to his side. Vert's eyes dropped, and feet shuffled. He'd been tracking his gaze.
"Real egotist too," Vert continued. "Thinks he doesn't need conventional weapons. That he's so strong. He's just trying to instill fear in us."

Vert sent several blasts in Knowles' direction. Though, they petered before making it halfway. Skimming Vert's gun, Dice saw half of its barrel had been chewed off. Vert shot Dice a look, before gingerly placing his hand over the chewed barrel.

"These guns are crap," Vert explained. "Most are built from spare generators we tore out of robots. I hoped they'd at least last longer than this, but... Well, robot tech isn't what it's made out to be."

Dice nodded, but his eyes were back on Knowles. None of the Clan stood a chance. They were pitiful, really. Dice frowned. He should've felt inspired — but it was meaningless. The rockets, the blasts, the shouts... All of their strain went in vain. Wrench fired tirelessly at U.R.O troops, but even he wore a face of apathy.

The strip's clean black marble was tarnished by crude gashes, speckling throughout. The dome base was smothered in flames and crashed jets. Thousands of hours of design and creativity... and it was destroyed in minutes.
Dice squinted. Something was tucked just by the edge of the base, behind Knowles and his crew. A person.
"I found Matches," Dice said, elbowing Wrench. "Look — next to the door of the base. They must be keeping her there until they can stop the airstrikes on the base."
Wrench's firing subsided for a moment. He smirked dryly. A pit formed in Dice's gut as he anticipated Wrench's next words.
"Then, that's where we're headed."
Vert pressed behind Wrench, his gun jumping between targets. He chuckled.
"Wait, what do we need matches for?" Vert asked. "And, where are we going?"
"We're going through the death arena over there," Wrench said. "Been awhile since I've been able to light a cigarette..."
Vert's eyes bulged.
"Have you seen what's happened to my volunteers? As much as I'd like to be slaughtered, we should stay over here!"
Wrench snorted.
"Yeah, well, you can stay over here then," he said. "Me? I have to save a friend."

Wrench marched forward, into the lightshow of blasts and explosions. Taking each step with caution, Dice went after him. He cast a look over his shoulder. Vert remained rooted in his place, hands stuffed in his pockets, but his eyes were among the battle. Finally, Dice gave a whistle. Vert followed.

Tears were put through Dice's bodysuit, as balls of energy grazed his skin. Knowles' squad had better aim than anybody else on the strip, and Dice took care to stand behind walls of clansmen. A single shot to the chest spelled death.
"I can't believe we're doing this," Vert said, as a grenade arced over his head. An electric pulse went off, leaving dozens of guns disabled. "This is — this is idiotic."
"I can't say I disagree," Dice muttered.

"What was that?" Wrench shouted. "I don't know what's gotten into you Dice, but you need to snap out of it! We're not abandoning Matches, goddammit! If neither of you wanted the risk of dying today, then you shouldn't have showed up!"
Vert's mouth hung open, limply. He mouthed something inaudible, and promptly closed it.
Vert leaned into Dice's ear.
"He really likes matches, doesn't he?" he whispered. "Is he a pyromaniac? Or, is he just not all there, upstairs?"
"'Matches' is the name of our friend," Dice said.
Vert's face reddened.
"Oh..." he said, with a laugh. "Well, I, uh — I already knew that. But, thanks anyway."
He cleared his throat.

"Wrench, don't worry, I'm not going anywhere," said Vert. "I didn't abandon my group and join you guys because I thought that I could avoid dying, even if that's exactly what it sounds and looks like. I joined you because you were the only ones who looked like they knew what they were doing."
"If this fight keeps up like this, I don't think our looks are going to last much longer."
Clansmen collapsed in front of Dice. As a U.R.O soldier dashed by, Vert aimed his gun. The trigger clicked, but the barrel only whined. Rubbing the back of his neck, Vert shied back behind Wrench.
"Looks like we hit the end of the line," Wrench said, as more U.R.O soldiers flanked around them. "If we're going down, I suggest that we go down together."
Vert wiped a streak of grime and sweat from his forehead, and grinned confidently at Wrench.

"I'm not going down today," he said. He flashed a communicator chip connected to his forearm. "Spark-plugs... Spark-park? Sparky-barky? Sparky, are you there? Come in, Sparky. This is a code red! Sync with my coordinates, and launch the backup strike."
Wrench tried to take cover behind a fresh wall of people, but they were steadily draining away. Dice scanned the battle. The U.R.O soldiers had them vastly outnumbered
Wrench snapped his head around to launch a few blasts, before turning back to scrunch his eyebrows at Vert's communicator.
"It's a communications device with a fellow coordinator, and key hacker," explained Vert. "He currently has direct access to the U.R.O's—."

A roar rippled through the crowd. An armada of missiles was flying toward them. The crowd crumbled, and Wrench hobbled for the door of the base. Dice stared at the flare of the missiles. The way the sun glinted off their noses. It snared him an invisible net. He saw a flash of an old nightmare. And old memory. A cold light, bouncing off a monitor.
"Dice!" Wrench shouted.
Dice blinked and stumbled after him. How could he have let himself be so stupid?
"So, you have direct control over a hacker unit?" Wrench asked Vert, once Dice had caught up. "Why is that?"
Vert heaved.
"It's a hacker. And, I have control because I'm one of the primary coordinators of this group," he said.
"You're one of the primary coordinators?" Wrench asked. "So, you're basically a commander then?"
"Yes. But, I'm — I'm not a commander."
Wrench frowned but nodded.
"If you're one of the primary coordinators, then why in god's name are you with us, rather than with the rest of your troop?"
"Because I felt like it. Is there a problem with that?"
Wrench's eyes sharpened but snapped shut as the missiles made impact. Leaning on Wrench to keep steady, Dice took a step forward. Matches was just ahead of them, in cuffs and a blindfold.
"Matches! We're coming for —."

Wrench let out a cough. Dice finally turned to see a downpour of plasma blasts from Knowles' crew. Wrench let out a shout as he fired on them, and Vert took a spare gun from a fallen resistance fighter.
"Time's up," a soldier said.

A swarm of U.R.O aircraft circled over the base, knocking the rogue U.R.O aircraft out of the sky. Only a few remained. Though, where had the swarm come from? Hadn't all of the U.R.O's aircraft already been deployed? How was there more?
Dice shrunk back. Fort Omicron was the biggest base in the U.R.O. This airstrip must've been only a blip. U.R.O responders were going to keep coming, until all the Clan was subdued.

Turrets unfolded out of compartments in the base's wall. Heat drained from Dice's face as he looked back to Matches. The chances were too high that he'd be shot before reaching her. Besides — how would he remove her cuffs? There was simply no way to save her.
He didn't want to save her.
"What are you standing there for?" Wrench said. "You go and get her out of the restraints— we can hold them off."
"I won't let you down," Dice said, scooping a gun up from the ground. His words were plastic, leaving a bitter taste in his mouth. Yet, they were all he had.
"We might let you down, unless these guys let up," said Vert, with a whimper.

Wrench shot Vert a look, while Dice stumbled over to Matches. Looking down at her, Dice clenched his fists. He could've said something. Anything. He stared, gun hanging limply at his side. Matches had betrayed him. There was no telling how much further she was willing to go.

His eyes focused in on her cuffs. Her blindfold. The device crowning her head. His arm shifted. His ears stung. His hand gripped around Matches' wrist, and he pushed the barrel of his gun against her cuffs. He removed the device and blindfold from Matches' head. For a moment, Matches' face was morphed — almost alien. Then Matches' eyes glimmered at Dice, a grin spreading across her face.
"You decided to save my sorry ass, instead of trying to save yourself?" she said. "Glad to see you have your priorities straight."
Dice scowled and gave a shrug.

"Glad you got that thing off of me," Matches said, pointing at her discarded helmet. "It was strapped so tight, it was killing me. Shame that my mind powers still aren't going to work in here though."
"Yeah... A real shame," Dice said, snarling. He pulled the trigger of his gun. "Crap."
"What?"
"It's not working."

Dice looked over his shoulder. Wrench and Vert struggled to wrench free from a pile of U.R.O soldiers and robots. A chill crawled down Dice's arm. He slapped the gun against his palm and pulled the trigger again.
"Maybe I should go back and get a new gun."
"No time. Just keep pressing it."
There were a dozen more clicks. Nothing. Sweat beaded down Dice's brow. He just had to stop thinking. Keep pressing.
A spark spurted from the tip of his gun, breaking through Matches' cuffs.
"Thank god!" Matches said. "My arm was really starting to cramp. My good—."
"— your good arm?" Dice said, raising an eyebrow.
"How'd you guess?"

Dice took aim at the soldiers. He bit his tongue. Finally, Matches wrapped her own hand around the gun. There was a click. A zap. Knowles troops rolled off of Wrench and Vert, rendered steaming corpses. Dice winced and looked away.
"Just a lucky shot in the dark," Dice said.

A robotic head rolled onto his foot and stared up at him. Burned through his skull. Its slit eyes admonished him for the dead soldiers. Though, had he really had an option? Dice folded his arms into his chest as a wave of nausea passed.
Chapter 22:
"What are you two standing there for?" Wrench said. "We need to head out of here. Let's. Get. Moving!"
Wrench's voice was thin and brittle. His head jerked over his shoulder. Knowles strode toward them, stunted only by a feeble few clansmen.
"If we plan to escape, this rescue mission really hasn't done us any favors," said Vert, casting a dubious look at Wrench.
"Shut up," said Wrench.
"Wait, I thought that you only ever told me to shut up," said Matches.
"Yeah, well I found a wise guy ten times more annoying than even you..."
"A wise guy who also happens to be the key coordinator of the Clan — this resistance," Vert said, proudly resting his arms on his sides.
"Was the key coordinator," Wrench said, bumbling toward Knowles. "Now come on — we all have a plane to steal."
Vert snorted. "Yeah, let's all walk toward the biggest threat on this airstrip. That makes sense..."
"If you have any bright ideas, lay them on me," Wrench said.
The air reeked of sweat and desperation. Dice looked around, running through different plans and possibilities. His eyes flitted over all the bodies that'd been shot down.
"Before we plunge into certain death, I just need to ask one more time: what did you guys need her for again?" Vert asked.
"God, Wrench was right about something for once," Matches said, glaring at Vert.
Wrench smirked. "Glad to have you back."
"Never thought I'd hear you say that."
"What else am I supposed to say? You still owe me a couple hundred radials... And a rematch at cards."

Matches chuckled, but it was halfhearted at best. Before there was a chance for her to breathe, a U.R.O jet flew over them. The ground rumbled. Dice turned. The massive entrance to the base had reopened. Dice broke into a splintered sprint as the base's turrets, soldiers, and aircraft launched a flurry of attacks. Dice kept close to Matches' side. He couldn't let her be captured again.
As the blasts died down, Knowles materialized from their clearing smoke. A vicious smile was on his face. His fingers scraped against his metal leg, sharpening. There had to be a way around him.
A plane crashed on each side of Knowles.
"Do you have any escape parties planned?" Wrench asked Vert, tiredly.
The bags under Wrench's eyes had deepened. In place of terror, his face held mild annoyance. He was entirely numb to it all.

"Yes," said Vert. "I ordered the Clan to hijack a few U.R.O planes and keep them at the end of the airstrip. Now that you mention it, I could probably try calling some of them here. Maybe. That's only if our plans to hijack the planes haven't already been intercepted..."
"I need you to sound more confident than that, in account of how shit the rest of your attack stratagem has been."
Vert said nothing. Knowles was only a few meters off.

Trepidation slowed their steps. Knowles sped into a sprint. Within seconds, he descended into a steady pace among them. Dice dug for a sign of fear. He just needed to find a hint of anxiety. Yet, he came up short. Knowles' posture was relaxed, and his eye serene. He knew nothing that could be done to him. All of their weapons were too slow. Sporadic direct attacks would be too feeble. Besides — Knowles' troops were marching not far off, from all sides. They were trapped in a death circle.
"I see you've made a new friend," Knowles said gesturing to Vert.
Vert shook his head. "Friend? No, no, no... You have the wrong idea. I have no idea who these people are."
Knowles' disregarded him, his red eye flicking to Matches.

"I'm impressed that you found a way to escape, intact..." he said. Yet, disappointment bled from his voice. "Though, at this point, I suppose I shouldn't be underestimating your ingenuity. You have a knack for tearing up my plans... My life."

He stared off in the distance, turning his head to brandish his metal half. His right arm swiped at the flesh half of his face. Had he wiped away a tear? It'd been too fast to tell. Though, it must've been faked. Knowles was only trying to goad sympathy.
That had to have been it.

"This past week has been a series of tragedies for me and the U.R.O," Knowles said, turning back to face them. His face was a deeper shade of red. His eye was cloudy. "I'd prefer to stave off one more tragedy, if I can. I'm intimately familiar with the survival instinct that exists within all of us... But, I need you all to surrender quietly."
Wrench spat at the ground. Knowles raised the corner of his lip in slight annoyance.
"Is that a no?"
Matches smirked.
"I can do that 'surrender' bit for you," Matches said. "But, I'm not keen on doing it quietly. You get me?"
Knowles gestured over his shoulder at his growing mass of soldiers.

"If you want to be smart, let me remind you that I have an army," he said. "They're all here. They're fully equipped to take any of you down, if necessary. And, look: I don't want another fight between us. Many of my soldiers have betrayed me today, and many more have died. Worse yet, much of the U.R.O's civilians — the very people we've sworn to protect — are dead. I don't want to escalate crisis any more than is necessary."
Vert scoffed.
"I doubt the U.R.O's governing powers consider us 'civilians'," said Vert. "The Clan was recently declared a band of traitorous radicals by President Fischer himself."
"Yes, you're right," Knowles said. "That was a poor choice of words by Fischer."
Knowles strode forward, placing one of his metal fingers on Vert's chin. A growl came from the bottom of Knowles' throat.

"'Terrorist' is a more... succinct term... But, that doesn't mean you aren't civilians. Citizens, who were gifted rights by our fine nation. Your deaths today would be a tragedy to me, even if by nobody else."

Vert trembled but managed to roll his eyes at Knowles' words. Knowles' own eyes remained fierce, and rigid. Acid rose in Dice's throat. Despite everything, Knowles carried an earnestness about himself.

"You may think I hate you and your club," Knowles said. "And, you see, you'd be right. The fact that you've incurred pity out of me, in spite of everything you've done, is one of the things I hate the most. But, that won't make me view you as anything less than a civilian."

Dice's head spun while untangling the threads of Knowles' logic. Knowles took a glance at Dice and smiled. It was as if he found delight in Dice's confusion. Could Knowles could read Dice as much as Dice could read Knowles'?
Knowles unlatched his finger from Vert's chin and gave a deep sweep of his arms.

"All of this chaos," he said, voice rising above the roars of blasts and aircraft engines. "All of it stems from a hotbed of misunderstanding. An unwillingness to believe that we have your best interests at heart. Understand this: we have a war going on, within the Kelvin Union. The fate of the U.R.O hangs in the balance. And you three? All you're doing is tipping the scales in the wrong direction."

Dice clenched his teeth. Knowles needed a punch in the jaw. He didn't have a moral high-ground. He was the biggest murderer standing on the airstrip. However, Dice couldn't bring himself to attack. He couldn't allow his emotions to drive him.

"I'm sorry things led to this," Knowles said, "I'm sorry we let people become so disillusioned as to fight their own protectors. However, if you give yourselves up to reason... You'll find that our goals are not so misaligned from each other."
The soldiers edged closer, their stomps piercing through Dice's hearing aid. Knowles raised his hand, prompting them to stop.
"I'd like to carry out my conversation with them, thank you," Knowles said.
He walked over to Wrench. Wrench's eyes were blazing. Knowles took no notice, scanning Wrench with the same indifference that he had toward his soldiers.
"A person's eyes reveal so many things about them," Knowles said simply. "Yours? They're small. Weak. You're the greatest coward here."
"Tell me something that I don't know," said Wrench. "And next time, I'd like you to mean it."
Knowles smirked.
"What are you smiling about?" Wrench asked. "If you want to kill us, just do it. No reason to toy with us."
Knowles shook his head.
"I don't want to kill you... and, I'm not toying with you. On the contrary: I'm teaching you."
"Teaching us what?"
"That the U.R.O cares."
"By killing all of these Clansmen? By sticking Matches in cuffs and a blindfold? By taunting us, while we're hopelessly outnumbered? You have a backassward way of going about things."
Knowles chuckled cruelly. "Out of all the people here, you're the one I feel hatred toward. Want to know why?"
Knowles' red eye locked onto Wrench, awaiting an answer. It didn't get one.
"Because you don't like me," Knowles finally said.
Wrench coughed, then scoffed.
"You think anybody here likes you?"
"Those who don't at least know to respect me. Fear me. Listen to me. But you? You won't even give me that courtesy. You only hold hatred — you're too afraid to admit when you're wrong."
"You got a lot of nerve to tell me that."

"I've looked up your background, Toby. You squandered your life away through underground criminal trades. Yet, you somehow think you're higher than me. Me: somebody who's just following orders. There's not an ounce of integrity in you, is there?"
"Always figured a gram was close enough."
Wrench lunged forward, bashing Knowles with his shoulder. Knowles just absorbed the impact, but a blast went off, knocking Knowles to fall to the ground. Dice was left dumbfounded.
As he looked around, he realized it didn't matter that Wrench had tackled Knowles. They were still surrounded by an army of troops, all closing in. It was bleak. Hopeless.
There was a rumble. Dice's gaze turned to the sky, to find another armada of U.R.O fighter jets. Dice's spirits fell. They rose as Vert let out a whoop of joy.
They weren't normal U.R.O fighter jets.
"Backup has arrived, people!" Vert said.
A gap opened amidst the soldiers as blasts rained down. Vert ran toward the gap and Matches followed after.
"Just a thought: maybe don't announce 'backup has arrived' when backup arrives next time?" Matches shouted.

Their voices became more distant. Dice's eyes were caught on Wrench, who was kept in a headlock by Knowles. Wrench's face turned purple. The fire in his eyes turned to ember. Dice's finger slid down the seam of his bodysuit. His ears burned red. He was a statue, left only to observe.
"This wasn't at all part of my plan," Knowles said, letting Wrench out of his headlock, and slinging him away. "But, you've clearly made your choice."

Dice dove at the ground, grabbing Wrench's loose gun. He aimed it at Knowles. However, Knowles' foot rested on Wrench's head and his arm splayed out to block any blast. Wrench coughed haggardly and spit out a tooth.

Knowles' eyes jumped between Vert, Matches, and Dice. Dice's stomach coiled each time Knowles' eyes jumped back to him. It was only ever for a fleeting moment, but it was long enough for Dice to know he couldn't read Knowles'. Knowles had a way of hiding himself when he wanted. He could glean more out of each glance than Dice.
"If you're going to shoot that at me, shoot it," Knowles said.

His arm raised toward Dice's face. His fingers clicked crisply as they slid forward, unlatching from Knowles' knuckles. They were ready to fire. Dice only smiled. Knowles' eye was directed at Vert and Matches — he was bluffing.
Knowles lowered his arm.
"You can't do it, can you?" Knowles said.
Dice took a step back, as he fingered the trigger. Pressing it, Dice felt his finger go numb. His stomach turned over, and his head rolled. He was bluffing just as much as Knowles.

He looked to the sky, where aircraft glided over sunrays. He looked to Vert and Matches, who were bounding to freedom. He looked to the U.R.O soldiers surrounding him, who were all either dead or crawling on their bellies. Everything was unspeakably far, yet unspeakably close.
"Drop the gun, or shoot it," Knowles said. "You have the chance to stop me. If your cause was worth anything at all... You'd kill me."

Dice looked down. Wrench was still trapped underneath Knowles' thick metal leg. Wrench's hands clawed at it, but he couldn't get it to budge. Rotors chirped as they pushed harder against Wrench's skull.
"I'm not going to be like you," Dice said.
Knowles rolled his eyes, and then raised his arm.
"I thought so," said Knowles. Confidence surged back into his eyes.

A knife-tipped fingers launched from his arm. Dice fell on his back. He clutched his stomach. It was as if thousand needles protruded from it. Though, it was just the one. That fact only made the pain all the worse.
"Don't worry," Knowles said. "It should only barely pierce skin. It'll probably leave a severe scar, but you'll recover."
Dice bit his tongue. Covered his mouth. Writhed on his side. Anything to keep from howling in pain. Sympathy mapped across Knowles' face.
"I'm sorry," Knowles said. "But, I'm called the 'Knife' for a reason. I have a job to do."
Dice studied him and tried to look for a lapse in his expressions. There wasn't one.
"Alright, Commander Tin-foil. Time's up."

His arms gripping around Knowles' neck, Vert yanked Knowles back. Knowles thrashed about, trying to shake Vert away. Vert's face scrunched. His arms held fast. Matches came under Knowles and grabbed his flesh leg. Knowles teetered. His metal leg unlatched from Wrench's head.
Dice rolled over and crawled toward them. The metal shard in his stomach tore at his skin, traveling inward. He'd only made it a meter, before rolling back over in defeat.

Knowles' metal arm nabbed Vert by the back, slamming him to the ground. Knowles aimed his arm. As Matches reeled her fist back, an orb of energy ripped through Knowles' armor and left shoulder. He collapsed on the ground. Shock coursed through Dice's veins as two more holes were put through Knowles' body.
Vert and Matches jumped back, their eyes welling with terror. Wrench gripped Dice by the arm and pulled him up. Dice saw Wrench's face, then looked away. It'd been slathered in an unadulterated rage.
"Let's get out of here," Wrench said, pulling Dice over his shoulder and limping forward.

He yanked the shard out of Dice's stomach. Dice wheezed from the pain. He knew blood was pouring from his wound. An alarm hammered in his head, telling him to lay down. Sleep. He forced himself to keep moving.
"Stay standing," Wrench said, readjusting Dice's position.
An aircraft descended just up ahead of them. Vert let out a laugh.
"They came back for us," he said.
"And here I was thinking that we were going to have to take another transport tube," said Matches, wearing her classic smirk.
"Don't get too cocky yet," Wrench said.

Wrench hobbled past Knowles' body. Knowles' good eye had gone glassy, his red eye had dimmed, and he was captive to a retching cough. Dice stared at the holes burned into Knowles' shoulders. He couldn't help but feel a sort of pity.
Knowles jerked forward.
"Give me Matches," Knowles said, in a shout.

Knives had shot out of Knowles' hand. Suddenly, it was harder to stand up. Dice looked at Wrench. All of the color had drained from his face. Dice slid his arms under Wrench's armpits, but wasn't fast enough. Wrench fell next to Knowles, in a cold thump.
Dice's heart thudded against his ribcage. It raced forward. He forced himself to count each beat. He expected the beats to end at any moment. He wanted them too. They didn't.
Wrench's did.

Everything became a buzz. Knowles sprung from the ground and tried attacking them. Vert overtook him. There were blasts from yet another backup fleet of U.R.O soldiers. A fleet large enough to wipe out all of Vert's Clan with ease. However, Dice couldn't look at it for long. Any of it. He and Matches stayed knelt at Wrench's side.

Dice held Wrench's hand, and brushed his other hand along Wrench's scarred forehead. He felt as warmth seeped from Wrench's body. Dice glanced at Wrench's chest. The four blades from Knowles' hand were there, wading in a pool of blood.
It wasn't fair. They didn't belong there. They should've been Dice's own chest. Yet, there they were. There they stayed.
Dice's hand hovered over Wrench's chest. Maybe he could pull them out. Though, there would be no use. Wrench's eyes were already dipping in and out of consciousness.
"Did I ever tell you you're a real bastard sometimes?" Matches said, squeezing Wrench's other hand.
"Just about a dozen times, smartass," Wrench said. He wheezed.
Dice watched Wrench's eyes. Wrench's pupils were shrinking.
"Wrench," Dice said.
He should've said more. However, his mind was blank.
"Don't worry about me," Wrench said, eyes closing. "I already told you: I didn't plan on coming out of this alive."
Dice opened his mouth to speak, before biting his tongue. His eyes and nose set on fire. Tears streamed down his cheeks.
"I—," Dice choked. He sputtered.
There was a blast off in the distance, followed by a series of shouts. Dice didn't look. He didn't want to. He didn't need to. He already knew what those shouts meant.
Everything needed to freeze. If he could just hang up time... Make things stretch a little longer...
"Dice, we have to make our escape," Matches said. "This is our last chance."
"You still owe me those radials," Wrench said, as a faint smile spread across his face. "Make sure to reshuffle your deck once we've made our way out of here."
Matches beamed and turned back to Wrench. "I thought that you hate it when I shuffle."
"I do. But, whenever I lose after you shuffle, I'm at least able to say you cheated..."
Matches laughed. Dice wiped his tears away. Wrench smiled as if about to laugh himself, but only a weak cough followed.
Something erupted in the distance.
"Alright..." Wrench said. "Time waits for nobody. Especially us, these days. Let's move."
Dice began putting Wrench's arm over his shoulder. Wrench could still be dragged to the plane. There might've been a medical bay. Perhaps Wrench's injuries weren't even as scathing as they seemed.
Wrench shook his head and pulled his arm away. His smile disappeared from his face. The last hint of color went with it. Wrench was gone. A lifeless husk took his place.
"No," Dice said, in a half whimper.
He shook Wrench. He pressed his ear to Wrench's face. Though, Dice knew he wouldn't find anything. He'd heard Wrench's last breath whisk out of him. Heard his life flicker away.
Dice's mind ran in a million different places. He focused on everything around him. He let his focus blur to nothing at all.
Two Clansmen stood behind him, accompanied by Vert himself. Dice wasn't ready. He couldn't let it end. It wasn't time.
It was all wrong. Fate... Chance... Things weren't directed by some unseen force. They just... were.
Then, weren't.
"It's time to go," a Clansmen said.
Vert didn't say anything. Though, Dice knew U.R.O's backup had already arrived. Another second wasted was the difference between death and freedom. That is, if there was a difference.
However, Dice's eyes remained on Wrench. His head pounded.
"Here," Matches said.

There was a gruff scrape. Matches held a gun in her hands. Cautiously, she placed it over Wrench's face. Dice scanned it over. The gun hardly covered Wrench and was studded with cruel scrapes and gouges.
It was perfect.
"Goodbye, stranger," Dice said, standing up.
He followed Vert to the aircraft. His feet were lead. Something tugged at him. The air burned his nostrils with an oily stench.
"No need to say goodbye just yet," Matches said. "Wrench still has one more round of spines in him."
Dice nodded.

The aircraft was only a meter away as Dice passed Knowles. Knowles was laid on the ground, moaning. His metal leg had been detached, and his flesh leg shot off. Dice foamed at the mouth. Wrench was dead. But, Knowles? He'd inevitably be wheeled into a government medical room, to be patched back into pristine condition.
Walking up the aircraft's ramp, Dice went nauseous.
"I'm sorry," Knowles said. "This wasn't supposed to happen. I didn't mean to kill him. I thought that he was... Matches..."
Vert motioned for Dice to keep walking. There was a blast near the aircraft's nose. Pressure rose. However, Dice couldn't resist the urge to look back.
"An accident?" Dice said.
"I meant to shoot Matches," Knowles said. "I thought that Wrench was Matches. I swear."
"Wouldn't have made any difference."
"No... You don't understand. It wouldn't have mattered if I'd hit Matches."
Dice bit his lip. "It didn't matter when you hit me either, did it? Face it, Knowles: nobody matters to you."
"I know you… Your past... You think you're so clean? So innocent? I know better! You have the blood of thousands on your hands! And, you're going to spill blood again! It's inevitable!"
Dice paused. What did Knowles know? What dirt did he have. He shook his head. He knew nothing. He was just a desperate man, trying to throw Dice off his edge.
Sneering, Dice walked off.
People poured out of the aircraft's every pore. If not people, it was weedy pipes and leaking puffs of steam. Dice and Matches took a seat along iron bars built into the aircraft's ceiling.
What had Wrench's last thoughts been? Had he wanted them to keep moving to their goal? Did he care? Had he known just how much of a sacrifice he'd made?
Dice listened in on the purr of the engine. He peered out the window. The aircraft seemed to tuck and dip at each sound the engine made.
The sound grew. Turned unruly. Dice tightened his grip around his bar as the aircraft swung through air. An orb of light glared ahead of them, before bursting into sparks.
They were still being pursued.

Their aircraft weaved between skyscrapers and flew over buildings. Dice watched as surges of electricity leapt from the lip of their aircraft, picking away at the U.R.O's numbers. Finally, Vert walked from his place at the front of the plane, joining Matches and Dice.

"EMPs," he said, with a grin. "The U.R.O is too afraid to use them around civilian population. But, we don't play by the same rules as the U.RO... Anyway, no need to worry now. You're in good hands. Our Clansmen pilots are the best there are. Especially our current pilot. He's been observing U.R.O crafts for years. He actually coded their interfaces, before defecting and joining us."
Vert stared, awaiting a reaction. He flashed another grin and cleared his throat.

"All of the aircrafts are piloted by artificial intelligence," Vert said. "Normally, that would be an advantage. However, there have been several flaws deliberately placed in their programming. All that it takes is exploiting those flaws, and then hitting them with an electrical impulse — it takes them down every time."
Vert fell forward as the aircraft tremored.
"Yes!" he said with a cheer. "The last aircraft!"
Vert hung a hand in the air. Dice hung his eyes.
"Look," Vert said. "We're flying over the crown jewel of the U.R.O! Aren't the buildings just magnificent?"
Dice studied his palm. It was covered in bruises and cuts. How long had they been there?
"So..." Vert said. "That Wrench guy really must've mattered to you guys, didn't he? How long did you know him?"
"About a week, but it felt like I knew him for years..." Dice said. He looked up. "Hey, is there any way that this plane can go faster from the base?"

"Already going top speed," Vert said. He rested on a knee. "You know, I thought that he had a lot of potential. He was real tough. You could see that on his face. I wanted to recruit him for the Clan if we escaped. To be honest, I don't think that we could've escaped without him..."
"I think we still could've healed him from his injuries," Dice said. "He didn't need to die."
Vert's lips pursed, and he took a step back.
"Yes... Well..." Vert said. "Our medical team isn't the best. Besides: I don't think that even the best medics would've been able to save Wrench."
Vert looked into Dice's eyes. Dice looked away.

"Well, if either of you are interested in becoming official members of the Clan, just ask," Vert said, edging back toward the front of the jet. "I'll leave you two alone now. I think that you've earned that much."
Dice readjusted his position on the bar but felt nothing. Everything was numb. It left him with an uncanny feeling, as though he were missing a limb.
Matches patted Dice on the back and gave a weak smile.
"You want to play cards?" Matches asked. She pulled a box of cards out of her pocket. "I bet that I can beat you."
"I wouldn't bet on anything," Dice said, cracking his knuckles.
"Alright then... Let's play spines."
Dice's eyes widened.
"Maybe you can make a bet, after all. Deal them out."
Matches did. When she was done, there was a pile of random cards sitting at the center, a deck of cards in both Dice and Matches' hands, and a third deck of cards across from them... Abandoned.
Dice and Matches played quietly, diverting their eyes from the third deck as long as they could.
Chapter 23:

Dice slid off his bar. He stretched his arms out and winced. His back was killing him. His head throbbed and his stomach lurched. As he stepped over people, a jet of steam blasted into his face. Coughing, Dice covered his mouth and nose. It had been too long since he'd last breathed clean air. The aircraft's height didn't help matters. The world was a swirling blur.
"You notice that the engine was stalling out too?" Matches asked, from her spot on the bar.
Dice's heart skipped a beat. "What?"
Matches smirked, sheepishly.
"It's probably nothing," she said.

Dice pressed his ear along the wall, honing on the putter of the engine. It sounded unusually weak. Though, was that just part of this aircraft's design? Was he being overly paranoid? Or, was it a sign? If only he'd monitored the engine during liftoff, to compare.
Dice pinched himself. He was slipping. They were flying in a glorified cage, riding with a group of people they didn't know, headed to potentially anywhere.
He needed to talk to Vert.
"Hey! Watch it!" somebody shouted.
Dice's foot recoiled from somebody's hand. He measured his next steps more carefully, only to stumble over three more people.
"Sorry! I'm very sorry!"
Regaining his balance, Dice gripped to the ceiling's iron bars. The aircraft shuddered. Dice's grip faltered and he hit the ground.
"A hero... and a hopeless klutz."
A hand clasped around his shoulder. Dice looked up. It was Vert.
"Thanks for coming over here," Dice said. "If I'd gone any further, I probably would've broken something."
"And I wouldn't have been able to do anything, because my medical team is garbage."
Vert chuckled, but there was a strain around his eyes. Dice looked around the aircraft. How many Clansmen were there?
How many had died from Omicron?
"Anyway, it was no problem Slice-and-Dice, really," Vert said, "I was already headed back here."

Dice scratched the back of his neck. "Oh. Well, in that case, I hope it wouldn't be any trouble if I talked to you about... See if... Could I ask you a question?" He gestured to the walls. "A question about all of this."
Vert nodded, his lips curling upward.
"Of course. I'm the guy with all the answers. I just have something quick I need to do — it'll only be a moment."

He raised a finger and cleared his throat. "Everybody, brace yourselves. We've just flown over the Mortimer District — the last district with 'human preservation' statutes. The Tyler District isn't far off. When we land we'll rendezvous with the Clan Chairwoman, Jackie Pierce, and the remaining members of the Clan. As you all know, we have to make a good impression there to pull our 'rebirth' off, so make sure to be on your best behavior."
Vert turned to Dice.
"Alright, fire away. What did you need to ask me?"
Dice's eyes were locked on the nose of the craft. The clouds rose past it, fading out of view. The craft was making its descent.
"I think you answered everything," Dice said, voice feeble.
"Great!" Vert said.
There was a warm, genial atmosphere about Vert. He carried it in his eyes. His shoulders. It reassured Dice, telling him there was a method to the madness.
Vert stepped onto a makeshift platform of loose pipes.
"If anybody has any questions, the best time to ask them is now," Vert said. "If not, we'll begin initiating our landing party."
Everybody was silent. Vert opened his mouth, preparing to move on.
"How many of us are there going to be at the Tyler District?" somebody asked.
Vert readjusted the collar of his shirt.
"Good question, yawn Manon," Vert said. "There are... A few other aircraft that made it out of the U.R.O base with us."
"That a good thing, or a bad thing?"

"Look at you — adept as ever. Asking all the big questions. Uh — I applaud the dent that we made in Omicron, but... I'd say that it was... Is there a more impressive word for 'failure'? Let me level with you: many Clansmen died. We're among the few who made it out alive. And, while I can't be sure on exact numbers, we seem to be the largest survivor group. Things aren't exactly where we want them to be."
A series of mutterings emerged. There was a clang as somebody kicked a wall. Several people raised their guns.

"Hey! Settle down! What we're not going to do is shrink our numbers even more!" Vert said, pushing a an unruly Clansmen away. "Look: I realize we're not in the most encouraging of circumstances. It's the exact opposite of... That. However, we need to keep our morale. We're the Clan. We just attacked Omicron and made it out alive! You can't go bigger than that! Nothing can stop us from fulfilling our goal!"
There was a series of cheers. Vert beamed.

"We're the premier surviving unit from Omicron," Vert continued. "I'm proud of you all. These announcements of mine? They're just to keep us on our toes. We have all sorts of people tailing us. People who have taken many of our fellow Clansmen. It's the little things that determine success or failure, comrades!"
Vert gave a firm nod and left for the cockpit. Dice scanned for Matches, before following after Vert. Matches would show back up, eventually.
"Slow the thrusters, but don't disable them entirely," Vert commanded. "We're already three times beyond recommended carrying capacity. We need to land this puppy smoothly."
Dice cleared his throat.
"As it turns out, I still have a few questions for you, Vert," Dice said.
Vert raised his hand at Dice and ran through a list of orders to a pilot. Finally, Vert turned back to stare Dice in the face.
"Alright, what do you want?" Vert asked.
Dice's throat went dry.

"I was just wondering what this stop at the Tyler District is all about," Dice said. "Weren't we supposed to be headed to the border of the Kelvin Union? To be honest, I have no idea what's going on. I and Matches are so lost."
Vert chuckled, and slapped Dice on the back. Rubbing where he'd been slapped, Dice grimaced.

"The Tyler District is a strong trading port," Vert said. "And, it has low monitoring by the U.R.O, so it makes the perfect place for outlaws like us to refuel, hang low for a while, and form strategies..."
"A while? How long will we be docked there?"
"Sometime between not-much-time and all-the-time," Vert asked. "Why? You got someplace to go?"
Dice nodded. "I'm hoping to get to the other side of the border. I need to get to the Kelvin Union."
Vert smiled.
"You're on the right ship then," he said. "Trust me: we'll get there. Maybe..."
Vert rubbed his hands, before shoving them in his pockets.

"To be honest with you, the Clan is pretty damn screwed. We've wanted to stay in the U.R.O and revive it. Bring it back to its former glory. But, we just can't. The U.R.O knows who we are, and they know how to infiltrate us. Waiting out in the Kelvin Union until things shift is our last hope — if we're not caught first."
Dice raised an eyebrow.
"What do you mean by 'waiting it out' and 'reviving the U.R.O'? I know there are problems, but... It's not really governmental, so much as it's public unrest."
Vert let out a harsh laugh.

"You really believe that, don't you?" he said, piercing Dice's eye. "I'm glad you're curious, but trust me... There are things you don't know about the U.R.O. They aren't perfect, even if they used to be. Don't worry though: I'll try keeping you and Matches under my wing in the Tyler District. Show you the dirty underbelly. You haven't seen the chinks in the U.R.O's armor yet? Look a little harder. They're there."
As Dice went to retort, Vert put his hand over Dice's mouth.

"Listen to me: people walk the streets with no radials to their names. Robotic diseases are rampant. Real disease? Same thing. The economy has collapsed. We've lapsed into a secret war with the Kelvin Union. Robots are phasing us out. Like it or not, the U.R.O needs to be cleansed. I can only hope the day is coming soon."
Dice pretended to hear Vert. Then, he gave a firm handshake and returned to the back of the aircraft.
Everything Vert had said simply didn't compute. The U.R.O Dice knew wasn't as bleak as Vert made it out to be. It couldn't have been. Could it have?
Dice thought back to his time in the Monterey District. He thought back to Haynam's death. Wrench's death. He thought of the forlorn look on Professor Cassius' face.
His thoughts tunneled back to his nightmares. Being trapped in a claustrophobic room, struggling for air. Struggling for a way out. He shuddered.
"Everybody hang on tight!" Vert shouted from the cockpit.

The aircraft dipped. Dice's stomach turned to stone. He crumbled into somebody, then hit the ground. Shock seared through him and his body quaked as he tried lifting himself. He gripped onto a railing and steadied back onto his feet. He looked around — everybody else was already strapped down or hanging to a bar.
"Keep calm, everybody," Vert said. "We're in the middle of a somewhat rough descent. That's all."
Dice turned up his hearing aid and wasn't convinced. He could hear the engine grinding against itself. His eyes flitted from the window, and then to the floor. He couldn't watch.
"There you are!"
Stumbling over several people, Matches made her way to Dice's dismal spot. A few disgruntled shouts and snorts were left in Matches' wake, but Matches didn't stop to apologize.
"There weren't many places I could've gone," Dice said, teeth chattering. "I thought you knew I was going to talk to Vert."
"How? You didn't say anything."
"And I couldn't see you anywhere after I'd left, so I guess we're even," Dice retorted, stiffly.
"Uh... Alright then? Anyway, what did Vert have to say? Did you learn anything new?"
"I don't know... Have you been using your mental-abilities to learn anything new?"

Matches shrugged. "No. Not going to do that again unless I need to, after going into your —." She stopped and took in a deep breath.  "They really need to add a new scent to this aircraft. It smells like melted iron, sweat, and death... with a hint of cinnamon. Didn't realize that there could be all four at once. In other news, I managed to get in touch with a few of the members of this Clan. Very interesting people, with a very interesting set of ideologies. This one person that I was talking to told me—."
"Quiet."
The hum of the engine stalled out. The floor let go of Dice's feet. His throat swelled. A dozen toothpicks pricked at the tips of his fingers.
Dice's feet slammed back on the floor as the engine slammed on.
"Sorry," Vert shouted. "Just a momentary hiccup in the engine. Nothing to be worried about."
Pressure nestled under Dice's scalp. Stars shone in the borders of his vision. Vert's words were worth nothing.
"If it's any consolidation, we're only about a minute away from the landing strip. Brace for impact, and wish our pilots luck."
That was worth something — if only he believed in luck.

Dice's bones rattled, turning his marrow to mash. Screams slashed at the air, shorting out the lights. Dice's lungs swelled again. This time, with smoke and steam. Dice clenched his teeth. The feeling of weightlessness could return at any moment.
The engine fell away. The floor remained in place.
"What the hell just happened?" somebody said.
"If we're placing bets, I think we died," Matches said.
Nervous chatters erupted, then cooled as Vert's voice washed through.
"We've landed," Vert said. A slight tremble was in his voice. "Just— just stay calm while we try to repair things."

A smack resounded as somebody landed a punch on a fellow Clansman. The attacker was swiftly tackled by several others, but this only prompted a new series of punching and kicking. Dice shrunk back and lowered his head.
The entire aircraft was preparing to implode when the lights flickered back on. The aircraft's ramp chattered, then lowered. Clamoring, the crowd rushed out. Dice squinted and counted the first wave.
Thirty-five and a half people — somebody had been trampled when halfway out the door.
The rush subsided. Dice continued to watch the spectacle. Matches stayed at his side, shaking her head.
"How much you want bet it's no better out there than it is in here?" Matches said. "Ah well... I suppose that nothing can be worse than being slammed against a wall in a sardine can, can it?"
Dice gave Matches a glare.
"You're right," Matches said, "with our odds, there's hardly a chance that things get better from here.
"You took the words right out of my mind..."
Vert and his comrades made their way out. Dice pushed Matches aside, and limped after them.

Dice soaked in the dazzling rays of sunlight. They'd landed in a cramped, fenced-in hangar — if it could've been called a "landing". The nose of their aircraft was smashed inward, its wings were bent, and its U.R.O seals were torn off entirely.
"We've arrived at the Tyler District!" Vert said to the Clansmen.
They ignored him, continuing to shoved past each other and claw for a way of escape.
"In its full glory, no less..." Matches said.
"I was wrong — it's at least better than being in the aircraft," Dice said.
Matches smirked. "But the aircraft is empty now."
Shrieking, a cluster of Clansmen fled from the fence. A charred body laid at its edge. Bolts of electricity flew from the fence's tips.
Vert pushed through the crowd of Clansmen, making his way to the fence. Webs of energy glowered over him, but Vert's eyes were resolute.
"Let us in," Vert ordered. "We're a Clan ship."
There was no response.
"This is head-coordinator of the Clan, Vert Salus. If you don't open your doors, I'll take this to our Clan Chairwoman."

The aircraft pad lowered, taking the crashed aircraft out of sight. A low grunt emerged from the other side of the fence. The fence's electricity dissipated, a section of the fence opening in front of Vert.
"Open sesame!" Vert said. He turned, motioning at the Clan. "Alright people, we need to get going. Matches. Dice. You stay with me."
"What are they doing with the plane?" Matches asked.
"Storing it in a temporary garage, until they can get a robot to fly it to one of the main hangar towers," Vert said. "If they can get it to fly, that is..."
"You get valet parking here?"
"Almost. Except here, the valet is free."

Dice and Matches kept close behind Vert as they exited the hangar. Dice soon wished he'd stayed at the back. Everybody was clamoring to get ahead, and Dice's heartrate rose as people pushed past him. He'd weaved through many rushing crowds. He'd never seen one as mad as this.

It didn't help that the hangar led into a narrow alleyway, built of fastened iron. Dice coughed and tried wafting away clouds of dust. Glancing at streaks of rust on the walls, Dice questioned the age of the Tyler District. For a place of such supposed commerce, it should've been pristine.

Dice's eyes raised to the sky. Rows of slums towered over them and littered the skyline. Each one was a papier-mâché of compacted trash and scrap metal, welded into makeshift boxes. There were hundreds of them, all crammed into random clumps. Dice marveled at the chaos of it all.

Their alleyway fed into a pocket of rooftops, walled in by more rows of slums. Ruffle metal bowed and crackled beneath his feet. Yet, swaths of people surrounded him, streaming from neighboring alleyways and toward flimsy trade stands built into the roofs.
The Tyler District was a festering mess. What if the Clan splintered apart, among the crowd? What if he lost track of the Clan?
A man in rags yanked at Dice. As Dice ripped his arm away, there was a sharp tear. Dice looked at his arm to find a fresh hole in his bodysuit — only one among many.
"Hey, out of the way!"

Dice was shunted by a group of people. Stepping out of their path, he snorted. The place was busier than even the underground of the Gordon District had been. Eyeing the vendors, Dice found one selling illegal guns. Another was selling what looked to be a stockpile of stimulators. Yet another was selling makeshift bionic enhancements.
Dice looked back down the alleyway he'd entered through. Maybe he should've headed back.
"Hey, look at that," Matches said, coming at Dice's side. "They're selling age extensions here. Maybe I should try one of those."

Vert chuckled. How could he possibly chuckle? There was pile after pile of unregulated, illegal technology. Anybody could take it. Who was to stop it from getting into the wrong hands? Where was the U.R.O?
Vert stopped in front of them and glanced at his wrist-pad. After smacking it a few times, he turned to embrace his Clansmen.

"I'm sure you're all enjoying yourselves in this marketplace," said Vert. "And I have a special meeting with Jackie Pierce, and the other head-coordinators. We'll reunite to begin our 'rebirth' in the coming hours. In the meantime, have fun and explore — just keep checking your wrist communicators, and you should be fine."
The group scattered, their prattle scattering with them.
"Matches? Dice? You stay with me."

Vert started walking. Dice trailed behind, but his eyes fell astray to a towering slum in the horizon. It stretched far above the rest, nearly scraping the clouds. It was crude, and unnatural. Yet, it felt so right.
"This has to be one of the strangest places that I've seen," Dice said, gesturing toward the buildings.
Matches chuckled.
"You say that at every district we go to," she said. "Haven't been that far outside of the Monterey District, have you?"
"Nobody that lives in the Monterey District strays too far from the Monterey District. Not usually, anyway... The place is big enough as it is."
"Can't argue there."

Dice rubbed his nose. For a moment, he thought that he could smell the smoke of the calculator cage. The burning, lemony scent of the MDPD. In the corner of his eye, there was a glare — just like the one he'd used to see over the old computing center. While he didn't want to admit it, some part of himself missed the Monterey District. He'd never made any friends there, but it had been a friend to him. Family, even. Now it was gone.
"Tongue tied?" Matches asked, after Dice had taken a prolonged pause.
Dice shook his head.

"No, just thinking," he said. "Look at those slums up there. They're pretty shabby, even if I've seen shabbier looking places at this point... But it's also beautiful, isn't it? The fact that people were able to build wherever, whenever needed? Create their own world, to their liking?"
Matches opened her mouth to speak. Though, as she followed Dice's gaze and studied the slums, her mouth closed. Finally, Vert gave a laugh.

"If it seems complex, it's because it was designed by robots," Vert said. "The whole damn place is. That's why it isn't terribly efficient for us, and why there are so many winding passageways throughout it."
Dice's eyes widened. The intricacies of the design all made sense now. Yet — it made no sense. It had been created by an intelligence far beyond his own.

Vert led them into another alleyway. Jagged spikes fed throughout it, and its ceiling was only a few inches above Dice's head. Yet, Dice found a sort of security in it. Only one direction in, and one direction out.
"Ouch," Matches said, pulling her foot from one of the spikes. "What were the designers thinking? Did they want to kill my feet?"
Vert shook his head.

"Power tracks," Vert said. "They easily reenergize robots that drive over them and make for easy transportation. In addition, they also make a nice blockade between the domain of humans, and the domain of robots."

Matches smirked. Vert returned it with a grim look. As they continued, Vert's posture slumped, and his head darted back and forth. Dice surveyed the area for what Vert may have been afraid of. Though, the alleyway was empty.

They reached the end of the alleyway and entered another pocket. It was less than half the size of the one that they'd left. Though, it was far more streamlined. The ground was a sturdy concrete and crowded with winding towers. Slums were absent, replaced by compact, interlocking tower structures. As Dice studied the towers, he found they turned to a winding maze of metal coves. He squinted as their lights glared.
"Really could've used a pair of Wrench's special goggles," Matches said.
Dice went to nod, but the muscles in his neck stiffened at Wrench's name. He rubbed his eyes and directed them toward the ground.
There was a thrum. Dice jumped out of the way, while a blur whipped past him. A robot. It was gone before Dice could even determine its engine.

The robot was followed by a swarm. Dice shielded his face. There'd been no need. The robots flew ound Dice with ease, their movements so seamless it were as if he wasn't there. Eyes straining to find focus, Dice gleaned as much as he could. His forehead matted. None of the robots matched the specialized machinations he'd seen Monterey District. Rather, they had minimalistic designs, only possessing wheels, limbs, boosters, and high-grade quantum processors. Dice ogled at one of the processors — it couldn't have been any lower than the tenth grade.
"I've never seen so many robots in one place," he said, with a mix of wonder and disgust.

As Dice moved forward, there wasn't a centimeter of wasted space. Robots roved all over, trading, scanning, building, and computing. An envy rose in Dice's chest as he struggled to keep up. It had been too long since he'd tested his mettle against an A.I system, let alone one that was up-to-date. What if he was hilariously behind?
Vert shot a knowing smile back at Dice.
"Agreed, Slice-and-Dice," Vert said, with a pant. "It almost feels like there are far too many, doesn't it?"
Dice passed an assembly line of robots. They all worked in sync, developing some sort of super-generator. They weren't just efficient. They were scarily efficient.
Vert led them up a structure's spiral stairwell. As they ascended, Dice fought to hold in the acid filling his throat.

"The Tyler District: a city built by robots, for robots," Vert said. "Only a hop and a skip away from Omicron, at that. How? A few years back, the robots managed to repeal 'human preservation' statutes. You might like to think that cities like this are sparse. Though, you'd be wrong. They're everywhere in this part of the U.R.O, and they're only spreading."
Dice leaned against the winding wall, his eyes closed. He tried directing his thoughts away from a growing breeze. From the fact of how far away from home he really was.
"It is a beauty though, isn't it?" Dice said. "The fact that they were able to design everything to be so complex? I can only imagine how this culture works. It's fast — even for me."
Vert scoffed.
