Dice stumbled into a pitch-dark room. The robot and the man entered after. There was a creak as the robot lifted the wall, sealing them in.
"What are the android's vitals?" the man asked.
"Low," said the robot. "It has taken critical damage. Its quantum processor is half burned, and I can already tell that It's running on fumes. It's draining energy."
"Brilliant," the man said.

He slammed a wall, and the room flickered a pale green. Dice's eyes surveyed it. On one wall were makeshift beds. On another wall was an old generator. In a corner was a food storage unit and a pile of various tools. The room was in a state of disrepair, its plaster peeling away, cracks riding between several walls, and the ceiling slumping.
The robot pushed past Dice, setting Matches on the ground. Dice rushed toward Matches. He put his hand on her face, burning it as he did. He didn't care. Life was already seeping from Matches' eyes.
"Is she going to be okay?" Dice asked.
"We have devices that should be able to fix him," the man said.
"You didn't answer my question!" Dice said. "There are more of you, right? There have to be more of you!"
The man snorted, and then shoved Dice out of the way.
"Sorry, but no," he said. "It's just us, in the middle of a wasteland. You were hoping for better than that? Tough luck."
He tossed a metal object to the robot.
"L-9," the man said. "Will that quantum processor work?"
L-9 shook its head.
"It's not the right one, Roy. I need the smaller one — the older model."
"Shit," said Roy. "I think that I had that one compacted in trade for energy, about a week ago."
He scrambled to the back corner of the room and fumbled through his parts. Matches body throttled, and L-9 was struggled to hold her down.
"What's happening to her?" Dice asked. "What are you two doing!?"
L-9 didn't respond.
"Will this work?" Roy said, tossing a slimmer chunk of metal. L-9 looked studied carefully, before shaking its head.
"No," said L-9. "This one might fry her systems."
"Well, that's the last one," said Roy. "Take it or leave it."
The digital eyes on its display screen flitted to Matches' face.
"I can't," it said, shaking its head. "It's too risky."
"Is there at least a chance that it might work?" Dice asked, with a rasp.
"Sure, there's a chance... But, like I said, it's not worth the risk."
"Well, we don't have any other options, now do we?"
Dice snatched the processor from L-9's hands. Tearing the old processor out, he placed the new one inside Matches. There was a click. A ragged rumble.
The rumble lulled to a steady vibration.
"That had to be the worst sleep of my life..."
Matches pulled herself from the ground and looked up at Dice. A warmth filled his chest.
"Anyway, where the hell are we?" Matches asked.
"I have no cl—."
There was a roar. An explosion. Dice closed his eyes. It wasn't real. It couldn't be.
Dice pried his eyes open. Matches writhed on the ground, an even bigger hole in her chest than before. Her eyes were wide with shock. Her mouth hung wide open.
Dice shoved Roy and L-9.
"Get out of my way!" Dice said.
He knelt and put his hand back to Matches' forehead. The heat had left. It was just... Cold.
"No... No, no, no, no..."
He put his hand on Matches' wrist. There was only a flicker of movement.
"Matches?"
No response.
"Matches, are you still with me?"
Matches rolled her head toward Dice. Dice felt a sputter of relief. It faded as the look of death gripped around Matches' face.
"I guess this had to happen to one of us at some point, right?" Matches said.
Dice shook his head. His eyes burned. "We came so close..."
Matches smiled.
"No, not close... We made it."
Dice's face stung as tears blended with the blood streaming down his face. He tried wiping it away, only to make the stinging worse.
"I feel tired," said Matches, closing her eyes. "I'm ready to go back to sleep."
"Matches, are you still with me?"
Dice scrunched his face, trying to hold in the tears. He could feel his nose going red, and his skin blotchy.
Matches reopened her eyes.
They were vacant. Matches' jaw slackened. Her face froze. Her skin turned hard as metal.
Somebody put their hand on Dice's shoulder.
"It's alright."
It was Roy.
Dice let out a stream of tears.
"It's never going to be alright."
Dice noticed how muggy the room was. How frail its structure was. Yet, as he looked into Roy's face, he found comfort. He turned to L-9. It was in its face too.

Even as Roy and L-9 came closer, Dice didn't leave Matches' side. The pain didn't leave Dice's body. The tears didn't leave his eyes. Yet, the comfort didn't leave either. As Dice stared down Matches' vacant eyes, he remembered the first time he'd seen them — the way they'd shone through the darkness. Even in their current emptiness, there was a hint of life.
There was a meaning. There was a purpose. He just had to look harder.
End

title: Asleep at the Wheel
paragraphs: By Christian Mueth
"You sure can run your mouth, but your mind isn't running with it... My answer is no."
"No? This is a once in a lifetime opportunity! You can't just—."
"Just stop for a damn minute and listen to yourself. You want me to save my business... By running it into the ground?"
"By running it underground. There's a difference."
"Like hell there is."
"Trust me. It's genius! You'll be the first restaurant in town to operate underground. It'll be the hot new trend!"
"Yeah... Sure... And how much exactly do you want me to spend on this 'brilliant' venture?"

"That's honestly up to you. And, uh... Well, also up to me, I guess, since that's what you're paying me for. The cost won't be much. You just need to buy a nice piece of property. Drill in it, then grill in it. Brilliant."
"I didn't spend twenty years building up my business, just to end up back in a basement."
"And, I didn’t spend twenty in real estate to end up — seeing you pass up this offer."
"Get real. What offer? Unless you have a viable piece of land to give me, your advice is utter shit."

"You have guts, Smith. Talking to me like that... Whatever. I'm eyeing a few prime locations, as a matter of fact. I'll — I'll get the list to you, by tomorrow. But, you shouldn't have to spend more than fifty grand."
"Fifty grand? That's... That's better than the hundred that I was planning on shelling out...”
"It is."
"You promise that you can keep your promise?"
"Of course. Why wouldn't I?"
"Promise?"
"Promise," I said.
More is better. Meet your quota, and never say no. That's how you go pro.
At least, that's the mantra I've always stuck by. Kind of the general knowledge of the real-estate industry. Never been sure how true my mantra is, though. I've never been that smart of a guy.
I wiped a bead of sweat from my forehead and rolled over in my bed, pressing my face into my pillow. I let out a moan. Why had I promised I could get that deal? Why had I been so stupid?
I banished the memory.

The night's frigid hands clutched me, then burrowed under my skin. My feet went numb. I drew my blanket closer to my chest, shivering. Another day, another missed electricity bill, and another night without electricity.
Ticking rapped at my ears. It scraped away at the drums. My eyes darted to another set of hands, resting on my bedside — the hands of my watch. I squinted.
"1:30," I slurred.
My eyes slanted, begging for rest. My eyelids stayed open. I was halfway through the night and not a wink of sleep had come to meet me. I rubbed my hands together and gave them a hot breath.
Several years ago, I'd watched a documentary about people in the arctic, who'd lived in igloos all their lives. I could never be one of those people.
Sitting up, I dangled the watch — watched as the seconds rolled away. Soon enough, it'd be 6:00. I just had to keep waiting.

I snorted. "Keep waiting". That's what I'd been telling myself for the past month. Some good that'd been. Weeks of begging people to make deals, dishonesty, and downright desperation, all for nothing. I'd worn myself ragged, but still wasn't any closer to getting warmer.

What was I supposed to do if I couldn't get this deal to go through? Hell, what if I couldn't find a place to sell? It wasn't like I could just go back to my old place. There weren't many other places to go, either...
Did the local post-office still need a new secretary? Maybe I could make that work.

As the watch swung, I caught a glimpse of my reflection. It was a warped image — bleary-eyed, and disheveled. Half-dead. It couldn't have been me. It looked nothing like me. I turned away. It had to have been me.

I chuckled. In my efforts to get people property, I was on the verge of losing my own. In trying to make a name for myself, I'd lost all credibility. Irony has a way of ironing one out. Yet, I had no other choice but to forge forward.

There was a crunch. My thumb and forefinger spasmed. Something wrapped around them — tightened. Heart skipping a beat, my eyes skimmed back to the watch. My brow furrowed. The watch's leather strap was furling inward. Jumping backward in my bed, I felt my blanket wrap around me and smother my chest. I yanked at the blanket, only for it to firm its grip. There was another crunch. My eyes snapped back to my watch — yet, it’d disappeared. In its place were series of interlocking wheels, hanging from my hand. They churned into one another, in an eerie caw. My stomach turning to a pretzel, I writhed against my blanket. After I finally thrust it away, it shifted in midair. Its ends fed into themselves, it turned to a wheel of cloth. The cloth shed away, only a metal wheel remaining.

I leapt from my bed and tore at the wheels clenching my hand. Though, the wheels’ teeth only sunk deeper and expanded. The tip of my finger corroded, exposing an interlocking series of wheels beneath. With a gulp, I stumbled toward the cold gleam of my door’s silver knob. This didn't make sense. My vision must've been pulling a trick on me. Perhaps I'd gone too long without food — without sleep.

I wasn't able to linger on these thoughts for long. As my hand neared the doorknob, its silver sheen deteriorated to another series of wheels. The wheels then spread to the door. They spread to the floor. Their countless spokes taunted me and their axles bore into my soul like staring eyes.

I ran my hands through my hair. I winced. The wheels along my left hand crept into my hair, tugging at it. I tore them away, taking clumps of hair with it. A rock dropped through my chest. My hand burned, as though a hot iron were pressed to it. Worse, my fingers morphed to a set of interlocking wheels and mechanisms. My eyes widened as the mechanisms migrated inward, invading my palm.

There was a squeal. My eyes shot down. The floor turned to sheets of iron, and steadily peeled away to a bottomless chasm of spokes. Turning on my heel, I sped toward my bed. My eyes ricocheted around the room. Where was my bed? My television? My coffee table? At the very least, I needed my power-blender. Though, I only found husks of wheels spilling on the ground. They rolled toward me. My eyes rolled away and I ran after them. My chest coiled. The spokes drew nearer, coming ever closer to encircling me.

My foot snagged something, knocking me to the ground. With a moan, I looked behind. An arm of wheels reared from the floor, before clasping my leg. I kicked at it. I clawed. I tried to crawl away. Yet, my left hand was useless, and my right hand floundered aimlessly. The ground buckled, further bending into the chasm. With a sigh, I surrendered. The arm released me, and I rolled into the blackness. Making my plummet, my gut raised to my throat and sent twinges of pain down my sides. Emptiness enveloped me. Wheels jabbed at my back. I looked up, back to the patch of light I'd fallen from. It shrunk as it raised away. Or, was I dropping further?

I hit the ground. Or, at least, something like it. Wheels seemed to cackle as they clacked against my back. I tried to roll from my stomach and sit up. However, at each move, I was met by more wheels. They twisted my skin and pushed against my bones. I tucked my head in submission, letting the wheels carry my deeper into the dark.
“It’s pretty isn’t it?”

There were chirps. Scents of freshly cut grass and smoke wafted to my nose. I shuddered. Our massive yard had recently been preened, and a bonfire lapped at the center of it. I leaned toward it, outstretching my stick. Somebody slapped the back of my hand and pulled it back. I looked — it was my father.
"Hey! Keep your distance. Remember what I said earlier? You can't just rush into things, like that," he said. His voice smoothed. "Patience. You were too close."

A wall of wheels opened ahead of me, followed by beams of light. The wheels beneath my spine moved faster. Harsher. Their axles grinded and popped. Joints popped. I gasped. They were my joints. Drawing closer to the light, I gained a better view of my surroundings. I was in a tight shaft, being pulled along a conveyor of wheels.

The wheels continued ramping up their speed. My muscles tensed and heartrate raised. I shot from the conveyor, and into the light —into the night. Wind rushed under me, carrying me forward. The stars winked by, as a blur.
I landed on pavement, with a crunch.
"Ow," I muttered.

Though, I strangely felt no pain. I felt nothing. I attempted to pull myself up, only to slide back to the ground. Rolling to my back, I glanced at my left side. A cluster of wheels had overtaken my forearm and climbed deeper. I suppressed a gag and used my right arm to pull myself up. I flicked away clumps of dirt from my shirt. They’d been morphing into wheels. I looked behind — my apartment building had disappeared. In its place was a sprawling web of gears and wheels. Looking down the street, I only found more wheeled buildings. Hairs along my right arm pricked up. A howl of wind rushed past. My ratty t-shirt and sweat-shorts nearly blew off. If only I'd dressed warmer.

Trying to ignore the lumbering numbness in my left arm, I made my way down the sidewalk. Peering along it, I was struck by overwhelming barrenness. Was there any other soul out there, seeing this? Was I the sole sufferer? My eyes retreated to the clouds, hoping to find a plane or helicopter arcing across the sky. Though, I was met by a swirling mess of clouds, wheeling into one another. I squinted — the stars seemed to be swirling as well. Breaths becoming leaden, I broke into a sprint. My eyes jumped from building to building, searching for one that was unscathed. There had to be a place of refuge somewhere.
I stopped when an owl fluttered in front of me and gave a hoot. My heart skipped a beat. I peered into its glassy eyes. I could count the reflections of a dozen stars within them.

The owl flinched, then peered into me. I was frozen. Once its gaze slit a pang in my heart, its head spun, all the way around. A chill ran down my spine and the owl gave another hoot. Its head made another turn. As it did, its neck stretched upward. It twisted and contorted. Finally, it unlatched from the neck and rolled to the ground. Its eyes shattered, turning to wheels. The feathers shed to the ground, then did likewise. I backed away. I needed to escape. I needed to forget. Though, I could feel myself being dragged back to the wells of my memory.
"Stay quiet. Stay careful. Stay vigilant."

I was in the woods of my parent's old property, at my father's side. He held a hunting rifle in hand, while I was armed with a BB gun. We were after a wild bobcat, in the dead of night. My father cautioned it was close by, and to keep my eyes wary.
"And, don't shoot unless I do first. Patience is key."
There was a rustling among the trees. A purr. A blast of sulfur. I followed suit, pulling my own trigger. Yet, to no results.
"Dammit. Almost had him..." my father said. "If only we'd been faster."
There was another rustle. A shout. My eyes jumped to the trees. Without second thought, I fingered my trigger.
"Owen, stop!"
It was too late. A cold thump hit the ground. I stalked forward, then became sick. I'd shot down an animal — but it was a bird.
"An owl," my father said, with a moan. "Owen, you killed an owl. Why didn't you listen to me?"
"But, I did. You shot first."
My father shook his head, and pulled my gun from my hands.
"You weren't patient. You weren't quiet. And you certainly weren't careful. Why didn't you just listen?"
Why hadn't I listened?

I let out a yelp. The owl had decayed to a churning lump, and its wheels rode up my calves. Breaking into a run, I tried shaking the wheels from my legs. A grimace mapped my face as they pinched my skin. Clinks resounded as some fell on the concrete, but many remained.

A ringing broke through my ears and I skidded to a halt. A slab of pavement ahead contorted and its corners softened. After a few seconds, it'd turned to a wheel, and I'd turned in the other direction. The lump of the owl’s wheels were still roving toward me. I bounded into the street and plowed forward. I smirked as I blew past the owl’s wheels, and the night's frigid air blew past me. Though, the smile faded as the wheels on my calves pinched tighter. I looked down — a patch of my skin had flaked away, replaced by metal gears and rotors. I glanced at the mound of wheels behind me. They'd sped up, and were closing in.

Pumping my limbs ever faster, I noticed a stiffness to them. Perhaps it was just due to the late hour and my lack of exercise. Yet, I couldn't help but feel as though the wheels were bringing chaos throughout my body, and I was merely moments away from falling to tatters like the owl.

My legs carried me past a series of buildings. My lungs burned, and my stomach went inside out. If I could've had it my way, I would've dropped dead then and there. Yet, I kept moving until I passed a building made of brick, with a broad alleyway. Finally — a normal building. I slowed to a jog, and then leaned along a trash-can.
Thrusting my head back, I took in deep gulps of air. It'd been too long running, with too little direction. If only there weren't so many wheels... So surreal.

I took in another breath of air, my lips furling in repulsion. My eyes darted to the left, where a dumpster sat. Why did the only safe alleyway have to have a giant dumpster in it? I walked deeper in, before halting. There'd been the slightest shift. A creak?

A squeak. The turn of a wheel. I staggered ahead, until I hit the alley’s dead-end. My heartrate climbing to my throat, I pressed my back against the dead-end and scanned for the source of the sound. My eyes landed back on the dumpster — to a piece of trash next to it. A desk-chair.
I chuckled to myself. I hadn't heard a set of wheels — it'd just been the chair, shifting in the wind. I was just being paranoid.

Taking another look at the chair, I noticed the way light bounced off it. It was built of smooth leather and possessed a sturdy design. It was a familiar design. In fact, it was very nearly an exact clone of an old office chair I'd had. I squinted and caught its logo — "DeerSmith". It was an exact clone.
"Are you kidding me?" he said, with a snort.
"I just need one more spin," I said.

The room whirled. Warm light spilled on my face from a nearby window. A blur of brown rushed past me. The blur slowed to stacks of boxes. My chair stopped, with a creak. Several of the boxes were labeled "Chad", and the rest were labeled "Owen".
"There. You spun. Had your fill yet? Because, I can’t keep waiting to pack that thing."
Smirking, I let out a sigh. "I'm really not sure. I think I might need to sit here a moment, and really think about that..."
"You really are the worst. You know that?"
He grabbed the back of the chair, and tilted it until I spilled to the ground.
Bringing myself back on my feet, I brushed the seat of my pants."Jesus — at least give a guy a warning, first."
Chad shrugged, then wheeled the chair away. My head spun around the office. The carpet and walls were utterly empty, save for a few stains and scuffs.
"This just doesn't feel right," I said. "Too clean. It needs more trash...”
There was a clang as Chad threw the chair onto a cart.
"What's gotten into you?" I said.
I strode up to Chad and gave him a punch in the arm.
"You can't go a minute without trying to say something smart, can you?" asked Chad.
I flashed a grin and leaned on a wall. "Hey: it's part of the charm. Besides, you only have to deal with my annoying mug for the next hour. Then, I'm off. Let's just tolerate each other for a —."
"You might think this is great for you, Owen... Leaving the office, selling the company, going out on your own... But, did you ever think about how it might affect the rest of us?"
"You all already have other job offers that you've taken up!" I said. "Are you seriously trying to guilt me, just for taking a better job?"

"No. I’m guilting you for just rushing into all of this, and leaving us behind... I dunno. Maybe I’m being harsh here, but did it ever occur to you that maybe — just maybe — we liked what you had going? This company you built is something special. You’re never going to get it back."
I paused, to give a thoughtful nod.

"It was a good run. But, I can't help but feel that this was never really my company. It's time to move on. There's no point in just sitting around... Movement. I need it. I don't have the temperament to stay here."
Chad's eyes went heavy. He put a hand on my shoulder.
"Good luck at being solo, I guess."
"I will. And who knows? Once I've made it big, maybe I can take you with me."
Chad grabbed his cart and pushed it away.
"Good luck."

I ran my hands through my hair. Three years. Here, then gone. Some "opportunity" my real estate venture had turned out to be. As it turns out, handling real estate in a city isn't so easy. There's plenty of pie, but too little of it is actually free to go around.

If I'd just stayed where I was, I wouldn't be dealing with my current "underground property" problem. I had no way to follow through on my promise. There was simply not enough land. Yet, I was on the hook to figure out something.
I'd be fine though. I had to be. I'd always figured out how to squeak by, in the past. I could do it again.

My eyes narrowed. The chair squeaked. It jostled. Maybe it was a breeze? Yet, the wind had died to a murmur. In trepidation, I pushed myself further against the wall. The chair slid forward. Its wheels groaned, then rattled. I huddled into a corner and the chair sped up. I looked to each side of the alley. Perhaps I could skirt around the chair. Though, as it came closer, its seat and armrests deformed into webs of wheels. My stomach coiled.
There was a roar. Light flashed. Two lights. Headlights.

A car rushed down the alleyway, its sides skidding the wall. It pulverized the chair into scattered pieces. Continuing to rush forward, it narrowly passed me and crashed into the wall. I choked. My eyes and nose burned, with tears. I'd narrowly escaped death. Yet, I could still hear the car’s engine running broiling with fury.

Shimmying along the wall, I made my way past the car. The hot kick of exhaust singed my ankles as the car shifted gears, from drive to reverse. I sprinted. My eyes ran along the walls of the alleyway — brick was crumbling away, exposing new layers of wheels and gears. My body tingled. There was a series of roars. I looked over my shoulder, only to find the car puttering toward me. The roars couldn't have been from that. Yet, the roars persisted.

My eyes shot ahead. A car rocketed down the street. Several more trickled after. Suddenly, there was a stream. Drawing closer to the street, my eyes narrowed — the cars were slightly askew in their design. Rather than having colorful, sheen bodies, they were skeletons of bars and gears.

Stepping out of the alleyway, I was met with a frigid gust. A car rode the gale, rushing past me as though I were a ghost. I looked to my left — a car veered in my direction and increased its speed. On instinct, I dove out of the way and onto the pavement.

Bad call. Waves of cars went by, swirling into wild currents. My ears rang with squeals and thuds as they swerved and crashed. I tried stepping away and searched for the alleyway, but the cars muddied my surroundings. I was adrift at sea, left to navigate the storm on my own.

Praying that none of the cars would plow me, I ran along the road's dividend. My prayers fell on deaf ears. A car mirror clipped my calf, and another car smacked into my left arm. It were as if they were out to kill me. Were they?

I peered through the window of one of the cars, as it hurtled by. In the driver's seat was a metal man. Or at least, something like one. In place of flesh were oscillating gears and wheels. Its eyes were nothing more than two thick screws, and a mouth was absent. As my eyes followed after it, its head turned in my direction. It could see me. Yet, it should’ve been just as mindless as any of the cars.
How mindless were the cars?

There was a crunch. I looked down to find flattened metal, in place of where my right foot had been. I should've screamed. My body should've been burning with pain. Yet, my entire calf was numb, having been overtaken by metal. It was a foreign lump. Yet, as the gears continued colonizing my skin, I questioned how foreign the metal was. Were they really not part of me? Or, was I not part of me?

I looked behind, hoping to find the car that had run my leg over. I came up empty. An emptiness settled in my gut. The cars were getting more vicious and precise. Maybe I was wrong: maybe they did have minds. I tried speeding my pace, but my right leg scraped behind. There was a twinge in my arm as a spark flew to it. The air buzzed of more bolting engines. To make room, cars drove along the sidewalks — sidewalks that’d turned entirely metal. Escape was no longer an option to me. All I had was surrender. Yet, my running continued, adrenaline pumping through me.

An ear-piercing screech resounded. I looked at the end of the street, to a towering building — Lambeau Tower. In the past, I'd stopped to take pictures and marvel at its robust foundations. Standing at seven-hundred feet, I’d seen few structures quite like it. Though, staring at it then, I watched it waver. The wind picked up. Subtle creaks leaked from down under. Lambeau Tower’s frame shifted. First back. Second, forth. Third, back and forth. Fourth... Still forth.

It dipped into an unrelenting plummet, the metal from its base rupturing. As it hit the ground, a shockwave rippled through my bones. Cars slipped into crashes and flipped. Neighboring buildings broke into sways of their own. Bumbling back, I balked. I stopped running and walked. A fog of debris shrouded Lambeau Tower in an air of mystery. The cause of its collapse was impossible to tell from where I stood.

The cars slowed to halts. The humming gears in surrounding buildings jammed to a stop. The street went taut with silence. I could hear the patter of my foot and peg-leg against pavement. The pitiful pitter of my pulse. I lingered on each breath, letting them rinse my lungs.

My breaths stopped short. There was a shriek. Lambeau Tower shunted forward. At first, merely in a slight shift. Though, the shift then turned to a crawl. Wheels from the bottom of Lambeau Tower thundered. Suddenly, it tore down the street, overturning rows of cars. Eyes bulging, I stumbled and then sprinted away. Shatters erupted as Lambeau Tower chopped through rows of buildings, as if they were no more than blades of grass. I brought my hands to my ears to dampen their piercing crashes, but to ill effect. My metal hand did little to block sound, and left scratches along my ears.
My eyes swung throughout the street. Most of it was cluttered by various cars and wheels weaving through the pavement. I leaned to the left — there was an fork in the road, just ahead.

A car careened through the air, landing in the fork. I shifted to the right, only to be blocked by yet another car. Ears throbbing and body flooding with shock, I ran in a desperate circle. Where was the way out? There had to be one.

There was a putter. I looked behind. Just on the edge of Lambeau Tower’s cloud of chaos was a set of headlights. They winked at me, drawing closer. The headlights were then followed by the body of a truck. I squinted — a metal man sat in the driver's seat. He gave me a wave and the car picked up its pace. I should've run. My body should've welled with fear. Yet, for whatever reason, I stood in place.

Shavings of dust and metal blew by me, clinging to my hair and skin. I suppressed a cough as Lambeau Tower's cloud crashed over me. My vision blurred, but I kept focused on the bleary pair of headlights amid it all. The frigid night air warmed as the truck pulled to my side and let out a beep.

My mouth gaped as I searched for questions. Coming up empty, I clambered over the side of the truck and into its rear. The truck roared. Its wheels spun like mad, peeling away from Lambeau Tower. I bit my lip as the truck veered to the left fork, hurtling toward the blockading car.
My chest sunk. The truck gave no sign of stopping. This was it. A valiant rescue, that lasted less than a minute long.

Shuddering, the truck picked up speed. Shivers ran down my spine. My hands fastened around the sides of the truck. I pinched my eyes. Finally, I opened my mouth to shout. Yet, I was drowned out by a crash, as we made impact with the car.

Somehow, the truck kept going. I opened my eyes, to see flaking gears and chips of metal. The car had utterly disintegrated, upon our impact. The metal man pushed on the gas, rocketing the truck past the car’s debris and down the road.

Wheezing, I looked to Lambeau Tower — it’d abandoned pursuit, diverging down another street. I whipped back the metal man. Notches of screws and rods of metal were in place of where its spine should've been.
"Thanks for saving me," I said, meekly. "You have no idea what I've been through tonight... It — it's just insane."
No response. Could it hear me? Could it answer? Had it known that it'd saved me, or had some other force intervened on my behalf?
I wanted to believe that the metal man had meant to rescue me. Yet, it was entirely possible that him stopping his truck to let me aboard had been coincidence.
I shook my head. I was overthinking things. I was alive, and that was all that mattered. My eyes shot to my arm — the metal was eating my shoulder and bleeding into my chest.
I was mostly alive.

Sighing, I watched the truck climb in speed. The speedometer’s needle leaned forward, before finally capping at 100 miles per hour. A gust clawed my face and lashed at my hair. The street was but a smear of gray. Speed — I was one with speed.
"Slow down, Owen! You're going to get one of us killed!"
"Please, nobody uses this road. Calm down and live a little... A little fast."
"Ever heard of 'live fast, die young'?"
"Yes. Words to live by."

I pressed the gas to the floorboard, making the engine sing. I zoomed past buildings, and down a winding forest road. No matter how many trees streamed by, it seemed endless more were still ahead. However, when I looked to the sky, the clouds only moved in a crawl. Despite my speed, I was still slow. I was still small.
I peered over my shoulder and looked at Bryce.
"Come on... Don't tell me this isn't amazing."
"It's really nice," Bryce said, petting the car's cherry door from out his window. "But, where are you getting all this cash from? Aren't you living on your own now?"
"I have my ways," I said, with a smirk.
"Owen... If this is another one of your schemes —."
"It’s not like that!"
"I'm not saying it is. I'm just trying to make sure you're doing the right thing here."
I laughed, shrugging him off. "All I know is that it feels right. That's all anybody can know, am I right?"

The tires squealed as I swerved out of my lane, then swerved back in. I checked my mirrors to marvel at the thick streaks my tires left in their wake. Bryce was sweating buckets, and his fingers dug into his seat's armrests.
"So tense," I said, laughing. "You should probably take a vacation, some time."
"And you should go back to taking driving lessons," said Bryce.
I flashed a grin and pumped further on the gas.
"Lucky for me, I don't have time to, because I'm actually going on a vacation. Probably to the Bahamas."
"Lucky you... I'll just be here, looking for a job."
Letting off the gas, I readjusted my mirrors. I could've sworn there'd been a smudge on one of them.
"Oh. Nice," I said. "What type are you thinking?"
"Truck driving..."
I cast Bryce a sidelong glance.
Bryce rolled his eyes and snickered. "I just finished getting my engineering degree... What type of job do you think I'm trying to get?"
I shrugged.
"Why do you care, anyway?" Bryce pressed. "What? You thinking of piggybacking?"
"I'm good on jobs, myself. Probably going to start my own business, or something."
"You know, an actual business degree might've helped with that..."
"Shut up. I know what I'm doing. Gates, Jobs, Zuckerberg... They all turned out alright."
Rolling into a bend, I squinted and held my hand over my eyes. The sun was blaring with a fury.
"Yep," Bryce said. "Because, you're totally the next Gates."
An ear-piercing screech resounded as I slammed my brakes. The car rumbled and the tires skidded. My body lurched into my dashboard. Finally, I recoiled back into my seat as we reached a halt.
"I am screwed," I said in a hush.

Just ahead of us, a car had pulled from the side of the road and parked in the center. For a split-second, I had the urge to honk my horn. Then, I saw the car's sky-blue paint. The custom, oblong headlights. As the driver stepped out and into the road, there was no denying who it was.
It was my father.
His gaze was piercing, and his face granite. Despite this, he wore a thin smile on his lips. There was a rustle as Bryce shifted back in his seat and brushed off his clothes.
"Roll up your window," I hissed.
Bryce merely swallowed and shook his head. I went to put my car in reverse — yet, as I did, my hand froze in midair. I couldn't bring myself to do it. Why couldn't I?
My father strode up to my driver's door and rapped on my windshield.
"Dad," I said, suppressing a choke. "What brings you here."
"Not much. Just going for a drive... And then saw you here. Wondered what brought you. Funny how that works."
"Funny," I said, cracking a smile.
My skin chafed against my pant legs, sweat oozing from my pores.
"So... Having fun in the peace corps?" My father asked. His tongue rolled in his mouth, as though he were trying to dislodge something from his teeth.
I looked away.
Bryce shot me a glare. "You never said anything about —."
I raised my hand, to cut him off.
"Nice car," my father said, with a stiff nod. His smile turned to a frown. "How'd you get your hands on something like this?"
I scratched my temples. "A friend loaned it to me for the day."
My father folded his arms into his chests, clenched his jaw, and let out a tired sigh. "Yes... I suppose that’s also supposed to explain your infamous joyrides people have been talking about lately?"
"Not my joyrides.”
"Of course, of course... Just like that missing quarter of a million dollars wasn’t your money."
I feigned a look of bemusement.
"A quarter of a million dollars? I don't know what you're —."

My father slammed his hand on the inside of my window. "You do. I recently had to take a peek at the books for Crosby Landscaping. And, wouldn't you know it? A quarter of a million dollars has just... Dripped away! Disappeared! And, do you know who I ended up tracing all of this lost money back to?"
His eyes bored through my skull.
"I'm sorry," I said. Though, I couldn't even look him in the eye. I was in a headlock with the road.

"What the hell were you thinking?" he said, his voice quivering. "This stunt of yours? It might kill the whole company. I want to say that we have a way to fix this... But, you've already spent most of it, haven't you?"
I frowned. My eyes burned. Then, they went firm.
"It'll all be fine," I said. "But I — I just don't have the time, right now."
"Wha—."

There was a screech as I put my engine in reverse and slammed the gas. My father's hands slid away from my car's door. He steadily shrunk as I rushed away. Finally, I put my car in drive, and turned into the other lane. My speed ratcheted, with me pushing it to its limits.
"What was that?" Bryce said.
"I can't live here anymore. I have to get out of here. Scratch the Bahamas."
"Wait — you're just going to take his money, and run?"
"He’ll be fine. You don't understand, Bryce... I need that money. It's the only way I can get to where I want to be."
Bryce nodded. "Stop the car."
"What?"
"Stop the car. I'm getting out. I'll get somebody else to pick me up."
"Bryce, I can't just drop you off..."
"And, I can't just sit by, while you do this."

I shuddered and looked at the churning buildings, and the asphalt pavement as it steadily succumbed to metal. My eyes shot to my arm. I pulled up my sleeve — the wheels had overcome my shoulders and were on my chest. Time was running out. I needed a way out.
"And, how are you doing this fine night?"
I jumped and looked back through the truck’s rear window. The metal man's head had swiveled 180°, its eyes plastering to mine.
This time, I was the one left unresponsive. My mouth went dry, and my eyes glazed over. The world slurred.

Sliding to the side, I hugged the edge of the truck. We turned down a steep street, and into what used to have been the local marketplace. Shops and kiosks were tarnished to deteriorating sludges of steel. Thunder resounded, but the sky was barren. The moon and stars were utterly exposed. I paused to stare at the moon. It'd fallen under the same disease as the city, having turned to a massive wheel.  It entered an arc, spinning through the air.
There was another clap of thunder. Behind, buildings toppled into each other like dominoes. Wheels and springs flung about, multiplying as they hit the ground.
"Quiet, are you?" the metal man asked, swerving down another street. "You have a lot to think about, don't you? I can see it on your face."

I shook my head, leafing through my thoughts. My chest tightened — I did have a lot. Without a decent piece of land, I'd be sleeping on the streets. Yet, upon seeing the state of the city, my chances of finding one were all but null.
"I love nights like these," said the metal man. "The nights when wanderers from the other world are out and about... You people always are so interesting. Always a story to tell."

The metal man turned his head back around, weaving through a street swallowed in silver weeds and arms. As we drove through, the truck's wheels stammered. Arms from the street groped at it, trying to drag us down.
"More spreaders," the metal man said with a laugh, pushing on the gas.

The air sliced in two as our truck's wheels were stripped. The truck’s body slammed to the ground. A series of plinks followed. Leaning over the side of the truck, I watched bits fall away and turn to a fine sand. A gust of wind carried through, blowing the sand away.
"Push the gas harder," I shouted. "Do something. We need to move. We're going to die!"
The metal man laughed again, then stepped out of the truck.
"It's fine," he said. "There's no moving, with the truck lodged like this. It looks like we'll need to walk."
The ground was littered with wild arms and wheels, desperately clawing. I could've jumped over the side. Instead, I shivered.
"I'm not walking," I said.
"Clearly not," said the metal man. He outstretched a hand. "But if you want a way out of here, you might want to reconsider."

Cautiously, I took the metal man's hand. Steadying my breaths, I stepped from the back of the truck and onto the ground. I winced, expecting the bite of metal fangs. No bite came. My eyes surveyed the ground. The storm of metal had calmed, with only an array of lazy wheels comprising up the street. Buildings drifted by as these wheels pulled me forward.
I let out a sigh of relief, and brushed sweat from my forehead.
"Well, I'm not dead," I said, with a forced chuckle.
"So it seems," said the metal man.

Its screw for an eye shifted, aiming at my metallic arm and legs. Following its gaze, I found that my entire left leg had faded to metal, with the metal now spreading to my opposite hip and stomach. Meanwhile, the metal of my left arm had spread across much of my back and chest. I pressed a hand against my chest, hoping to find my heartbeat. There was only a dull ping.
"Oh god... Am I running out of time?" I asked.

"Are you running out of time?" the metal man repeated. The metal on its face shifted, almost curving into a smile. "The better question is: are you running after time? From what I've seen, time is always running somewhere. Running out. Running in. Running over. Running under... The trick is for one to stop chasing it."

My eyes whipped back up. We'd passed through the cluster of marketplaces and reached the edge of a park. My eyes narrowed — somehow, the trees and leaves of the park remained untainted by the plague of metal. Even the sidewalk feeding through it was gravel. Metal wheels lapped at its edge but were unable to penetrate it.
"I don't think I've ever been here before," the metal man said. He walked forward, through the park's entrance. Dumbfounded, I followed after.
We climbed a steep hill. Rocks slid underfoot, and leaving me nearly crawling up the trail. As a heave ran through me, the metal man's hand gripped my shoulder and hoisted me up.
"Why isn't this park overrun by those wheels?" I asked, marveling at the vegetation. I tore a leaf from a low-hanging branch and peeled it in my hand.
My mouth gaped. On any other night, the park would've seemed entirely mundane. It was mundane. Yet, to find mundanity amid chaos was somehow more perplexing than chaos alone.
"Why is it still overrun by trees?" asked the metal man. "Old roots and wood... Should've been the first thing to go, when you think about it. I guess things have a way of surprising us."
We neared the top of the hill. A map of stars crowned it, spinning madly. I watched as one star streaked across. My steps slowed to soak it in.
"So, what's your story?" the metal man asked. "You could've been anywhere tonight. What brought you here?"
"I couldn't answer if I tried," I said. "I'm just as clueless as you are about why I'm here. I can only hope for things to become clear soon."

We reached the top of the hill. I looked into the landscape of the park — into the clusters of trees, the interweaving trails, the looping streams of water. I took in a deep breath, and my muscles loosened. The park seemed to ebb through me. As the branches rustled, the hairs on my right arm rustled with it. My eyes swum with the current of the water. A golden leaf came loose from a tree, floating to the ground. My stomach fluttered. I dipped into a crouch position and ran my hand through the soil.

A breeze whirled into my face. Following it, my head cocked to the left. On the edge of the trail was a house, overlooking a lake. A thick fence surrounded it, and a stream of water bordered it as a moat. My body was magnetized. Standing up, I stumbled toward it.
"Where are you going?" the metal man asked.
"Where I feel like," I said, drifting down the side of the hill. "Don't you see that house, over there?"
The metal man's body jittered. "I'll follow you, until I do."

Grass tickled my legs. Leaves cheekily leaped from the trees, and toward my face. As I traveled down the path, in hope of reaching the house, the house seemed ever further away. It were as if it was drifting back the closer I came. My eyes flicked from the trail — maybe things would be faster if I were to cut between the grass. Shaking my head, I went back to the trail.

Time rushed by, and I finally reached the edge of the stream. The house’s iron fence loomed over me. A thick padlock was fixed around the gate. I looked for a way to scramble over, but barbed wire lined all sides.
The metal man tapped my left shoulder, leaving a clink.
"Why did you stop?" he asked.
"There's no way in. No way over," I said, with a chuckle. "Not even sure why I came here... I guess it just reminded me of my parents' old house, is all. We can go back."
Chilly wind whistled through my ear.
"What do you mean 'no way in'?" the metal man asked. "We can keep going forward."
I ran my hand through my hair and laughed coldly. "Yes. Genius plan! Let's rush headlong into a giant fence."
"What fence?"
I shot the metal man a look.
"Are you blind? Don't you see that massive fence in front of us?"
The metal man shook its head. "I don't have much eyesight to speak of... However, as far as I can tell, there's only an open grove ahead."

Heartrate racing, I squinted at the fence. The metal man must've just been slow-witted. Maybe he was willfully ignoring the fence, altogether. I snapped my arm up and gripped around a bar to the fence. There was a screech. The bars disintegrated to wheels. Yanking my hand away, I stepped back and looked around. Wheels were spreading across the fence like a wildfire. As they fell to the grass, they rushed through, transforming everything to cold metal. It spread toward the house, then onto the pathway I was standing on.

I needed a way out. There had to be a quick way out, wasn't there? It wasn't possible that there was no way out. I refused to believe it. Though, as I went to pull my leg from the ground, it clasped around my ankles. I pulled at my other leg, but it too wouldn't budge. Wheels clenched around it, rooting me in place. I let out a yelp.
"Help!"

My head snapped back around, to see the metal man reaching toward me. The pathway's wheels were gripping around him as well, with increasing ferocity. In the sky, the stars and moon were spinning ever faster. Then, faster.
Faster, still.
"What do we do?" I pleaded, as the wheels reached my stomach.
"It appears that you've reached your shift point," the metal man said, with a wail.
"My what?"

"Your shift-point... Many a traveler that comes down here eventually has one. Generally, they have it far later on. I've never been there to witness one myself before, thankfully. But, it appears I witness it now. Best of luck on getting past it."
There was a roiling roar. Squirming and groaning, the house melted into a cascade of metal. It morphed into a wave and rushed toward me.
"What the hell is a 'shift-point'?!"
"The better question would be, 'what isn't it?'"
"I need clear and quick answers! You're not making any sense!"
The metal man's lower body fell away.
"Who said I had to?"
The metal man craned its neck upward as its upper body fell to dust, before its head finally crashed to the ground. Its assorted parts vanishing to nothingness, my chest sunk.

My body tensed as metal spread through my body. The wave sped toward me, gaining mass and force as it went. My eyes danced around the park. Perhaps another metal man would come, driving another car to rescue me. Yet, all I saw were clusters of trees, also steadily succumbing to the metal.
I clenched my jaw. I wasn't thinking quick enough. Why could I never think sharp when it mattered most?

My skin slowly went numb, as the metal made its way up my chest — My neck. As everything went fuzzy, I stared into the sky. It rushed around, like a whirlwind. Everything was moving fast. I was moving slow. Then, I stopped moving. My jaw went dead. My eyes froze.
Why couldn't everything slow down? The house — why did it have to disintegrate? Why did everything have to fall apart, all around me? Why couldn't things stay in sync?
Sync...
I looked to the stars and watched them spin. Flashes of my life went past my eye — fast. The stars moved with them. A breeze funneled through my body.

I thought back to the house. To the park. The calm that it’d brought, before the wheels overtook them. I needed to return to that calm. That comfort. I steadied my breaths. My head ached, but a rush of relief coursed through. Staring into the stars again, my mind reached out. I thought back to the way things were before.

As wheels clustered over my eyes, there was a piercing creak. The spinning slowed, then stopped entirely. My body warped into the sky, spiraling between sparkling trails of comets and stars. I was torn through the moon. Then, I was back on the ground. Leaves fluttered down from the trees. The wheels receded, folding flesh on my bones. The stars turned backward. Everything turned backward. Rotors and iron struts were overtaken by vegetation — by life. The stream sprung back.
While light dancing along the water, I strode up to the stream. I scanned for any sign of the house I’d seen. Yet, there wasn't a hint. Just a wide, open field of grass and weeds.
A bird chirped, off in the distance. A moth blew by my face. I smiled. My field. My place. I glanced at my watch — it was 1:31. There was still time. There'd always be time.
Something clutched my shoulder, sending chills through me. I turned around. It was a hand.
It was the hand of the metal man.
"You did good, Owen," he said. "I've never seen anybody pass their shift-point, before."
My chest went heavy. "I still don't think you have. But, I guess it doesn't matter."

I sat down in the grass and stared out to the open field. There as a clank as the metal man sat next to me, then placed an arm around my shoulder. I looked for a sign of more metal, outlying the park — there was none. Only the metal man.
"Everything matters, in the circle of life," said the metal man.
"Maybe... Maybe not. We all see ourselves as the center of the circle, don't we?"
"Do we?"
"I do. I did. And, if we all are the center... Then there is no center. There's just us, moving uncontrollably."
"We can keep control."
"Control is overrated though, isn't it?"
I took in a deep breath of the night air. I looked up and drank in the moonlight.
"I think I'm just going to sit here, awhile."
The metal man nodded. "So will I."
End

title: Batman Fan Fact Compilation
paragraphs: The Gothamite's Omega Database
Published Facts
Alfred:
Alfred sees himself as the father of Bruce, and even goes so far as to think of Bruce as his son. (Source: All-Star Batman Vol. 2)
Alfred worked in theater, and then went on to become a military medic in his youth. (Source: All-Star Batman #10)
Whenever Alfred communicates with Batman via the Batcomputer, he uses the code-name "Penny-One". (Source: All-Star Batman #13)
In his early years, writers tried making Alfred into his own private detective. (Source: Batman #21)
Alfred has his own secret password to the Batcave: "Balmoral". Nightwing is the only other person who knows about it. Not even Batman knows about it. (Source: Nightwing #68)
Alfred has a daughter named Julia Pennyworth. She works as British Special Intelligence, and has helped the bat-family on numerous occasions. (Source: Batman Eternal #26)
When Batman went missing after a massive earthquake in Gotham, Alfred used his spy-training to help protect the citizens of Gotham and fight crime. (Source: Legends of the Dark Knight #118)

Unlike Batman, Alfred has no qualms with using firearms when necessary, and keeps a shotgun for defense. He's even dreamt of using it to kill Joker. (Sources: Batman and robin #17, and Superman/Batman #2)

Under the mind-control of a Yellow Lantern Ring, Alfred nearly killed Batman and Green Lantern. Batman freed Alfred with the trigger line, "Be thy own palace, or the world is thy jail." (Source: Green Lanterns 2016 #16 and #17)
Atom:
The Atom is capable of being nearly anywhere by shrinking down to the size of a proton andarea

Ray Palmer helped create the "Red Giants" Superman defense-system in Batman's Justice Buster armor by shrinking red suns from dead solar systems, and inserting them into the armor's gauntlets. (Source: Batman Endgame)
In addition to being able to change size, the Atom can also change his weight and density. (Source: The All-New Atom #5)
Aquaman:
Aquaman once gave a struggling waitress enough money to put her kids through college. (Source: Aquaman #1)
Aquaman has war plans to take over the Earth. (Source: Throne of Atlantis)
Aquaman has fought Superman to a standstill before. (Source: Aquaman #6)
Flash has admitted that Aquaman is strong enough to kill him in a fight, if he's not holding back. (Source: Trinity #10)
Aquaman once said that the most dangerous thing about Batman is his mind. (Source: Justice League #24)
Aquaman's trident is capable of piercing Darkseid's skin and deflecting Omega Beams. (Source: Justice League #6)
Before joining the Justice League, Aquaman was part of a team called "the Others". It was devoted to finding and protecting Atlantean relics. (Source: Aquaman #8)
The Lady of the Lake once replaced Aquaman's left hand with a water hand, granting him hydrokinesis. (Source: Aquaman #1)
Aquaman possesses immense strength, due to his body having adapted to the intense pressures of deep sea life. (Source: JLA Year One #1)
Despite other Atlanteans needing special suits to swim through Lava, Aquaman is capable of swimming through lava without suffering any harm. (Source: Aquaman #26)
Due to the Brain's Basal Ganglia being inherited from aquatic ancestors, Aquaman was once able to use his telepathy on it to give a White Martian a seizure. (Source: Justice League Rock of Ages)
According to Batman, Aquaman is the "secret weapon" of the Justice League. This is because people overlook how smart Aquaman really is. (Source: Aquaman 2016 Annual #1)
In addition to being an effective melee weapon, Aquaman's Trident can be used to test the chemical composition of water and shoot bolts of electricity. (Source: Aquaman 2011 #50, #52)
Batgirl:
When Barbara Gordon was Oracle, she was in charge of monitoring all of Gotham and the Justice League. (Source: Gotham Knights #24)
When Batgirl first met Batman and Robin, she got in a fight with them and fled the scene. (Source: Batgirl Year One #3)
Just like Batman, Batgirl has an eidetic memory. This allows her to work as one of the best detectives in the DC Universe. (Source: Batgirl #49)
Green Arrow once claimed that, as Oracle, Barbara Gordon never submitted an inaccurate report to the Justice League. (Source: Flash #216)
Before becoming Batgirl, Barbara Gordon tried becoming a field agent for the FBI. Though, she was rejected due to not meeting the height requirement. (Source: Batgirl Year One #1)
Batgirl initially wanted to be named "Batwoman". However, after a group of thugs called her "Batgirl", she reluctantly accepted that name instead. (Source: Batgirl Year One #3)
Batgirl once went on a date with Clark Kent. Though, she ultimately thought that Clark was a "basic drag". (Source: Superman 1939 #268)
Batgirl can tell what a person is writing from afar, just b watching the way their pen moves. (Source: Batgirl 2011 #16)
Batman:
Batman created the backup personality, Batman of Zurr En Arrh, in case of crisis (Source: Batman R.I.P
Modern Age Batman still carries shark repellent, in case of run-ins with King Shark (Source: All-Star Batman Vol. 1)
In Batman's starting years of operation, he considered revealing his true identity to Harvey Dent. (Source: Dark Victory)
Gotham is supposedly located somewhere in New Jersey. *No Source
Batman has a bat-cow. *No Source
Batman has bat-bunkers throughout Gotham. (Batwing #14)
Batman has a Justice-Buster Armor (aka Fenrir) designed to take down the Justice League if they ever were to go rogue. (Source: Batman Endgame)
Batman has a Hell-Bat armor that he designed with the help of the Justice League. He once used it to take down Darkseid. (Source: Batman and Robin #33)
Commissioner Gordon once adopted the mantle of Batman. (No Source)
Batman funded and designed the Watchtower. (No Source)
Silver-Age Batman had a bat-train. (No Source)
Batman has a photographic memory. (No Source)
Batman has an arsenal of Bat-vehicles stored in the Batcave. (Source: JL Rebirth Vol. 2)
Batman's "No Kill Rule" was established in Batman #4, in 1940, due to an editor demand from fears of gun violence. (Source: Batman #4) *used twice
The Batmobile got its name after Alfred nicknamed it that in jest. Batman took a liking to it, and the name stuck. (Source: Batman and the Monster Men)
When Green Lantern let Batman borrow his ring for a moment, Batman used it to try recreating his parents. (Source: Green Lantern #9)
Batman's plan to stop himself if he ever goes rogue is Superman (Source: Justice League #20)
Batman designed the Justice League a teleporter. (Source: JLA #15)

Thomas and Martha Wayne had a son before Bruce, who died in a car accident. Though, there's a Batman villain called "Owlman" who claimed to be Bruce's long-lost brother. (Source: Batman Night of the Owls)
Batman's middle name is Thomas. (Source: I Am Bane) *done twice
Batman was trained to escape any trap by Zatara (Source: Detective #833)
Batman once fought off an army of Ninjas in his pajamas (Source: Batman Night of the Owls)

Bruce Wayne initially tried committing suicide after his parent's death. However, in this moment, he had the breakthrough that he could use his life to help people. Thus, the idea of becoming Batman was seeded. (Source: Batman Rebirth #12)
Batman was able to defeat a weaker version of Amazo with a Batmobile missile. (Source: Batman Under the Hood)
Batman has a new sidekick named "the Signal". (Source: Batman and the Signal #1)
Batman used to hide Green Arrow's arrows as a prank. (Source: Justice League #0)
Lois Lane has driven the Batmobile before (Source: Superman #22)
When Wonder Woman tried using her lasso of truth to get Batman to reveal his true identity, his answer was simply, "I'm Batman." (Source: Wonder Woman Annual #1)
In order to conceal his identity from Superman, Batman once put a field around his suit that inhibited Superman's X-ray vision. (Source: Man of Steel #3)
Batman can speak Kryptonian. (Source: Superman/Batman #30)
Batman hates apple pie. (Source: Superman Rebirth #20)
Jim Gordon's son, James Gordon Jr., is a serial killer. (Source: Batman Black Mirror)
Batman was chosen for the Sinestro Corps by a yellow lantern ring before. (Source: Sinestro Corps War)
During his training, Batman was able to kick down a tree. (Source: Batman Year One, Batman #18)
Batman has a tiny laser implanted in his palm, which he can remove to escape traps. (Source: Batman Annual #2)
Batman has shoes that can allow him to walk on walls. (Source: Batman Zero Year)
Batman has reverse engineered the Green Lantern Ring. (Source: Batman/Superman #30)
Batman has a hidden Batcave on the moon. (Source: Superman #5, Dark Days the Forge #1)
Batman has a high-tech contact lens that connects to the Batcomputer. (Source: New 52 Batman #1)
Despite Batman initially taking Dick Grayson as his ward, he eventually adopted him as his son. (Source: Gotham Knights #21)
When Batman traveled to the alternate Flashpoint timeline, Thomas Wayne told him "Let the Batman die with me." (Source: DC's the Button)
Batman's greatest fear is becoming as insane as the villains he fights and failing Gotham. (Source: Batman #24)
Bruce Wayne once helped start up a global army of bat-vigilantes to protect the world, known as "Batman Incorporated". (Source: Batman Incorporated #1)
Batman's override password to the Batcave is "MarthaWayne1940". (Source: Justice League Rebirth #8)

Batman is constantly trying to complete a machine that would keep him alive forever, via perfect clones, as well as an A.I. that could perfectly replicate Alfred's consciousness. (Source: All-Star Batman #11)
Batman has a rod that emits a drop of red-sunlight, which can render Superman's powers inert. (Source: Batman/Superman #20)
Batman's go-to password is 10:48. It's the exact time his parents died. (Source: New 52 Batman and Robin #1)
Batman was ten years old when his parents died. (Source: Batman Rebirth #12, Batman and the Monster Men #4)
Batman has defeated Lady Shiva — the greatest martial artist in the DC Universe — twice in combat. (Source: Death in the Family, Superman/Batman #3)
Batman and Superman met as children, when Bruce Wayne's car broke down on a road-trip through Smallville. (Source: Superman/Batman Secret Files)
Batman has an army of Bat-bots that follow his voice-command. (Source: Batman #20)
Batman has a virtual reality training device that he uses to prepare himself for intense missions. (Source: Batman #20, Batman and Robin #23)

Batman doesn't kill the Joker because he fears that, if he crossed that line, he'd go unhinged and become no different from the criminals he fights. (Source: Batman #850, Batman Ego, and Justice League Rebirth #7)
Batman once let Robin man the machine gun, loaded with tranquilizer darts, of a Bat-tank. (Source: Batman the Cult)
Batman has said that Bruce Wayne is his mask, whereas Clark Kent has said that Superman is his mask. (Source: Batman #600, Trinity #2)
In an alternate universe in the omniverse, Batman and Captain America teamed up to fight Nazis. (Source: Batman/Captain America)
When faced with hard cases, Batman takes micro-sleeps to brainstorm answers. (Source: Batman R.I.P)
While Batman relies on Lucius Fox for some things, he still designs a lot of his own tech. (Source: Batman #635)

Batman and Spider-Man have teamed up twice before in the omniverse. Once to stop Kingpin and Ra's Al Ghul, and a second time to stop Carnage and Joker. (Source: Batman & Spider-Man, Spider-Man & Batman)
When investigating tough suspects, Batman has his own truth serum he concocted to get them to talk. (Source: Death in the Family)
Martian Manhunter has said Batman should be the person to lead the Justice League. (Source: JLA #250)
Not long after the death of his parents, Bruce Wayne was sent to a rehabilitation center. This was where he first met Harvey Dent. (Source: All-Star Batman #3)
Batman's intelligence is almost on par with Lex Luthor's. He's capable of studying and analyzing alien tech. (Source: Doomsday Clock, JLA #8, JL #1)*
Batman once sat in Metron's Mobius chair, giving him temporary access to all the knowledge in the DC Universe. (Source: Justice League #42)
Batman used to own the Daily Planet, but it was later bought out by Lex Luthor. (Source: Batman Hush, Justice League #52)
Batman has a suit dedicated to missions in deep space. (Source: Batman/Superman #37)
When Bruce Wayne was a child, his father told him "Waynes never stay down. We rise." (Source: Batman #22)
Batman keeps snacks in his utility-belt. (Source: Trinity #11)
Batman's first female sidekick wasn't Barbara Gordon's Batgirl, but Kathy Kane's Batwoman. (Source: Detective Comics #233)
Batman has a charity dedicated to economic and scientific advancements called the Wayne Foundation. (Source: Detective Comics #356)
Batman dodged Deadshot's sniper twice, making him the only person to make Deadshot miss. (Detective Comics #474)
There's an alternate universe where Batman is a rogue vigilante operating in the 1940s. (Source: Batman Gotham Noir)
When Dick Grayson became Batman, he initially had problems seeing through the cowl and moving with the weight of the cape. (Source: Batman #688)
Batman has a routine route he takes throughout Gotham each night. He calls it his nightly workout. (Source: Batman #664)
Batman's batsuit is retrofitted with a back brace and shock absorbers, to prevent his back from ever being broken again. (Source: Batman #665)
Every afternoon, Batman records what he's done for Alfred to read. (Source: Batman #673)
One of Batman's Batwings are armed with lasers, which he uses against meta-humans that are beta-level and above. (Source: JLA #10)
Batman's utility belt is capable of producing electric-shock bursts. (Source: Nightwing #14)
Wildcat helped train Batman how to box. (Source: JLA #28)
Batman once said that he could beat Martian Manhunter with just a book of matches. (Source: DC New Frontier)
Despite Batman's bulletproof armor protecting him from fatal injury, he can still feel intense pain if shot in the same place several times. (Source: Justice League vs. Suicide Squad)
When Batman and Superman first met, Superman was convinced that Batman had superpowers. This was due to Batman's ability to disappear without detection. (Source: Man of Steel #3)
If out of gadgets, Batman is able to detach and throw his cape to stun and ensnare his enemies. (Source: All-Star Batman #8)

On the anniversary of his parents' death, Batman always ventures to crime alley to fight thugs and meet with Leslie Thompkins — a woman who comforted him on the night his parents died. (Source: Detective Comics #457)
Batman has plans to defeat the Justice League because he feels it's his responsibility to make sure that there's somebody who can stop them if something were to go awry. (Source: Justice League #8)
Before the creation of Arkham Asylum and Blackgate Penitentiary, Batman's villains used to simply be kept in "Gotham Prison". (Source: Batman #300)
Batman has a holographic barrier to disguise the entrance to the Batcave. (Source: Detective Comics #615)
Batman keeps a black paintball in his utility belt, to blind or stun an opponent. (Source: Batman #590)
Ra's Al Ghul has been for thousands of years. Batman has said he makes Joker look like a minor annoyance. (Source: Detective Comics #700)
Batman is said to know every street tunnel and passageway throughout Gotham City. (Source: Batman #445)
Batman keeps a powerful magnet in his belt, which he can hold to cling onto ceilings. (Source: Batman #444)
Batman keeps hypersonic devices in his belt, which can stun more powerful opponents. (Source: Batman #608)
Batman once fought a shark unprepared and won. (Source: Batman #251)
After being temporarily blinded by an explosion, Batman built an interconnected series of min-cameras, connected to his brain via a micro-chip, in order to still see. (Source: Batman #226)
Ra's Al Ghul discovered that Bruce Wayne must've been Batman, after deducing that Batman must've been wealthy due to all of his resources. (Source: batman #232)
Batman has a third identity known as "Matches Malone". He's a gangster that Batman uses to investigate Gotham's seedy underbelly. (Source: Nightwing #14)
Batman has an eidetic memory. This is part of why he's been able to attain the status of "World's Greatest Detective". (Source: Batman #230, Batman #451)
Batman has a stealth device that can mask the sound of even his own heartbeat from Superman. (Source: JLA #1)
Dick Grayson Batman had a "bat-taser" that he could launch from his gloves. (Source: Batman Black Mirror)
After Jason Todd died, Batman tried removing all traces of him from the Batcave. (Source: Batman #436)
Before the death of his parents, Bruce Wayne often ditched school to explore Gotham. Once, he was even "arrested" by Jim Gordon, because his parents reported him missing. (Source: Batman #26)
The original bat-plane had a television aboard it. (Source: Batman #203)
Despite Batman's no-kill rule, he possesses several lethal weapons, such as an explosive grenade and a laser torch. (Source: Batman #203)
When Bruce first trained Dick Grayson in combat, he told him "We're not brutalizers. We've got to think with our heads, not with our fists." (Source: Batman Year 3)
Dick Grayson became Batman after Bruce Wayne's death. But, the Joker could tell Grayson wasn't the real Batman, stating: "You smell like feathers, little bird." (Source: Detective Comics #880)

Bruce has always felt responsible for his parents' death, and sees it as his greatest failure. Among other things, becoming Batman was a way to make amends with his perceived failure. (Source:  Batman #432)
Batman's first love was Julie Madison. He was engaged with her, but they eventually split. (Source: Batman #208)
Batman's cowl contains a neck brace, in order to protect himself from breaking his neck in high-impact scenarios. (Source: Batman Gothic)
When fighting normal thugs, the Batmobile can launch a non-lethal electric net, which shocks them into submission. (Source: Batman #626)
When Scarecrow terrorized Batman and Joker with a nightmare toxin, Batman's greatest nightmare was living a normal life with his family. (Source: Superman/Batman #65)
During a Black Lantern invasion, the corpse of one of Batman's clones was turned into a Black Lantern Zombie. (Source: Blackest Night)
Batman keeps an X-ray device in his utility belt for detective work. (Source: Superman #20)
During much of the Bronze Age of comics, Batman abandoned the Batcave and began operating out from beneath his Wayne Foundation building. (Source: Batman #320)
While the average human heartrate is around 70 BPM, Batman's heartrate is below 40 BPM. This is due to his extremely athletic lifestyle. (Source: JLA #1)
Batman has a miniature crime-lab in the back of his Batmobile. (Source: Batman #206)
Batman has a high-powered magnetic batarang, which he once used to take out multiple robots at once. (Source: Green Lantern #16)
Batman once defeated Prometheus — a villain who can download the fighting skills of others into his brain — by hacking his helmet and uploading a motor neuron disease. (Source: JLA #38)
The giant penny in the batcave is often misattributed to Two-Face. Batman actually earned it while fighting the Penny Plunderer. (Source: World's Finest #30)
One of Batman's methods of escaping without detection is using a "flare capsule", which temporarily blinds onlookers. (Source: JLA Earth 2)
Despite Batman's efforts, Gotham City is still the most crime-ridden city in the DC Universe.  (Source: Justice League #9)
After Batman's death, the mayor of Gotham declared that the city was in a state of emergency. (Source: Battle For the Cowl #1)
Batman became a White Lantern once, after Deadman mistakenly decided Batman was worthy of the ring. Later on, the ring rejected Batman. (Source: Brightest Day #14)
Batman discovered that speedsters tend to keep their feet solid while phasing their bodies. He exploited this weakness in a fight with Reverse Flash, by stabbing his feet. (Source: Batman #21)

While the comic "Zero Year" was initially intended to replace "Batman Year One" as Batman's origin, Scott Snyder confirmed that, due to DC Rebirth, both origins are canon: "When we announced 'Zero Year', people thought we were going to do a new origin... Which, I mean, we were. The New 52 erased the possibility for 'Year One' to be the origin anymore because Jim Gordon, Selina, and Batgirl had changed. And, we were one of the last holdouts who hadn't done a new origin for the New 52. But, now that we've done Rebirth, it all kind of gels into one thing." (Source: Youtube Channel Monkey's Fighting Robots video, "Batman's Scott Snyder talks Nerd Rage and 'Secret Empire' Controversy")
Bruce Wayne was partially inspired to become Batman by his father's love for the character of Zorro — a legendary Mexican vigilante. (Source: Batman #595)

Batman traveled to a parallel universe and saved his parents from being murdered. Though, the Bruce Wayne of that universe was still inspired by Batman and trained to become his own Batman. (Source: Detective Comics #500)
Batman was tricked into his first fight with Superman by Lex Luthor. He ultimately lost the fight. (Source: Lex Luthor Man of Steel)
Batman has a prototype Batman Beyond suit and a bat-spaceship designed for deep-space missions. (Source: Superman/Batman #64)
Batman's favorite Christmas gift is the last gift he received from his parents: a toy train. (Source:  Legends of the Dark Knight #79)
Batman keeps a Yellow Lantern ring hidden away in his batcave, in case he were to ever need to fight a Green Lantern. (Source: Forever Evil #4)

On New Year's Eve, Gotham City's "New Year's Ball" was rigged with a bomb that was set to explode on New Year's day. While disabling it, Batman ended up riding Gotham's ball all the way into the New Year. (Source: Batman #247)
In order to maintain peak awareness, Batman doesn't drink alcohol. He just drinks ginger ale and pretends it's champagne. (Source: Dark Knight Returns #1)
Batman was able to hack into NASA's satellites within an hour and download their entire database on his computer. (Source: Batman Abduction)
Batman has a special mechanism in his entrance to the batcave that will detect intruders and lead them into a fake "man-cave" rather than the batcave. (Source: All-Star Batman #5)
Superman has claimed that, due to Batman's martial arts training, he's versed in nearly every weapon known to man. (Source: Superman/Batman #10)
Batman has a lie-detector built into his cowl, which can tell him if somebody is lying or not during interrogations. (Source: Batman #3)

Gotham City has a population of a little over 8 million people. This would make it second only to New York City, which has a population size of 8.5 million, in population size for a U.S city. (Source: JLA Year One #2)
Batman's cowl has a glass cover that can slide over his face, to protect him from exposure to noxious acids and gases. (Source: All-Star Batman #3)

During Bruce's training years, he studied with an FBI agent named Arthur Mckee. Through Mckee, Bruce learned the importance of maintaining criminal aliases in Gotham's underground. (Source: Batman #589)
After being given Superman's powers by the evil Silver Banshee, Batman became obsessed with monitoring Earth's crime and steadily went insane. (Source: Superman/Batman #56)
Bruce Wayne was once appointed as a temporary U.S Senator. (Source: Brave and the Bold #85)
Batman has been shown capable of bench-pressing 1,000 lbs (453.5 kg). In comparison, the world record for bench-pressing is 1,102 lbs (499.8 kg).

In the Post-Crisis Continuity, Batman trained for 12 years and began his career at 25. In the New 52 Continuity, Batman trained for 7 years, and began his career at 20. (Sources: Batman Year One #1, Batman #21)
In case someone were to expose Bruce Wayne as Batman, Batman created several backup civilian identities to step into at a moment's notice. (Source: Robin #125)
Batman has a "photo-reactive" suit that morphs into camouflage, depending on his surrounding environment. (Source: Green Arrow #134)
It generally takes 9-12 minutes for the Gotham Police to respond to a crime. It only takes Batman 3. (Source: Detective Comics Annual #2)
Batman has a bat-blimp. It was an unused prototype vehicle, created by Lucius Fox for Wayne Enterprises. (Source: Batman #29)
Batman once defeated Artemis, one of Themyscaria's fiercest warriors, by shooting her with a poison dart. (Source: Superman/Batman #9)
Batman has a Batmobile that utilizes holographic camouflage. This allows it to disguise as a normal car through heavy traffic. (Source: Batman #51)
Batman once had himself imprisoned in a cell in Arkham and escaped, to test Arkham's security systems. (Source: Batman Annual #2)
Batman keeps a device from the future called "the lightning rod", which can absorb speed-force energy from speedsters. (Forever Evil #4)
Batman built a trophy room in the Hall of Justice, full of weapons from the League's thwarted enemies. He disabled each weapon beforehand. (Source: JLA 2006 #7)
Batman owns a nuclear bomb, which he acquired after a deadly fight with the Joker. (Source: Superman/Batman #33)
Batman defeated the omnipotent god "Metron" by tricking him into turning human to discover "ultimate knowledge", and then sucker-punching him. (Source: JLA 1997 #14)
Bruce Wayne breezed through his courses in Cambridge University, Sarbonne University, and the Berlin School of Science, due to his eidetic memory and speed-reading. (Source: Shadow of the Bat #0)
Batman once hacked into a high-tech security network with a device no more advanced than a cell-phone. (Source: Batman Inc. 2011 #4)
Batman has a camera in his cowl that he uses to record all of his missions. (Source: Batman 2011 #19)
Using military-grade protocols from the Batcomputer, Batman was once able to hack LexCorp and steal its files. (Source: Batman Confidential #3)
Batman has said he hates magic because it's "too hard to anticipate or control... Too much like insanity." (Source: Trinity 2016 #17)
Batman has a special ointment under his mask to protect his exposed skin. (Source: Catwoman 2011 #1)

Despite once having the opportunity to let the Joker fall off a building and die, Batman chose to save him. He reasoned that the Joker's death wasn't his call to make. (Source: Legends of the Dark Knight #12)

Batman is heavily distrustful toward the concept of Government. According to him, "It's always been my conviction that, when nobody can see what the Government is doing, the Government becomes abusive." (Source: JLA 2006 #17)
Nightwing has said that Batman is rarely ever free, because he's made it a point to answer every call. (Source: Nightwing 2016 #43)
Batman's gauntlets are armed with defibrillators, to save people in emergency medical scenarios. (Source:  Justice League 2011 #36)
According to Joker, "Robin's greatest fear is being responsible for Batman's death, and Batman's greatest fear is being responsible for Robin's death." (Source: Batman and Robin 2011 #15)
Batman once managed to defeat three white martians on his own with a book of matches and a trail of gasoline. (Source: JLA 1997 #3)

During his training years, Bruce Wayne was tricked into helping murder a terrorist, by Morgan Ducard. After this, Bruce Wayne broke into a frenzy, nearly killing Ducard. (Source: Batman and Robin 2011 #6)

Batman chooses to focus on his efficiency as a hero, over being a "symbol" for the people. He once said, "I've never been one for popularity contests. Most of the people in Gotham are scared to death of me. And I prefer it that way. This job […] is about skill. Determination. Self-sacrifice." (Source: Blue Beetle 2016 #12)
Batman has a disguise that can mask over his face (Source: Batman 2011 #1)
Black Adam:
Black Adam is considered one of the most powerful beings on Earth. He once reduced an entire nation to ashes in only 36 hours, killing millions. (Source: DC's 52 #45)
Black Canary:
In addition to having one of the strongest sonic blasts in the DC Universe Black Canary is a skilled Martial Artist, with a black-belt in Judo. (Source: Batgirl Year One #6)
Barbara Gordon claimed that Black Canary could in combat. (Source: Birds of Prey #125 1999)
According to Roy Harper, Black Canary is braver than himself and Roy Harper. (Source: JLA 2006 #3)
Blue Beetle:
Ted Kord is one of the smartest humans in the DC Universe. According to Guy Gardner, he's even smarter than Batman. (Source: Blue Beetle 2006 #14)
Booster Gold:
Booster Gold was born in Gotham but operates in Modern Day Metropolis. (Source: Booster Gold Vol. 1)
Superman was initially jealous of Booster Gold when he came on the scene. (Source: Booster Gold #7)
Booster Gold's full name is "Michael Jon Carter", in reference to the pulp hero "John Carter". (Source: Booster Gold #6)
Booster Gold inadvertently gave Sinestro the idea for the Sinestro Corps when trying to warn him about the future. (Source: Booster Gold 2007 #2)

Booster Gold used to have a cape for his costume. However, after being choked by his cape while helping Superman in a fight, Superman removed it and told him "You can't handle the cape."  (Source: Booster Gold 2005 #3)
Catwoman:
Catwoman once managed to steal the Batmobile from Batman, by stealing the keys from his utility belt. (Source: Catwoman 2002 #82)
Cyborg:
Cyborg used to have a lung, but ultimately gave it away to stop an Atlantean attack. His remaining major organs are his heart and his brain. (Source: Justice League #15)
Cyborg is capable of tapping into nearly every computer on Earth, except the Batcave. (Source: Justice League #8)
When concentrating, Cyborg is able to alter the subatomic structure of his armor to appear fully human. (Source: Cyborg #3)
Cyborg is effectively able to travel inside digital technology, via a virtual reality in his brain called the "Cyberverse". (Source: Cyborg #6)
