Cyborg claimed he's capable of killing Superman in less than five seconds, via sonic frequencies that can scramble the brain. (Source: Cyborg #9)

Cyborg claims to be plugged into every computer on Earth, including the Bat-Computer. However, in Justice League Rebirth #8, Batman comments that he'd updated his computer to keep Cyborg out. (Source: Justice League 2011 #9)
Cyborg is one of the few heroes capable of going toe-to-toe with Shazam. Shazam said he considers Cyborg, "One of my best friends." (Source: Cyborg #9)
Darkseid:
Despite Green Lantern rings being one of the most powerful weapons in the DC Universe, Darkseid once destroyed one with his bare hands.
On Earth 2, Darkseid managed to successfully take over Earth and remake it into a new "Apokolips". (Earth 2: World's End #26)
DC Universe (general):
The god and creator of the DC Multiverse is "the Presence".
Batman and Green Lantern were both co-created by Bill Finger.
The Watchmen was initially meant to be a story about the Charlton Comics characters, "the Sentinels of Justice".
Arguably the most powerful villain in the DC Universe is the Anti-Monitor, who can devour universes. (Source: Crisis on Infinite Earths)
Penguin is considered the worst crime boss in Gotham. He once drove a Governor to suicide by killing his entire family. (Source: Batman #23.3)
Deathstroke:
Arsenal called Deathstroke the "greatest tactician on the planet". (Source: Identity Crisis #3)
Despite Deadpool being a spoof of Deathstroke, DC created a spoof of Deadpool called "Red Tool" (aka, Wayne Wilkins). (Source Harley Quinn #26)

Batman and Deathstroke are evenly matched opponents. Deathstroke was once even able to beat Batman to the point of near death, telling him "You've trained yourself to fight. I've trained myself to kill." (Source: Deathstroke #7)
The serum in Deathstroke's body increases his brain's processing speed, so that his reflexes are ten times faster than that of a normal person. (Source: Deathstroke #7)
Using a magical sword that adapted to attacks, Deathstroke was able to give Superman a challenge in a fight. Though, Deathstroke ultimately lost the fight. (Source: Deathstroke #9)
When Deathstroke and Lex Luthor fought, they came to a standstill. However, Lex Luthor admitted Deathstroke could've killed him, if he'd been faster. (Source: Action Comics #892)
Enlisting the help of the Tattooed Man, Deathstroke was once able to defeat Supergirl with a kryptonite sword. (Source: Titans 2008 Annual #1)
Due to his enhanced reflexes, Deathstroke is fast enough to counter attacks from speedsters. (Source: New Teen Titans 1980 #2)
Flash:
Batman and Flash used to compare lists of their enemies, to see which of them had the worst. They stopped the competition once they arrived at Joker and Reverse Flash. (Source: Flash Rebirth)
The Flash has said Batman is the only person in the Justice League he can relate to, when it comes to forensic work. (Source: Flash #21)
When a speedster runs beyond the speed of light, they disappear into the Speed-Force. (Source: Titans #6)
The Flash's Rogues Gallery was once willing to team up with him, in order to defeat the Riddler. (Source: Flash #52)
The Flash's mind runs in light-speed, which makes him resistant to telepathy. (Source: New 52 JLA #8)
Flash was initially distrusting of Hal Jordan. However, after discovering he was a space-cop, they became instant friends. (Source: Flash Rebirth)
Flash has a long-lost evil twin brother known as "Cobalt Blue", who was separated from his family at birth by a drunk doctor. (Source: Flash #144)
When Barry Allen had to wield Hal Jordan's Green Lantern ring, he was able to use his speed to think of infinite Green Lantern constructs at once. (New 52 Flash Annual #2)
The Flash's speed allows him to process and evaluate scenarios at such a quick rate that he can react before anything even happens. (Source: Flash #2)
The Flash was once chosen for a Blue Lantern Ring due to his incredible capacity for hope. (Source: Blackest Night)
The Speed-Force is a multiversal constant, with all of the main DC Earths being contained within a Speed-Force wall. (Source: Grant Morrison's Map to the Multiverse)
While Wally West was a kid, Barry Allen would train him to remember science facts. Barry called them "Flash Facts". (Source: JLA #3)
Wally West has the unique ability to lend other people his speed. (Source: JLA #20)
Flash's super-sped metabolism allows him to heal from injuries at an incredibly fast rate. (Source: Flash #29)
The Reverse Flash hates Barry Allen because he desperately wants to be Barry but knows he never can be. (Source: Flash #79)
When the Flash runs at high speeds, the Speed-Force generates a protective aura that works to prevent injury from bits of dust and rain. (Source: Flash #72)
The Flash has receivers built into his mask that allow him to listen to police communications. (Source: Flash #82)

According to the Reverse Flash, the reason Barry leaves his eyes exposed in his mask, rather than hiding them behind white lenses like in Wally West's, is because it allows people to trust him more. (Source: Flash #75)
When Barry Allen was a child, he was a massive comic-book fan. This went on to help inspire him become a superhero. (Source: Flash Rebirth)
In the future, Iris West writes a full biography of the Flash's life. (Source: Flash #79)
The Flash is capable of redirecting the heat generated from his speed onto his opponents. (Source: Flash #85)
When hitting light-speed, Flash can use his infinite-mass punch, which is supposedly strong enough to even hurt Superman. (Source: JLA #3)
When a Central City airport closed on Christmas Eve, due to a snowstorm, Flash used his speed to get everyone in the airport to their destinations on time. (Source: DC Holiday Christmas Special #1)
The Flash can run fast enough to suck the air out of the atmosphere. He's used this ability to knock out several opponents. (Source: Flash #210)
The Flash can vibrate the crystals in Altostratus clouds in a way that allows on him to run on them for a short time. (Source: Flash #26)

The Flash was able to phase his molecules through Supergirl when she was fighting him. This means that the Flash's phasing ability can overcome the near-impenetrable skin of kryptonians. (Source: Supergirl #16)
Wally West once ran on a treadmill built by the god-like "Blacksmiths of Mammord". It accelerated his pace to the speed of light squared, turning him into pure information. (Source: JLA #11)
The Flash once used his speed to recreate a shredded document piece by piece. (Source: Flash #103)
Wally West has claimed that a second can feel like hours to him, and a day can "become a lifetime". (Source: Flash #71)
Wally West is capable of using the speed-force as a weapon by holding it open and allowing its infinite energy to obliterate his opponent. (Source: Flash #155)
When Wally West first accessed the speed-force through Johnny Quick's speed-equation, he was able to practically make time stand still. (Source: Flash 1987 #91)
Flash once disassembled a car in midair, just before it could crash into a group of construction workers. (Source: Flash 2010 #1)
When Barry Allen runs fast enough, he's capable of creating massive wormholes. (Source: Flash 2011 #7)
Flash listens to audio-books while he runs, via an earpiece in his cowl. (Source: Flash 2016 #45)
The Flash was once able to extend his molecular-vibration frequency to a crashing plane, allowing it to phase through a bridge and land safely. (Source: The Flash 2011 #3)
Green Arrow:
Green Arrow once used Kyle Rayner's Green Lantern Ring. Though, he was only able to produce a single arrow. (Source: Green Lantern Rebirth #4)
Green Arrow once considered running for Mayor of Star City. (Source: Green Lantern #87)
Green Arrow knows how to cook the spiciest chili in the DC Universe. The only member of the Justice League that can eat it normally is Batman. (Source: Green Lantern #85)
Green Arrow has claimed that he can shoot 29 arrows per minute. In contrast, old English Archers could only shoot 12 arrows per minute. (Source: Green Arrow #12)
The reason that Green Arrow used to use boxing glove arrows was that he and Green Lantern were big boxing fans. (Source: Green Arrow #19)
Green Arrow provided Batman with training on how to be a skilled archer and marksmen. (Source: Green Arrow #134)
Green Arrow is capable of shooting multiple arrows at once. (Source: Green Arrow #28)
When the Arrow Car was stolen and about to be auctioned away, to a villain, Bruce Wayne managed to buy it as a favor for Green Arrow. (Source: Green Arrow #34)
During a trance induced by the plant "Black Mercy", it was revealed that Green Arrow's greatest wish is to be a great father. (Source: Green Lantern 2005 #8)

Green Arrow currently isn't a member of the Justice League. When offered membership, he proposed to become a "satellite member" instead, admitting that he wasn't the best "team player". (Source: Green Arrow 2016 #31)
Green Lantern:
Green Lantern is widely considered the greatest Green Lantern by the heroes of the DC Universe. (Source: Green Lantern Rebirth, Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps #22, Booster Gold #1)
Green Lantern Rings are often considered the greatest weapons in the DC Universe. (Source: Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps #20)
When John Stewart first became a Green Lantern he refused to wear a mask, saying he had "Nothing to hide." (Source: Green Lantern #87)

Hal Jordan's father died as a test-pilot in a plane crash. Though, rather than letting himself become scarred by the experience, Hal took it as a sign that there was nothing left to fear and went on to become a test-pilot himself. (Source: Green Lantern #29)
While Hal Jordan eventually became a test-pilot, he initially enlisted in the air-force on the day he turned 18. (Source: Green Lantern #29)

There are seven main human Green Lanterns: Alan Scott, Hal Jordan, Guy Gardner, John Stewart, Kyle Rayner, Simon Baz, and Jessica Cruz. (First Appearances: All American Comics #16, Showcase #22, Green Lantern #59, Green Lantern #87, New 52 Free Special Edition #1, and Justice League #31)
During the prime of his Green Lantern career, he was capable of using his ring to split atoms, turn blood to gasoline, and stop the Earth from spinning. (Source: Action Comics #784)

John Stewart was initially an architect turned Green Lantern. However, after the success of the Justice League cartoon, he was retconned as having been both an architect and a Marine Sniper veteran. (Source: Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps #20)

The yellow weakness in the Green Lantern rings is actually just an impurity, best distilled as fear, inserted to keep the Lanterns from becoming to powerful and corrupt. Willpower can overcome this impurity. (Source: Green Lantern #1)
One of Hal Jordan's favorite features on his ring is the ability to mute Guy Gardner's transmission. (Source: Green Lantern #7)
There are 3601 sectors of space for the Green Lantern Corps to protect in the DC Universe. Each sector has at least two Green Lanterns assigned to it. (Source: Green Lantern #11, Green Lantern #21)
When a Green Lantern dies, they get put in an Oan coffin and sent through a portal to the "Crypts of Oa". (Source: Green Lantern Corps #3)
The average lifespan of a Green Lantern is four years, three months, one day, thirteen hours, and seven minutes. (Source: Green Lantern #27)
Because Green Lantern is the man without fear, he thinks horror movies are funny and hates watching them. (Source: Green Lantern #23)
Guy Gardner once mooned Batman. Batman's response was simply that Guy Gardner needed to shave. (Source: Green Lantern Corps Recharge #1)

The Green Lantern Corps was initially blocked from using lethal force with their Green Lantern rings. However, this block was disabled by the Guardians of the Universe during the Sinestro Corps War. (Source: Green Lantern #23)
Green Lantern rings double as universal translators. This allows Green Lanterns to easily communicate with other alien lifeforms. (Source: Green Lantern #15)
Green Lantern's ring is capable of channeling kryptonite radiation. (Source: DC Presents #26)
Hal Jordan once used his ring to hold the continents in place, when aliens attempted to terraform Earth. (Source: JLA Year One #10)

After losing Abin Sur's ring, Hal Jordan forged himself a new ring out of his own willpower. It's purely powered by his will and is an extension of himself. (Source: Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps #38)

Hal Jordan has wielded the rings of every Lantern Corps, except for the Star Sapphires and the Indigo Tribe. They represent love and compassion, respectively. (Sources: Green Lantern Corps #59, Green Lantern #38, #39, #42, #50, Blackest Night #8)
Green Lantern Rings allow for faster-than-light travel. The rings also compensate for special relativity's time-warping effects. (Source: Justice League 2016 #41)
Over his years of being a Green Lantern, Hal Jordan has become a skilled forensic detective. (Source: Green Lantern 2011 #25)

During a trance induced by a plant called the "Black Mercy", it was revealed that Hal Jordan's greatest wish is to have a life where he's still friends with Sinestro, and his father is still alive. (Source: Green Lantern 2005 #8)
Joker:
The Joker suffers from "super-sanity". This explains why he has so many different personalities. (Source: Serious House on a Serious Earth)
Joker was written to die in his first appearance. However, an editor decided to bring him back for more stories after the fact. (Source: Batman #1)
Joker has said that his goal in torturing Batman is to make him a sharper opponent. (Source: Batman a Death in the Family)
On Earth 3, there's an alternate heroic version of the Joker known as "the Jokester". (Source: Countdown to Final Crisis #32)
The Joker once refused to help the Red Skull after finding out he was a Nazi, saying "I may be a criminal lunatic, but I'm an American criminal lunatic." (Source: Batman/Captain America)
The Joker once tried and failed to terrorize Metropolis. When Superman asked him why he'd bothered, the Joker answered, "Why not?" (Source: Superman #9)
The first thing Joker ever said to Batman was, "You! Prepare to die!" (Source: Batman #1)
It's been implied that the Joker knows Bruce Wayne is Batman, but that he only cares about Batman. (Source: Batman #429, Batman #680, Batman #17)
In the aftermath of Jason Todd's death, the Joker went temporarily sane out of remorse. (Source: Batman #451)
When Scarecrow terrorized Batman and Joker with a nightmare toxin, Joker's greatest nightmare was a world where everyone saw him as a joke. (Source: Superman/Batman #65)
When Martian Manhunter traveled through the Joker's mind, he discovered there was still peace and love buried at the center of it. (Source: JLA #35)

The Joker has claimed on numerous occasions that he loves Batman, and that he believes Batman is in love with him. Though, there's no telling if he was "joking" or not. (Source: Death of the Family, Batman #625)

The Joker once obtained the powers of Myxyptlk, effectively becoming a God. He used these powers to endlessly torture Batman to death, until Superman proved that Joker couldn't bring himself to fully erase Batman and was thus still subservient to his influence. (Source: Superman Emperor Joker)

After thinking he killed Batman, Joker went sane. He supressed memories of his crimes, had surgery, fell in love, got a job as an accountant, and adopted the identity of Joseph Kerr. (Source: Legends of the Dark Knight Joker Going Sane)
The Joker defeated Aquaman in a fight, and terrorized Atlantis. Aquaman ultimately had to enlist the help of Batman to defeat him. (Legends of DC #26)
The Joker's plans are so intricate that the Riddler has admitted that he isn't capable of understanding them. (Source: Batman #15)
Joker once defeated Deathstroke by goading him with a hostage, and then shooting him with a poison dart. He left the antidote behind, as a presumed joke. (Source: Deathstroke 1991 #58)
Justice League:
The Watchtower is located 22,300 miles above Earth. (Source: Justice League #30)
In their first origin story, the Justice League united to stop an evil alien race called the Apellaxians. (Source: JLA #9)
Before they were best friends, Kyle Rayner and Wally West were initially distrustful of one another. (Source: JLA Vol. 1)
In the New 52, there was a time when Superman and Wonder Woman dated. (Source: Justice League #13)
During Martian Manhunter's time in the Justice League, the Justice League would use his telepathic abilities to communicate via "telepathic links". (Source: JLA #32)

While the Justice League has often been funded and managed by Batman, there was a time when it was funded and managed by the evil businessman "Maxwell Lord". (Source: Justice League International Vol. 1)
The Justice League once tried having a Thanksgiving Dinner with the Justice Society. However, it was raided by supervillains, and they ended up needing to order pizza. (Source: JSA #54)
The Trinity has a secret room in the Watchtower called "the Lounge", where they conduct secret meetings. (Source: JLA #21)
Wonder Woman and John Stewart came up with the designs for the Hall of Justice, and Bruce Wayne paid for its construction. (Source: JLA #7)
According to Green Arrow, after the Justice League has a successful mission, they celebrate by getting beer and take-out pizza. (Source: Green Arrow #46)
The Justice League regularly allows for public tours throughout the Hall of Justice. (Source: JLA #32)
The Justice League Watchtower is designed to be able to repair itself from damage. (Source: JLA #71)
The Justice League Watchtower has a special training room called "the Kitchen". Its function is to simulate combat scenarios via holograms. (Source: JLA #18)
Lex Luthor:
Lex Luthor lost his hair due to an explosion when he was younger, while testing Kryptonian tech. (Source: Superman Birthright)
Lois Lane used to date Lex Luthor. (Source: Man of Steel #4)
After the death of New 52 Superman, Lex Luthor took his place to honor his legacy. (Source: Justice League #52)
Batman used to own the Daily Planet, but it was later bought out by Lex Luthor. (Source: Batman Hush, Justice League #52)
Lex Luthor knows Bruce Wayne is Batman. He proved it by blowing a hole in Wayne Manor's passageway to the Batcave. (Source: Justice League #31)
Lex Luthor knows how to cure cancer. However, rather than sharing his knowledge with the world, he chooses to keep it to himself. (Source: Justice League #41)
When Lex Luthor was 15, he lived in Smallville and made a temporary friendship with Clark Kent. (Source: Superman Birthright #7)
Lex Luthor has admitted that, "all things being equal", Superman will always win and the only way to defeat him is by "taking him off his game". (Source: JLA 2006 #14)
Martian Manhunter:
Superman has called Martian Manhunter the strongest being on Earth (Source: Justice League #20)
Martian Manhunter once regenerated his entire body from just his arm. (Source: Martian Manhunter #8)
Martian Manhunter once morphed the shape of his brain, so that he could understand the way Joker thinks. (Source: JLA Rock of Ages)
Martian Manhunter has shown himself capable of fighting the entire Justice League single-handedly, on multiple occasions. (Source: Justice League #8, Martian Manhunter #2)

Due to being the detective "John Jones" in his free-time, Martian Manhunter was suspicious of the Justice League when he first heard about them. So he compiled files on them, similar to Batman's. (Source: JLA #50)
While humans only have five basic senses, Martian Manhunter claimed he has nine basic senses. (Source: JLA Year One #6)
Martian Manhunter has an honor code against altering the minds of others. He claims that "there is no greater violation". (Source: JLA 1997 #115)
Nightwing:
Nightwing preferred living in Gotham lofts over Wayne Manor, because it brought him closer to the part of the city that needed saving. (Source: Nightwing #1)
Dick Grayson decided to become the superhero Nightwing after Superman told him a story about a Kryptonian vigilante of the same name. (Source: Nightwing #102)
During Grayson's training as Robin, Batman taught him to take advantage of his surroundings, and his enemy's lack of focus. (Source: Nightwing #23)
When Batman and Nightwing first fought, Nightwing managed to make it a draw. However, Nightwing was so distraught that he considered himself having lost the fight. (Source: Batman #600)
Nightwing once tried building his own car for crime-fighting out of spare parts from a junkyard. (Source: Nightwing #16)
Nightwing and Starfire almost became married, but their wedding was crashed at the last minute. (Source: New Titans #100)
Due to owning "the Grayson Family Circus", and a trust fund from his parents, Dick Grayson is assumed to have a net-worth of several million dollars. (Source: Nightwing #13 and #16)

When Bruce Wayne died, Dick Grayson replaced him and made Damian Wayne his sidekick. After Bruce's return, Grayson initially intended to keep Damian as his sidekick, but was too afraid of becoming a "dad". (Source: Nightwing #20)
Batman has said that, aside from Alfred, Nightwing knows him better than anybody else. (Source: Batman #2)
Nightwing's grandfather, William Cobb, was the leader of an evil conspiracy known as "the Court of Owls". In secret, he bred Dick to be their ultimate leader. (Source: Nightwing #9)
Despite his grievances over his career as Robin, Dick Grayson still keeps his old Robin costume in his closet. (Source: Nightwing #14)
Despite hating guns, Batman trained young Dick Grayson to be a skilled marksman so he'd "know more than the punks who rely on guns for courage." (Source: Nightwing 1996 #33)
In his spare time, Dick Grayson writes crime fiction. However, none of it is published. (Source: Nightwing 1996 #40)
Plastic Man:

Plastic Man is virtually "unkillable". After being shot back in time 3,000 years, he survived as scattered pieces on the ocean floor. He wasn't revived until he returned to modern times. (Source: JLA 1997 #76)
Robin:
Batman has admitted that Robin is faster than him. (Source: Robin Year One)
Dick Grayson was given the nickname "Robin" from his mother, because he was always "Bobbin' Along". This was a reference to the song, "Comes Bob, Bobbin' Along". (Batman: Dark Victory)
Every Robin has died, except Dick Grayson. (Source: Death of the Family, Detective #809, Batman Incorporated #8, and Detective Comics #940)
Tim Drake designed a subway that would be able to take Batman to any point in Gotham in a matter of seconds. (Source: Detective Comics #937)
Dick Grayson became Robin during the third year of Batman's career. (Source: Batman #436)
Years before Jason Todd was killed by the Joker, Dick Grayson was nearly killed with a baseball bat by Two-Face. (Source: Robin Year One #2)
Tim Drake, Batman's third Robin, was named after director Tim Burton.
Dick Grayson has admitted that Tim Drake is a better tech-specialist than him, as well as an all-around better partner for Batman. (Source: Nightwing #6)

Tim Drake was initially the only Robin to have a living parent, until his father was killed by Captain Boomerang. Damian Wayne is currently the only Robin to have two living parents. (Source: Identity Crisis)

Inspired by Batman, Tim Drake devised a hit-list for various rogues. It was designed so that he could apprehend the right rogues at the right times by taking into account their threat levels, proximities, strengths, and weaknesses. (Source: Red Robin #14)
Tim Drake designed a taser suit for combat with more powerful opponents, which could release 100,000 volts of electricity. (Source: Robin #84)
Batman once took Dick Grayson on a mission with the Justice League. After Dick saved the day, Batman said Grayson would one day lead the Justice League. (Source: Justice League #51)
Red Hood:
When Deathstroke fought Red Hood, Red Hood had the option to kill him but opted not to. Though, at the time, Deathstroke had lost his healing factor. (Source: Deathstroke #16)
Red Hood was once able to sneak away from Supergirl, without her super-hearing detecting a thing. (Source: Supergirl #35)
Red Hood has a kryptonite bullet, which he stole from a vault in the Batcave. He almost used it to kill Bizarro, but decided against it. (Source: Red Hood and the Outlaws 2016 #7)
Once, when Jason Todd was sick with the flu, batman took the night off to comfort him and watch TV with him. (Source: Red hood and the Outlaws 2011 #3)
Red Tornado:
According to Batman, Red Tornado's interface is so complex that it can't fit on the Batcomputer. (Source: JLA 2006 #16)
Shazam:
Due to his magic and super-strength, Shazam was once able to knock out Superman in two punches. (Source: JLA #29)
Superman has said that he sees Shazam as his equal in every way. (Source: Action Comics #768)
Due to having the speed of Mercury, Shazam moves so fast that Flash once thought he had the speed-force. (Source: Flash 1987 #107)
Superboy:
Like his father, Jonathan Kent has super-speed. The Flash taught him special moves, to help hone his speed. (Source: Superman 2016 #45)
Supergirl:
Supergirl was killed by the Anti-Monitor in 1986. She wasn't officially brought back until 2004. (Source: Crisis on Infinite Earths, Superman/Batman Vol. 2)
When Supergirl first arrived on Earth, Wonder Woman took her to Themyscaria for several weeks of training. (Source: Superman/Batman #9)
Supergirl has claimed that she's stronger than Superman, due to years of yellow sun exposure in her escape pod to Earth. However, Superman says that he holds back. (Source: Superman #5)
Superman:
Superman once defeated Darkseid just by singing. (Source: Final Crisis)
Superman's cells supposedly produce anti-gravitions that allow him to fly. (Source: Superman Birthright)
Martha Kent knitted Superman's costume out of the blankets he came in, from Krypton. (Source: Superman Secret Origin)
Superman can see across the entire electromagnetic spectrum (Source: All-Star Superman and Whatever Happened to the Man of Tomorrow)
Superman has a son: Johnathan Kent. He's named after Superman's father, Pa Kent. (Source: Superman Rebirth #1)
Superman has a special ability known as the "Super Flare" (aka, "Solar Flare"), which allows him to generate a giant explosion. (Source: New 52 Superman #38)
Batman and Superman met as children, when Bruce Wayne's car broke down on a road-trip through Smallville. (Source: Superman/Batman Secret Files)
Despite having lost his powers at the time, Superman was able to calm a mugger and stop them from murdering somebody, at gunpoint. (Source: Superman #39)
Batman has said that Bruce Wayne is his mask, whereas Clark Kent has said that Superman is his mask. (Source: Batman #600, Trinity #2)
Superman and Spider-Man have fought in the omniverse before. However, Spider-Man ultimately lost. (Source: Superman vs. Spider-Man)
Superman's cape is made from the blanket that he was wrapped in when he arrived to Earth. (Source: DC Sneak Peek: Action Comics)
Superman used to produce a protective aura around his body, which is why his costume was never damaged. (Source: Superman #3)
Superman avoids getting his picture taken by vibrating his face to blur the image. (Source: Superman #2)
After Krypton exploded, its remains formed into a gas giant. Superman eventually visited it, with the help of Hawkman and Hawkwoman. (Source: Superman #18)
Superman was the person who named Batman's Justice League defense armor, "the Justice Buster". Batman initially named the armor "Fenrir". (Source: Batman Endgame)
Superman once called Batman, "the most brilliant man I've ever met." (Source: Action Comics #784)
Superman once tried creating peace for a day. However, he eventually realized that he couldn't solve every Earth issue on his own. (Source: Superman Peace on Earth)
On Earth One, Martha Kent convinced Superman not to wear a mask so that people could know there was nothing to fear. (Source: Superman Earth One Vol. 1)
Despite being an award-winning journalist, Superman's Clark Kent identity has also successfully pursued a career as a novelist. (Source: Superman Under the Sun)
Superman has no need to eat and never gets hungry, due to the fact that he obtains all his energy from the sun. (Source: Superman #14)
Superman shaves by reflecting his heat vision onto his face, from a piece of rocket metal. (Source: Man of Steel #4)
When Superman needs a quick recharge of his powers, he often flies himself close to the sun. (Source: Superman #13)
There's an alternate universe where a random person named "Clark Kent" coincidentally develops powers identical to Superman. (Source: Superman Secret Identity)

When Superman was a kid, his eyes would emit random bursts of heat vision. So, Martha Kent designed him his glasses out of the crystals in his spaceship to block the heat-vision. (Source: Superman Secret Origin)
The first person that Superman revealed his powers to, outside of his family, was his high school sweetheart Lana Lang. (Source: Superman All For Seasons, Superman Secret Origin)
Lead can protect Superman from Kryptonite radiation. Batman once designed Superman a lead-lined suit, to allow Superman to collect kryptonite and dispose it. (Source: Superman/Batman #44)

During the 90s, Superman absorbed too much energy from a sign, and was turned into living energy. He had to put himself in a containment suit to control himself, and his new energy-based powers. This was part of DC's attempt to give Superman a new look and was dubbed "the Electric Blue Superman". (Source: Superman #123)

When the Daily Planet ran out of funds to give presents to children in need, Batman and Superman teamed up to give them a good Christmas. Batman provided a large check for the gifts and Superman, hiding, used his powers to fly "Santa" and his sleigh in for the kids. (Source: Superman #64)

In the "Injustice" universe, Superman killed the Joker and became an evil despot after Joker killed Lois Lane. In the "Kingdom Come" universe, Superman vowed not to kill Joker, and instead exiled himself in the Fortress of Solitude for several decades. (Source: Kingdom Come Special #1)
Superman was the first choice to inherit Abin Sur's ring. However, he was later deemed ineligible due to not being a native of sector 2814. (Source: Action Comics #642)
Clark Kent was hired at the Daily Planet for getting the first exclusive interview with Superman. (Source: Man of Steel #3)
When Superman was infected by a Doomsday virus, his power levels were amplified to such an extent that he was able to fly into a black hole and survive. (Source: Superman Doomed #2)

In the editor's page of 1966's Action Comics #340, an editor revealed that Superman's SSN was 092-09-6616. This SSN initially belonged to Giobatta Baiocchi, but he died a year prior to the issue's release. (Source: Action Comics 3340)
Superman keeps life-model decoys of Clark Kent in his apartment closet, in case he ever needs to be Clark Kent and Superman at the same time. (Source: Superman Confidential #5)
When Superman first went back into action, the people of Earth assumed he was just a very powerful man, rather than an alien. (Source: Superman/Batman #13)
Superman once used Hawking's discovery of "Hawking Radiation" to help himself escape from a near-impenetrable force-field. (Source: Superman/Batman #80)
In addition to red sun radiation, sonic blasts, kryptonite, and magic, Superman is also vulnerable to psionic attacks. (Source: Superman #22)
Superman can recognize Batman's heartbeat from thousands of miles above Earth. He claims to know it as well as Lois Lane's. (DC Metal #2)
Superman's X-Ray vision doesn't work on Arkham Asylum, due to its architecture being full of lead pipes. (Source: Justice League 2011 #9)
Nightwing once said that, despite Batman's claims to the contrary, "Superman is the most human guy I've ever met." (Source: Nightwing 1997 #30)

Superman's favorite movie is "To Kill a Mockingbird". Dan Jurgens (comic writer) said he chose this movie because he saw Superman being inspired by Gregory Peck's performance as Atticus Finch. (Source: Superman 1987 #81)

Joker once nearly convinced Superman to break his moral code and kill him, after poisoning Lois and placing the antidote in his bloodstream. Batman narrowly stopped Superman, and the poison was later discovered to be non-lethal. (Source: Action Comics #719)

During Infinite Crisis, Superman fought an alternate version of himself from Earth 2. Due to the entire DC Universe already being in imbalance, their punches shattered space and time. (Source: Adventures of Superman #649)
Wonder Woman:
Wonder Woman has super speed granted to her by the gods. (Source: Tower of Babel)
Wonder Woman has defeated Batman in combat before, and Batman has even admitted that she has no known weakness. (Source: Wonder Woman Hiketeia, Justice League #20)
Wonder Woman comforted Batman when Superman died, and comforted Superman when Batman died. (Source: Justice League #0)
Wonder Woman was Harley Quinn's childhood hero. (Source: Harley's Little Black Book #1)
Because he always thinks in opposite, Bizarro was once able to break the Lasso of Truth. (Source: Matt Wagner's Trinity)
Wonder Woman was initially going to be named Suprema, but the name was changed in order to avoid confusion with Superman.
When Wonder Woman was born, she was granted seven gifts from the gods: the eye of a hunter, a loving heart, wisdom, strength, speed, flight, and sisterhood. (Source: Wonder Woman #1)
The Amazons have a special "Themyscarian Concrete" they use, which is as strong as Superman's skin. (Source: Superman #40)
In the New 52, whenever Wonder Woman removed her bracelets, she was capable of accessing an inner God-mode. (Source: Wonder Woman #12)

Despite Superman's superior strength, due to her extensive training and magical weapons Wonder Woman has bested him in combat on many occasions. Batman has even acknowledged she's a superior fighter. (Source: Wonder Woman #219, JLA #27, Justice League #11, Trinity #14)
In the "New 52" timeline of the DC Universe, Wonder Woman didn't reveal herself to the world until modern day. (Source: Justice League Vol. 1)
Wonder Woman's lasso can tell her the best pressure points to hit her enemies at. (Source: JLA #61)
Wonder Woman was once able to withstand an explosion from a nuclear missile. (Source: Wonder Woman #31)
Wonder Woman once put a spell over her lasso that allowed herself, Martian Manhunter, and Superman to tow the weight of the Earth. (Source: JLA #75)
Before the New 52, Wonder Woman wasn't bulletproof. She could be harmed by firearms and very sharp arrowheads. (Source: Wonder Woman Secret Files)
Wonder Woman helped deliver Superman and Lois Lane's son, Jonathan Kent, in the Fortress of Solitude. (Source: Action Comics #977)
Despite her potential to become a god like her relatives, Wonder Woman chooses to hold back to avoid abusing her power. (Sorce: Wonder Woman #20)
Wonder Woman's lasso is capable of freeing people from mind control. (Source: JLA 2006 #20)
According to Batman, Wonder Woman is the "best melee fighter in the world." (JLA 2006 #13)

title: Checkmate Inmate
paragraphs: Why did overtaking the world have to be such a pain in the ass?

Darkness hounded at Dr. Savant. His ears rang. He closed his eyes to escape, only to be met by flickers of fire. Flashes of agony. His hand snapped to his forearm. A harsh burn was there. It was already an hour old, but the pain still stabbed.

Dr. Savant breathed in, then out. Meditation was key to overcoming pain. Large intakes of oxygen were all that the frontal lobe needed to be distracted by the external and remember the internal. Yes, the burn on his forearm was already starting to fade. It didn’t exist.
Iron shrilly scraped against iron. A clang resounded. Lights buzzed on. Dr. Savant recoiled and shielded his metal eye.
“Protecting your face with a cannon for an arm? Can’t imagine that’s comfy…”
It was officer Brent. His hands rested on his belt buckle, as he put on a doughy grin. Clones of him surrounded Dr. Savant in mirrors, in three directions.
“Yeah, well, you disabled them,” said Dr. Savant. “This is about the only thing I can do.”
“We could’ve let you do less. I wanted to have the boys handcuff you. The only reason you’re allowed to do anything is because the chief doesn’t want to step on any political toes.”
“Don’t worry: Tarkistan won’t be trying to take me back, any time soon.”
Brent nodded, but chewed on his bottom lip.
“Yeah, I’d imagine. First you try nuking America, then you try nuking your own country… You rule an entire country, and then try to nuke it? What’s the deal with that?”
“It wasn’t a nuke. It was a laser.”
“Good point. So, what’s your game plan? What are you hiding? Why did you let us arrest you?”

Dr. Savant suppressed a laugh. Brent’s speech was cold and mechanical. Yet, tinges of emotion seeped in. The room was so barren. Nonetheless, Brent walked around Dr. Savant, glowering. He moved as if he owned the room.
“Let you?” Dr. Savant said. “I thought you guys apprehended me. Thwarted my plan. That is, you guys, and ‘Captain Merit’. I’m sure that’s the story being put on the broadcasts, right?”
Brent leaned in, his jaw jutting. The heat of his breath bristled against Dr. Savant’s skin.

“I know your capabilities, doctor,” said Brent. “Guys like you don’t lose by accident. I see you come in and out of this place, like it’s a revolving door. And, each time, you seem more comfortable than the last.”
“Have to admit: you guys do make some mean eggs.”
Brent slammed the table. It shook, just for a moment.
“Answer me, doctor: why are you here?”
“I want to take over the world. But, since I can’t, I’ve started thinking: maybe just taking over this prison will do.”
Brent’s heartrate was pounding, ever so slightly. His face flushed red. His hand gravitated toward his taser. Dr. Savant merely leaned further back in his chair.

“I have a question for you, Brent. I terrorize my people — the country of Tarkistan. Then I come here. I try and fail to take over the world, a million times over. Every time, I’m barely beaten. Every time, you let me live. You put me in a cell. Why am I alive?”
Brent seethed. “Because, Captain Merit lets you live.”
“You guys could kill me at any time though. Shoot me, starve me, stick me in an electric chair. Why haven’t you?”
“We can’t. The law won’t let us. But, I’ll make sure of one thing: we don’t ever let you get away with your plan.”
“Sure you will, Brent. Sure you will.”
There was another buzz.
“Alright Brent, time’s up,” speakers warbled. “We have to throw him in confinement now, with the rest of the prisoners.”
Brent glared at Dr. Savant. “If you’re hiding a superweapon under your sleeve, be aware: this time, I’m going to find it. And, I’m going to make sure that we have you put on death row.”
Dr. Savant waved his cannon for an arm. “Goodbye, Brent,” he said. “Have a nice weekend.
Brent muttered something that Dr. Savant couldn’t quite hear.
The iron curtain creaked open. It clanged shut.
Another door creaked open, from behind Dr. Savant. There was the sound of applause, and cheers. Dr. Savant grinned and turned around. His arms outstretched, he sauntered ahead.
“Yes, that’s right: I have returned!”

He entered a cluster of crowd of inmates. Though, their eyes told a different story. They were audience members, and Dr. Savant was the star of the show. Bodyguards even flanked Dr. Savant’s side. Granted, the bodyguards were more for the inmates’ safety than Dr. Savant. Yet, was there really a difference?

title: Christian Mueth Summer 2026 Poems:
paragraphs: Life is like a painting: it’s however you want to interpret it.
Sweetness:
Oh, sweet nothing!
Your sweet nothings…
So sweet a thing.
My everything.
Panned:
Wendy darling,
Your eyes, sterling,
End me, darling!
Heart’s unfurling.
Kiss. Ease hooks in me.
Miss. Please set me free!
Play pretend…
Say you’ll miss me.
In the end…
It’s my one plea!
Binary Systems:
Not all things are binary.
Some things are analog.
Many find this scary.
Can’t fit their boxy blog.
Many are analog and binary.
Some things are somehow not, given that.
It’s totally all arbitrary.
Come with me and put on a mad hat.
It Tracks:
Tonight’s moon is blue,
I drive out seeking,
A train and its tracks.
So much I must do,
And I am screeching,
For what my soul lacks.
I haven’t a clue,
How it’s still leaking.
One more of its acts?
Star Woven:
Stars twinkle. Planets gleam.
Space crinkles at the seam.
Smirk. Inkle. In a dream …
Shadowed and Cornered:
In the corner of my eye,
On the ceiling to the sky,
A chase abounds, until I find,
Elusive shadow, undefined.

title: Click-Clack
paragraphs: By Christian Mueth

I'm one out of a poll of millions. I'm every voice that has ever been drowned out by the crowd. I'm every murderer that ever got away. I'm every person who's ever worn a mask. I'm every mask that never had a person to wear it.
I'm faceless.
It's December of 1953, midnight. It's the 13th day of the month. Or, is it still the twelfth? I've always had bad luck with dates...

I suppose it doesn't matter. It's frigid cold. So much so that it pierces skin. It strips the trees. Even the roads weather down to the — well — weather. Nights like these are what go on to haunt the world. Jack Frost is a creature that works most viciously in the dark.
A baby has been born. A shriek ripples from the hospital room. Shrieks. Except, these shrieks don't come from the baby. No... Not from the baby, but the mother. The nurse. The doctor.

The cold reception of this newborn baby is far colder than the winter climate could ever be. However, it isn't unjustified. See, the baby has been born with no face. There isn't a hint of a facial feature on him — no mouth, no eyes, no nose... Nothing. Just a patch of smooth skin where a face should've been.

According to the doctor and the nurses, he has no chance of living. The many dozens of doctors and nurses that will follow give the same diagnosis. However, they're all wrong. According to me, this baby will live. Or, at least, it'll go on to endure something that resembles "living". By what basis do I make that diagnosis?
That monstrosity of a baby was me.

Such an odd thing, really... A baby being born without a face. Nobody bets on that. Nobody would ever bet on such a baby surviving either. Somehow, I exceeded all expectations. I suppose that means I won the lottery? Something like that...

"You're lucky to be alive." I used to hear it all the time. It was said so often that I sometimes found myself wondering if it was the only thing that people knew how to say. Repetitive phrases like that simply get under my skin. It's one of the reasons why I don't like people very much. People might've been looking to placate me. But what they never realized is that, every time that they used those phrases, it was like bringing a hot iron to my feet. I'm not alive, despite most medical definitions stating the contrary. Can you truly be alive if you can't see? Breathe? Eat? Speak? Smell? Even smile?
Many see my survival as some miracle. I hear it as a curse.

Yes — I hear it. Despite not having facial features of any kind, I was still born with ears. They're my sole window into the world, and I treasure them. However, I've found that even my ears betray me at times... While my other senses might have never shown me the things they should've, my ears have shown me things they probably shouldn't have.

Take right now, for instance. It's raining. I hate the rain... It dulls my ears and makes the whole world murky. Yet, if it wasn't for the rain, I would be able to perfectly hear somebody having a hushed conversation in a phone booth behind me. A conversation about a funny looking man who has no face. I'm glad the rain has spared me from fully hearing the laughing. Or how hideous I apparently look. Or how I should be penned up in a circus. If I had, I would've known that my true story is lost to them. I would be compelled to share my true story, in full.
Yes... I'm very thankful that I never heard them.

It's still raining. But, I'm in the bus now. Rain is just a backdrop to hushed chatters, loud snores, the slight squeak of the steering wheel as it turns, and the heaving of the driver who's turning it. It feels as if everybody is being lulled to sleep. However, it always feels that way in the bus, to some extent. Everybody prefers to dream, because nobody knows where they're going. Not really. People get on the bus and tend to get off whenever they "feel" it's right. They're hardly ever right though. Nobody is ever right.
Except me.
I know exactly where I'm going. I'm wide awake, even if I don't have wide eyes to prove it. Where I'm going, I'm never going to hear things the same way again.

The bus screeches to a halt. The doors lazily swing open. It's my stop. I can tell by the sound of the guitarist strumming a tune and shaking his plastic cup down the sidewalk. It's been a long time since I last heard his awful music. However, our routine hasn't changed. I clutch my typewriter tightly as I step off the bus. The driver yells something at me that I ignore. The guitarist comes up to me, speeding up his strumming. I refuse to tip him and pull my hood over my head. He goes back to his corner and refuses to stop playing.
I begin calculating my every stride. I can't let myself mess up. I grew up on this block. I know it like the back of my hand. Which I admittedly don't know very much — but, for the sake of argument…

I turn as I reach the entrance to my destination. Though, when I do, I slam into a brick wall. Pain shoots up my body. That definitely wasn't there last time. I must've miscalculated. Maybe I took a step too wide? A step too short? It doesn't matter. I'm left groping around like an idiot, until I finally find the entrance. The door creaks open. The door creaks shut. Soft jazz music spills into my ears. Too soft. I can hear the static in each note. The music must be coming from a speaker, overhead.

I can also hear bread crackling as it's cut by a knife. There's a light chewing. The stir of a whisk in a bowl. Then, there's running water, followed by the sound of something being rubbed against a cloth. Somebody just finished washing their hands.

I'm in a bakery. I can hear it. Something that I can't hear is the frantic bustling of a thriving business. Nobody is in here, except me, one other person, and an irksome emptiness. Granted, the emptiness didn’t choose to be here. The truth is, I haven’t been in this building for a while. The last time I was, it was a pawn shop. However, that was before it was bought out and revamped by the only person who'd play jazz music in a bakery—
"Mack!" I punch out on my typewriter.

I can hear him walking to the counter. I recognize him by the jingling of coins and a pocket knife in his pocket, as well as the sound of his flip flops slapping against the ground. Still not sure why he always insisted on wearing flip flops in the fall, in the middle of the city.
I slam my typewriter on the counter, and let Mack read off the paper.
"Frank!" he exclaims, reaching over the counter to slap me on the back — a lot harder than he needs to, but not as hard as he must want.
I nod. Then, the room surrenders to the sound of self-motorized mixers, and rising bread. Mack doesn't say a word, and I don't lay a finger on my typewriter.
Mack's breathing intensifies.
I can tell that my presence is unnerving, and that he's just moments away from sweating buckets.
Mack clears his throat.
"So... So! So..." he says. "I haven't seen you in years. In fact, I think that I was still in high school when we last met! And, I see that you've still kept the typewriter after all of these years!"
Mack lets out a chuckle. I return the chuckle with dead silence.
Only silence.
Mack's flip flops squeal. He's turned around so that he doesn't have to face me.
"Man... I was really rough on you back then, wasn't I?"
The room echoes with a screech as I drag the typewriter back to myself.  My fingers press along the keys, my heart skipping a beat at the completion of each word.

"Every morning you and your friends would corner me," the paper reads. "Then, you'd knock me to the ground, and kick me until I wouldn't move, or couldn't move. Whichever came first. On the mornings when that wasn't enough for you, you'd shove cotton in my ears until there was enough to make it so that I couldn't hear. Every morning. Until I finally learned your names, and how to hide."
I tear the paper off and slide it across the counter. Mack is forced to turn back around. And, I pull my hood off to force him to look at me.

I don't have the pleasure of seeing Mack's reaction — the inevitable mixture of horror and regret. I would pay anything to see it. But, the clamminess of Mack's hand as he hands the paper back is enough to tell me everything I need.

"I—I'm sorry," Mack says, tripping over his words. "That was a long time ago. I wasn't the same person then. I know that I can never make it up to you, but trust me when I say this: if I could take back what I and my friends did to you, I would."
Mack taps my hand with his, attempting to get me to shake it. I don't.
"What brought you here anyway?" Mack asks, adopting a harsh tone that's all too familiar.
I want to write more and force him to face the fact that he’d terrorized somebody who couldn't run. Couldn't fight back. Couldn't even see his face. But, I don't. I can't. I write something else.

"Six months ago, Bill died. It made me think back to you. You were his closest friend. I know that you bought the pawn shop — the only place that I was ever able to hide from you — just to slight me. But I want to put our rivalry to rest. I know how hard things must be for you. We should have closure."
Mack lets out a short laugh after he’s torn the paper away and read it.
"Thanks. That means a lot. You know... I miss Bill. But something that has been helping me get through it is in realizing how lucky we are for every minute that we get to be alive."
I don't have the heart to tell him, but some people are luckier than others.

When I reunited with Mack, an old wound flared up with fresh pus. All it took was the sound of his voice to return me to the past... To pound my face back into the gravel. Even thinking back on his voice now, I shudder.

I used to think that nightmares muffle away when you get older. Though, I was only half right. Nightmares certainly muffle. But, never away. They simply stop occurring at night. They stop occurring as dreams.

Though, the nightmare that Matt's voice brought is dull, compared to the nightmares that I get as the backs of leaves snap under my feet. Or the nightmares as ambulances whiz by. Or as the wind nips at my skin.
Or as the warmth of lights brushes against me and I enter a waiting room.
I walk up to the hospital's waiting room desk. Show them a note that I wrote. They take it, and then tell me an address. I leave. I don't come back. I'll never come back.

I'm gripping the upholstery of a greasy seat, trying my hardest to ignore a persistent click. It comes from the engine of the taxi-cab. Clearly, the engine doesn't have much longer. Yet, as the clicking continues, I no longer hear it coming from the engine. It morphs. It now comes in the form of a hazy memory... A sound… I remember the disapproving voice of a doctor...
It’s another nightmare. I need to get it out of my head. That was too long ago. I can't keep letting it —
"Uh..." the taxicab driver says.
The car's tires squeal, and my stomach lurches as I'm thrust to the side.
"Sorry! Sorry!" the driver says, nervously.
I can only pray that he doesn't drive into a river before I'm let out.
"What's with your face?" he asks.
I ignore him. I need to ignore... Forget.
I feel along my seatbelt. It's frayed. On the verge of breaking. I might as well have not put it on.
I feel around my seat. There are a few wrappers laying around. A piece of gum stuck to the leather. And... An old sandwich?
There's a roar as an obnoxious motorcyclist rides by. The honking of a horn. Enraged shouts.
The city is beautiful, indeed. Yet it occurs to me that, while I've heard it, I've never seen its true face. It's just as faceless to me as I am to it.

I'm not sure how much time passes — time for me has only ever been the steady ticking of a clock, anyway — but the car screeches to a halt as the driver slams on the breaks. I grab my typewriter and stumble out the door. I've reached my stop.
I climb up several flights of stairs. I start down a long hall. My fingers feel along the numbers plastered on each door. Then, they feel the one they're looking for. I stop walking.
A few knocks. A few seconds. The door creaks open.
"Frank!" somebody exclaims, as they open the door.
It's my former doctor, Adrian Conroy. I could recognize his voice anywhere.
"This is completely unexpected! What brings you here?" he asks. "How did you find me?"
I remain facing his direction, taking great care not to move. To not even allow a flinch.
"Well... Come in! Come in!"

I follow him into his room. Dr. Conroy has always liked to make a point that he lives in a wealthy neighborhood and makes a high salary. His apartment must be lavishly decorated. Though, walking through the apartment, I can't tell how it’s different from any other. The sound of my feet against the ground is the same as it would be anywhere else.
"I would offer food, but..."
Dr.  Conroy lets out a laugh, before dragging something across the floor.
"Come. Sit.
I do. I settle in, and Conroy lets out another laugh. However, this laugh is shriller than the last.
"You brought your typewriter. I'm glad! It's funny to think that, out of all the means of communication I tried with you, the typewriter is the one that stuck."
My fingers clack against the keys.
"You credit yourself for far more than you actually deserve."
I tear the paper off. Hand it to him.
Dr. Conroy isn't like Mack. There are some people who are despicable, but hopelessly stupid and cowardly. Dr. Conroy was of a far more cunning breed. A breed of his own.
There's no other person that makes me seethe more than he does.
"Oh, Frank," he says. "I've done everything that I can to help you. I don't know where you got the idea that I haven't. Tell me... Did you come all this way just to write me that lie?"
"Your nurses came up with all the ideas for how to help me. You were paid millions to cure me by millions of people. And, this room is ultimately what you did with all of it."
This time, Conroy tears off the paper. He rips it off hardly after I manage to finish it.  Then, he crumples it. He lets a silence stew.
"You have the wrong idea, Frank. I can promise you that I did everything that I could. And, besides — I wasn't being paid to cure you. Not by most. Most people know that you're incurable..."
Dr. Conroy gives a sigh. I can taste the pity seeping from it. I want to gag.

"I was being paid to study you. You're a strange specimen... Every mammal needs to be able to eat and breathe. You can't do either. And somehow, you're still here. I can't figure out how you've done it, for the life of me... But I shouldn't be blamed if I spent millions to at least try."
My pulse hammers through my fingertips as I punch the keys on the typewriter.
"We were shoved onto every talk show and news outlet. On each one, you promised that you had a cure coming. And, you never even tried. You were just dissecting me like a frog."
Dr. Conroy clicks his tongue.
"Let's not forget that your parents were the ones who authorized those media appearances. Frank, I couldn't just—."
I click the keys.
"You never even tried."
Dr. Conroy stands up and paces around me. I'm clueless as to what he's doing. I don't even want to have a clue.

"I spent decades building a reputation," Dr. Conroy said. "I used to think that I could help people. I really did. Then, you came along... You were famous. I was famous enough to be your doctor. That's all there was to it. The unfortunate truth is that you spit in the face of all modern medical science. Maybe I should've tried harder, cut the experiments, and focused all my resources on an elusive cure for you. But, here's the thing: you're not natural. You're probably something that supersedes that. And, if that's the case... You're a hopeless case."
If I could, I would smile. Instead, I begin clapping my hands. I give him the applause he so desperately craves.
I've waited all my life for him to finally admit that he never tried. That he just gave up.

"I know I'm a freak," I type. "I know that I can't be cured. But... I also know that you've been lying to me. To yourself. To everybody. And, you've been doing it for the past twenty years. You never wanted to help people. You wanted fame. And what you forgot was that, unless you're lucky, fame always comes at a cost."
Conroy rips the paper from the typewriter.
"Is that a threat, Frank?"
I type some more.
"No. But, this is: Bill Graham was murdered six months ago. Mack Goodman was murdered last Tuesday. I hated both of those men. Guess which man I hate even more."
"Are you insinuating that you killed those men?"
I nod. I think myself clever too. At least, until Conroy speaks again.
"And, what do you think you're going to do to me? You can't see me. And, even if you can kill me, you'll never get away with it. Everybody knows who I am!"
I type my last note.
"That's why I'll get away. Everybody knows your face. Too many people. But mine? Nobody knows mine."
Conroy doesn't bother reading the note. He knocks my typewriter out of my hands. Lunges at me. Claws at my head. But I pull out my pistol. The trigger clicks.
He's dead.
Nobody knows what I am. Some people like to call me a miracle. Some people call me a curse. Dr. Conroy would've called me a mix of both.
They're all wrong.

I'm one out of a poll of millions. I'm every voice that has ever been drowned out by the crowd. I'm every person who's ever worn a mask. I'm every mask that never had a person to wear it. I'm every murderer that ever got away.
I'm faceless.
End

title: Dual-Man
paragraphs: By Christian Mueth
Some say heroes are born. Others say that they’re made. I believe that heroes are posers, all imitating one another. Jerking themselves off to themselves.

But I guess I’m no different. I have a sweet body and own a mansion. Yet here I am, crawling through a grimy ventilation shaft to save some chick. What was her name again? Jessie Johnson, Daisy Doe, or some crap like that... We kissed once. That’s all I remember.

The shaft’s walls groan under my weight, and crease like tinfoil. I try adjusting my position, but my muscles are stiff boards. My tights chafe against my thighs and make a squeal along the metal. Head hammering, I slow my movements.

Something your marketing team never tells you about building huge muscles is that they’ll constantly get in your way. Same with the spandex. Plus, you can’t even see your muscle definition under spandex. But action figures need to be made, am I right?
I should’ve just followed Captain Casualty’s lead, and kept things casual… He somehow gets away with ratty T-shirts.

There’s a whir. A blast of air funnels through the shaft, and wafts into my face. I smack my lips — the air is musty. Dusty. My nostrils itch. Great — I can already feel them beginning to flare. My body ripples, straining to fight back the urge…
I sneeze.

Echoes reverberate through the shaft. I’m frozen. Though, maybe the sneeze seemed louder than it was. I have enhanced hearing. Yes — there’s no way I could’ve been heard from behind the metal. I glance at my immaculate reflection.
“It’s all good,” I say. “We’re cool.”
“Are you going to come down here to face me, or are you going to keep hiding?”
Shit. I could recognize that heavy-handed speaking style anywhere.
The Harbinger. My sixth greatest nemesis.
I take in a deep inhale, inflating my chest.
“Don’t you worry, I’m coming down there,” I say, my voice still echoing within the ventilation shaft.

My fist reels back, before hurtling toward the shaft’s floor. There’s a magnificent crash. My eyes close and my stomach rises, as I anticipate my plummet from the shaft. Though, I’m only met with an upswell of pain in my wrist. Reopening my eyes, I see that the punch has just left a dent in the metal.
I shake my wrist and give another punch.
“Ah! God!”
It must be a special type of metal. Maybe the Harbinger finally discovered a material that renders me weak.
“You can’t even get out of an iron vent? How pathetic can you get?”

A blast goes off. The world oscillates, then slams into me. In a daze, I pull myself up from a concrete floor. I fan away a plume of dust and rubble with my cape. At least the cape is good for something.
Whipping my head around, I see the interior of a warehouse stretching from every side of me. Harsh lights beat throughout.
I clear my throat. “Dual-Man! Ready to duel!” I grin to myself.
It’d taken me an hour to come up with that line. Worth it.
“I foretold you’d be here,” the Harbinger says.
I turn around. The Harbinger is perched atop a ray-gun, wearing his stupid trench coat and demon mask.
“Oh yeah? Well, did you foretell this?”
I give a grunt and a spark runs through my body, followed by a blue glow. Nerves tingling, my hands almost seem to fold out of my skin. After a few moments, I’m split in two. Then four. Eight.
The Harbinger leaps from his ray-gun and begins shooting blasts of energy from his palms.
“You may be many, Dual-Man, but your intellect is no match for mine!”
I weave among the crowd of myself, laughing. “Ever hear the phrase, ‘two halves are better than one?’”
“That’s—.”
I give the Harbinger a clean sock to the jaw, knocking him to the ground. Adrenaline rushes through my body. Perfect way to end a conversation.
“Where are you holding her!?” I yell, from a hundred directions.
Feebly, the Harbinger points ahead. My girlfriend is behind an office’s window a few yards away, watching some movie on a TV. I wave. She yawns, her eyes remaining fixed to the screen.
“The door is unlocked for her, and everything,” says the Harbinger. “I didn’t want to be one of those sexist kidnappers.”
I nod. “Yeah, I hate those sons of bitches.”
I adjust my utility belt and unsnap a bottle from one of the flaps. My duplicates unsnap bottles of their own and begin spraying at the ray-gun.
“Anyway, your plan is over!” I say. “Good luck counteracting this anti-freeze I’ve developed!”
The Harbinger smiles at me, serenely. The ray-gun is whirring now, and its tip shines red.
“Anti-freeze? It’s a heat-ray.”
“Wait, what? In that scrambled message you sent… I thought you said it was a freeze-ray!”
“Well, the message was scrambled. Maybe you misheard?”
“Maybe you misspoke. I have enhanced hearing, man.”

The Harbinger is back to my level, staring me in the face. Meanwhile, my duplicates fumble at the ray gun, to no avail. A countdown has started on the front of the ray-gun, displaying only two minutes left. I pace in a circle and run my hand through my hair.
“It’s fine… It’s fine!” I say. “Mr. Man-Mantis is supposed to be here any minute. He’ll disable it.”
The Harbinger laughed. “He’s not coming.”
“Huh?”
“He didn’t tell you? He’s having knee-surgery, today.”
I whip out my cell-phone. “Guess I’ll see if Dexter-Hex…”
“Photo-shoot with the Sustainers.”
“The Banister?”
“I think he’s being replaced.”
I put my phone back. Sweat is beginning to form, and my spandex isn’t liking it. I pray that I can get out of this, and that my “Dual-Man Cologne” will be strong enough to hide my odor.

“Brilliant! Just brilliant!” I say. “What, did you think I had a computer degree? I can’t disable this thing! Do you know how much my ‘Dual-Man’ merchandise is going to tank, because of you? Just kill me now…”
The Harbinger rests his hand on my shoulder.
“It’ll be fine… Trent Turner.”
I step away and give him a glare. “How do you — how do you know who I am?”
“Well, for one, you look exactly like the billionaire Trent Turner.”
I nod. He has a point.
“And for another… Well…”
His mask and trench coat fall away.
“I’m you.”
I shake my head. It can’t be. But he’s now indistinguishable from the rest of my duplicates, save for a cruel smile on his face.
On my face…
“It doesn’t make sense,” I say.
Though, I can already see all my duplicates folding back into him. Now, it’s just me.
“Think about it. Why is it that I never try to kill you?”
“I thought you just had really bad aim…”

“It’s because I can never let this end, Trent. I can never let you end. Every time you punch me, the populous eats it up. So I spawn you — a copy. I wipe your mind of all memories. We fight. And in the end? They buy every action figure, comic book, and cereal that we throw at them… They get the conflict they secretly yearn for. We make millions.”
It can’t be. Yet, I feel my bones trembling. A spark flows from him to me. I know it’s true. “You’re every villain I’ve faced?” I ask.
“I’m also the hero that stops them.”
I take a step toward him.
“But… Countless lives...”
“Oh, Trent. I’ve never killed anybody. All of this… It’s all spectacle. Nothing more.”
“But, we could’ve used our powers for—.”
“For what? We create jobs. We inspire. And meanwhile, we prosper. What more could you want?”
I take another step. My mind merges into his. Memories come flooding back of hours spent building, planning, and strategizing. I’ve done this before, countless times.
I walk up to the ray-gun. I flip the off-switch.
“Time to do this again, countless more times.”
My girlfriend remains glued to the TV screen. The rubble remains stuck to the ground. The room rings, hollow. Though, I laugh.
Heroes are never truly born. Heroes are never truly dead.
Heroes are never, truly.
End

title: Ghost’s Story
paragraphs: By Christian Mueth

The house stooped, to glower over Mitchell. Panels along the house twisted into pretzels. A breeze went through, spinning its windows sideways, then turning them inside out. Mitchell’s stomach turned inside out with them.

Every home in Tyger’s Neighborhood was respectable; decent. A nuclear family’s favorite brand of white bread would be proud to live in one of them. Then, there was the house on the end of Galley Street. It was the scum stuck on the bottom of a shoe. Many had tried to scrape it away, but none ever succeeded.
The neighborhood had left a wood to grow around it and elected to ignore it. Yet, today, Mitchell couldn’t afford to.
“Mitch the bitch, you can run, but you can’t hide!” somebody called out.

Mitchell plucked the bloody thorns from his arms, then tried tucking his shirt back around his swollen waist. It wouldn’t budge — streams of sweat were set against him. He swept his ratty hair out of his eyes and dragged himself toward the front door to the house. The porch’s floorboards grumbled beneath his feet, cautioning him to turn back. A bolt of electricity shot from the sky, landing at Mitchell’s feet. Lightning? Mitchell looked to the sky — there wasn’t a cloud.
Hand hovering over the rusted doorknob, his heart flopped wildly against his ribcage. This couldn’t be worth it. Yet, there was the small but strong part of him that knew it was.
He pulled his trading card out from his pocket. He forced a smile. It was an “Iceblaster Dragon” — extremely powerful. He couldn’t just turn around and give it up.
He shook his head as he clasped his hand around the doorknob. It gave a small jolt. He didn’t care.
Barney and his cronies had already taken enough away from him.
“Come on, Mitch, dearest,” Barney said, putting on a tauntingly high voice. “Why don’t you come out and play, Mitchy? Lord knows you could use the exercise, baby boy.”
The shadows of Barney’s crew filtered between the thorn-bushes and spindly tree trunks. Only a few yards away separated Mitchell from having the snot kicked out of him.
“Come in,” the house seemed to whisper to him. It was swaying, as though in an inviting dance. “I never have company.”

Dark memories flashed through Mitchell’s head of nights around campfires, hearing stories that made his stomach hurl smores. He shook his head. Campfire stories were tall tales. Everybody knew that. He turned the knob, and shoved the door open a crack. It wouldn’t move any further.
There was the smack of Barney’s fist against his palm. “Mitch, get ready to be Mitch mash.”
Mitchell had to move further, room or not.
Wriggling his body between the crack, Mitchell could feel his lungs cave. He’d just barely made it through when Barney and his crew made their way across the wood.
“I don’t think we should be in here,” said one of Barney’s friends. “Didn’t a butcher make hotdogs out of dead bodies in there?”
“I heard it was an old midget, and that he also drank napalm to breathe fire,” said another.
Barney rubbed his hands together and paced in a circle.
“Where do you think he went?” someone asked
Mitchell slammed the door. There was a collection of gasps.
“He went in the house,” somebody said.
There was a snort of derision from Barney. “Mitchy has a stomach for a lot of things, but not that. There’s no way he’s left the same. Can’t wait to watch the police drag his body out. Come on guys.”
There was a series of crunches. With a wheeze, Mitchell pressed his back against the door as a barricade. Minutes ran by, and there was not a sound. Barney had left.

Mitchell peeled his sweaty back from the door and made his way down the hall to the house. It was just as tattered as the exterior to the house had been. Most of the floorboards were rotting, and the wallpaper was curling toward the ceiling. Books were strewn across the floor, covered in bite marks – no doubt from hungry mice. There were a few squeaks, followed by the slight pattering of mouse feet. Other than that though, there was a distinct lack of life.

Perhaps it was better that way. The outside of the house had given him the creeps. Besides, he’d earned the right to be alone. His mother had constantly been pushing him to go outside and make friends. Every time though, it was hot enough to melt an entire ice cream store, and all anybody wanted to do was pummel him into the ground.
Most kids sucked. The whole world sucked, in fact. Maybe this was a fact of life?
At least he could be safe in this cruddy house. It wasn’t scary as anybody had said it’d be. Maybe tall tales really were just that.
He let out a sigh of relief.
“Perfect day to kick back, and rest.”
Mitchell gulped. The words were the exact sort of thing he would’ve said. Yet, he hadn’t said them.
“Then again, some people never rest. Wouldn’t you say?”
There was the slightest creak. Mitchell wished with all his soul that it was more mice. Even rats would be alright.
Reluctantly, Mitchell turned. He jumped. “Jesus!”
There was a woman, who was practically glowing. No — she was glowing. Her skin had a bluish hue to it. Her whole body levitated above the ground, and a rush of dust whirled below her feet.
“That’s right! You better be scared!” she growled. “I know what you’ve done! You’re not going to avoid my judgement!”
Mitchell’s back was raw, after colliding into bits of plaster jutting from the wall. Yet, the shock from his pain paled when compared to his shock from this pale phantom.
“I was just playing with cards,” the boy whimpered. “And then I was chased. I only came because I had to — honest.”

“You were chased, were you? Eighteen years of avoiding me, and that’s your explanation?” the ghost said. She shrieked and rushed toward Mitchell. “No, you won’t get away! I can’t tell you how much thought I’ve put into this moment!”

Suddenly, her movements weren’t so sudden. The whole room slowed down. The ghost was actually a beautiful woman, when one looked past the general aura of death about her. Her blue hair flowed from her head as a river, and her face possessed fairylike features. At least, fairly fairylike. Her eyes were what entranced Mitchell most. They were an endless tunnel that scrunched up in such a funny way.
Then, it hit Mitchell that he was about to get hit. Time resumed.
“Eighteen years?” Mitchel whimpered, and scrambled from the wall.  “I don’t even know how to drive a car!”
The woman collided with the wall, knocking down a picture frame.
“Maybe if you weren’t always drunk, you’d have better luck!”
Mitchell looked back the way he came; the ghost was blocking the way. He ran further down the hall. There had to be another exit somewhere.
“Hey, come back and face me like a man,” the ghost cried out. “You’re really blurry — my glasses fell off before I entered the afterlife, so I can’t see three feet in front of my feet.”

She couldn’t see him? Thank god. Mitchell doubled over and took in giant heaves. It was just his luck that he’d jump from one horrifying chase to another. If he kept up this rate, he’d be on track to run track.

Mitchell ducked his head toward the ground, as a vase hurled over his head. It was followed by a plate, turned flying saucer. Looking down each side of him, he only found dead ends. The ghost was floating down the hall now, her eyes more squinty and furious than ever.
“You’re a dead man, Derrick!” the ghost said. “My heart was broken in two by you. Do you now that?”
Maybe there was another way out of this. Mitchell fought to catch his voice, as a wheezing attack rose in his chest. He should’ve brought his inhaler. Stupid move.
“Can we do time out? Really, please!” Mitchell said, lifting his grubby palms. “Who’s Derrick? I’m not him.”
The ghost only sped up her pace, her arms flailing wildly at the air. Mitchell closed his eyes, bracing for impact. A ghost couldn’t be worse than a dodgeball. Hopefully.
“You might be right,” the ghost said with a huff. “You look nothing like Derrick.”
Mitchell reopened his eyes. The ghost was a mere two inches from his face, studying him intensely. Mitchell took a step back.
“I think I’d know if I was Derrick,” said Mitchell. “I’m not a big dummy.”

The ghost smirked. “Are you sure you’re not Derrick, just pulling a trick on me somehow?” she said. She was hovering around the room now, attempting to clean up the debris that had been strewn about. Yet, wherever she hovered, a chilly air blew the debris from beneath her.
“Not again,” she muttered, under her breath. “Fool me nine times, shame on you. But, ten times?”

Mitchell crossed his eyes. All of those stories, and this was what was in the house? He went back down the hall, for the main entrance. If he could get out of here with his head, it would be an achievement.
“Where are you going?” the ghost said.

“I want to go home.” Mitchell’s mind was already alit with the thought of resuming his videogames. He’d been about to beat one of them. “Sorry to break into your house and stuff, Miss… Miss Ghost. It was an accident, really.”
He tried breaking into a sprint, but the carpet moved away beneath him. Worse, a cramp cut into his side.
“Excuse me?” the ghost said, her voice raising.
The ceiling quaked, with flakes of dust falling everywhere. Mitchell rubbed his hair; he was going to look like he had worse dandruff than he already did.
“What kind of manners are those?” The ghost had hovered her way back in front of Mitchell. “You break into my house, and you think you can walk out without even giving me your name?”
Mitchell shrugged. “I’m not supposed to give my name to strangers.”
Especially strange strangers, he thought.
“I could’ve called the cops on you,” said the ghost.
“Technically, you don’t own this house anymore.”
“The afterlife doesn’t care about technicalities!”
Calling the police actually didn’t sound half bad. Mitchell looked around. There were no phones, from what he could tell. The electricity probably wouldn’t have worked, anyway.
“It’s Mitchell,” he said, relenting.
“Thank you.” The ghost made a smirk. “Also, my name isn’t Miss Ghost. It’s Maddy.”
Maddy. That fit. Mitchell puckered his lips and fought to keep himself from snorting.
“So, can I go now?” Mitchell asked.
“No.”
Maddy nudged Mitchell back away from the door, and toward the kitchen. Wincing, Mitchell scoured the house for windows to jump out of.

“You sure you don’t want to stay for a snack?” Maddy asked. Mitchell shook his head, but Maddy was already rifling through the cupboards. “Trust me, it’s no trouble. Believe it or not, regretting the sins of one’s past life gets dull after a spell. You have no idea how hard it is to live here for forty years, without a person to talk to, or anything to do.”
That last bit sounded like a dream to Mitchell. He wrote “become a ghost” in his mental bucket list.
Maddy raised her hands in despair. “I can’t even eat anything!”
Mitchell scratched it out.
Maddy floated to Mitchell, with a fossilized biscuit. Sheepishly, Mitchell took the biscuit and pretended to take a bite. It was a stone.
“So, who’s Derrick?” Mitchell said, more to distract Maddy’s attention than anything.
Maddy looked to the ceiling, with a wistful look in her eye. Mitchell tossed his biscuit, as she did.
“A selfish, no good, cheating piece of—,” Maddy stopped herself. “How old are you?”
“Twelve.”
“He was a very no good man.”
Mitchell nodded. “I see.”
“There are a lot of regrets I have,” Maddy said, with a sigh. “But, no matter. How’s your world getting by?”
Mitchell paused. Nobody ever asked him how his life was going; not really.

“It’s good mostly, I guess,” said Mitchell. “School sucks. I don’t like my teachers. Or my classmates. The weather is bad, also. Too hot. But, it’s nice in my room. You’d probably like it outside, better than in here.”
“The world outside definitely sounds familiar.” Maddy was smiling now. The blue was beginning to fade from her body. “So, if you like being in your room so much, what brought you here?”
Mitchell itched his arms. The wood’s thorns had created a bit of a rash along them.
“Barney,” he said. “Well, actually, my mom made me go outside. He was out there. He made his friends throw rocks and chase me, for one of my cards.”
Mitchell stopped, and cleared his throat. His face was blotching, and his eyes were starting to burn. He’d had just about enough of this stupid haunted house.
“It gets better,” Maddy said.
Mitchell didn’t buy it and wasn’t sure if she bought it either.
“What about you?” Mitchell asked. “If life turns out so great, why did you wind up as a ghost?”

“Before I died… Well, I vowed to prove whether there are any more good men on Earth,” she said. “A fair enough statement, I guess. Unfortunately, it’s not the sort of vow you should give before you die.”
Mitchell laughed. “I’m glad that I’ve never died while making any of my dumb promises.”
“Promises are definitely dumb.”
Mitchell shook his head. “Not all promises,” he said. “A good promise just depends on who and what. You just put your best foot forward.”
Maddy’s eyes widened, in a sort of awe. “Is that so?”
“Yeah. I made a promise that I could hang upside down for ten minutes, once. They all laughed. Really didn’t think I could. I did.”
A bit more of the blue from Maddy faded. She had dark hair, and her eyes were an intense green. Yet, as the blue faded, Maddy seemed to be fading too.
“These boys… Do they bother you a lot?” Maddy asked.
Mitchell shrugged. “Mostly when Barney is around. He always gets them to gang up on me. I could probably take him if I really tried, though.”
“Probably not easy, I imagine.”
“Definitely not easy. My mom keeps telling me to just kill them with kindness. I’ve tried. Really. But, it just… It doesn’t really work.”
“Stay strong. Stay above it.”
“That’s easy for you to say,” Mitchell said. He gestured at Maddy’s feet. “You’re always up in the air.”
“More than you even know…” Maddy muttered. She cleared her throat. “Whatever you do Mitchell, don’t stop being who you are. Do that, and they’ll eventually learn to accept you. You’re a good person.”
Mitchell looked back to the main entrance. It all sounded great, but pulling that sort of thing off was another thing entirely.
